title: Report: Steve Tisch was present for NFL quarterly ownership meetings
summary: The NFL is having a less-than-ideal week when it comes to optics.
full_text: The NFL is having a less-than-ideal week when it comes to optics. Beyond the ongoing mess arising from the handling and the messaging relating to the health situation involving Eagles quarterback Jalen Hurts, former Giants co-owner Steve Tisch continues to pop up at team and league events. The January release of the Epstein files implicated Tisch, through emails he exchanged with Jeffrey Epstein, and created an obvious problem that needed to be investigated . The league vowed to " get the facts first " before deciding whether to discipline Tisch. Then, after Tisch and his siblings transferred their equity into their children's trusts, Commissioner Roger Goodell pointed out when pressed on the inaction that Tisch is no longer an owner . But Tisch remains the Giants’ chairman of the board . And he was front and center in the draft room in April. The photo attached to this article was taken at the Week 2 Monday night game in L.A. Most recently, Tisch was present for Tuesday's quarterly ownership meetings in New York, via Mark Maske of Front Office Sports . The obvious question is why? And the best explanation for the entire situation seems to be that, when the league and the Giants faced a delicate situation regarding what to do about Tisch, someone decided that the right answer was for Tisch to put his equity into trust for his children and otherwise behave as if nothing happened. And so Tisch is technically out, but he's still very much in. And the paperwork regarding the equity transfer to the people who would have inevitably inherited it anyway gave the NFL the perfect cover not only to take no action but to otherwise turn the page and move on. That's always the play. Find a way to turn the page and move on. Given the NFL's 365-day news machine (which has allowed this specific outlet to survive for nearly 25 years), there's always a next page.
author: Mike Florio

title: Reports: Titans released DT Jordan Elliott after he went to car to get gun
summary: Multiple reports detail a situation that could have turned into a tragedy.
full_text: '' On Tuesday, the Titans abruptly released defensive tackle Jordan Elliott without elaboration as to the "incident" that sparked the move. Multiple reports indicate it was a serious situation that could have gotten a lot worse. Austin Stanley and Easton Freeze of AtoZSports.com and Aaron Wilson of KPRC in Houston report that Elliott went to his car to get his gun following an altercation on October 15. Via AtoZSports.com, the Nashville Metro Nashville Police Department said on Tuesday afternoon that no reports had been filed regarding the incident. Wilson's report adds more details . Per Wilson, Elliott and tackle JC Latham argued after a play. Elliott was then told to leave the practice field. Elliott reportedly went to the players' parking garage to get his gun from his car. Titans defensive tackle John Franklin-Myers de-escalated the situation. It's unclear whether he actually got the gun and brought it back to the practice field. Presumably he did; if Franklin-Myers had simply stopped Elliott from going to his car, that likely wouldn't have been enough to prompt the Titans to cut Elliott. Via Wilson, the whole thing was captured by surveillance cameras. Elliott, 28, had signed a two-year, $8 million contract in the offseason. A third-round pick of the Browns in 2020, he spent four years in Cleveland and two in San Francisco. He played last year for Titans coach Robert Saleh, during Saleh's second, one-year stint as the San Francisco defensive coordinator. After appearing in the first five games of the 2026 season, Elliott was inactive for Sunday's win over the Colts. The Titans eventually decided to cut Elliott five days later, and the entire situation had been kept under wraps until the Titans released Elliott without explanation. It's unclear whether the league was informed of the incident. It would have been prudent, if not mandatory, for the Titans to promptly contact the league office, both to inform them and to seek advice on how to proceed.
author: Mike Florio

title: Dan Quinn tells Jayden Daniels to "take your shot" even then there's a penalty flag on the field
summary: One of the lingering questions from this week's Monday Night Football relates to the perception that Commanders coach Dan Quinn didn't know his team was facing a fourth-and-two play from the San Francisco 13 when it was, you know, facing a fourth-and-two play from the San Francisco 13.
full_text: One of the lingering questions from this week's Monday Night Football relates to the perception that Commanders coach Dan Quinn didn't know his team was facing a fourth-and-two play from the San Francisco 13 when it was, you know, facing a fourth-and-two play from the San Francisco 13. After the game ended, Quinn (who was ready to address the viral lip-reading moment) said he " definitely " knew it was fourth down, before essentially acknowledging that he didn't instantly realize a post-snap foul on the offense could be declined. At his day-after press conference (which, by virtue of the fact that it happened means he hasn't been fired, yet), Quinn addressed the decision of Jayden Daniels to throw the ball to a wide open Sourdough Sam, who was standing in his 49ers mascot costume well beyond the back of the end zone. "Even when you know there's a penalty, like, you still take your shot, man, to go throw it, complete it, you don't know if it's gonna get picked up," Quinn said regarding his message to Daniels. It's more than the flag getting picked up. A penalty on the offense, coupled with the decision of the officials to not stop the play, didn't alleviate the obligation to get a first down. It remained a "gotta have it" play. It didn't become an occasion to throw the ball away. Daniels addressed the situation in his post-game press conference. "I've just got to execute better in that situation regardless of a flag or not," Daniels said. "You know, fourth down . . . I have to be better, you know, in that spot." But it wasn't a matter of better execution. It was a matter of better real-time decision-making. He decided to essentially give up on the play. Daniels also confirmed that he knew a flag had been thrown. "I did know. I didn't know what it — it could have been offsides, it could have been on us," Daniels said in response to the last question of the session. "You know, I'm not really into that type of stuff, you know?" The final comment is confusing. Why wouldn't he be "into that type of stuff"? The concept of situational football doesn't end when a play starts. Things can happen during a play that dramatically change the situation. In this case, the flag created one of two new situations. If the defense was offside, it was a free play. In that situation, Daniels should have taken a shot to the end zone because the penalty always could have been accepted if it didn't work out. If the penalty was on the offense, he still needed to convert. No one knew what the flag was for, but since there wasn't an obvious jump by the defense (which we see all the time, and which quarterbacks like Aaron Rodgers always use to go for the jugular), the best decision in that situation would have been to try to get the first down, no matter what. The worst decision would have been to just throw the ball out of the end zone, which is the decision Daniels made. It's another example of an institutional failure to coach Daniels to be ready for all situations and/or a failure of Daniels to want to have all the answers for all possible situations. Based on Quinn's comments, Daniels got coached about it after the game. Why wasn't he coached about it before the game? The end result further reveals the tangible flaw in the overall approach to ensuring that the quarterback, the offensive coordinator, and head coach aren't taking a trial-and-error approach to pro football. Again, it's not on-the-job training. The training happens (or at least it should) during meetings, practices, more meetings, more practices, even more meetings, and even more practices. All that said, the more reasonable explanation is that Quinn and Daniels didn't know it was fourth down. While not as egregious as what happened at the end of overtime against the Giants, it makes the lingering bad vibes regarding the institutional command of situational football a little bit worse.
author: Mike Florio

title: 49ers are the heaviest division favorites in the NFL
summary: San Francisco's odds to win the NFC West are at -650
full_text: Prior to this season, the NFC West was expected to be the most competitive three-team race in football, with the Rams as the favorites, the defending Super Bowl champion Seahawks close behind, and the 49ers a good team but a clear third. Six weeks into the season, things look different. The 49ers are now 6-0 and the overwhelming favorites to win the NFC West. In fact, with the betting odds at -650, the 49ers are the heaviest favorites to win their division of any team in the league. The Seahawks are a distant second at +630, the Rams are third at +1200, and the Cardinals are the NFL's longest long shots to win their division at +15,000. The 49ers have a three-game lead over the 3-3 Seahawks and a four-game lead over the 2-4 Rams and Cardinals, and the 49ers have already beaten all three division rivals head-to-head. It would take something totally unforeseen for the NFC West to end any other way than with the 49ers on top. The NFL's next-biggest division favorites are the Jaguars at -290 to win the AFC South. The Chiefs are -250 favorites to win the AFC West, the Bills are -200 favorites to win the AFC East, the Panthers are -120 favorites to win the NFC South, the Ravens are -110 favorites to win the AFC North, the Vikings are +105 favorites to win the NFC North and the Cowboys are +130 favorites to win the NFC East.
author: Michael David Smith

title: Report: Rams TE Terrance Ferguson not ready to come off IR
summary: The Rams placed tight end Terrance Ferguson on injured reserve with an ankle injury on Oct. 2.
full_text: '' The Rams placed tight end Terrance Ferguson on injured reserve with an ankle injury on Oct. 2. That makes him eligible to return to practice next week. Adam Schefter of ESPN reports that Ferguson is not ready, and "it will take some time" before his 21-day return-to-practice window opens. Ferguson left the Week 3 game against the Broncos with his injury. He has seven catches for 63 yards and a touchdown. The 2025 second-round pick made 11 catches for 231 yards as a rookie.
author: Charean Williams

title: A.J. Brown sends prayers, support to Jalen Hurts
summary: Patriots wide receiver A.J.
full_text: Patriots wide receiver A.J. Brown didn't leave Philadelphia on the best of terms with Eagles quarterback Jalen Hurts. But Brown still wishes the best for Hurts, who is out for the season with multiple blood clots in his lungs. " It’s a tough situation , man," Brown said Tuesday, via Glenn Erby of USA Today. "I've got a lot of love and respect for him, praying for him. I didn't know how serious it was. I think all of us kind of found that out, but he's a tough guy. He's a tough guy, and he can handle anything. . . . He can handle it, and I pray God continue to keep his hand on him. It's a lot of love and respect from this way." Hurts and Brown played together for four seasons before the Eagles honored the wide receiver's trade request on June 1. Brown caught 339 passes for 5,034 yards and 32 touchdowns in his four seasons in Philadelphia, making two Pro Bowls and helping the Eagles win a Super Bowl. Once close, they did not speak after the trade until a joint practice in August.
author: Charean Williams

title: Report: Jay-Z selects Jay-Z to do Super Bowl LXI halftime show
summary: For each of the past two Super Bowls, the NFL announced the halftime performer in September.
full_text: ' For each of the past two Super Bowls, the NFL announced the halftime performer in September. As October enters the homestretch, there has been no announcement as to Super Bowl LXI in L.A. On Tuesday, Dave Brooks of Puck reported that Jay-Z, who produces the annual spectacle, has selected himself to do the honors for the next Super Bowl. Per the report, Justin Bieber and Miley Cyrus also were considered. The NFL first hired Jay-Z in 2019 to produce the Super Bowl halftime show, with a renewal in 2024. The arrangement reportedly pays $5 million per year. Brooks notes that Jay-Z could make the announcement this weekend, when he plays a pair of shows at SoFi Stadium, the site of the next Super Bowl. There presumably would be some sort of big splash in conjunction with ESPN/ABC which is televising the Super Bowl.
author: Mike Florio

title: NFL looking to play 10 international games in 2027, possibly with one in Asia
summary: The NFL will play a record nine international games this season.
full_text: The NFL will play a record nine international games this season. The league has approval to play up to 10 next season, and NFL executive Peter O'Reilly said that number is being discussed. “We like continuity, but we are looking at new regions, and Asia would be one of them,” O'Reilly said. In 2026, the NFL will play in Australia, Brazil, the United Kingdom, France, Spain, Germany and Mexico. O'Reilly has previously mentioned taking the game to Japan and Italy. The Saints and Steelers will play the first NFL game in France on Sunday.
author: Charean Williams

title: Allen Sills dismisses concern about team physician bias as "nonsense" (it's not)
summary: When it comes to whether the Eagles properly handled the health care provided to Eagles quarterback Jalen Hurts for his blood clots, the NFL is hardly a neutral, disinterested party.
full_text: When it comes to whether the Eagles properly handled the health care provided to Eagles quarterback Jalen Hurts for his blood clots, the NFL is hardly a neutral, disinterested party. It was the NFL, through chief medical officer Allen Sills, that arranged for the evaluation of Hurts in London, which is part of what the league does to support all NFL teams that are imposed upon to play internationally. On Tuesday, Sills spoke to reporters at the quarterly ownership meeting in New York. And he arguably protested too much when it comes to lingering concerns about the NFL's culture regarding medical care for players. "Any idea or any suggestion that a team physician is ever being influenced by a coach, a General Manager, a team owner — it just doesn't happen," Sills insisted. "There is no doctor who is taking orders from a football person, a non-medical person. Period." Setting aside whether he's directly aware of how all 32 teams operate (he surely isn't), in this context an express order isn't needed. Team-hired doctors understand the assignment; the teams want players to be available to play. In nearly every case, the player wants to be available, too. Any doctor who develops a reputation in the building for being unnecessarily cautious when it comes to clearing a player to play will inevitably be replaced by a doctor who will. And those assignments are very lucrative, both in what they pay to the doctor and in how they provide the doctor with built-in marketing for the rest of the doctor's practice. "The notion that there are external factors or that any of our physicians would put a player in harm's way, that's nonsense," Sills said. The dismissal of that possibility does not mesh with the facts. The mere existence of the Unaffiliated Neurotrauma Consultant program for diagnosing concussions and clearing players to return from concussions directly refutes Sills's contention. If team doctors could be relied upon in every instance to set aside the unspoken (because it doesn't need to be said) urgency to find that a potentially concussed player is good to go or to clear a concussed player to return, there would be NO NEED for doctors with no team affiliation. As to most other health issues, the situation isn't as critical. Orthopedic injuries don't put a player at risk, and a shot or two of Toradol never hurt anyone, right? (Well, maybe not .) In those rare instances where the shared desire for the team and the player to "be available" intersects with the player's best interests as a patient, there's inherent pressure on the team-hired doctor to get along by going along. It's unfortunate that Sills refused to recognize this basic fact. Hopefully, he said it for P.R. purposes and not because he truly believes it. Finally, Sills invoked "patient privacy concerns" to justify not taking questions about the treatment Hurts received. That's a copout. Hurts has already authorized the issuance of multiple statements that shared with the world various details about his private medical issues. It's easy to use "patient privacy concerns" as a shield when, in reality, the player quite possibly would authorize doctors to answer any and all questions about a situation that has already become extremely public. At this point, why would Hurts object to his doctors explaining what they did and why they did it? Through it all, the NFL and the Eagles simply want to move on. All's well that ends, as the late NFL Commissioner Paul Tagliabue liked to say. Hopefully, this one won't end until all necessary questions are asked and answered — and until the NFL recognizes that, for certain health conditions, a UNC-style approach is needed.
author: Mike Florio

title: NFL will have heightened security for game in Paris after recent civil unrest
summary: The game in Paris between the Steelers and Saints will go on as scheduled Sunday.
full_text: '' The game in Paris between the Steelers and Saints will go on as scheduled Sunday. The NFL, though, said it will heighten security in light of the civil unrest in the French capital. NFL executive Peter O'Reilly said Tuesday the league is coordinating with the U.S. State Department and Parisian and national authorities overseas. “There’s nothing more important from our standpoint than the teams’ security, the fans’ security — everybody involved with this game,” O’Reilly said at the fall league meetings, via the Associated Press. “Obviously being very vigilant in everything we do, in all of our planning on an hour-by-hour basis, working closely with the two teams.” Rioting erupted across France on Saturday as demonstrators protested rising living costs and declining public services. It was the country's worst civil unrest in years, with violence and looting in major cities as rioters clashed with police. The NFL did not consider moving the game, which is being played at Stade de France outside of Paris in Saint-Denis. It marks the NFL's first game in France. "We feel confident that we would not have any impact on the broader resources needed," O'Reilly said. “That’s always top of mind for us, and we feel confident that we wouldn’t be depleting resources in a negative way around this game.” The Saints flew to Paris after their victory over the Giants on Sunday. The Steelers will travel later this week.
author: Charean Williams

title: NFLPA calls for "full investigation" into Jalen Hurts situation
summary: Union issues statement regarding the NFL's handling of the case.
full_text: The NFL Players Association has chimed in on the story that the NFL and the Eagles would very much like to see go away. The NFLPA issued a statement on Tuesday night calling for an investigation into the handling of the Jalen Hurts situation, which resulted in the player traveling to London with a blood clot in his leg, playing with a blood clot in his leg, and traveling back to Philadelphia with a blood clot in his leg. “The NFLPA is not aware of any NFL investigation into the medical care provided to Jalen Hurts," the union said. "In fact, the league previously informed the union that it did not plan to review the care he received. Before conclusions are drawn about how this situation was handled, there must be a full investigation into what occurred. Determining the facts is essential to ensuring players receive the highest level of care and protection going forward.” Given that NFL investigations regarding the proper application of the concussion protocol typically take a couple of weeks to resolve, it's odd (to say the least) that the NFL would so quickly conclude that the Hurts situation "was handled appropriately" by the team. Everything about this situation smacks of a desire to close the book and move on, and to question or criticize anyone who would raise fair and proper questions. Fortunately, the NFLPA is now among those asking the same questions.
author: Mike Florio

title: Eagles-Commanders stays in prime time for Week 8
summary: NFL reportedly "strongly considered" replacing it with Browns-Steelers.
full_text: The NFL considered moving the Week 8 Eagles-Commanders game out of prime time. In the end, the NFL decided to stay put. Via multiple reports, the rematch of the Week 1 game between NFC East rivals will be televised nationally by NBC and Peacock on Sunday night, November 1. Rob Tornoe of the Philadelphia Inquirer , who first reported that the NFL was thinking about moving Eagles-Commanders out of the Sunday night spot, reports that the league strongly considered replacing it with Browns at Steelers. In past years, there has been a rule requiring one of the two home-and-home games between division rivals to be televised on Sunday afternoon. The fact that the league considered moving Browns-Steelers to Sunday after their Week 4 game in Cleveland was played on Thursday night shows that, if the rule still exists, it's more of a guideline. Either way, it'll be the 2-4 Eagles (who don't have their starting quarterback) and the 1-4-1 Commanders instead of the 4-2 Browns and the 4-2 Steelers in a game that would have featured Mike Tomlin's return to Pittsburgh and Cleveland's reward for claiming first place in the AFC North after six weeks of the 2026 season.
author: Mike Florio

title: Sunday's late-afternoon window on CBS averaged 26.368 million viewers
summary: The late-afternoon window on Sunday continues to generate the biggest audiences for NFL viewing.
full_text: ''' The late-afternoon window on Sunday continues to generate the biggest audiences for NFL viewing. In Week 6, the CBS 4:25 p.m. ET kickoff — which had Bills-Raiders and Chargers-Chiefs both getting extensive distribution — racked up 26.368 million viewers. It was the most-watched broadcast on any network for the week. Usually, the 4:25 p.m. ET window is dominated by one specific game. The split between two of the NFL's most popular teams and two of its best quarterbacks combined to deliver, across the board. This week, Fox has the 4:25 p.m. ET games, with Packers-Lions undoubtedly getting top billing. The other game at 4:25 p.m. ET is Rams-Raiders.
author: Mike Florio

title: Rams put Davante Adams, Poona Ford on IR
summary: Wide receiver Davante Adams is expected to miss the next 6-10 weeks after rupturing his hamstring in last Sunday's loss to the Cardinals and the Rams moved him off of the active roster on Tuesday.
full_text: '' Wide receiver Davante Adams is expected to miss the next 6-10 weeks after rupturing his hamstring in last Sunday's loss to the Cardinals and the Rams moved him off of the active roster on Tuesday. The Rams announced that Adams and defensive tackle Poona Ford have been placed on injured reserve. Ford is going to miss the rest of the season with a triceps injury. The only corresponding move was the previously reported signing of kicker Brandon McManus. He replaces Blake Grupe, who was placed on injured reserve Monday due to a torn ACL. Adams had 30 catches for 480 yards and four touchdowns, so his loss leaves a sizable hole across from Puka Nacua at the top of the team's receiving corps. Konata Mumpfield, Tutu Atwell, and Jordan Whittington have 13 combined catches for the Rams this season. Ford had 15 tackles and a tackle for loss while appearing in all six games this season. Kobie Turner is also expected to miss extended time with a groin injury, but he has not been placed on injured reserve at this point.
author: Josh Alper

title: Eagles sign RB Elijah Mitchell to active roster, waive Jaydon Blue and Carson Steele
summary: The Eagles made changes to the running back room on their 53-man roster on Tuesday.
full_text: The Eagles made changes to the running back room on their 53-man roster on Tuesday. They announced that they have signed Elijah Mitchell off of their practice squad. They also waived Jaydon Blue and Carson Steele. Steele was waived with an injury designation after hurting his shoulder in Week 6. Mitchell signed with the Eagles this offseason and returned to the practice squad after being cut in August. He played in one game for the Chiefs last year and ran 327 times for 1,523 yards and nine touchdowns over three seasons with the 49ers. Blue signed to the active roster ahead of last Sunday's loss to the Panthers, but did not play. Steele had one catch for four yards against Carolina and played in two games overall. The other backs on the roster are Saquon Barkley and Dameon Pierce. Barkley has missed the last two games with a hamstring injury.
author: Josh Alper

title: Patriots CB Carlton Davis upgraded to limited practice participation on Tuesday
summary: The Patriots got cornerback Carlton Davis back at practice on Tuesday.
full_text: ' The Patriots got cornerback Carlton Davis back at practice on Tuesday. Davis was listed as a non-participant on Monday's estimated practice report due to the neck injury that has kept him out of three games this season. Davis has 16 tackles in his three appearances. Guards Ben Brown (knee) and Alijah Vera-Tucker (hamstring) remained out of practice. Head coach Mike Vrabel said both players are likely to miss Thursday's game against the Bears. Defensive tackle Joshua Farmer (personal) was also listed as a non-participant for the second straight day. Wide receiver A.J. Brown (ankle), cornerback Channing Canada (hamstring), right tackle Morgan Moses (foot), and cornerback Karon Prunty (hamstring) remained in the limited category. Kicker Andy Borregales (personal), offensive tackle Marcus Bryant (ankle), safety Kevin Byard III (chest), offensive tackle Will Campbell (knee), linebacker Christian Elliss (chest), running back TreVeyon Henderson (ankle), linebacker Dre’Mont Jones (shoulder), quarterback Drake Maye (right shoulder) and safety Craig Woodson (shoulder) were all listed as full participants.
author: Josh Alper

title: Justin Tucker was among five kickers the Dolphins worked out
summary: The Dolphins worked out five kickers after cutting Riley Patterson, who missed an extra point in Week 5 after missing two field goals earlier in the season.
full_text: The Dolphins worked out five kickers after cutting Riley Patterson, who missed an extra point in Week 5 after missing two field goals earlier in the season. They signed Zane Gonzalez . Among those trying out, though, was former Ravens kicker Justin Tucker, according to the NFL's personnel notice. Since serving a 10-game suspension for violating the league’s Personal Conduct Policy over sexual misconduct allegations, Tucker has tried out for the Saints, Colts, Jets, and now Dolphins over the past two seasons. Multiple women accused Tucker of misconduct during massage-therapy sessions. He denied the allegations, and he was never charged criminally or sued civilly. He has not signed anywhere since, last playing in the league in 2024. He is a five-time first-team All-Pro, who has made 89.1 percent of his field-goal tries. Tucker, though, converted a career-low 73.3 percent of his field-goal attempts in his last season. He also missed two extra points. Michael Badgley, Will Ferrin and Joshua Karty were the other kickers who tried out for the Dolphins on Tuesday.
author: Charean Williams

title: Bears list Jonah Jackson as a limited practice participant
summary: The Bears had one change to their estimated practice report on Tuesday.
full_text: '' The Bears had one change to their estimated practice report on Tuesday. Right guard Jonah Jackson (hip) was upgraded to the limited category after being listed as a non-participant on Monday. The Bears only conducted walkthrough sessions each day. Jackson played 50 of the team's 77 offensive snaps during their Week 6 win over the Falcons. Running back Kyle Monangai (toe, thumb), linebacker T.J. Edwards (hamstring), and linebacker Jack Sanborn (concussion) were listed as non-participants for the second straight day. Linebacker Keyshaun Elliott (quad) and cornerback Tyrique Stevenson (hip) remained in the full participation category. The Bears will issue injury designations for Thursday's game against the Patriots on Wednesday afternoon.
author: Josh Alper

title: 49ers release DL Naquan Jones
summary: The 49ers released defensive lineman Naquan Jones, the team announced Tuesday.
full_text: The 49ers released defensive lineman Naquan Jones, the team announced Tuesday. The 49ers could be making the move to clear a roster spot for wide receiver Christian Kirk. Kirk's 21-day return-to-practice window opened last week. He has been on injured reserve all season with a calf injury. Jones appeared in three games and totaled two tackles with the team this season. James Thompson's return made Jones expendable. Thompson returned Monday night after missing time with a high ankle sprain in Week 2, and Jones was inactive. Jones, 28, has appeared in 63 games with eight starts in his six seasons, totaling 104 tackles, 6.5 sacks and five passes defensed.
author: Charean Williams

title: Giants sign LB Trace Ford to active roster
summary: The Giants announced a series of roster moves on Tuesday afternoon.
full_text: The Giants announced a series of roster moves on Tuesday afternoon. Those moves included the official releases of running back Najee Harris and linebacker Jihad Ward. Both moves were reported earlier in the day. Linebacker Trace Ford will fill one of the openings on the team's 53-man roster. Ford was signed off of the practice squad, but the Giants left the other spot open for a future move. Ford played at Oklahoma State and Oklahoma before signing with the Giants as an undrafted free agent in 2025. He has played in three games this season as a temporary elevation and has seven tackles.
author: Josh Alper

title: Owners approve Arctos purchasing a limited stake in the Falcons
summary: NFL owners approved Arctos' purchase of a limited stake in the Falcons on Tuesday, the team announced.
full_text: NFL owners approved Arctos' purchase of a limited stake in the Falcons on Tuesday, the team announced. The transaction was for 7.5 percent of the team. Arctos has also committed to an additional 2.5 percent stake at a later date, subject to a separate vote of NFL ownership. It was previously reported that 10 percent of the team has a valuation of $10.6 billion . Arctos, founded in 2019 and acquired by KKR in 2026, is the largest institutional investor in professional sports franchise stakes globally and the only firm approved for multiteam ownership across all five major U.S. leagues (NBA, NFL, MLB, NHL, MLS). “We are pleased to welcome the team at Arctos to our ownership group as a limited partner,” Arthur Blank, the team's owner and chairman, said in a statement. “Arctos has an impressive track record and has garnered tremendous respect across the sports landscape for their expertise and business acumen. Most importantly, they align with our Core Values and share our vision for continued investment in the organization and our surrounding community. “The proceeds from this transaction provide additional resources to further strategic investments in my family’s philanthropic focus areas as we continue our pursuit of helping create a brighter future for the people and communities we serve. I also express my gratitude to Byron Trott and the team at BDT & MSD Partners for their time and expertise through this process.” Blank owns 73 percent of the franchise. Other limited partners are Brian Barker, Rosalind Brewer, Ron Canakaris, Dominique Dawes, Warrick Dunn, Doug Hertz, Alan Kestenbaum, Edward Mendel, Will Packer, Derek Smith and Rashaun Williams.
author: Charean Williams

title: Rams add K Brandon McManus
summary: The Rams have found a new kicker.
full_text: '' The Rams have found a new kicker. According to multiple reports, veteran Brandon McManus has agreed to join Los Angeles. McManus, 35, was most recently with the Packers last season. He made 24-of-30 field goals and 32-of-33 extra points in 14 regular season games. But in the playoff loss to Chicago, he missed two field goals and an extra point, leading the Packers to move on in the offseason. McManus is a Super Bowl champion, having won it with Denver to cap the 2015 season. He made all 10 field goals and all three extra points in that postseason run. In 186 career regular-season games, McManus has made 82.0 percent of his field goals and 97.4 percent of his extra points. Los Angeles placed kicker Blake Grupe on injured reserve on Monday after he suffered a torn ACL during Sunday’s game against the Cardinals. The club had released Harrison Mevis last week after a rough start to the season. The Rams will be on the road to face the Raiders in Week 7.
author: Myles Simmons

title: League reportedly concludes Jalen Hurts's blood clot "was handled appropriately" before Week 5 game
summary: NFL, Eagles were and are in lockstep on situation that has many unanswered questions.
full_text: To no surprise, the NFL won't be taking any action against the Eagles for its handling of the Jalen Hurts blood clot prior to Hurts playing in Week 5. While the league has yet to issue a statement to that effect (or to make anyone available for questioning by reporters on the issue), an unnamed source told Jonathan Jones of The Athletic that the NFL has concluded the situation " was handled appropriately " by the team. It's not a surprise because the Eagles have said , and the league has confirmed , that the team "remained in communication" with the NFL throughout the process. That's the best way to avoid league scrutiny; the Eagles involved the league in the various decisions that were made. Jones also reports that Dr. Allen Sills, the NFL’s chief medical officer, worked with the Premier League's chief medical officer to have Hurts evaluated at the Cleveland Clinic in London on the evening of Saturday, October 10. The unnamed source told Jones that the team, the staff, the doctors, and Hurts determined he could play the next day against the Jaguars at Tottenham Hotspur Stadium. Jones also reiterates the claim, which surfaced after multiple reports claimed Hurts was advised not to sleep , that Hurts "returned to the team hotel around 2:45 a.m. local time Sunday and slept until about 10 a.m.," and that he "took a nap" at the stadium before the game. The unnamed source also repeats (as the NFL told PFT last week ) that the team did not violate the injury reporting rules by, for example, failing to downgrade Hurts to "questionable" the moment his availability was, you know, in question or by failing to disclose that his "calf" injury was in reality a blood clot. Again, the league's position isn't a surprise. The NFL and the Eagles were and are in lockstep on this issue, which based on the evidence that has been disclosed to date calls into question a lingering cultural reality that healthcare for players seems to be more about checking the boxes required to allow a player to " be available " to play and less about treating the player like any patient who would show up with a problem that requires diagnosis, treatment, and recommended steps to ensure a full and successful return to health, with all other considerations taking a back seat. Much more should be demanded of the league and its teams on issues like this. So far, however, the NFL Players Association has been conspicuously silent. Many details remain unavailable. Reports from established "insiders" have painted a picture that has been confusing at times, downright bizarre at others. From the question of whether the league and its teams are truly providing meaningful healthcare to player-patients to the question of whether the league and its teams are creating even more inside information that could be misused for betting purposes (while the millions who are constantly bombarded with gambling ads are kept in the dark regarding the truth as to a player's health), the Hurts case raises very real questions that, with the passing of time, the playing of more regular-season games, and the inevitable emergence of the next story that attracts the media's attention, will fade away and never be adequately answered.
author: Mike Florio

title: Caleb Williams has gone from 32nd last year to first this year in completion percentage
summary: Bears quarterback Caleb Williams is a different player in 2026.
full_text: '' Bears quarterback Caleb Williams is a different player in 2026. In 2025, Williams finished the season ranked 32nd in the NFL with a completion percentage of 58.1 percent. This year, Williams ranks first in the NFL with a completion percentage of 72.5 percent. On Sunday against the Falcons, Williams completed 30 of 36 passes, a completion percentage of 83.3 percent. That was the best mark of his career. Williams is throwing the ball more accurately than ever. When Ben Johnson became the Bears' head coach last year, one of his stated goals was for Williams to have a completion percentage of at least 70 percent. Even as the Bears and Williams improved significantly in Johnson's first year, Williams' completion percentage stayed low. But during training camp this season, Johnson sounded confident that Williams' completion percentage was going to keep trending upward . Johnson couldn't have been more right about that. Williams is throwing the ball more accurately than any quarterback in the NFL.
author: Michael David Smith

title: Falcons release LB Bralen Trice

The 2024 third-round pick has appeared in four games this season — the first four of his career. He’s registered two total tackles and one pass defensed in 76 defensive snaps and five special teams snaps. Atlanta also announced the club has signed linebacker TJ Quinn to its practice squad.

title: Cowboys sign QB Kyle Trask to their practice squad

full_text: The Cowboys needed a third quarterback after losing Joe Milton off their practice squad. Milton signed with the Eagles this week after Philadelphia starter Jalen Hurts was lost for the season. Dallas signed quarterback Kyle Trask to the practice squad, the team announced Tuesday. He joins Dak Prescott and Sam Howell at the position. Trask spent training camp with the Panthers, but has remained a free agent since they cut him Aug. 30. He was briefly on the Falcons' practice squad last season. The Cowboys also announced they signed safety Juanyeh Thomas to the active roster from the practice squad. In a corresponding move, they waived cornerback Caelen Carson.
author: Charean Williams

title: On the day his six-game suspension ended, Jed York attends quarterly NFL ownership meeting
summary: On the same day his six-game suspension following an August arrest in Ohio ended, 49ers owner Jed York was present at the quarterly gathering of the most exclusive club in American sports.
full_text: On the same day his six-game suspension following an August arrest in Ohio ended, 49ers owner Jed York was present at the quarterly gathering of the most exclusive club in American sports. Via multiple reports, York is attending the 2026 fall meetings in New York. York quickly pleaded no contest to a pair of misdemeanors after he was arrested in a prostitution sting operation in East Palestine, Ohio. He had arranged a meeting with a fake sex worker, and he was apprehended while looking for a fictitious lot at a trailer park. He voluntarily skipped three games. Earlier this month, the NFL suspended York for six games, giving him credit for the three games in which he self-suspended. The league also fined York $500,000. As mentioned earlier today and on PFT Live , the NFL has a lingering disparity regarding the financial consequences of player and owner suspensions . Players, when suspended, lose 100 percent of their compensation. They also become potentially responsible to repay portions of previously-paid signing bonuses or roster bonuses. Owners lose none of their NFL income; they simply pay a separate fine. And that won't change, because the league is the owners. Changing the suspension formula to match the impact of player suspensions would be the equivalent of Congress voting to enact term limits or any other bill that would directly impact them in a potentially negative way. It also won't change because there's no public push to change it. There's no public push for it to change because few in the media make the point that the system creates a dramatic difference between the impact of a suspension on a player's earnings and an owner's.
author: Mike Florio

title: Panthers waive OT Albert Reese
summary: The Panthers waived offensive tackle Albert Reese, the team announced Tuesday.
full_text: The Panthers waived offensive tackle Albert Reese, the team announced Tuesday. The Panthers signed Reese as an undrafted free agent out of Mississippi State, and he made the initial 53-player roster. He has been inactive for every game this season. Taylor Moton's return made Reese expendable, with 11 offensive linemen on the active roster. But he could return to the practice squad if he clears waivers. The Panthers have not made a corresponding move, leaving their roster at 52 players.

title: Cowboys LB DeMarvion Overshown says he will return to the lineup this week
summary: The Cowboys won't have Dee Winters this week after the linebacker strained his Achilles in the loss to the Packers.
full_text: The Cowboys won't have Dee Winters this week after the linebacker strained his Achilles in the loss to the Packers. But they will have linebacker DeMarvion Overshown back this week. Overshown expects to return for Monday night's game against the Eagles after missing five games due to a hamstring injury. “I’ve definitely taken this rehab, this recovery, very serious," Overshown said, via Jon Machota of TheAthletic.com. "I’ve been trying to get back on the field since the week after I got out, so getting this opportunity to go this week, I’m thankful that I’m still able to get to do what I love.” Overshown seems likely to wear the green dot in his return. Overshown has played 20 games and missed 38 with injuries in his four seasons. He has totaled 125 tackles, five sacks, one interception, four passes defensed and one forced fumble.

title: Colts add WR Mecole Hardman, P Thomas Morstead to practice squad

full_text: After firing General Manager Chris Ballard on Monday, the Colts have added a couple of depth pieces to their greater roster. title: Eagles will not be punished for how team handled Jalen Hurts' blood clots situation, NFLPA responds
summary: The NFL concluded the process to clear Hurts for Week 5 in London was handled appropriately
full_text:
The Philadelphia Eagles will not face any punishment from the NFL regarding how they handled Jalen Hurts ' medical situation, according to The Athletic . On Monday, the team announced that Hurts is expected to miss the rest of the 2026 season after blood clots were discovered in his lungs.
The league has reportedly concluded that the process that led to Hurts being cleared to play in Week 5 vs. the Jacksonville Jaguars in London with a superficial blood clot "was handled appropriately." The league will not levy any punishment on the franchise for how it handled its medical process, or for Hurts not being given an injury designation ahead of the game.
On Tuesday, the NFL released a statement providing more information on what it knew regarding Hurts' situation and the medical professionals treating him. The league says it was in contact with the Eagles during the tests, going back to the first one in London. The league also clarified what it called "misinformation" regarding reports that Hurts did not sleep for 36 hours ahead of their international game.
Here is the full statement from the league:
"The league had been in contact throughout the process with the Eagles medical personnel, and the Cleveland Clinic in London where the tests were conducted. The league's Chief Medical Officer Dr. Allen Sills arranges for medical resources with leading providers in every international market with approval from the NFL Players Association. Medical care for players is provided by club medical staff in coordination with independent doctors. There was also misinformation regarding Jalen not sleeping for 36 hours before the game. That was not true and no one told him not to sleep because of his situation. The club told all players, coaches and personnel to try to stay awake as long as they could on Saturday as the team was returning back home after the game in London. The team did not have a bye week and like other NFL teams that travel to London and back, they were trying maintain as much of a normal routine as possible."
The NFL Player's Association (NFLPA), released a statement on Tuesday night responding to reports that the NFL will not punish the Eagles for the handling of the situation. They claim the league informed the union that they didn't plan to look further into the management and treatment of Hurts' health. The NFPA is asking the league to launch a full investigation.
Here is the full NFLPA statement :
"The NFLPA is not aware of any NFL investigation into the medical care provided to Jalen Hurts. In fact, the league previously informed the union that it did not plan to review the care he received. Before conclusions are drawn about how this situation was handled, there must be a full investigation into what occurred. Determining the facts is essential to ensuring players receive the highest level of care and protection going forward."
On Thursday of last week, the Eagles issued a statement saying that a superficial blood clot in Hurts' calf experienced movement, leading the team to rule him out for their Week 6 matchup against the Carolina Panthers . The Eagles also revealed that the NFL was made aware of the situation last week. It was the first of several confusing developments that led to more questions than answers.
Just days after Hurts' blood clot diagnosis became public, it was reported that the team did not plan to place him on injured reserve. Hours later, Hurts was being placed on injured reserve. Then came the bombshell on Monday, when a follow-up scan revealed Hurts' superficial vein thrombosis had developed into deep vein thrombosis, including "bilateral pulmonary emboli," meaning blood clots were now in both of Hurts' lungs.
It's not exactly clear why Hurts was allowed to play a football game and take a long international flight with a superficial blood clot, or whether the Eagles' decisions made his situation more serious. But the NFL has concluded that the team took the appropriate steps in handling the issue.
Jonathan Jones offered additional reporting to help clear up some misconceptions about this wild story.
There was a report that Hurts was told by doctors not to sleep as a precaution due to his blood clot, so he didn't sleep for 36 hours before playing against the Jaguars. The NFL specifically targeted this rumor in their statement, making it clear that the team was encouraged to stay up late to remain on Eastern time.
Hurts was not told to stay awake because of his medical condition. He returned to the team hotel around 2:45 a.m. local time on Sunday and slept until around 10 a.m. Hurts also took a nap at the stadium before kickoff.
Tom Pelissero eventually walked back this reporting, saying Hurts' agent clarified that while the quarterback was up until early Sunday morning being evaluated at a hospital, he was able to sleep before the game.
Saturday, Oct. 10: Superficial blood clot discovered in Hurts' calf during a visit to the Cleveland Clinic in London following a team walk-through.
Wednesday, Oct. 14: Follow-up appointment in Philly reveals superficial blood clot had moved, causing Eagles to shut down Hurts indefinitely. He undergoes further testing.
Monday, Oct. 19: Eagles and Hurts' agent, Nicole Lynn, issue a joint statement laying out the updated diagnosis of deep vein thrombosis. Here's the full statement:
"Over the last few days, Jalen Hurts has received comprehensive medical evaluations by physician experts. In the interest of transparency, we are providing additional information on the diagnosis and treatment plan related to his condition.
"Jalen was initially diagnosed by specialists in London with a left calf superficial vein thrombosis. After further testing and monitoring, the current diagnosis is a deep vein thrombosis, as well as bilateral pulmonary emboli. He is clinically stable and has no significant functional limitations. His treatment should only involve anticoagulation (i.e. "blood thinners"). During this time, he will not be allowed to participate in any contact activities, including football.
"Jalen's prognosis is very good, and we expect a full recovery. We anticipate that he will have the opportunity to resume contact football activities when off the blood thinners. In the meantime, he will remain active around the team and continue to condition. More importantly, we anticipate that he will have no long-term effects."
author: Jordan Dajani

title: NFL, Saints address plans for Paris game during Week 6 as protests escalate in France
summary: The league says its continuing with its original plans and monitoring the situation
full_text:
Protests escalated in France over the weekend over living costs and education, raising concerns over the NFL game between the Pittsburgh Steelers and New Orleans Saints scheduled to take place in Paris on Sunday. The unrest stems in part from citizens demanding better school conditions, teacher shortages and public services, but it has since grown as violent groups have rioted, clashed with police, and set fire to public buildings. At least 1,800 across the country, according to CBS News .
Hundreds of thousands have taken to the streets across the nation to demand change from the government, as both protesters and law enforcement have turned to violent methods. Concern over player, personnel, and fan safety has become the main topic surrounding next week's international game, the first-ever regular-season matchup to take place in France.
The league said they are increasing security for the game and said officials are collaborating with Parisian and national authorities overseas and the U.S. State Department, saying, "presence will be heightened."
NFL Executive VP of club business, international and league events Peter O'Reilly provided a security update at the league's annual fall owners meeting. He said the league has had people in Paris for the last 10 days.
"There's nothing more important from our standpoint than the teams' security, the fans' security -- everybody involved with this game," O'Reilly said . "Obviously being very vigilant in everything we do, in all of our planning on an hour-by-hour basis, working closely with the two teams."
He added, "We feel confident that we would not have any impact on the broader resources needed. That's always top of mind for us, and we feel confident that we wouldn't be depleting resources in a negative way around this game."
O'Reilly said there was never a time when the league felt the game couldn't be played in Paris and that "all our plans for the Paris game are moving forward."
The league released a statement last week saying they still plan to conduct the game as scheduled on Oct. 25 and provided a similar update on Sunday after news of the social unrest spread.
"Preparations continue as scheduled for NFL events and the game at Stade de France next Sunday," the NFL said . "We continue to work closely with local authorities and partners on all operational and security matters. We are also providing the two clubs with regular updates. There's been no disruption or impact at league sites."
Saints executive Greg Bensel backed the league's statement and offered some insight into the league's safety precautions.
"We concur with the NFL's statement and are planning to play the game. In addition to working closely with the NFL, we have also maintained daily security updates with our security partners in France," Bensel said . "Members of our football operations staff and internal security team have been on the ground in France for the past few days and there has been no disruption or impact at any of our team sites."
Last week, the league's statement said, "We're excited for the first-ever regular season game in Paris, and preparations continue as scheduled for NFL events and the game at Stade de France on October 25. As we do for every NFL game, including our international games, we work closely with local authorities and partners on all operational and security matters. We look forward to welcoming fans to Paris later this month."
The game is scheduled for 9:30 a.m. ET, 2:30 p.m. local time.
The league has changed games in the past due to various factors, including weather and field conditions, so it is not entirely out of the realm of possibility that the game could be moved. The Saints are considered the home team, so if they did move it, which they clearly do not plan to do right now, New Orleans would be the obvious new location.
While protests have taken over Paris, it's not the only place in France affected. Here's more from CBS News:
"Authorities said masked groups on Saturday set fires and attacked public buildings, including city halls, in several cities.
"In Limoges, a city in central France, flames engulfed the 19th-century City Hall, causing its roof to collapse. Haute-Vienne prefect Maurice Barate told LCI television that the fire was deliberately set and nearly destroyed the building. The fire was under control Sunday."
"Around Paris' Place de la République on Sunday morning, dislodged cobblestones, shattered storefronts and broken glass marked the aftermath of the events. Looting and damage were reported around the square and in some other tourist and shopping areas in the city center.
"Paris police said Sunday that 855 people were arrested in the French capital region alone. The Paris prosecutors' office said that 557 of them were kept in police custody."
author: Shanna McCarriston

title: Lions expect Kerby Joseph to play in 2026, Brian Branch nears return: Can Detroit defense turn a corner?
summary: With a healthy safety tandem, the Lions might be in for a defensive renaissance
full_text:
The Detroit Lions own the worst defense in the NFL , but help is on the way. They could soon have both starting safeties in the lineup for the first time this season, as Brian Branch is set to make his 2026 debut in Week 7 and Kerby Joseph is on track to play at some point this year.
Branch tore his Achilles last December and opened the year on injured reserve, but the Lions opened his practice window on Oct. 7, and coach Dan Campbell said on Monday that he expects the former Pro Bowler to be activated ahead of Sunday's divisional showdown against the Green Bay Packers . Campbell noted, however, that Branch could be on a snap count in order to ease his way back into action.
The return of one half of the safety tandem shifted the attention to the other. Joseph is on the PUP list with an inoperable, chronic knee issue which dates back to last year's training camp, and he has not played since October 2025. But Campbell said he expects Joseph to suit up this season.
"He's doing well," Campbell said . "I'll leave it at that. He really is. He's doing a good job. I'm not gonna give you a timetable, but I've been pleased with where he's at. He's in a good headspace right now, which is great, because that's hard. You're coming off this, you're wanting to go, and you're working at it, and at some point it's time for football. We all know that and recognize it, but we'll take it one day at a time."
The last time Branch and Joseph spent a full healthy season together as the leaders of the Detroit secondary, the team enjoyed its best defensive campaign in a decade. The Lions fielded the seventh-ranked scoring defense in 2024, which helped them win a franchise-record 15 games and reach the divisional round of the playoffs.
Joseph is a former first-team All-Pro who led the NFL in interceptions in 2024. Whether he will ever return to that level largely depends on his ability to stay on the field with the long-term knee problem, but if he is even partially as productive upon his return, he and Branch could again form one of the league's most proficient safety duos. For a Detroit team that has been ravaged in the defensive backfield over the last year, their reemergence could be a difference-maker.
The discrepancy between Detroit's top-flight offensive output and woeful defense is a perennial issue, but it reached a new level in 2026 with the safeties on the sidelines. The loss of cornerback Terrion Arnold hurt immensely, too, with his untimely arrest and release from the roster this past offseason limiting the Lions' ability to backfill the position. This team is the worst in the NFL at preventing opponents from moving the ball and ranks 30th in scoring, which entirely neutralizes the unstoppable attack of Jared Goff , Jahmyr Gibbs , Amon-Ra St. Brown and Sam LaPorta on the other side of the ball.
While Detroit should be expected to buy aggressively at the trade deadline, it might not have to address the safety position. If the in-house options are back at full strength for the stretch run, the front office can focus primarily on investing in the cornerback group. Upgrades over the current starters at both safety spots, plus one of the corner positions, ought to deliver at least modest improvement in pass defense, if not a dramatic turnaround.
Following their 3-2 start, the Lions stand in sole possession of last place in the highly competitive NFC North, half a game back from the Green Bay Packers and Chicago Bears , who are tied for second behind the undefeated Minnesota Vikings . The division is well within reach, but not if the Lions cannot defend the pass. Last week's win over the Arizona Cardinals was the first time they won a game by more than one possession.
author: Carter Bahns

title: Commanders' Terry McLaurin out for the season after knee injury on 'MNF'
summary: McLaurin suffered a torn patellar tendon in Washington's loss vs. the 49ers
full_text:
Commanders wide receiver Terry McLaurin 's season is over. Washington head coach Dan Quinn told reporters on Tuesday that McLaurin suffered a torn patellar tendon and will be sidelined for the remainder of the 2026 season.
On Monday Night Football, the WR was carted off with his left leg in an air cast late in the first quarter of Washington's Week 6 "Monday Night Football" loss at the 49ers . The fear, according to Quinn's postgame comments, was always that it was a significant injury, and tests on Tuesday confirmed it.
McLaurin went down while running a route, clutching at his knee, and was unable to get to the sideline under his own power.
Commanders WR Terry McLaurin was carted to the locker room after suffering an apparent knee injury on this play. Hope he's okay 🙏 pic.twitter.com/1XL4ezzQgi
McLaurin, 31, has been a staple for Washington since being drafted in the third round in 2019. He had missed one game (Week 4) due to a hamstring injury but still leads the Commanders with 230 receiving yards this season, including a 27-yard catch early in Monday's contest.
McLaurin's injury is just the latest for a snake-bitten Commanders team that lost Jayden Daniels (elbow) for a couple of games earlier this year and has not had Laremy Tunsil all season after he tore his triceps in training camp. Marcus Mariota , Stefon Diggs , Sam Cosmi and Chig Okonkwo have also missed time, and starting running back Jacory Croskey-Merritt landed on IR this week as well.
Washington (1-3-1) trailed 14-3 at the time of McLaurin's departure. The Commanders mounted a second-half comeback, but couldn't finish, falling to the 49ers, 23-17.
author: Zachary Pereles

title: Mr. Irrelevant to Mr. Efficient: How Brock Purdy became NFL's all-time passer rating king
summary: A former seventh-round draft pick is now the greatest per-throw passer in league history
full_text:
There is a new all-time passer rating leader in the NFL . A mere five years ago, nobody would have expected his name to be Brock Purdy .
The San Francisco 49ers quarterback was one pick away from going undrafted in 2022, and now he stands atop the career leaderboard for the ultimate signal-caller efficiency metric. Purdy threw his 1,500th pass in Monday's 23-17 win, which made him eligible for inclusion in the career passer rating standings and earned him a spot ahead of active surefire Hall of Famers like Lamar Jackson and Aaron Rodgers . He is also the all-time standard-bearer for success rate and adjusted yards per attempt.
Also in the Week 6 victory over the Washington Commanders , Purdy joined elite company with the third-most games with a 110 passer rating or better over the first five seasons of a career. Only Russell Wilson and Patrick Mahomes accumulated more, per Next Gen Stats.
Purdy, a two-time QBR leader, is far from the most physically gifted quarterback in the NFL. But he leads all players in touchdown passes this year with 14 and accounted for the longest completion of the season thus far with an 82-yarder. He might be on his way to the MVP award. He has been the best player on the best team through six weeks, but his MVP case goes deeper than that; he is the primary reason why the 49ers are Super Bowl favorites.
Not bad for a "game manager."
Purdy shed that label — or perhaps instead perfected the art of game management — during his rise as one of the league's preeminent passers. The longer he plays like the most efficient quarterback in NFL history, the more he looks like a steal as the final pick of the 2022 draft. Purdy will always be known as a former "Mr. Irrelevant," but he is as relevant as anyone in football through six games in 2026.
That begs the question of how the 49ers pulled off the biggest steal of the 2022 draft. What did other teams miss in their evaluation of Purdy? What has San Francisco done to turn him into a star? How has he developed from a fringe prospect into an unstoppable passer?
Here is the formula behind Purdy's climb to excellence.
What Purdy lacks in stature as a 6-foot-1 quarterback and in physical tools, he makes up for with an uncanny ability to comprehend his offensive system and read defenses. That mental acuity has been the great equalizer between him and the more athletic quarterbacks, and it's arguably even given him a leg up on them.
"It's so important when it comes down to knowing coverages, knowing scheme, where our players are supposed to be, how many steps they're breaking and where the ball should be over a certain 'backer," Purdy said earlier in his career . "All those things, man, it matters. If you go to a combine and all those things, you're just throwing on air. Yeah, you look good with the strong arm and fast, jumping, all that stuff. But when it comes down to 11-on-11, and you've got guys that are a foot taller than you, and you can't see, it comes down to the processing."
That is precisely why Purdy thrives in the Kyle Shanahan offense.
The 49ers' system is designed to make life easy on the quarterback but only if he can process timing, anticipation and spatial awareness at a high level. All of the pre-snap motion in this offense not only confuses the defense but also requires the quarterback to comprehend how the defense will react. Purdy also has to recognize when a receiver will be open before he actually is. And the high rate of play action Shanahan calls forces Purdy to make quick decisions as defenders barrel toward him.
This week, Shanahan called Purdy "automatic" at running the system, which he said is the highest compliment he can give a quarterback.
There might not be a statistic more emblematic of Purdy's unmatched comprehension of the scheme than this: The Commanders on Monday blitzed him on 41.2% of his dropbacks (a season high), yet his 17.6% pressure rate was his second-lowest of the season. That speaks to his ability to make snap decisions. He gets the ball out of his hands quickly because he knows precisely where it needs to go. That will be on display again in Week 7 against an Atlanta Falcons defense that ranks second in pressure rate.
Purdy is among the most accurate passers in the NFL and ranks second in career completion percentage for active quarterbacks at 68.1%. His propensity to put the ball on the money is most obvious when he layers his throws.
The middle of the field is the most dangerous area in a Shanahan offense because of how linebackers and safeties tend to align themselves to stop it, yet Purdy is adept at picking that area apart with excellent touch on his passes.
The throw by Purdy and catch by Kittle 😮‍💨 WASvsSF on ESPN Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/TcSnsKxb3Z
49ers defensive coordinator Raheem Morris was bewildered by Purdy's ability to thread the ball through those tight windows in training camp and labeled him the "Layer King." Purdy pushed back on the moniker, but he explained to ESPN the art of weaving the ball over a linebacker just in time for his receiver to make the catch before the safety closes in.
"I think it's definitely one of the hardest throws on the field," Purdy said. "Those are things that I sort of prided myself on young ... Now in the NFL, I'm trying to take it to another level."
Purdy might not own the strongest arm, but it is potent enough to make all the throws asked of him. He is also arguably underrated as a runner. His oft-unsung quickness allows him to step up in the pocket and scramble to escape pressure laterally at an elite level. His sack avoidance metrics exemplify just how proficient Purdy is at frustrating opposing pass rushers.
The five sacks Purdy has taken in 2026 are the fewest of any quarterback. He also led the league in sacks taken per game last season (a more accurate measure than total sacks, since he missed eight regular-season games with turf toe) and ranked fourth in 2023.
Purdy averages a modest 156.6 rushing yards per season and will never rank alongside the more potent mobile quarterbacks like Josh Allen and Lamar Jackson, but his runs are effective, as his career rushing success rate of 56.3% shows. That is an above-average, albeit not elite, mark for a quarterback.
A lot of quarterbacks would succeed if they traded places with Purdy. His system and the stars around him are significant factors in his own accomplishments. That is not to take anything away from Purdy since, after all, he still needs to deliver the ball to his playmakers, but it does partially explain why someone with modest physical tools is able to produce at an MVP level. There are future Hall of Famers all over the San Francisco offense. Claiming that they are not a big part of Purdy's success would be disingenuous.
Christian McCaffrey , George Kittle and Trent Williams are all-time greats at their respective positions. McCaffrey and Kittle make the easy throws worth more than they might be in other offenses because of their tremendous yards-after-catch capabilities. Williams delivers some of the most reliable protection the NFL has to offer at left tackle. And this year in particular, Mike Evans has performed like arguably the most impactful free agent signee of the year.
Everyone in San Francisco makes everyone around them look better, and Purdy, with his incredible decision-making skills, perhaps elevates his offensive teammates as much as anyone.
author: Carter Bahns

title: Are the Rams cooked? A look at why Sean McVay's team is so disappointing, and if they can bounce back
summary: A disastrous special teams unit, Matthew Stafford's missing deep ball and a flurry of key injuries have sent the preseason Super Bowl favorites spiraling to a 2-4 start
full_text:
The Los Angeles Rams were the clear-cut favorite to win the Super Bowl this season. They had the reigning NFL MVP at quarterback with Matthew Stafford , a dynamic duo at wideout in Puka Nacua and Davante Adams , and a revamped defense that included trading for Myles Garrett , and persuading Aaron Donald out of retirement. This looked like it could be a super team, but through six weeks, the Rams are 2-4.
The supposed super team is currently dead last in the NFC West, and Sunday's 18-16 loss to the lowly Arizona Cardinals has the NFL world wondering whether the Rams will ever bounce back this year. This was the largest upset loss (13.5-point favorite) by an NFL team in about three years, and now the Rams have some ground to make up in one of the toughest divisions in the NFL.
Why are the Rams playing poorly and what does history say about their chances of bouncing back? CBS Sports researcher Doug Clawson dove into the numbers to provide us with some insight.
Stafford won MVP last year after leading the NFL in passing yards (4,707) and passing touchdowns (46). He hasn't looked the same this season. The stats back up the eye test. This Rams offense just hasn't been explosive like it was in 2025, and Stafford isn't going deep as often. Stafford ranks 14th in percentage of completions gaining 20+ yards (13%). Last year, he ranked third in that category (19%).
Percentage of passing attempts over 20+ air yards
Another factor in Stafford's struggles is his downfield connection with Puka Nacua -- or lack thereof. Stafford is 8 of 20 with zero touchdowns and two interceptions when targeting Nacua 10+ yards downfield this season, and has the same number of completions as interceptions (2) targeting him 20+ yards downfield.
It's not fair to say that the Rams offense is "bad." They rank top three in yards per game (401.3), joining the Kansas City Chiefs and Carolina Panthers as the three clubs that average over 400 yards of total offense, but L.A. ranks 20th in scoring offense (22.5). The New York Giants and Pittsburgh Steelers are scoring more points! There's certainly time for Sean McVay to adjust, but the explosive plays just haven't been there.
The Rams have the worst special teams EPA in the NFL this season (-35.8). That means their special teams have cost the Rams roughly 36 points through six weeks. No other team has a special teams EPA worse than -16.9. It's the worst special teams EPA by any team through 6 games since Washington in 2013 (-41.5).
What goes into special teams? Well, for starters, the Rams have the worst field goal percentage in the NFL this season at 60%. They are actually 3 of 7 on field goals in the fourth quarter or overtime over the past two seasons -- which ranks worst in the NFL.
The Rams are also the only team in the NFL to rank in the bottom 10 in kickoff and punt return averages... on BOTH sides this season. L.A. ranks third-worst in average starting field position (28.0), and opponent average starting field position (34.5).
Opponent kickoff return average
Opponent punt return average
As CBS Sports Research points out, the Rams have yet to play a game with all of their stars, as Myles Garrett and Aaron Donald haven't shared the field just yet. Garrett played 40 defensive snaps in the season opener before undergoing knee surgery that landed him on injured reserve. Still, Aaron Donald hasn't looked like Aaron Donald thus far, as he's recorded just two QB hits and seven pressures with zero sacks in four games this season. It's the first time in his Hall of Fame career that Donald has gone four straight games without a sack in a single season.
As we exit Week 6, injuries are beginning to mount for the Rams. That includes star wideout Davante Adams and a couple of important defensive tackles in Poona Ford and Kobie Turner .
Out 6-10 weeks (hamstring)
As you would expect, the 2-4 Rams are no longer the favorites to win the Super Bowl over at DraftKings Sportsbook, but surprisingly, they are tied with the Seattle Seahawks in having the fifth-shortest odds at +1200. Those are better odds than the Jacksonville Jaguars , Chicago Bears , New England Patriots and undefeated Minnesota Vikings .
With that said, odds aren't the best indicator of future success. According to our SportsLine projections, the Rams' playoff hopes have fallen from 90.1% to 26.0% since the start of the season. Their Super Bowl odds, on the other hand, have dropped from 16.3% to 1.5%.
So, the question is: can the Rams rebound? This is just the fifth instance where an outright preseason Super Bowl favorite has a losing record through six games over the past 50 seasons. None of the previous four teams made their conference championship game (2015 Seahawks, 2002 Rams, 1999 Vikings, 1987 Giants).
Only one team in NFL history has won a Super Bowl when under .500 this late into a season, and that was the 2001 Patriots. That year, quarterback Drew Bledsoe went down with a serious chest injury in Week 2 and was replaced by some guy named Tom Brady . New England started that season 3-4, but finished on an 8-1 run to win the division, and ultimately defeated Kurt Warner's Rams in the Super Bowl despite being two-touchdown underdogs.
