title: Jalen Hurts blood clot diagnosis timeline: Where the situation started, how it developed and what now
summary: A look at everything that's happened with Hurts' health
full_text:
Philadelphia Eagles quarterback Jalen Hurts is expected to miss the rest of the 2026 season after blood clots were found in his lungs. Speculation about the injury began shortly after the team announced he had a superficial blood clot in his left calf, which sidelined him for the Week 6 game against the Carolina Panthers .
The team said his prognosis is "very good," and he is expected to make a full recovery. He's currently on blood thinners, which prevent him from participating in any contact activities until he's fully recovered. The severity of the injury has caused great concern over Hurts' future and has some calling for an investigation into how the Eagles approached the injury and treatment.
A lot has transpired in a short amount of time, and the timeline can get a bit confusing. His diagnosis also changed over the course of a week. So let's break it down to the facts:
This is the game where Hurts said the blood clot was "provoked." He was cleated in his calf during the 24-20 loss.
After practice, Hurts sought treatment on his calf, the original spot of the blood clot. Hurts was listed with a calf injury on the Week 5 injury report, but he was a full participant in Friday's practice ahead of the Eagles' trip to London to face the Jacksonville Jaguars .
The team flew to London on the Friday before their international game, arriving late Friday night for the trip across the pond. The team would be in London for less than 48 hours. Hurts flew with the team, and the flight from Philly to London takes between seven and eight hours.
While in London, Hurts was seen by specialists, who reportedly found the blood clot through an MRI. According to reports, Hurts was in the hospital until 4 a.m. local time. Initial reports said Hurts was advised by medical professionals not to sleep and had been up 36 hours before taking the field on Sunday. However, the QB's agent, Nicole Lynn, later released a statement saying that although Hurts stayed up late, he managed to get some sleep before the game. She said the team set up a room for him at the stadium.
The Eagles' medical staff and independent doctors told Hurts and the team that "activity and mobility were important and that Jalen could safely play," per a statement the team released on Oct. 15.
Hurts played the full game, throwing for 220 yards and a touchdown. The Eagles lost 19-17 and fell to 2-3 on the season.
The Eagles flew home from London the night of the game. Hurts was on the flight, which, again, would have taken between seven and eight hours.
Hurts was once again listed with a calf injury, this time on the Wednesday, Oct. 14 injury report, but was a full participant. Speaking with the media, before his test, he called his injury a "unique experience."
After practice, he underwent a second ultrasound, where doctors found the blood clot had moved, which can lead to a serious health situation.
After being a full participant in Wednesday's practice, Hurts was a non-participant in both Thursday and Friday's practices.
The team released a statement explaining that Hurts was diagnosed with a superficial blood clot when he initially sought treatment. They made the announcement that Hurts would be sidelined for their Week 6 game.
pic.twitter.com/9SeK1XzYRL
The Eagles signed quarterback Joe Milton off the Dallas Cowboys practice squad. The move felt like a premonition of Hurts going on IR, due to the number of quarterbacks they were carrying.
Shortly after reports that they would not be placing Hurts on IR, the Eagles did, in fact, put the QB on IR . Any player on IR is required to miss a minimum of four games.
Hurts was ruled out ahead of the Week 6 contest, and Tanner McKee started in his place. McKee went 26-of-45 with 215 yards, one touchdown and no interceptions. The Eagles fell to 2-4 on the season.
The Eagles released a statement with an update on the situation. They said Hurts was "initially diagnosed by specialists in London with a left calf superficial vein thrombosis. After further testing and monitoring, the current diagnosis is a deep vein thrombosis, as well as bilateral pulmonary emboli." Pulmonary emboli means there were multiple blood clots now in his lungs, which is a serious situation.
The team said it expects him to make a full recovery and anticipates "that he will have the opportunity to resume contact football activities when off the blood thinners." More reports also came out at this time about Hurts' hospital stay in London and his lack of sleep before the Week 5 game.
pic.twitter.com/aBfyK55oxd
On Monday, there were multiple reports that Hurts' season was likely over, given his situation. While it seems likely, there has been no confirmation from the Eagles on an official timetable or return plan.
The Eagles will not face any punishment from the NFL for how they handled the situation, according to The Athletic . The report says the NFL concluded that the process "was handled appropriately." The league will not give any punishment to the team for how it handled its medical process, or for Hurts not being given an injury designation ahead of the game.
author: Shanna McCarriston

title: Rams QB Matthew Stafford on verge of tying NFL record for most losses ever by a quarterback
summary: While it's not a record Stafford likely wants to hold, it does show he's been solid enough to stick around this long
full_text:
It's been a rough year for the Los Angeles Rams so far. They were the preseason favorite to win the Super Bowl, but through six weeks, the Rams are just 2-4, and it's starting to look like a possibility they could miss the playoffs.
To make matters worse, if the Rams lose on Sunday, that would be the 123rd loss of Matthew Stafford's career, which would put him in a tie for the most losses by a quarterback in NFL history. That's probably an NFL record that he would prefer not to have.
As things currently stand, Stafford has 122 career losses, which puts him one behind Vinny Testaverde.
Let's take a look at the five quarterbacks with the most losses in NFL history:
Vinny Testaverde (1987-2007)
Matthew Stafford (2009-present)
To even make this list, you have to play for a long time, and Stafford has done that.
The 38-year-old has been in the NFL since 2009, when the Lions made him the No. 1 overall pick in the NFL Draft. During his 12 seasons in Detroit, he won many games, but he couldn't get the Lions over the hump. He never won a playoff game in the Motor City, and he eventually requested a trade out of town, which led the Lions to deal him to the Rams in 2021 .
During his first season in Los Angeles, Stafford won the first playoff game of his career while leading the Rams to a win in Super Bowl LVI.
Here's a look at Stafford's career record with each team:
With two more losses this season, which seems extremely likely at this point, Stafford will be the sole owner of the NFL record for most losses. As weird as it sounds, the fact that Stafford will likely break that record is actually a testament to his success and his longevity. If you're in the NFL long enough, no matter how successful you are, you're definitely going to lose at times. The key is to bounce back from failure.
If you fail too often as a QB, you'll eventually get benched, and you won't be around long enough to lose 122 games.
Of the five quarterbacks with the most losses, two of them — Brees and Favre — are in the Pro Football Hall of Fame, so Stafford does have some good company.
You have to have some success to stick around, and Stafford has definitely had that. Not only does he already have a Super Bowl win under his belt, but he was also voted MVP for the first time in his career in 2025. Those two things are what could eventually put him in the Hall of Fame.
Including Stafford, there are only 15 quarterbacks in NFL history who have won at least one Super Bowl AND one MVP. Of the previous 14, 10 of them are already in the Hall of Fame, and another three — Tom Brady, Aaron Rodgers and Patrick Mahomes — will soon be joining them. That means 13 of the 14 previous quarterbacks to pull off the Super Bowl/MVP double are enshrined in Canton or will be soon. The only QB not to make the Hall of Fame out of this group is Joe Theisman, who had his career cut short after suffering a gruesome leg injury in 1985.
Even if Stafford ends his career with the most losses in NFL history, there's certainly still a chance that he ends up in the Hall of Fame.
Unfortunately for Stafford, though, he'll likely hold the all-time losses record for the rest of his life. Aaron Rodgers (95 losses) and Joe Flacco (94) are the only active quarterbacks with more than 90 losses, and they likely won't end up playing long enough to break the record. Rodgers has already said he's going to retire after this year , and Flacco isn't currently a starter.
Outside of those two, Andy Dalton (83 losses) and Kirk Cousins (80) are the only other active quarterbacks with at least 80 losses. Dalton is no longer a starter, and it seems unlikely that the 38-year-old Cousins will stick around long enough to break the record, so those two are probably out.
Baker Mayfield might have the best chance to top Stafford. The Buccaneers QB is 31 and has a career record of 58-65. That averages out to a record of about 8-9 every year. If Mayfield plays just seven more seasons and averages an 8-9 record, that would put him at 128 losses, plus, you'd be able to add any losses that he suffers this year.
If Mayfield doesn't top the mark, then Stafford might one day make the Hall of Fame despite being the losingest quarterback in NFL history.
author: John Breech

title: What is the 'Peanut Punch' showing up across NFL? Why it's changing how defenses attack the football
summary: What was once a novelty is now a tool every defensive player uses
full_text:
During the second quarter of the Washington Commanders ' loss to the San Francisco 49ers , Niners' RB Christian McCaffrey took off through the middle of the defense on a screen pass. As Commanders' rookie Sonny Styles took McCaffrey down, EDGE K'Lavon Chaisson came flying in…throwing a punch at the football. The Peanut Punch, specifically.
The ball jumped out of McCaffrey's hands, onto the ground, and ended up being recovered by LB Frankie Luvu for a Commanders' turnover.
Elite peanut punch by K'Lavon Chaisson 👊 pic.twitter.com/zp180jRnz0
Fumbles are more and more common around the NFL this year, and part of it is due to the Peanut Punch. Once a novelty made legendary by Bears ' CB Charles "Peanut" Tillman, the Peanut Punch has become the primary cause of fumbles around the NFL. Through six games, there have been 175 forced fumbles, the highest number through six weeks since 2013. If we divide it between rushing and receiving, the 1.4% fumble rate on receptions is tied for the fifth-highest since TruMedia started tracking in 2000.
While there are many reasons for fumbles being so high, the expansion of the Peanut Punch around the league has been a very fun aspect to watch throughout the season. From players truly connecting on the punch and forcing fumbles to the wacky misses that end up seeing players get ejected for punching a guy's helmet, the Peanut Punch has become a constant threat to watch whenever your favorite team has the ball.
Despite being 2-4, the New York Jets have been one of the quietly fascinating teams to watch this season, mainly because they're forcing turnovers. They're second in the NFL in forced fumbles (10) through six games and have nine forced fumbles on the defensive side of the ball. In their loss to the Patriots on Sunday, LB Jamien Sherwood showed off some incredible hustle to force a fumble. When he got in range, guess what he did? That's right, he punched at the ball.
Jets head coach Aaron Glenn spoke to CBS Sports about how his team trains the timing of their punch-outs and how to judge punching the ball versus traditionally ripping it.
"I think it's two totally different situations," Glenn said. "There are some punch outs where, man, you want physical body on body, where you can punch and wrap. And then there are times when you're making an attack from an angle perspective to where, man, you want to take the ball, you want to rip it out.
"We practice both of them. We put in the same amount of time [practicing] both of them. I think they're both very effective techniques to be able to get the ball. I don't know where we're at for punch outs, but we have a number of balls from the ground. I think you can see our guys actually practicing those things. You get both of them from the punchouts and the rip out."
In a video the NFL released about the Peanut Punch, Philadelphia Eagles ' HC Nick Sirianni mentioned having the Eagles' video guy get them a cut-up of every fumble Tillman forced in his career, and he showed it to every coach and player on the team. Sirianni mentioned a blueprint the Eagles use to determine how and when to use the punch and get the ball out, and the Eagles have executed it well. Since Sirianni took over in 2021, the Eagles are second in the NFL in forced fumbles, behind the Pittsburgh Steelers .
What's really stood out about the Peanut Punch and its usage is that they've come from different angles. Players running in behind the ball carrier, angling in to help on a tackle. We've even seen DBs use it to force incompletions at the last second. In this story written about the Peanut Punch by ESPN's Matt Bowen in 2016 , Tillman is using the punch after squaring up a ball carrier and standing in front of them.
Tillman has used the punch from different angles before, but you don't really see many defenders squaring up and punching the ball out. It's primarily used to help defenders, coming in from different angles. Being able to get the ball out in practice like that is cool, but players attacking the football when the speed of the game is ratcheted up to 100 is what separates good teams from championship ones.
So how do ballcarriers protect themselves from the Peanut Punch? NFL legend and CBS Sports colleague JJ Watt broke it down during the Bills-Raiders broadcast. He showed that establishing more points of contact as a ball carrier prevents the ball from coming loose at the bottom, near the elbow, where it normally breaks free.
Holding the ball tightly and wrapping your other arm to create a harness with the ball prevents NFL players from getting the ball out, but it can also potentially break wrists ( as evidenced by Jim Nantz ):
JIM NANTZ JUST TRIED TO PEANUT PUNCH @JJWatt 🤣 "I did not think you were gonna go that hard" "my wrist is broken" 😭 pic.twitter.com/ocdRBn282r
Ball carriers on offense have to be hyper-aware of players punching at the ball in scrums and close quarters. New England Patriots' RB Rhamondre Stevenson has been on the wrong end of many fumbles in his career (seven since entering the league in 2021, to be exact), and with teams honing in on his hands, he has seen how teams are attacking the football.
"I think teams are just focusing on getting the ball out, no matter what they gotta do to get it," Stevenson said. "I think there's more punching, more ripping at it [the ball], and doing whatever they can to create a turnover."
Ballcarriers have to practice security against the Peanut Punch more often than ever now, because teams are going after them so much more.
Special teams is an area where Peanut punches can be especially chaotic, as is the case with kickoff or punt returns. New York Giants ' special teams coach Chris Horton said he talks with his team a lot about ball placement as a way to prevent becoming a victim of the Peant Punch.
"When we practice, we spend a lot of time emphasizing being intentional about protecting the football," Horton said. "If I'm running to the left, the ball should be on the left side, that way the defender can't punch it, or if he does, the ball is on the sideline and out of bounds. When we're out here [in practice], we want our guys going after the ball so we can get that experience so we know how to take care of the football."
The Peanut Punch has gone from a rare individual play to something you see in every game you watch on Sundays. When you're watching your favorite team protect or attack the football, you know that the punch is coming.
Most of the time, offenses know it too.
Yet, they still can't stop it.
author: JP Acosta

title: Jim Nantz says viral 'Peanut Punch' sparked calls from Josh Allen and a former U.S. President
summary: Nantz had some notable names checking in on him after the viral punch-out attempt in Week 6
full_text:
It's the "Peanut Punch" heard around the NFL . One of the subplots of the action that unfolded across the league in Week 6 resided in Las Vegas during the Bills-Raiders matchup. No, it didn't have anything to do with what happened on the field. Instead, it had to do with a viral moment inside the NFL on CBS booth with our friend and lead NFL play-by-play announcer Jim Nantz.
Nantz attempted to punch a football out of the grip of lead color analyst J.J. Watt's arm. As you might expect with a future Hall of Fame defensive lineman gripping onto the ball, Nantz was not able to create a turnover, and many — including some of the most powerful people on the planet — thought he hurt his wrist in the process.
"I've gotten more people reaching out to me with concern about what's going on with my wrist," Nantz told the Pat McAfee Show on Tuesday. "I was joking when I said right [after the punch], I think I broke my wrist. There was that immediate, like, reverberation thing going on.
"I heard from people you can't believe. Josh Allen texted me an hour after the game and said, 'Did you just break your hand? I'm hearing you broke your hand.' I heard from a former President of the United States, reached out and wanted to know if my hand was broken."
"I did go a little too aggressive with the peanut punch on @JJWatt and it did sting.. I gave it my best and as soon as I did it I regretted it.. I'm not gonna be on the injury report this week and I'm good to go" ~ Jim Nantz #PMSLive pic.twitter.com/qZ5GI4tZaO
That goes to show how much Nantz has become a fabric of our sports viewing experience that a former leader of the free world checked in on his status. While Nantz didn't go so far as to break his hand, he did acknowledge that it stung when it was hammered into the football.
"Let me clarify. I did kind of go aggressively here after this ball because J.J. encouraged me to do so, and it did sting. I'm not gonna kid you," he said. "JJ said, 'I didn't know you were going to come after it that hard.' Some are saying it was the greatest punch thrown in Vegas since [Manny Pacquiao] a few years back.
"I gave it my best, and as soon as I did it, I regretted it because I felt like everything had been compressed. I did think I was going to wake up Monday with [my wrist] about triple the size, but I'm fine. I'm not going to be on the injury report this week. I'm going to be good to go. No broken bones."
So, the good news is that we don't have to worry about Nantz landing on the injury report this week, as he declared he has no injury designation for Week 7. He won't even be questionable when he, Watt, and Tracy Wolfson travel to Baltimore, where the Ravens will host the Cincinnati Bengals .
author: Tyler Sullivan

title: Giants release Najee Harris days after criticizing New York's running back rotation
summary: The move comes right after the veteran voiced frustration over his limited role and a crowded backfield rotation in Week 6
full_text:
The New York Giants ' running back room and rushing rotation remain in flux, and they have just booted the back who started Sunday's game from the team. The Giants are reportedly releasing Najee Harris , per NFL Media.
Harris signed with the Giants in August, and rushed 31 times for 99 yards in five games played. He received the "start" for New York's Week 6 matchup against the New Orleans Saints , but rushed just four times for two yards.
Quarterback J.J. McCarthy , who entered the game in the fourth quarter, ended up leading the Giants in rushing with 26 yards on just two attempts. Tyrone Tracy Jr . rushed six times for 18 yards and a touchdown, Devin Singletary rushed four times for 14 yards and Cam Skattebo was not given a rushing attempt.
Harris criticized the Giants' running back rotation after the game on Sunday, saying it was difficult for anyone to find a rhythm.
"It's hard to get in a rhythm with one or two plays," Harris said, via The Trentonian . "The first couple runs will be like, 'OK, how are they playing it?' And then the next ones will be, 'OK, this is how you attack it.' But if you're getting a play here and then get taken out for a series, there's nothing you could do. That's why I'm saying, 'I don't know.' I've never been through none of this before."
Harbaugh was asked by reporters on Monday if he understood why Harris was frustrated with the rotation. The coach said he understood the frustration and respected it, but then explained that playing time had to be earned.
"I would love for us to be in that kind of a circumstance," Harbaugh said. "A Derrick Henry circumstance or a Saquon Barkley circumstance or whatever it might be. That would be great, and we haven't. Our run game hasn't earned that yet, and none of those guys have. My advice would be to any player, and it's all the guys, we had the same conversation. I've had the same conversation with all the running backs, the receivers, it's no different than any position, but do the most you can with the opportunities you get. Make the most of those opportunities and you're sure to get more opportunities. You know? Do something."
The Giants are likely to add another running back in the near future, but perhaps Harbaugh goes back to Skattebo in Week 7 against the Houston Texans . Skattebo, who lost a key fumble in overtime of the eventual Week 5 tie with the Washington Commanders , played just six snaps this past Sunday and did not receive any touches. He is the Giants' leading rusher on the season with 294 yards and one touchdown on 81 carries.
"I didn't expect to have zero," Skattebo said after the Saints game, via The Athletic. "I was expecting to not play as much just like I did. The message was to keep your head down and keep going. They understand the type of player I am, and I just got to continue doing my job and do it to the best of my ability."
Despite the uncertainty at running back, the Giants lead the NFC East at 3-2-1.
author: Jordan Dajani

title: Mike Evans injury update: WR avoids long-term injury, but how will 49ers fare if he misses time?
summary: The 49ers' offense struggled mightily in Evans' second-half absence against the Commanders
full_text:
The San Francisco 49ers had to finish their 23-17 "Monday Night Football" win over the Washington Commanders without their top receiver, as Mike Evans left the game just ahead of halftime with an Achilles tendon injury. While the 49ers held onto their lead and closed out the victory without him, Evans' absence was noticeable as the offense scored just three points in the final two quarters. Fortunately for San Francisco, Evans may not miss much additional time.
Coach Kyle Shanahan said after the game that Evans experienced a flare-up of the Achilles tendinitis that bothered him throughout the week and that he will not undergo further testing.
"It's something that he's had before, something that bothered him throughout the week," Shanahan said . "When you have Achilles tendinitis like he does, it kind of is what it is. It flared up tonight, and I hope he recovers throughout the week. You don't think it's a long-term thing, but right now it almost cost him this game and ended up costing him two quarters.
"Hopefully he'll be able to play next week, but if not, we'll have to have the rest of the group step up, and hopefully we can get him healed up by after the bye week."
It was a close call on whether Evans would suit up in Week 6 in the first place. He did not practice leading up to the game, and Shanahan noted that even though he declared himself healthy enough to play, there was always a chance that Evans would not be able to remain on the field for all four quarters.
Evans was seen during the game stretching his Achilles tendon. The flare-up occurred thereafter when he made a catch late in the second quarter. He immediately went into the locker room, and television broadcast cameras captured him grabbing at his Achilles in the tunnel.
The undefeated 49ers hit the road in Week 7 for a matchup against the Atlanta Falcons and will be idle the following week. They return from their bye in Week 9 for a home date with the Las Vegas Raiders .
If the tendinitis forces Evans to miss Sunday's game in Atlanta, the 49ers and their top-three scoring offense could have a difficult time moving the ball. The contrast in production with Evans in and out of the lineup against the Commanders was stark. He caught three passes for a game-high 94 yards in the first half as San Francisco rolled to a 20-3 lead, but the team managed just three points in the second half and nearly blew the three-score advantage.
Evans paces the 49ers in targets and receiving yards in his first year with the team and ranks 13th in the NFL in yards and sixth in touchdowns. He has been among the league's most prolific free agency signings from the 2026 offseason.
Shanahan chalked up the second-half struggles to sacks and a general lack of offensive execution, but it is difficult to imagine the 49ers would not have found it easier to move the ball if their top wide receiver was still on the field.
"It's definitely a big deal when you lose a player like Mike," Shanahan said. "Just the way it ended up being, Mike wouldn't have had a chance to have much of an effect there in the second half. Now, if we would've gotten some first downs and stuff and got driving, we would've felt the lack of presence of him, but we didn't get enough first downs to show where we would miss him."
Wide receiver injuries decimated the San Francisco offense over the season's first month and a half. While Shanahan said there is a possibility Christian Kirk will return from injured reserve for Week 7, it is not a guarantee. He also noted that Demarcus Robinson is unlikely to return for the trip to Atlanta.
The rash of injuries, amazingly, did not slow the 49ers down in their perfect start to the season. But if Evans joins the laundry list of unavailable receivers for any period of time, there is a chance the offense will look more like it did in the second half on Monday than how it appeared over the rest of its first six games.
author: Carter Bahns

title: Titans release DT Jordan Elliott after 'incident' at team facility
summary: The veteran defensive tackle appeared in all five games this season after following head coach Robert Saleh to Tennessee from San Francisco
full_text:
The Tennessee Titans earned their first win of the 2026 season and of the Robert Saleh era this past Sunday against the Indianapolis Colts , upsetting their rivals in Indy, 26-20. However, they were forced to release one of their defensive linemen this week after an "incident" at the team facility.
On Tuesday, the team announced that it had released defensive tackle Jordan Elliott after reviewing an incident that happened on Thursday. The Titans issued a statement through team reporter Jim Wyatt.
"On Thursday, Oct. 15, there was an incident at our team facility involving Jordan Elliott.
Following our review of the incident, we have made the decision to release Elliott from our roster. We will have no further comment on the matter."
It's unclear what the incident was or if any more information will come out about it.
Elliott has played in all five games this season with one start and has recorded 11 tackles. He followed Saleh over from the San Francisco 49ers , as Elliott spent the past two seasons out in Santa Clara, making 29 starts in 31 games played.
Elliott's surprising release is not the only strange occurrence the Titans are dealing with, as the team also made starting cornerback and $58 million free-agent addition Alontae Taylor inactive in Week 6. They didn't just bench him; they took his uniform away. It was described as a coach's decision, and Saleh has refused to elaborate on the situation.
"We'll discuss it as a staff and make a decision that is best for the team moving forward," Saleh told reporters on Monday.
The Titans return home this week to host the 4-2 Cleveland Browns , who currently lead the AFC North.

title: Dan Quinn denies confusion after viral fourth-down clip in Commanders loss to 49ers
summary: Broadcast cameras appeared to catch Washington's head coach surprised by a turnover on downs against the 49ers, but he insists he was just fielding a question from his staff
full_text:
To say Washington Commanders head coach Dan Quinn was under a microscope in Week 6 is an understatement. Washington was playing the best team in the NFL, the San Francisco 49ers, on a national stage eight days after the team ran out the clock on themselves in embarrassing fashion, leading to a 27-27 tie with the New York Giants .
How Quinn managed his timeouts and the clock was going to be something everyone was watching, and it almost looked like Quinn made another embarrassing gaffe early in the second quarter.
On a fourth-and-2 from the 49ers' 13-yard line, Washington elected to go for it. Quarterback Jayden Daniels threw the ball away — which is a conversation for another day — but there was a flag on the field. Officials called the Commanders for an illegal shift, and the 49ers declined the penalty, accepting the turnover on downs.
ESPN's cameras appeared to capture Quinn saying, "Oh! It was fourth down," as if he did not know the situation.
“Field goal.   Oh, that was 4th down?” certainly looks like lip readers believe Dan Quinn was completely unaware that it was 4th down and wanted to kick a field goal 💀💀💀 pic.twitter.com/yJYuAUmVZX
After the game, Quinn was asked about the video that had since gone viral on social media.
"No, I definitely knew it was fourth down," Quinn said. "We were going for it, and I was — I think what you're referring to, I was probably saying like, with the illegal shift, there's not a penalty to go for a field goal. Like, it doesn't go, like — it's the turn on downs. I think somebody had asked me, 'Can we kick a field goal?'  So, no, we were going for it. We knew we had to go for some fourth downs to be bold in the game.
"But no, I knew what happened. I think I probably was just commenting that I remember, at least on the headset, somebody asked me, after an illegal shift, like it was a turnover on downs, and Jayden saw the foul, too. He also came out and saw the penalty."
If you go back and watch the video, that does not look like what was happening. Quinn looked surprised that the play was fourth down, not that he was correcting someone else. But you never know what kind of conversations are going on in those headsets.
There are no moral victories in the NFL , but Monday night was not a total tragedy for the Commanders. Washington put together a strong second half, storming back from down 23-3 to score 14 unanswered points. However, the Commanders could not pull off the upset, and questions remain about the man in charge.
At 1-4-1, this is Washington's worst six-game start to a season since 2020, when the "Football Team" started 1-5. That team ended up rebounding to win the NFC East.
author: Jordan Dajani

title: Grading and ranking NFL first-year head coaches in new places after Week 6
summary: How the league's 10 new head coaches rank through the first third of the 2026 regular season
full_text:
With six weeks in the books, the NFL is now a third of the way through the 2026 NFL season. That means now is a fair time to check in on the 10 new head coaches hired this offseason.
Ten is tied for the most head-coaching changes in a single offseason ever, and six of the hires are first-time NFL head coaches. The head-coaching veterans in new places are Mike McCarthy, Kevin Stefanski, John Harbaugh and Robert Saleh. Here is a look at the 10 we will be grading and ranking through Week 6, listed in alphabetical order by team:
Let's dig into the 2026 new head coaches' report cards.
It's hard not to feel bad for rookie NFL head coach Jeff Hafley in his first season in charge. He's doing the best he can for a franchise that is paying more for players not on its roster (an NFL-record $179 million in dead cap hits) than for the players on its roster ($156 million) in 2026.
As a result, the Dolphins are just the fifth team since at least 1950 to not lead in any of their first five games of a season, per CBS Sports Research. They joined Washington (1954, 1965), the Minnesota Vikings (1962) and the Houston Texans (2005) as the only teams to pull off this sad feat. Miami has the worst scoring offense (14.0 points per game) by mere decimal points.
They entered 2026 with the least experienced roster (608 career starts) by any team to open a season in recorded history since such data tracking began at the start of the 21st century, per CBS Sports Research. They also had one career Pro Bowl selection on their roster entering Week 1, running back De'Von Achane in 2025, which is tied for the fewest by any team to open a season in recorded history (2000). Oh, and Achane went down with a torn ACL in Week 3.
That really makes it almost impossible to evaluate Hafley's acumen as an NFL head coach. He's playing with an arm tied behind his back on a weekly basis in Year 1 of the Dolphins' latest rebuild.
It's been a rough start to the Robert Saleh era in Tennessee. Offensive coordinator Brian Daboll's group has the NFL's second-worst scoring offense (14.0 points per game), mere decimal points ahead of the Miami Dolphins, and the league's worst total offense (236.3 total yards per game). Quarterback Cam Ward , the 2025 first overall pick, has the worst expected points added (EPA) per dropback (-0.15) since he entered the league last season.
However, special teams coordinator John "Bones" Fassel's unit generated the first blocked punt return of 2026 in the Titans' 26-20 comeback win over the Indianapolis Colts . Tennessee overcame a 13-point deficit at halftime by outscoring the Colts 26-7 in the second half. Saleh has a lot of work to do, but his squad is entering Week 7 on a high note at least.
Kevin Stefanski deserves a mulligan for having to start Cooper Rush the first two weeks of the season. Once starting quarterback Michael Penix Jr . returned to the lineup in Week 3, the Falcons soared, crushing both the Green Bay Packers and the New Orleans by a combined score of 80-38. Then, the struggles returned with consecutive home losses against the Lamar Jackson-less Baltimore Ravens and the Chicago Bears .
Atlanta is now 2-4 or worse for the first time since 2020, and it is 0-3 at home to start a season for just the third time in the 21st century (2003, 2020). Stefanski needs to be able to help his talented team find a more consistent existence going forward.
The Arizona Cardinals snapped their four-game losing streak in style in Week 6, upsetting the preseason Super Bowl betting favorite Los Angeles Rams on the road 18-16 with six made field goals and no touchdowns. That makes the Cardinals the owners of the largest upset win (13.5-point underdog) by any team this season, per CBS Sports Research. Week 6 also marked Arizona's first win since its season opener, also at SoFi Stadium, against the Los Angeles Chargers.
Quarterback Jacoby Brissett doesn't really scare defenses deep downfield. He is averaging 6.9 air yards per pass attempt, the seventh fewest in the NFL this season. However, LaFleur made things work in Week 6. Now, LaFleur's mission needs to be maximizing the 2026 NFL Draft third-overall pick, running back Jeremiyah Love's rookie year, while hoping for a more dynamic starting quarterback in 2027.
The Las Vegas Raiders even being .500 six weeks through the season while starting a 38-year-old, post-Achilles tear Kirk Cousins is downright impressive. Las Vegas doesn't quite have the horses on the offensive line and the defense needed to truly contend, but it has been a much more fun watch than people would have thought. It is a disturbing trend that the defense, not Kubiak's side of the ball, has allowed 27-plus points for the fourth straight game, after allowing 27 points across Weeks 1 and 2 combined.
Las Vegas has a bright future ahead with Kubiak and Cousins helping develop 2026 first overall pick quarterback Fernando Mendoza .
John Harbaugh was trending to place a lot higher here as of just a couple of weeks ago, with the  Giants entering Week 5 out to a 3-1 start despite season-ending knee injuries to quarterback Jaxson Dart and three-time Pro Bowl edge rusher Brian Burns . However, the last two weeks have dropped him down the list. A tie with the Washington Commanders and the slump-buster that ended the New Orleans Saints' three-game losing streak make for a brutal stretch.
Fortunately for Harbaugh, the rest of the NFC East has no desire to climb up the standings with the entire division going winless two weeks in a row.
The Steelers are starting to find their groove under new head coach Mike McCarthy. Pittsburgh is averaging the fifth-most points per game (28.5) since Week 3, a major improvement after averaging the second-fewest points per game (11.5) in the league through the first two weeks.
Pittsburgh also just completed its largest fourth-quarter comeback (13 points, 16-3) since the 2002 AFC Wild Card Round against the Cleveland Browns in its 26-19 overtime road win at the Tampa Bay Buccaneers. McCarthy's offense has added more life this season to the Steelers' attack, and Pittsburgh is in a 4-2 bottleneck at the top of the AFC North as a result.
Inheriting two-time NFL MVP quarterback Lamar Jackson is a blessing for new Baltimore head coach Jesse Minter, but he hasn't had him the last two weeks because of an ankle injury. In Week 5, Minter's squad went on the road in primetime and beat the Falcons on "Sunday Night Football" with backup quarterback Tyler Huntley . In Week 6, Huntley wasn't enough in a 13-10 loss against the Cleveland Browns.
Minter showed a coaching edge in Week 5 in Atlanta and the Week 3 win in Brazil against the Dallas Cowboys. The Ravens' +24-point differential is the eighth-best in the NFL this season, and they have the same record as the Browns and Steelers atop the AFC North.
New Bills head coach Joe Brady has an unfair advantage among his class of 2026 head-coaching hires because he has been his team's offensive coordinator since 2023. Quarterback Josh Allen leads the NFL in total touchdowns (17), and running back James Cook's 627 yards rushing rank as the third most in the NFL. The Bills were also able to overcome a five-turnover performance against the Los Angeles Chargers to win 24-16 in Week 3.
While Brady spends the bulk of his time on offense as the play caller, he is still responsible for overseeing his defense as his team's head coach. His Bills lead the league in points per drive (3.13) while ranking dead last in points per drive allowed (2.76). Buffalo's 28th-ranked scoring defense (28.5 points per game allowed) is holding Brady back from reaching an A-grade.
Cleveland Browns first-time NFL head coach Todd Monken is currently pulling off a miracle: His Browns are in first place in the AFC North in Week 6 or later for the first time since 2014. That's absolutely incredible. There's certainly a smoke and mirrors element to it as the Browns have the worst point differential (-16) by a team with a winning record this…
