title: NFL trade deadline: Saquon Barkley to Seahawks among 10 moves that need to happen
summary: These needle-moving deals would define the trade deadline
full_text:
The closer the NFL calendar creeps to the Nov. 10 trade deadline, the clearer it becomes which teams are buying and which are selling. Three weeks out, there is already a divide between contenders and pretenders, so playing the role of matchmaker provides a myriad of potential trade pairings.
A sweep across the league shows how Super Bowl contenders with roster holes, like the Seattle Seahawks and their running back position, match perfectly with downtrodden teams that own tradeable veterans, like the Philadelphia Eagles .
Sometimes the obvious trade proposals never come to fruition. But in a lot of cases, if it makes sense on paper, then it makes sense in practice. There are a number of reunions, like Khalil Mack's potential return to the Chicago Bears , that just feel right.
Here are 10 of those trades that feel so fitting that it would be a shame if they did not go through.
The Seattle Seahawks ought to have extreme seller's remorse as they field a bottom-tier rushing attack and watch Kenneth Walker III run wild in Kansas City. Much of their disappointing 3-3 start can be attributed to an offense that ranks second-worst in EPA per rush, which leads one to wonder how much they regret letting Walker go in free agency.
He is very much the missing piece, and they will rely on Zach Charbonnet and Jadarian Price to fill that gap when they return from injured reserve. Neither is an established No. 1 running back, though, so Seattle would benefit from admitting it needs a high-caliber starter, then placing Charbonnet back in his more natural secondary role and allowing Price to develop as a rookie third option.
They would have to pay a hefty price to pry Saquon Barkley away from Philadelphia because of his immense value and his giant cap hit, but with the Eagles poised to watch this season wither away in the wake of countless personnel losses, they should be willing to at least field calls on their superstar running back. Seattle is in as much of a win-now mode as any team in the league and thus is in a position to give up premium draft capital for a player who can help it return to the Super Bowl.
If Jerry Jones cannot turn the Dallas Cowboys into a winning football team, he is at least going to go down swinging. The Joey Porter Jr . trade earlier this season was one big move, but the defense clearly needs more blockbuster additions in order to climb out of the depths. Since Jones addressed the back end of the unit with the Porter deal, it may be time to turn back toward the line of scrimmage and address, again, an edge rusher group that is still lost without Micah Parsons .
While Arizona Cardinals general manager Monti Ossenfort said in August that he has "no interest" in trading Josh Sweat , there might not be a more obvious trade candidate on a team that is not built to contend for anything in 2026. Sweat denied any displeasure with his contract, but there was offseason smoke that he sought a restructured deal or a trade.
He is an expensive veteran for a franchise attempting to build a young core and boasts the kind of perennial sack production and team contract control that a competitive team would pay a premium for. If the Cowboys moved a couple of draft picks to land Sweat, this would be a win-win.
The NFL's stingiest defense is to credit for the Minnesota Vikings ' perfect start. The margins in those five victories were nail-bitingly slim, though, because the offense has only done just enough to capitalize on Brian Flores' coaching masterclass on the other side of the ball.
The passing game is what it is. There is no in-season upgrading over Kyler Murray , and the wide receiver group will always be in good shape so long as Justin Jefferson is there. The main area that needs improvement and, more importantly, can be improved, is the rushing unit. Aaron Jones and Jordan Mason (once healthy) are a serviceable tandem, yet the attack has accounted for only three touchdowns and ranks in the bottom quartile in EPA per rush. An infusion of stardom would take this offense to another level and make the Vikings true Super Bowl contenders.
Enter Jonathan Taylor . Whether the Indianapolis Colts would part with their best player just over two months after they signed him to a two-year contract extension (the third-largest deal for a running back in NFL history) is unknown, but with general manager Chris Ballard fired and coach Shane Steichen potentially on his way out the door , too, this franchise could be headed toward a tear-down. Teams will call about Taylor. Minnesota needs to make sure it is in the conversation.
If there is one trade that is most likely to be completed by the deadline, a Khalil Mack reunion in Chicago has to be at the top of the list. The pairing almost makes too much sense. The Bears need pass-rushing help. Mack remains productive in the latter years of his career, albeit not quite at the All-Pro level of his Chicago heyday. The Los Angeles Chargers are prime candidates to sell expiring contracts, considering their 0-6 record. Everything points to these teams working together to send Mack back to his old home.
The lift Mack would provide for an offense-first team could be a difference maker that sparks a deep postseason run. Now that Caleb Williams is healthy again, the Bears have the potential to score at will. The defense lags behind just enough to warrant a splashy trade deadline move, and this one is just waiting to be completed.
There is a wide receiver injury crisis in Pittsburgh. Aaron Rodgers was on a hot streak until health issues depleted his supporting cast. In order to maximize the supposed last year of his career and stay in contention for the AFC North crown, the Steelers need to plug some immediate help into Rodgers' receiving room.
Michael Pittman Jr. and Roman Wilson are on injured reserve, and Ben Skowronek has a calf issue. It is up to DK Metcalf , rookie Germie Bernard and a couple of practice squad elevations to keep the passing game afloat.
All of that makes the Steelers potentially desperate buyers at the deadline. Chris Godwin Jr. should be on their radar. The Tampa Bay Buccaneers , whom they just defeated in overtime, are drifting further into the abyss and should be ready to sell. His three-year contract makes him an expensive asset who struggles to stay on the field, and that is a profile that the Buccaneers would seemingly want to part with.
He is healthy now, though, and that is what matters to the Steelers. Plus, he should be a tremendous fit next to Metcalf. Godwin spent every year prior to this one on the other side of a towering No. 1 target in Mike Evans , so he would be right at home in the same lineup as a similarly sizable go-to weapon like Metcalf.
The Buffalo Bills are winning games in one way and one way only: Scoring a boatload of points. They have to. The defense is a sieve, specifically in the back end. No matter how much pressure Greg Rousseau and the front provide, opponents are able to pick apart the pass defense to the tune of 285.8 yards per game — the second most in the league. The slot defensive back spot is the biggest weakness, and there is an obvious upgrade potentially sitting on the trade market in Cardinals safety Budda Baker .
Baker is versatile enough to play nickel or fall back deeper into coverage and would immediately be the best player in the Buffalo defensive backfield. He is the Cardinals' highest-paid player and remains under contract through 2027, but he carries a dead cap hit of only $3 million for next year, so moving on from him would not put Arizona in a long-term financial bind. That is an attractive proposition for a rebuilding team.
Jauan Jennings was in a 49ers uniform less than a year ago and would be a perfect fit back in one this season. He led all San Francisco wide receivers in catches and yards in 2024 and 2025 and knows the Kyle Shanahan offense front and back, so with the 49ers fighting through a litany of wideout injuries, why not reunite with someone…
author: Carter Bahns

title: 6 lessons learned in Week 6: Bears' defense gets a weapon back, lackluster Giants have two superstars
summary: Plus, the NFC East makes unwanted history, and it might not get better
full_text:
No one had a worse Week 6 than the Los Angeles Rams . After his team lost to the Cardinals as 13.5-point favorites on Sunday, Sean McVay announced Monday that wide receiver Davante Adams (ruptured hamstring) is out 6-10 weeks, defensive tackle Poona Ford (torn triceps) is out for the rest of the season, and defensive tackle Kobie Turner (groin) is out 4-6 weeks. Oh yeah, and new kicker Blake Grupe tore his ACL.
The "dream team" is quickly falling apart, becoming a nightmare just over a month before it began. Myles Garrett hasn't played since undergoing knee surgery after Week 1. Matthew Stafford looks like a shell of himself. At 2-4, the Rams are just the fifth preseason outright Super Bowl favorite in the last 50 years to be under .500 through six weeks.
It's yet another example of how quickly and how drastically things change in the NFL , and it should serve as a reminder of how quickly and how drastically things still can change. Last year, at this junction, the two best teams in the NFL were the Colts and the Buccaneers , both 5-1. Neither made the playoffs.
So, Week 6, what do we do with you? The best way to sum it up: We know a lot, but there's a long way to go. Here's what we learned.
Here's a list of defensive backs who have had three sacks and two forced fumbles in a single game:
19 seconds of Kyler Gordon taking over https://t.co/1BDag2E6BS pic.twitter.com/fFbXHVOIMA
This was Gordon's first game of the season! He's obviously not going to be a three-sack-per-game player, but he is one of the best blitzing defensive backs in the game, and Dennis Allen knows how to scheme up creative blitzes. From 2022-24, Gordon was one of just two cornerbacks with at least 100 pass rush snaps, and he had a 15.9% pressure rate. He's a physical, versatile playmaker who plays like he was shot out of a cannon.
And then the injuries came. He played in just five games (including playoffs) last year. Frustration mounted. On Sept. 1, GM Ryan Poles said "I don't know" when asked about Gordon's future with the franchise. Ben Johnson didn't have any nicer words, either. Gordon missed the first five games of this year.
But Sunday's game shows just how important Gordon can be. In an NFL where secondary versatility is key, Gordon played 10 snaps on the defensive line and seven snaps at slot corner. He was on a pitch count, and the Falcons were still clearly clueless as to how to deal with him.
Gordon has a history of making an impact. Since the Bears drafted him, they have allowed just 6.9 net yards per attempt with him on the field compared to 7.6 net yards per attempt with him off the field. Welcome back, indeed.
Before the season, I named Evan Williams as a potential breakout guy, and my goodness, is he breaking out. Jonathan Gannon is helping. Look at where he starts on this eventual interception.
EVAN. WILLIAMS. 📺: NBC pic.twitter.com/H2dBumCPkg
This is ridiculous. Evan Williams covers so much ground #Packers https://t.co/zgcIk4bp6q pic.twitter.com/RdxMnPIsWd
Williams played 31 snaps as a box safety, 31 snaps as a free safety, nine snaps as a slot corner and seven snaps as a defensive lineman Sunday. He has always been a dominant run stopper, but now he's getting free rein to use all of his outstanding athleticism. He is the highest-graded safety in the NFL, per Pro Football Focus.
Williams' utilization is just one of many aspects in which Gannon has been terrific. Sumer Sports had a great breakdown of how he has made his defense so much more difficult to decipher.
Jonathan Gannon's defensive usage changes from 2022 w/ PHI to 2026 w/ GB so far, per @SumerSports : *Blitz %: 25.2% -> 32.2% *MOF disguise %: 27.8% -> 40.1% *Stunt %: 13.6% -> 31.4% *Cover 1: 21.1% -> 10.7% *Cover 2: 5.6% -> 22.7%
And that heightened blitz number is giving teams fits: Green Bay's defense has the third-best EPA-based success rate in the NFL when it blitzes. Sunday, Dak Prescott was 12 for 20 for 79 yards -- a season-low 4.0 yards per attempt -- against the blitz.
Remember, Gannon is doing this with no Micah Parsons (yet) and injuries to Edgerrin Cooper and Javon Hargrave , among others. It might not have gone well in Arizona, but Gannon is shining in Green Bay.
The conversation surrounding the NFC East-leading (NFC Least?) Giants is who will start at quarterback after J.J. McCarthy came in for Jameis Winston and played well in a Week 6 loss to the Saints . The NFC East is very much there for New York's taking, even with a backup quarterback. There's another thing we didn't expect to say a month and a half ago.
Even if the season eventually comes crashing down -- the schedule is about to get a lot harder, starting with the Texans on Sunday -- New York can feel very, very good that it's found two young, ascending stars. Malik Nabers is starting to look like his pre-injury self, and Abdul Carter might be a superstar already.
Nabers had 12 catches for 165 yards against the Saints. In the past three weeks, he has had 29 catches for 398 yards and two touchdowns. It's the most receiving yards by any Giants player in a three-game span since Odell Beckham Jr . in 2015. Yes, that's prime OBJ, and Nabers is only a year removed from an ACL tear.
Malik Nabers v. Saints 12 Catches 165 Yards 80% Catch Rate Nabers has 29 catches for 398 yards in his last 3 games. He's 5th in the NFL in catches & 6th in yards returning from his injury. pic.twitter.com/ciHXSab3gv
His 46-yard leaping grab was the top highlight, but the one at the 0:25 mark of that video is my favorite: He spins off one defender, shrugs off a linebacker(!), makes another guy miss and picks up a first down. This is, to me, Nabers' most elite quality: explosiveness anytime, any place. What should be a 4- or 5-yard gain turns into 13. His 52 YAC were a season high.
Carter, meanwhile, only had four pressures, but his impact was much larger than that. All four of his pressures were "quick pressures" (within 2.5 seconds), and he drew two holding penalties. His 19 quick pressures this season are tied for second-most in the NFL. The sack numbers aren't quite there yet, but he is absolutely wreaking havoc and looking like he will do so for years to come.
All four NFC East teams lost this week, one week after the Commanders and Giants played to a comically bad tie, and the Eagles and Cowboys both lost.
That makes the NFC East the first division ever to go winless in back-to-back weeks in which all of its teams played .
It doesn't appear to be getting much better. A quick synopsis:
Current SportsLine projections do not have a single NFC East team reaching eight wins.
Let's take a look at how some Week 6 losers did on special teams.
Yes, there was an 8-yard punt. No, it wasn't his fault.
The @Panthers block the punt! CARvsPHI on CBS/Paramount+ Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/RzY4XuJCcE
Special teams are more important than ever. The kickoffs are crucial, and because teams often get shorter fields with the new kickoff rules, having a kicker who can connect from long distances is also crucial. For some teams, all you need is one first down to be in range.
Entering "Monday Night Football," teams in the top half in special teams EPA this season were 54-39-1 (.580 win pct). Teams in the bottom half were 37-52-1 (.417 win pct).
There are eight AFC teams multiple games above .500 this season.
There are four NFC teams multiple games above .500 this season.
We already talked about the NFC East, but we're seeing a massive imbalance between the divisions, too. The NFC South is battling the NFC East to see who's worse. In the NFC West, the defending champion Seahawks are 3-3 and can't stop turning the ball over, and the preseason Super Bowl-favorite Rams are 2-4 with huge injury issues.
Yes, the AFC has its share of duds. The Dolphins , Chargers and Titans are arguably the three worst teams in the NFL. But when you look at the potential playoff landscape of both divisions, you see far more drama in the AFC.
Both conferences have one powerhouse division where…
author: Zachary Pereles

title: Prisco's NFL Week 7 Power Rankings: Rams are a mess, Texans climb eight spots
summary: Pete Prisco shares his Week 7 Power Rankings for the 2026 NFL season, including some big risers and fallers
full_text:
The lock to win the Super Bowl before the season is in last place. Think about that.
The Dream Team has turned into a nightmare. The Los Angeles Rams went into the season as the heavy favorite to win the Super Bowl for a lot of reasons. They were loaded with talent. They had the reigning MVP in quarterback Matt Stafford leading a high-octane offense.
They added elite edge rusher Myles Garrett and two top corners, Trent McDuffie and Jaylen Watson , in the offseason to fix a defense that was a problem in 2025. They have a great coach in Sean McVay.
Despite all of that, the Rams sit at 2-4 and are off a horrible home loss to the Arizona Cardinals as double-digit favorites. They are tumbling down my Power Rankings and will now be without receiver Davante Adams for 6-10 weeks due to a hamstring injury .
After losing a shootout to the Buffalo Bills last Monday night at home, the Rams had their supposed get-right game against the Cardinals Sunday, but it was far from it. The Rams lost 18-16 on a last-second field goal to continue their disappointing start to the season.
The Rams are 17th in scoring offense and 21st in scoring defense, as average as you can get. That has them last in the NFC West.
Los Angeles can still regroup in the next few weeks thanks to a soft schedule. But it better. The schedule really toughens up late.
Then again, the Cardinals were considered part of the soft schedule too.
The Rams, who are down to No. 18 in my rankings this week, aren't a fast team on offense, and it shows. On defense, with Garrett missing all but the opener with a knee injury, they are tied for 26th in the league in sacks with eight.
The next four weeks will decide the fate of the Rams. They play at the Raiders , home against the Chargers , at Washington and at Arizona. They need to go at least 3-1 in the stretch. Anything else would be a problem.
The stretch does look like something they can navigate. Then again, how many survivor pools were lost on Los Angeles losing at home to the Cardinals, who came in with one victory?
Dream team?  Uh, not quite.
author: Pete Prisco

title: NFL Draft's first-round gamble: What Jets, Browns can learn from Super Bowl winners and failed rebuilds
summary: Multiple first-round picks helped the Chiefs, Eagles and Seahawks win Super Bowls, but the Jets and Browns know the other side of the story
full_text:
Three of the NFL's most recent Super Bowl champions have something in common. The Chiefs used two first-round picks in 2022 on Trent McDuffie and George Karlaftis , then won back-to-back championships. The Eagles took Jalen Carter and Nolan Smith in 2023 and won the Super Bowl two seasons later. And the Seahawks also drafted Devon Witherspoon and Jaxon Smith-Njigba in 2023, with both developing into stars before Seattle won it all in February.
But there's another side to this story, and the New York Jets know it all too well. They had three first-round selections in 2022, landed some pretty good players, and somehow never made the playoffs. Four seasons later, only one of those players remains on the roster.
The Cleveland Browns have been down this road, too. They made five first-round picks across the 2017 and 2018 drafts, eventually won a playoff game, but couldn't sustain that success. And with the Jets holding three first-round picks in 2027 and the Browns holding two, both franchises are about to get another chance.
So what separates the teams that turn extra first-round picks into championships from those that find themselves starting over? Having Patrick Mahomes certainly helps, but not every Super Bowl winner needs a first-ballot Hall of Famer under center. Put differently: How much comes down to making the right picks, and how much depends on everything else?
To answer that, we went back through every NFL Draft since 2000 and found 103 instances in which a team had multiple first-round picks. In all, those teams selected 216 players, including 25 quarterbacks. And as we've seen play out in real time, there's a big difference between finding good players and building a winning football team.
It's easy to forget how promising the Jets' 2022 draft looked . They took Sauce Gardner fourth overall, Garrett Wilson at No. 10 and then traded back into Round 1 for Jermaine Johnson at No. 26. Gardner and Wilson were named Defensive and Offensive Rookie of the Year, while Johnson became a Pro Bowler in his second season.
Three first-round selections, two Rookie of the Year winners and a Pro Bowl pass rusher. You can't really draw it up any better than that.
The individual success, however, didn't translate to wins. The Jets went 7-10 in 2022 and 2023, then 5-12 and 3-14 the following two seasons. They cycled through quarterbacks, fired head coach Robert Saleh during the 2024 season and eventually moved on from general manager Joe Douglas, too. Then came the roster reset. Gardner was traded to Indianapolis in November 2025 for two first-round picks and receiver Adonai Mitchell . Johnson, who suffered a torn Achilles in 2024, was dealt to Tennessee for defensive tackle T'Vondre Sweat in March 2026. Only Wilson remains.
From a scouting standpoint, it's hard to call the 2022 draft a failure. But from a team-building standpoint? Four losing seasons, no playoffs, a fired coach and GM, and two of those three first-rounders playing elsewhere tell a different story.
The Jets, you might remember, weren't the only New York team with multiple first-rounders that year.
The Giants selected Kayvon Thibodeaux fifth overall and Evan Neal two picks later, hoping they had found an edge rusher and a franchise offensive tackle. Outside of quarterback, those are the two most valuable positions on the field, and to solve them early in the first round certainly made sense.
New York made the playoffs in 2022 and even won a playoff game. But after that 9-7-1 season, the Giants won just six, three and four games over the following three years. Thibodeaux, while he hasn't lived up to lofty expectations, has shown he can get after the quarterback, including an 11.5-sack season in 2023. Neal, meanwhile, struggled with injuries and inconsistent play at right tackle, prompting the Giants to move him to guard in 2025. He didn't play a snap that season because of a hamstring injury, was released before the 2026 season and is now on the Raiders ' practice squad.
The Jets' problem wasn't necessarily identifying talented players. The Giants' problem was that one of their two premium selections failed to deliver. Different circumstances, same disappointing result.
And recent history offers plenty of contrasting examples.
Wins by season after draft
Trent McDuffie, George Karlaftis
Aidan Hutchinson , Jameson Williams
Sauce Gardner, Garrett Wilson, Jermaine Johnson
Kayvon Thibodeaux, Evan Neal
Kyle Hamilton , Tyler Linderbaum
C.J. Stroud , Will Anderson Jr .
Jahmyr Gibbs , Jack Campbell
Devon Witherspoon, Jaxon Smith-Njigba
Caleb Williams , Rome Odunze
J.J. McCarthy , Dallas Turner
Marvin Harrison Jr. , Darius Robinson
Detroit and Houston were in very different situations when they entered their respective drafts, but both offer examples of how quickly things can change when a franchise gets it right.
The Lions were coming off a 3-13-1 season when they selected Aidan Hutchinson second overall in 2022, then traded up to No. 12 for Jameson Williams. Detroit improved to 9-8 that fall, and a year later, the Lions were back in the first round with two more selections, taking running back Jahmyr Gibbs at No. 12 and linebacker Jack Campbell at No. 18.
Four first-rounders in two drafts, and the results soon followed. Detroit went 12-5 in 2023 and reached the NFC Championship Game, then won 15 games the following season. Hutchinson became one of the NFL's best pass rushers, Gibbs emerged as one of the NFL's best backs, and Williams and Campbell developed into important contributors.
What made Detroit's turnaround different was that it didn't need to find a quarterback. Jared Goff arrived in the 2021 Matthew Stafford trade, seemingly a throw-in alongside the two first-rounders the Lions received from the Rams . But GM Brad Holmes knew Goff from their time together in LA, and while the Rams were ready to move on, Holmes believed he could still be a franchise quarterback. So instead of drafting his replacement, the Lions built around him.
Houston, meanwhile, needed a quarterback. Coming off a 3-13-1 season, the Texans selected CJ Stroud second overall in 2023, then traded up one spot later for Will Anderson Jr., and it wasn't cheap. Houston sent Arizona picks 12 and 33 that year, plus first- and third-rounders in 2024. But Anderson has been so good that no one even thinks to bring up what the Texans gave up to get him.
The payoff was immediate: Houston went 10-7 in each of the next two seasons, then 12-5 in 2025, making the playoffs all three years. Stroud and Anderson became foundational pieces, even if Stroud couldn't quite match his brilliant rookie season in '24 and '25. And hiring DeMeco Ryans before that draft was just as important. The Texans found their quarterback, improved their pass rush and put a coaching staff in place that could develop the rest of the roster.
There's another advantage to having multiple first-round selections: Sometimes a team doesn't need to rebuild at all.
The Chiefs were coming off a 12-5 season when they traded Tyreek Hill to Miami in March 2022 for a package that included a first-round pick. They used some of that capital to move up for McDuffie at No. 21, then selected Karlaftis at No. 30. Kansas City also signed JuJu Smith-Schuster and Marquez Valdes-Scantling , who combined for 1,620 receiving yards that season, while Travis Kelce added another 1,338 yards and 12 touchdowns.
(By the way, Hill picked up where he left off; in Miami, he caught 119 passes for 1,710 yards and seven touchdowns. The Dolphins finished 9-8 and reached the playoffs but lost to Buffalo in the Wild Card round with Skylar Thompson starting in place of an injured Tua Tagovailoa . Meanwhile, the Chiefs still won the Super Bowl without one of the NFL's most dynamic players.)
Kansas City led the NFL in scoring in 2022, Mahomes won MVP, and the Chiefs repeated as Super Bowl champions the following season. McDuffie and Karlaftis became important pieces of the defense, but the bigger story was how…
author: Ryan Wilson

title: Revisiting the 2026 NFL Draft: Evaluating how well Seahawks have done re-tooling Super Bowl roster
summary: Injuries to top picks like Jadarian Price and Bud Clark have derailed early returns of Seattle's draft class
full_text:
The Seattle Seahawks were tasked with replacing pieces of its Super Bowl roster through the 2026 NFL Draft. Thus far, the class has been defined by injuries and the practice squad.
General manager John Schneider made eight selections over the course of three days. Who did the Seahawks draft, and how have they fared? CBS Sports revisits the 2026 NFL Draft .
Price had been associated with Seattle for weeks leading up to draft night. Seattle had lost Kenneth Walker III in free agency, and Zach Charbonnet was still recovering from an injury. The Seahawks seemed content picking Jeremiyah Love's teammate with the last pick on Thursday night.
Price has 28 carries for 119 yards, as well as four receptions for 21 yards this season. Most of his success has come on plays stretched to the boundary rather than between the tackles. Interior blocking has been a bit of a problem, and the stats bear that out. He is averaging 1.16 yards before contact, according to TruMedia. He has been adequate as a pass catcher and inconsistent in pass protection. Coaches are not going to be happy with his two fumbles, but run game issues extend beyond him.
Price had been battling a chest injury before re-aggravating it in practice earlier this month. He was placed on injured reserve and will miss at least one more game.
Seattle's draft strategy appeared to focus on replacing pieces lost from its Super Bowl roster. In addition to losing Walker, cornerback Riq Woolen signed with Philadelphia in free agency, so the team drafted Neal. He has played two defensive snaps all season, and both were late-game rushes by Bam Knight. Neal was recently placed on the injured reserve with a hamstring injury that will sideline him for at least two more games.
Clark was competing for a starter's role in the secondary, but his season was over before it began. The rookie out of TCU suffered a broken ankle during the preseason and was placed on season-ending injured reserve.
Aside from Price, Stephens is the only other draft selection to play this season. He has played what essentially amounts to three games' worth of snaps at right guard.
Iowa has a long history of offensive line success in the NFL , so it was a worthwhile gamble for the franchise on Day 3. Stephens does a good job angling blocks to seal run lanes and plays with a sturdy foundation. Sustaining blocks has been a bit of an issue as his hands and feet are not always married. Stephens is always looking for work, however, and will drive his feet on contact in the run game.
Dansby, Eastern, Henderson and Fuller are all on the team's practice squad. Undrafted free agent cornerback Avery Smith has occupied a role exclusively on special teams.
author: Josh Edwards

title: NFL Week 7 picks and score predictions: Bears top Patriots in Thursday thriller, Chiefs edge Seahawks
summary: Here's your weekly dose of John Breech's NFL picks
full_text:
For anyone who has ever wondered what I do in the 24 hours before I turn my picks in, I've decided to give you a peek behind the curtain.
Last night, I spent nine hours trying to figure out who's actually good this year and I came to the conclusion that the 49ers and Chiefs might be the only good teams in the NFL. Everyone else is average. And to be honest, I almost scratched the 49ers off my list because they almost blew a 20-point lead to the Commanders on Monday night.
I was going to include the Vikings on my "good" list, but I don't trust their offense. I also thought about the Bills, but I don't trust their defense.
Outside of Buffalo, Minnesota, San Francisco and Kansas City, every other team in the NFL has at least two losses. As we all know, the NFL's ultimate goal is total parity and I think the league might have finally achieved it. Every week is unpredictable.
After spending nine hours making my list of good teams, I ate some Waffle Crisp. That took 45 minutes. I then spent four hours watching the Bears' new Hallmark movie, which is about 90 minutes long, so yes, that means I watched it 2.5 times.
Turn those TVs on because Holiday Touchdown: A Bears Love Story is premiering RIGHT NOW on Hallmark Channel 🌟 pic.twitter.com/R8q4XtoxQ9
Since Hallmark started featuring NFL teams in their movies back in 2024, the team featured has averaged 13.5 wins per season in the year they get the Hallmark movie, so maybe I should also add the Bears to my good list. So there are now five good teams and everyone else is average.
Speaking of average, let's get to my picks.
All lines via DraftKings ; All times ET
I don't usually pick the winner of a game based solely on the injury report, but I might have to do that here. I am fully expecting the Patriots injury report this week to look like a CVS receipt. If you've never seen a CVS receipt, they're roughly seven yards long and that's if you buy just one thing. If you buy more than one thing, your receipt will likely be as long as an entire football field. I'm pretty sure the only reason we're destroying the Amazon rainforest is so we can create more receipt paper for CVS.
Anyway, I was watching New England play the Jets on Sunday, and during the game, the Patriots lost 60% of their starting offensive line with LG Alijah Vera-Tucker (hamstring), RG Ben Brown and RT Morgan Moses (ankle) all going down. As if that's not bad enough, Romeo Doubs also left the game with an injury. There have been so many injuries that I'm just going to bookmark the tweet below to keep track of who might not be playing this week.
The Patriots could be going into Thursday night against the Bears without their: FB WR2 WR3 LG RG RT RG2 RG3 CB2
The problem for the Patriots is that this is a Thursday game, so there won't be very much time for anyone to heal.
The other problem for New England is that the Bears' pass-rush has been surprisingly good this year, so this is not the game where you want 60% of your offensive line to either be hobbling around or not playing. The Bears have 17 sacks through six games, which is tied for the fifth most in the NFL, and now, they get to go up against a banged-up Patriots line.
Drake Maye has looked spectacular over the past three weeks, but he's been playing with a lead. During this current three-game winning streak, the Patriots have only trailed for about 10 total game minutes out of 180 and Maye does well when he's playing with a lead. What's going to happen if the Patriots have to play from behind? Well, just go watch film of the Patriots' 35-6 loss to Jacksonville in Week 3 and you'll get a rough idea.
I think the Bears will blitz Maye into oblivion and force him to make mistakes that we saw him make earlier in the season. He threw six interceptions through the first three weeks, but has only thrown one over the past three weeks. I think early-season Maye returns in this game.
Not only do we have a beat-up Patriots team hitting the road on a short week, but they have to face an NFC North team.
I'm not sure what the biggest mismatch is right now in the NFL, but I'm going to go ahead and say that it's the NFC North versus any team from the AFC East. Through six weeks, the NFC North has played five games against the AFC East and they've gone 4-1. Watching an AFC East team try to beat an NFC North team is like watching four baby fawns try to fend off a hungry bear.
I think what I'm trying to say here is that there's no way I'm picking against the Bears.
PICK: Bears (-3) 27-20 over Patriots
The Bengals might have just become the first NFL team ever to somehow lose on their bye week. They went into their off week tied for second place in the AFC North, and somehow, after not playing a game, they have dropped to last place. I blame the Browns. Things seem to get weird whenever the Browns are in first place and that's a world we live in right now.
This game is between two teams that I'm still trying to figure out. Are the Bengals good? Are they kind of good? Are the Ravens for real? Can either team beat anyone with a winning record?
The answers to these questions seem to be: Maybe, probably, still thinking about it and we'll find out this weekend.
These two teams both have a winning record, but they haven't really had to beat anyone to get there. The Bengals' three wins have come against three teams that have a combined record of 3-14 (.176). The Ravens' four wins have come against teams that have a combined record of 7-17 (.292). Every other AFC team with a winning record has beaten teams that have a combined winning percentage of at least .300, but not the Ravens and not the Bengals.
That being said, the Bengals are about two plays away from being 5-0, so they might be good. As for the Ravens, they had a chance to take control of the AFC North in Week 6, but they blew a 10-0 lead to the Browns. There is no team better at blowing fourth-quarter leads than the Ravens, which is definitely not something you want to be the best at in the NFL.
The Ravens have blown FIFTEEN fourth-quarter leads of at least 7 points since 2020. No other NFL team has even blown 10. At some point, you have to stop calling it bad luck. This is who they are.
The upside for the Ravens is that they might be getting Lamar Jackson (ankle) back this week, but it's impossible to say for sure, because no one seems to know when he's going to return.
Basically, Lamar might play, but he might not.
Jackson has historically played well against the Bengals, but if he also tends to play differently when he's coming off an injury. Just look at last year: After missing three games with a hamstring injury, he was never really the same after that. That doesn't mean he's going to struggle if he plays on Sunday, but it does mean that it's hard to predict how he might look.
Whether Jackson is on the field or not, this will be a huge test for the Bengals' revamped defense and I'm guessing the Ravens will be serving up a heavy load of Derrick Henry, especially if Jackson is on the field and can't quite run full speed.
If you watched the Bengals' defense play last year, then you know they couldn't stop anyone, especially Henry. Imagine someone taking a snowplow through the Smurf Village and you'll have an idea of what it looked like last year when Henry was running against Cincinnati's defense. The Bengals are definitely better this year, but I won't know how much better until I see them play against the Ravens, and that's because the Ravens have the one offense in the NFL that the Bengals can't figure out. In the last six meetings between these two teams, the Ravens have gone 5-1 while averaging 29.2 points per game.
In the battle of the two quarterbacks who have dealt with a lot of injuries over the past few years, I'm going to take the one who's actually healthy.
PICK: Bengals (+3) 27-24 over Ravens
The last time these two teams faced each other was on Thanksgiving 2025, which is almost fitting, because the Packers definitely have something to be…
author: John Breech

title: Jalen Hurts blood clots: Biggest unanswered questions for Eagles about star QB's health
summary: The Eagles and Hurts' agent revealed more information about the quarterback's blood clot situation on Monday, but there are still lingering questions
full_text:
How did Philadelphia Eagles Super Bowl MVP quarterback Jalen Hurts end up being expected to miss the rest of the 2026 season with blood clots in his lungs? We're going to lay out what happened, what Eagles coach Nick Sirianni disclosed publicly, and the three biggest unanswered questions remaining about Hurts' health scare and ordeal.
Hurts took a cleat to the calf in Week 4 against the Los Angeles Rams, but he didn't request treatment until a few days later. The Eagles then played the Jacksonville Jaguars in Week 5 in London. Following the team's international flight, an ultrasound revealed a superficial blood clot in his calf, but doctors still cleared him to play.  Hurts was up into early Sunday morning before playing the Jags because he was at a London hospital being evaluated. His agent Nicole Lynn told The Ringer on Monday that Hurts was able to get some sleep at a room in the stadium before kickoff.
Hurts then flew back from London to Philadelphia with the team and returned to practice last week. The follow-up ultrasound indicated that the blood clot had moved, which is why he was ruled out for Week 6 at home against the Carolina Panthers. Additional testing changed his diagnosis to having deep vein thrombosis and blood clots in both lungs. That's why Hurts is now on blood thinners and expected to miss the rest of the season.
Eagles head coach Nick Sirianni's press conference kicked off on Monday , with him fielding a number of questions about the confusion surrounding Hurts' situation. Sirianni was asked how the quarterback was allowed to play and fly back home from London with the team while he was diagnosed with blood clots. Here is what the coach had to say.
Why did Hurts play despite the blood clot and getting little sleep after travel and spending most of the night in a London hospital?
"The health of our players is always at the forefront of our minds, and we leave that up to the medical experts, but we always, always care deeply about our players. When you are completely focused on together and connection, you're always thinking about the well-being of your guys, and that's where we were in that situation."
What do he or the Eagles feel should have been done differently?
"I'm not a medical expert. I lean on our guys in all those situations. I'm a football coach. I lean on our medical experts in every situation. I have full trust and full faith in them. It's not just me that has major care for our players. It's them as well, so we're all there. I'm glad to be part of an organization that cares about our guys the way our guys do."
Why was Jalen Hurts allowed to fly home knowing he had a blood clot?
"Again, I'm not a medical expert. Same deal there. We get medical information from our guys, and we always put the players' health first and foremost in every situation, and that's where we were there."
Was Sirianni briefed by the medical team before Monday's press conference on why he was allowed to fly with the blood clot?
"Yeah, guys, I talk to them a lot. Again, the medical export experts are there and I think I've answered this question multiple times. We put out a statement for you guys to hear, put out multiple statements for you guys to hear. And so and I told you guys that last week that I was going to leave it at that of where where we were on that because we put out a detailed statement for you guys to hear and to understand."
Who was part of that conversation?
"I fully trust the people that are involved in helping us all make these decisions and you know we have great people here.  The same doctors and trainers that helped 21 of our 22 starters be available in the Super Bowl [Super Bowl LIX that concluded the 2024 season] are the same guys today that deeply care about our guys to help them. ... You know, again, don't have much more to say about that. That's why we put the statement out and also full trust in those guys and always, always, always, the players' health is at the forefront of our mind and that again goes down to our connection and our team. It kind of feels like you're questioning that. I know you guys have a job to do, but I've got the relationship with the players that I have because of the time that we spend together and because of the care that we have for each other. So it's always at the forefront of our mind. Again I get all the questions. I know you guys have questions about this. But we care deeply about our guys."
Will the Eagles' front office or medical staff address reporters?
It remains unclear if Eagles executive vice president/general manager Howie Roseman or Eagles owner Jeffrey Lurie will address the public to provide more details on Hurts' situation. Or if the team will have anyone from the medical staff talk through the decision-making process on Hurts' health. Sirianni was the only high-ranking person from the franchise to field questions on Monday.
Here is the only answer Sirianni provided to answer the question of why Hurts was allowed to fly back home while knowing he had blood clots.
"Again, I'm not a medical expert. Same deal there. We get medical information from our guys, and we always put the players' health first and foremost in every situation, and that's where we were there," Sirianni said.
Air travel increases the chances of clotting. While Sirianni could not provide a direct answer, the Eagles medical staff presumably felt it was safe to have Hurts on a plane after he played against the Jaguars.
The answer to this question appears to be yes. The statement put out by Lynn, Hurts' agent, and the Eagles ended this way:
"Jalen's prognosis is very good, and we expect a full recovery. We anticipate that he will have the opportunity to resume contact football activities when off the blood thinners. In the meantime, he will remain active around the team and continue to condition. More importantly, we anticipate that he will have no long-term effects.
"We are thinking of Jalen and looking forward to a strong recovery."
There is a precedent for such a return to play after experiencing blood clots. San Antonio Spurs All-NBA center Victor Wembanyama was diagnosed with deep vein thrombosis (DVT) with a blood clot in his right shoulder in February 2025 after the NBA All-Star game. He was then shut down for the last 30 games of the 2024-2025 NBA season after the clot formed in his right shoulder.
Like Hurts, Wembanyama went on blood thinners and was able to fully return in the 2025-2026 seasonm where he won NBA Defensive Player of the Year honors while finishing third in league MVP voting. He led the Spurs to a Western Conference title before San Antonio lost the NBA Finals to the New York Knicks in five games.
author: Garrett Podell

title: Is a Colts fire sale coming? What that could look like and what big names could be traded away
summary: The Colts don't have a 2027 first-round pick. But what could they get for top veterans in preparation for a 2027 rebuild?
full_text:
The Chris Ballard era as the Indianapolis Colts general manager came to an end on Monday . A 26-20 home loss against the previously 0-5 Tennessee Titans in Week 6 was enough for Colts owner Carlie Irsay-Gordon to pull the plug on Ballard six games into his 10th season on the job.
Under Ballard, Indianapolis reached the playoffs twice (2018 and 2020), going 1-2 in those two trips. The Colts' 72-82-1 regular-season record under his management ranked 17th in the league during Ballard's tenure. Indianapolis' five missed playoffs in a row (since 2021) is the Colts' longest such streak since 1988 to 1994, and the team never won an AFC South title under Ballard.
Now, the franchise is left to pick up the pieces with a 2027 rebuild on the horizon. The good news is that the 2027 NFL Draft is widely regarded as one of the most talented in years. The bad news is that the Colts don't have a first-round pick thanks to trading their 2026 and 2027 first-round draft choices, as well as wide receiver Adonai Mitchell , to the New York Jets in exchange for All-Pro cornerback Sauce Gardner last season.
However, there are multiple ways for Indianapolis to recoup draft capital through veterans on tradable deals. Let's take a look at what a potential fire sale of three of the Colts' top players could look like.
Three-time Pro Bowl defensive tackle DeForest Buckner all but demanded a trade after the team's Week 6 loss against the Tennessee Titans.
"I'm sick and tired of the same song and dance every year," Buckner told reporters postgame on Sunday .
At 32 years old, Buckner still has plenty of gas in the tank. His 4.0 sacks through six weeks are tied for the 10th most in the NFL , while his 19 quarterback pressures rank as the seventh most among defensive tackles in 2026. The Colts would be unwise not to make him available, as he is set to become a free agent in the 2027 offseason. What could his market look like?
For a player at his age and contract status, this could be one of his last prime seasons, but for legitimate contenders, that could be worth a third-or fourth-round pick. Teams who could be interested could include the Green Bay Packers (4-2), the San Francisco 49ers (5-0) and the Minnesota Vikings (5-0).
The Packers lost defensive tackle Javon Hargrave for the season with a torn Achilles, so it would make sense for them to place a call for Buckner. The 49ers make too much sense. That's where Buckner played his first four seasons, culminating in the 49ers losing Super Bowl LIV to the Kansas City Chiefs to conclude the 2019 season. He was traded to the Colts for a first-round pick in the 2020 offseason. San Francisco is going through its regularly scheduled injury catastrophe, which has hit their defensive line hard. If the Vikings want a mentor for rookie first-round pick Caleb Banks and another high-level contributor for defensive coordinator Brian Flores to get creative with, they would make sense as a win-now team.
Colts left guard Quenton Nelson , an eight-time Pro Bowler and a three-time first-team All-Pro, is primed to be one of the NFL's most coveted free agents next offseason ahead of his 31st birthday on March 19. This season, Nelson is currently Pro Football Focus' highest-graded guard in the entire NFL with an 89.2 offensive grade.
He is a big fish who could net the Colts a second-round pick or perhaps a first-round choice if the bidding for his services gets frisky at the trade deadline. The complication is that he would be a rental or someone who would demand a top-of-the-market extension for whoever trades for his services.
Who could line up for him? The Packers, a team that has been playing mix-and-match with an injury-plagued front, have stabilized their offensive line with the same starting five combination. But they could be in the mix, since they're currently rolling with aging veterans they signed off the street to start for them.
If the Houston Texans (2-4), winners of two in a row, continue to climb, perhaps they would be interested. However, their asking price could be higher since they're a fellow AFC South team. The Vikings could be interested if they want to upgrade for undrafted free agent Joe Huber at left guard, with Donovan Jackson out with a torn meniscus. The 49ers, who are currently starting 2025 seventh-round pick Connor Colby at left guard, could make an all-in trade for Nelson.
The Colts don't need to trade three-time Pro Bowl running back Jonathan Taylor . He is still just 27 years old, and he re-signed with Indianapolis on a two-year extension worth $44 million with $39 million in total guarantees in August. However, if the Colts want to jumpstart their rebuild in earnest, parting with Taylor now could perhaps net them a first-round pick. They could point toward the impact top-end running backs Kenneth Walker III , Bijan Robinson , Jahmyr Gibbs and others are having all around the league as reason to demand a 2027 or a 2028 first-round pick in return.
Indianapolis could perhaps engage two AFC North teams, the Cincinnati Bengals (3-2) and the Pittsburgh Steelers (4-2), in a bidding war. The Bengals are averaging the fifth-fewest rushing yards per game (82.8) in the entire league this season, while Aaron Rodgers could use more support for the Steelers' 13th-worst running game (99.2 rushing yards per game) in what appears to be his NFL swan song.
The Packers trading a 2028 first and another pick or two for Taylor could give them the runway to release Josh Jacobs after some legal trouble landed him on the commissioner's exempt list for the first six weeks of the 2026 season. They rank dead last in the league in rushing (59.8 rushing yards per game), and Taylor is a former Wisconsin Badger. Trading for him would earn them public relations bonus points by dumping Jacobs and bringing a local product home.

title: Billboards are going up asking Cardinals management to sell the team
summary: The Arizona Cardinals are a member of the National Football League (NFL). There are 32 member clubs. The Cardinals are the oldest continuous NFL team, beginning in 1898. In the 128-year history of the franchise, the team has won a grand total of two titles, in 1925 and 1947. Next season will be the 80th […]
full_text: The Arizona Cardinals are a member of the National Football League (NFL). There are 32 member clubs. The Cardinals are the oldest continuous NFL team, beginning in 1898. In the 128-year history of the franchise, the team has won a grand total of two titles, in 1925 and 1947. Next season will be the 80 th anniversary of the 1947 championship season. The 1925 title wasn’t actually won by the Cardinals, but the league took the title away from the Pottsville Maroons and then gave it to the second-place club, which was the Chicago Cardinals. RELATED: THE STORY OF HOW THE BIDWILL FAMILY BECAME OWNERS Last year, the Cardinals under head coach Jonathan Gannon lost the most games in a single season with 14. The final two seasons netted 26 losses, and Gannon was sent packing. In the franchise’s history, the team has played in three league championship games, winning one. They have competed in 18 playoff games. The NFL did not begin a postseason system until 1933, which means Arizona will average playing in a playoff game every 5.1 seasons. After moving to Phoenix from St. Louis in 1988, the club has found limited success, winning three division titles, playing in 12 playoff games, and losing to the Pittsburgh Steelers in Super Bowl XLIII after the 2008 season. Since the 2016 season, the Cardinals have played in just a single playoff encounter, a 34-11 loss to the Los Angeles Rams after going 11-6-0 in 2021. Since 2016 (with divisional finish): 2016: 7-8-1 (2 nd ) 2017: 8-8-0 (3 rd ) 2018: 3-13-0 (4 th ) 2019: 5-10-1 (4 th ) 2020: 8-8-0 (3 rd ) 2021: 11-6-0 (2 nd ) 2022: 4-13-0 (4 th ) 2023: 4-13-0 (4 th ) 2024: 8-9-0 (3 rd ) 2025: 3-14-0 (4 th ) Longtime fans still remember the 1974 and 1975 seasons under head coach Don Coryell, in which the franchise won back-to-back division crowns, but lost in their first playoff games. In 1976, the team went a respectable 10-4-0 but didn’t make the playoffs, and then in Coryell’s final season, finished 7-7-0. Or the magical Super Bowl year with QB Kurt Warner, when the team held the late lead only to have it snatched away. The following year, both under head coach Ken Whisenhunt, the franchise won their division but fell hard in the playoffs 45-14. The NFC Championship Game loss to the Carolina Panthers in 2015. Fans have vivid memories of these exceptional Cardinals teams. But here’s the rub: all of that was so long ago. What about now? Here it is 2026, and the roster is still devoid of an accomplished quarterback, with defensive struggles, and high-round draft picks that have fizzled out and traded away for almost nothing. What about now? Most points to the ownership group, which consists of five Bidwill family members. Michael Bidwill, is listed on the team’s website as the owner. Michael represents the fourth generation of the Bidwill family as sole owners of the club. It began in 1932 when Charlie “Blue Shirt” Bidwill bought the Cardinals while on a yacht he owned, and had guests on board for a classy dinner. One of the guests was Dr. David Jones, who owned the Cardinals and was complaining about the team and the everyday toil. Charlie, on the suggestion of his wife Violet, agreed to purchase the Cardinals. When Charlie passed away in the spring of 1947, his wife inherited the team and became the first woman to own a professional football team. Since then, the team has been owned by Charles Bidwill, Jr. and his brother Bill, then Bill Bidwill as the primary owner, then Bill and Michael Bidwill, and now Michael as principal owner. Bill Bidwill had five children: Michael, Bill, Jr., Tim, Patrick, and Nicole. While Michael is listed as the principal owner, he shares the ownership group lineage with his siblings, representing the third generation of the Bidwill family running the franchise. No other Bidwill family member is on staff with the Cardinals. Not happy There is a contingent of the Cardinals fanbase that is just sick of losing seasons. They believe that the team doesn’t spend on high-priced free agents during the free agency period, which could come in and make a difference right away. Every year, the franchise gets a bump in its evaluation on the Forbes list. In 2024, the team was valued at $4.8 billion; the following year, that jumped to $5.5 billion. What happened to make such a jump? A Super Bowl appearance? Best quarterback in the league? The club signed the league’s best head coach? Nope. Nothing. The franchise vaulted in value just for existing. And in 2025, the Cardinals made $571 million. So, the owners of the team got $700 million extra in value, plus took home $571 million in profit. All in one swoosh. The Cardinals fanbase is asking why the front office isn’t using some of that cash on big-name players. Go after them, and pay them handsomely. Show them the advantages of not playing in a cold city, and every game is inside a climate-controlled dome. Keep in mind, the Cardinals are just one of many ventures that Michael has found success in. His portfolio, identified as “Bidwill Family Holdings,” extends to luxury real estate developments, premium hospitality ventures, and hospitality-focused private equity funds. Petitions have circulated asking any disgruntled Cardinals fan to sign. These petitions aren’t for better restroom facilities at the stadium, or to lower their ticket prices, or asking about why the beer costs so much on game day. Nope. These petitions are asking for the Bidwill family to sell the team. Get totally out of the football business. And now, another group began a GoFundMe and spent the money on billboards, asking the same questions and pleading for a new ownership group. On social media, the hashtag #BIDWILLOUT has grown with a simple statement: Sell the team. A total of $7,000 was raised in just two days for a series of digital billboards. The message: MICHAEL, PLEASE SELL THE TEAM. Signed, the Fans. One billboard is in Surprise, another in Mesa, while the other is near Tempe Marketplace. Another is planned for downtown Phoenix. The reality The NFL is comprised of 32 member franchises. Each is wholly owned by people and corporations. Two things: The NFL is not going to ever oust an ownership group as long as it hasn’t done anything illegal, and #2: there isn’t a number two. The Bidwill family can keep their franchise for as long as they want. They are already in their fourth generation of owners. And their team increases in value every single year, regardless of, well, anything. Just for existing. Just look at the franchise’s value for the last five years: 2022: $3.2 billion 2023: $3.8 billion 2024: $4.3 billion 2025: $5.5 billion 2026: $8.6 billion Just look at the franchise’s earnings for the last five years: 2021: $467 million 2022: $467 million 2023: $546 million 2024: $560 million 2025: $571 million Keep in mind, a great percentage of these earnings come from the collective of the NFL. For every Cardinals jacket you buy, it is split 32 ways. So, when someone purchases a New York Football Giants cap, Arizona gets 1/32 of the profit. The same goes for the current TV packages. Each team makes over $400 million annually, regardless of whether anyone shows up for home games or not. Then there are other national sponsors such as Oakley, Ford Motor Company, Verizon, Ticketmaster, Pepsi, Toyota, Bank of America, Coca-Cola, Bud Light, and AT&T. With each of these corporate sponsors, the Cardinals are paid an equal share of the profits. Do not for one second think that a fan boycott will solve this. The team will still rake in millions. Look at the pandemic year. Fans weren’t allowed to attend NFL games. How many NFL teams folded? I have never been more proud of the Arizona Cardinals fans! Cardinals Fans United is the most powerful force in the NFL! Do not stop keep it up! Love you guys! #MontiOut #BidwillOut #RallisOut #selltheteam — Justin Sane (@JustinS54965881) October 16, 2026 This year, Arizona is averaging 62, 079 per home game. Last year, it was 63,524. Pretty much, fans are…

title: Former Cardinals employees enter into lawsuit
summary: Two former Arizona Cardinals employees have filed a lawsuit against the team plus owner Michael Bidwill. The lawsuit is fairly broad, but alleges discrimination involving race relations and not being paid properly. RELATED: GRADING THE MARV HARRISON TRADE The lawsuit was filed by Don Shumpert, who was an offensive assistant coach with Arizona from 2020 […]
full_text: (Photo by Kevin Abele/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Two former Arizona Cardinals employees have filed a lawsuit against the team plus owner Michael Bidwill. The lawsuit is fairly broad, but alleges discrimination involving race relations and not being paid properly. RELATED: GRADING THE MARV HARRISON TRADE The lawsuit was filed by Don Shumpert, who was an offensive assistant coach with Arizona from 2020 to 2021, and Kendra Hogue, who was the former assistant to the Cardinals’ COO, Jeremy Walls. Walls has been the team’s COO since 2023 and remains in this position. Hogue’s allegations are numerous and wide-ranging. The bulk of it involves racial discrimination. In the suit, she states that, as a black woman, she was subject to disparate treatment and that the workplace environment was intolerable. She also alleges constructive termination, defamation, harassment, retaliation, and intentional infliction of emotional distress. This forced her to resign from her position. Shumpert’s allegations are less vague and pretty much to the point. He states in the suit that he joined the team as a coaching fellow in 2019, then joined the staff. Several years later, he was finally promoted to running backs coach, but also had the responsibilities of his former position. This meant he was working two positions and being paid for one. When Shumpert, who is black, met with the front office to discuss a pay raise, he met with GM Steve Keim and Cardinals head coach Kliff Kingsbury. According to the suit, he was told they weren’t in a position to discuss the matter. He points out in the suit that several white coaches on the current staff had been given new titles that came with pay increases. Shumpert specifically mentions two white coaches who were given title increases, yet without actually having their responsibilities change. Shumpert did mention a few other isolated instances, including ones with Bidwill. A week after he met with Keim and Kingsbury, he was fired. He has alleged that the Cardinals made false statements about the circumstances of his departure. The Cardinals responded to the lawsuit, stating that none of the allegations are factual. In the meantime, the lawsuit went before a federal judge. He then ruled that a discrimination lawsuit must be settled via a third party rather than in open court. This meant the decision would be made by a magistrate instead of being handled in a courtroom, thus limiting the financial damages if the team is found liable. This in itself is considered a victory for the franchise to keep the case out of the courtroom. But it had a solid foundation. Both former employees had signed agreements when they were hired stating: “that any dispute, controversy, or claim related to their employment be resolved through binding arbitration rather than a lawsuit.” NFL teams are not billion-dollar entities without knowing how to defend themselves before any lawsuit ever comes into play.

title: Falcons poach Commanders OLB Charles Snowden, cut Bralen Trice
summary: The roster shuffling is in full swing now. After the Falcons surprised everyone by signing veteran quarterback Andy Dalton, they’re shaking up their EDGE group with the addition of Charles Snowden. The team has signed him off the Washington Commanders practice squad and cut Bralen Trice, per The Athletic’s Josh Kendall. This isn’t an earth-shattering […]
full_text: MIAMI GARDENS, FLORIDA - NOVEMBER 17: Charles Snowden #49 of the Las Vegas Raiders walks between plays during the first half against the Miami Dolphins at Hard Rock Stadium on November 17, 2024 in Miami Gardens, Florida. (Photo by Brandon Sloter/Getty Images) | Getty Images The roster shuffling is in full swing now. After the Falcons surprised everyone by signing veteran quarterback Andy Dalton, they’re shaking up their EDGE group with the addition of Charles Snowden. The team has signed him off the Washington Commanders practice squad and cut Bralen Trice, per The Athletic’s Josh Kendall. The Falcons are signing DE Charles Snowden off the Commanders' practice squad and releasing Bralen Trice to make room on the 53-man roster, according to a team source. — Josh Kendall (@JoshTheAthletic) October 20, 2026 This isn’t an earth-shattering move, but the 28-year-old Snowden seems like a quality addition. Listed at 6’6” and 250 pounds, Snowden struggled to make an impact early in his career after arriving in the NFL as an undrafted free agent, but found a home with the Raiders in 2024 and 2025, appearing in 31 games with 18 starts and picking up 4.5 sacks combined over those two years. While those aren’t exactly eye-popping numbers, Snowden was a reliable tackler who was useful in coverage in a pinch and delivered solid pressure along with solid run defense; Trice had had his moments as a pass rusher in 2026 but was struggling against the run and with his tackling. The Falcons likely view this as a direct upgrade on Trice for the moment, while Trice seems fairly likely to land back on Atlanta’s practice squad. Given how thin the Falcons EDGE group has looked, it’s always a good idea to add more capable players to the mix. James Pearce Jr. is a couple of weeks away from returning and the Falcons have had to lean heavily on Cameron Thomas and Samson Ebukam thanks to injuries to Za’Darius Smith and Yasir Abdullah and a reluctance to commit to major snaps for Jared Ivey and Trice. Snowden should be able to give this team quality snaps on all three downs once he gets up to speed. Give Snowden a warm welcome, and we’ll see if he figures into the team’s plans for Sunday against the 49ers.

title: Atlanta’s best things to do, see, and eat before heading to a Falcons game
summary: So you’re from out of town and have decided to fly into the great city of Atlanta for a Falcons game. Or maybe you live outside the city proper and are looking to drive (or MARTA) down to Mercedes-Benz Stadium for a game. Or maybe you’re a resident within the city limits and are hopping […]
full_text: Photo by Ric Tapia/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images So you’re from out of town and have decided to fly into the great city of Atlanta for a Falcons game. Or maybe you live outside the city proper and are looking to drive (or MARTA) down to Mercedes-Benz Stadium for a game. Or maybe you’re a resident within the city limits and are hopping over to catch the Birds in action. No matter what your scenario, a proper game-day guide is suitable for anybody looking to really experience all of the great things this city has to offer. Although the Falcons have not been putting up too many victories over the past decade, the city of Atlanta is undefeated when it comes to experience. Let’s go through a bit of a step-by-step guide for any and all folks looking to get the most out of their experience centered around a Falcons weekend. Places to stay and things to do in Atlanta There is an abundance of selection in where to stay over the course of a weekend in and around the city. If you are not incredibly price conscious and are going all out, Midtown is a good option which is incredibly vibrant and surrounded by things to do and see, including the Atlanta Botanical Garden, Piedmont Park and the High Museum of Art. Midtown is within the confines of where the MARTA (Metro Atlanta Rapid Transit Authority) goes, and you can easily get to downtown for the game and other outings utilizing the train. MARTA offers free non-overnight parking and the cost of a round trip ticket is $5. A one day pass is $9. If you’re set on staying in downtown, then there are a variety of neighborhoods which will ensure a great experience, and those are headlined by the historic Old Fourth Ward, especially near the Beltline (a 22-mile trail of pure walkability encircling Atlanta) and Ponce City Market. Inman Park is another area which sits right on the Beltline that’s surrounded with great restaurants, coffee shops and historic buildings. It’s not too far from the aforementioned house of Dr. King, either. As you would expect, the transportation when it comes to the game itself is most robust when you’re in downtown already, with MARTA serving as the backbone, but also with Bird Scooters located all over the city and the option to rent a bike if cycling is more your thing. Best places to eat in Atlanta If you don’t know already, Atlanta’s staple food is wings. I’ll argue with anybody who says this isn’t the wing capital of the world. As such, if you don’t have the dietary restrictions which for whatever reason would coordinate your body against them, I highly recommend trying one of the many top tier wing spots in the city. Also, it’s Atlanta, go get the lemon pepper wet. I don’t know if I should or shouldn’t include them in the recommendation, but Magic City unironically has gained significant notoriety in recent years for their kitchen and specifically for their wings. What you choose to do with that information is up to you. Other high tier wing places include JR Crickets, The Local (which is also located at Ponce City market) and Fox Bros BBQ (price for a 10-piece ranges from $13-$18 with Fox Bros charging around $24 for a 12-piece as they don’t have an option for 10). It’s a ways away from downtown, but if you for whatever reason venture outside the Perimeter, then I’ve found in my experience that the city of Buford has one of the best food scenes I’ve ever experienced. Almost any type of food you can imagine can be found within a drive down Buford with the ethnically diverse Gwinnett County coming to life in the cuisine. If you’re looking for something more high end, some of the top tier steakhouses in Atlanta include Kevin Rathbun’s steakhouse located in Inman Park, Bones restaurant located on Piedmont Avenue, and if you want to venture out a little further than downtown, Arnette’s Chop Shop in Brookhaven. (All of these will carry with them on average much steeper prices, and it’s not too hard to spend over $100 per head). Mercedes-Benz Stadium parking, rideshare, and transit options As previously mentioned, MARTA is the easiest way to get to the stadium. It will cost you $5 round trip, and when you compare that with parking costs around the stadium (between $20 and $50, generally) it’s a steal. If you are driving, purchase your spot ahead of time. Stubhub has a ton of options for each home game. Rideshares like Uber and Lyft are also a possibility — but if you opt for this method, you might want to plan to walk to one of the restaurants near the stadium and have a snack and a drink to let traffic die down a bit postgame. The Mercedes-Benz game-day experience After you’ve spent what is hopefully a wonderful weekend in Atlanta, the main event will come at what is in my opinion the best stadium in the world, located at 1 AMB Dr NW, Atlanta, GA 30313. The Mercedes-Benz Stadium is a ground worthy of exploration even without an event happening there. The magnum opus of the Benz is its incredibly affordable food prices, which have been a staple of and a PR driver for the stadium since its inception. Arthur Blank has been very stout on the food affordability aspect of his new stadium and the prices really can’t be beat by any other professional sporting venue in the United States. A hot dog and a soda cost $2.00 each, fries are $3.00, a burger runs a $5 bill. There’s much more selection of course, but know that this is one of those rare sporting venues where you will likely save money waiting until you go into it as opposed to eating somewhere outside of it before the game. This is $20 worth of food at MBS! pic.twitter.com/cgVFEIgpO4 — Mercedes-Benz Stadium (@MBStadium) August 18, 2023 The 63,000 foot Halo Board — the largest in the world of its kind — circling around the stadium enhances the viewing experience of the game. The massive glass wall located on the 300 level concourse skybridge overlooks the beauty of downtown Atlanta. The wifi connection at the stadium is state of the art and better than most wifi you will come across anywhere else and there are a multitude of charging stations. It’s been designed powerful enough to support all 70,000+ people that the Benz seats. The stadium also features the wall of football helmets featuring each high school in the state of Georgia, a place in the 300s dedicated to the franchise’s ring of honor inductees as well as the Molly B’s concession stand with speciality food options prepared for each event at the stadium. Outside, you will find the giant Falcon statue, which is the largest bird sculpture in the world. Hopefully your trip features a big Falcons win, and plans to once again visit Atlanta as this is a place where just one weekend isn’t enough.
