title: Four Takeaways from Falcons Field-Level Experience
summary: The Atlanta Falcons social media team gave me and multiple personalities on Falcons Twitter a once-in-a-lifetime opportunity to experience a Falcons game from one of their field-level suites this past Sunday. While the result wasn’t what any of us wanted, seeing the game from field level is an experience you can’t quantify easily in words. […]
full_text: ATLANTA, GEORGIA - OCTOBER 18: Kyle Pitts Sr. #8 of the Atlanta Falcons catches a touchdown pass against the Chicago Bears during the fourth quarter of the game at Mercedes-Benz Stadium on October 18, 2026 in Atlanta, Georgia. (Photo by Kevin C. Cox/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Atlanta Falcons social media team gave me and multiple personalities on Falcons Twitter a once-in-a-lifetime opportunity to experience a Falcons game from one of their field-level suites this past Sunday. While the result wasn’t what any of us wanted, seeing the game from field level is an experience you can’t quantify easily in words. I met a ton of amazing people for the first time and put faces to some of the profiles you routinely see in what I consider one of the better NFL fanbases on the platform. However, during the Falcons’ 31-23 loss to the Chicago Bears, I had four clear takeaways, and I think I felt them more than I would from my usual seat (probably in the 300s). Special Teams Woes Rookies make rookie mistakes Not beating the Bears today giving them a free TD on a Zachariah Branch miffed punt. That’s how you deflate a defense pic.twitter.com/VIWgqfJ4uC — Clint Goss (@NFLDraftDome) October 18, 2026 When Olamide Zaccheus came out for the first few returns, I was confused about why we weren’t using third-round rookie Zachariah Branch more in the return game. He was a dynamic returner, an All-SEC selection, and came into the league with track speed. However, after he fumbled twice, both times right in front of the field-level suites, it was clear Branch wasn’t ready to be the primary returner. In fact, the entire special teams unit, outside of the specialists, was atrocious. According to Pro-Football-Reference , the Falcons lost almost 3.5 expected points to special teams alone, that’s with the 6.36 expected points that the punting game (5.41) and kicking units (0.95) gave. When Branch fielded that punt inside the 10-yard line, you could feel the uneasiness as it descended from the sky. He clearly didn’t feel comfortable fielding that punt, and if you fumble once, it’s easy for it to stay in the back of your mind for the rest of the game, and it could have factored into his second fumble. Zachariah Branch visibly, and understandably, frustrated following his second fumble of the game. Bijan Robinson talking to the #Falcons rookie on the sideline, and appears to be praying with him. pic.twitter.com/QM8FYWCMPd — Miles Garrett (@MilesGarrettTV) October 18, 2026 The Bears started four of their fourteen drives in Falcons territory; the Falcons did not start a single drive in Chicago territory, adding to their league-worst average drive start. The Falcons have been unable to get anything done or spark special teams. As Michael Penix Jr. continues to develop into a potential franchise quarterback, any advantage would help this offense, and Branch likely needs to round into form for that to happen. The Bears Offense is Really Good The Falcons defense had plenty of injuries in the secondary and at linebacker, but they showed no mercy and jumped on them from the start. Caleb Williams is so special, and his ability to get more out of a play than what was drawn up makes him dangerous, especially when he gets out of the pocket. Williams’ ability to get out of the pocket, despite how the defense plays it, is exceptional, and even though the rushing attack wasn’t explosive, it was effective enough that the Falcons defense had to respect it. Caleb Williams was a perfect 24/24 for 248 yards from a clean pocket in the Bears' Week 6 win over the Falcons. His 24 attempts are the most without an incompletion from a clean pocket in a game since at least 2018. Powered by @awscloud pic.twitter.com/Vrx6fZNBRu — Next Gen Stats (@NextGenStats) October 18, 2026 Also, watching Williams throw the ball from so many different arm angles and platforms was a highlight of the field-level experience. It absolutely pops out of his hand. Caleb Williams returned and picked up right where he left off against Atlanta. 30/36, 305 PASS YDS, 1 TD, 0 INT vs Falcons The Bears are putting themselves in a strong position to make the playoffs. pic.twitter.com/cfWgMJhCjM https://t.co/DOysGBliAY — Football Performances (@NFLPerformances) October 18, 2026 The Sheer Size and Speed of These Human Beings Cannot Be Exaggerated On one of Olamide Zaccheus’s kick returns, I watched the lane open up for him after he fielded the ball. As he approached, it was still there, and I thought, “Oh, this is six,” but it closed so fast it was like a fly trying its luck against a Venus Flytrap. Outside of that, as the Falcons lined up from their six-yard line in the third quarter, the size of Kyle Pitts and how he is just as big as the offensive linemen, with just a slightly leaner frame, puts into perspective how truly massive a human being he is and how hard it must be to bring him down on a down-to-down basis. Kyle Pitts what a play! CHIvsATL on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/1K7vEntXHI — NFL (@NFL) October 18, 2026 If you ever get a shot at being near the field and experience how fast and hard these hits are, it is definitely worth it. The Falcons Have a Huge Problem With Attendance…And It’s Not on The Fans One of the Fox camera operators spoke with one of the creators in the suite, Kam, and he gave us one of the most damning indictments an organization can face. Talked to a couple of Fox media members after the falcons/bears game. “Never have any of us ever seen a home game have such a low atmosphere from the home fans, and a much stronger support from the away fans. Do you know why it was like this? It’s all we were confused about… — 🤟🏽Kam (@Kam7810) October 18, 2026 As fans, it was a bit embarrassing to get to third down and watch the offense struggle with its cadence and operation on what’s supposed to be its home turf. However, the problem doesn’t lie only with the product on the field, where the Falcons haven’t hosted a playoff game at Mercedes-Benz Stadium since it opened in 2017. It also lies in the price of getting into the stadium. Every offseason, we’re given the spiel that the in-game experience is affordable; however, it doesn’t account for the cost to get into the building. For the Falcons-49ers game, as of 11:59 on Monday, October 19th, the cheapest ticket is $166.60 in the 300-level. Now, there is a silver lining: if you plan, you can get to the Saints game on January 3rd, 2027 for $68.45, but with today’s economy, people may need time to solidify their plans. If you’re working a regular 9-to-5, it doesn’t make financial sense to decide in the week leading up to the game to go on Sunday. It feels like the common person is being pushed out of the Benz, leaving room for opposing fans, especially those with a presence in Georgia like the Bears, to take advantage and literally take over the venue. The Falcons don’t have a pricing problem instead of a fan problem. While the experience inside is unrivaled, getting fans in seems to be the issue. The press run this franchise does every preseason talking about the concession prices is a PR masterclass. Blank gets his praise and everyone ignores how unaffordable the get in price is for a team that hasn’t sniffed the post season in a decade. https://t.co/q316xX3bBc — Adnan Ikic (@SayWhichWay) October 19, 2026 Overall, it was an incredible experience, and I can’t thank the Falcons’ social media and marketing team enough for letting me be part of it. The wings were phenomenal, and there were plenty of sweets for someone with a sweet tooth like me to enjoy. Also, the sliders? Tremendous. Again, the result isn’t what we hoped for, but this team’s late fightback was awesome to watch and experience, and sharing it with some amazing individuals in the Falcons content creation space made it even better. A huge shout-out to those who traveled to enjoy the experience, including the representatives from the Atlanta Falcons UK and Atlanta Falcons Germany. Everyone I…

title: NFC South Week 6 Review: There’s finally a team over .500
summary: As it often does, the division split wins and losses this week, with the Saints and Panthers coming out on top. The Buccaneers failed to build on last week’s win, and the Falcons are in the midst of their 2nd losing streak of the season. Here’s the Week 6 NFC South Review:  Tampa Bay Buccaneers […]
full_text: TAMPA, FLORIDA - OCTOBER 18: Jalen Ramsey #5 of the Pittsburgh Steelers sacks Jalon Daniels #10 of the Tampa Bay Buccaneers during the first half of the game at Raymond James Stadium on October 18, 2026 in Tampa, Florida. (Photo by Mike Carlson/Getty Images) | Getty Images As it often does, the division split wins and losses this week, with the Saints and Panthers coming out on top. The Buccaneers failed to build on last week’s win, and the Falcons are in the midst of their 2nd losing streak of the season. Here’s the Week 6 NFC South Review: Tampa Bay Buccaneers (1-5) Week 6 Result: Buccaneers 19 – Steelers 26 Week 7 Opponent: Carolina Panthers Jalon Daniels is fun to watch, mainly because he’s not playing for my team. The UDFA is doing his best, but the limitations are clear, and as Falcons fans can attest, Zac Robinson won’t do much to alleviate them. The Buccaneers had a 13-point lead going into the 4th quarter and squandered it, giving up 16 points and pushing the contest to overtime. Being careless with the football and asking a UDFA to throw the ball 43 times proved to be their undoing. There’s a chance Baker Mayfield could return soon , but it’s unlikely he’ll mask this team’s issues. Next week they take on the division leaders in Charlotte. JALEN RAMSEY CALLS GAME! STEELERS WIN 🗣️ pic.twitter.com/MYHqLZM0jO — NFL (@NFL) October 18, 2026 Carolina Panthers (3-2) Week 6 Result: Panthers 25 – Eagles 14 Week 7 Opponent: Tampa Bay Buccaneers After a bye week they desperately needed, the Panthers took care of business against a decimated Eagles . Carolina’s offense looks like a well-oiled machine right now. They sit atop the division as the only team in the South above .500. Some might call them “schedule merchants,” but you don’t get to pick the opponents you play, and as every NFL fan has learned, there’s no such thing as easy games in this league. Carolina can build an even more commanding division lead this weekend when they face the Buccaneers. TT stands for two touchdowns 😼 #CARvsPHI 📺: CBS pic.twitter.com/CPF5vmFPGl — Carolina Panthers (@Panthers) October 18, 2026 New Orleans Saints (2-4) Week 6 Result: Saints 34 – Giants 27 Week 7 Opponent: Pittsburgh Steelers The Saints got a much-needed road win in New York. The offense came alive in the 2nd and 3rd quarters and did just enough to put the game out of reach. JJ McCarthy gave them a scare late in the game, but Kellen Moore’s team was able to survive. Tyler Shough’s all-around play wasn’t that impressive, but he delivered when he absolutely had to. This defense is still one of the worst in the league, but the offense can keep them afloat against most sub-par opponents. They’ll return to the dome and host the Steelers, who are coming off an overtime win against the Buccaneers. Atlanta Falcons (2-4) Week 6 Result: Falcons 23 – Bears 21 Week 7 Opponent: San Francisco 49ers The Falcons have lost two games in a row for the second time this season. The offense came out flat, scoring only one touchdown in the first three quarters, and the defense is playing guys at the bottom of the roster across multiple positions. The late effort was good to see, but it was too little too late. This offense struggles under pressure, and it struggles as a unit. The play calling in these scenarios often relies on long developing routes and lacks quick hitters. Penix is struggling to diagnose pressure and is holding the ball too long, and the offensive line is struggling to win one-on-ones and sort out the blitz. Bijan Robinson also had his worst game as a pass blocker. Things won’t get easier soon, as the team hosts the 49ers and a pair of familiar coaches. Caleb Williams' first drive back ends in a TD to Colston Loveland 🐻 CHIvsATL on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/krhXYNpu6F — NFL (@NFL) October 18, 2026 The Panthers are the only winning team in the division, and if others can’t find their footing soon, it looks like the cats will run away with it. There’s still more than half a season to play, but this could be the least dramatic finish we’ve seen in the NFC South in a long time.

title: Ravens vs. Bengals odds: Opening lines for Week 7 matchup
summary: Entering Week 7, there is one question on the mind of every Ravens fan: will Lamar Jackson play against the Bengals? The two-time MVP quarterback has not practiced in two weeks and missed Baltimore’s last two games. Backup Tyler Huntley managed to steal an overtime win in Atlanta in his first start, but he could […]
full_text: MIAMI GARDENS, FLORIDA - OCTOBER 11: Joe Burrow #9 of the Cincinnati Bengals reacts against the Miami Dolphins during the third quarter at Hard Rock Stadium on October 11, 2026 in Miami Gardens, Florida. (Photo by Carmen Mandato/Getty Images) | Getty Images Entering Week 7, there is one question on the mind of every Ravens fan: will Lamar Jackson play against the Bengals? The two-time MVP quarterback has not practiced in two weeks and missed Baltimore’s last two games. Backup Tyler Huntley managed to steal an overtime win in Atlanta in his first start, but he could not move the ball against the Browns last Sunday. A 1-1 record in two games without one of the most impactful players in the entire sport is not a bad outcome, especially if the rest allows Jackson to be closer to full-strength for the Ravens’ tough stretch of upcoming opponents. Next up are the Bengals, who enter the week as 2.5-point underdogs for their trip to Baltimore ( via FanDuel Sportsbook ). Cincinnati has their usual explosive, pass-heavy with a middling defense outside of one of the league’s best pass rushes. These matchups often turn into shootouts, which will not be sustainable with Huntley under center. Jackson opens up the playbook and helps the run game by forcing defenses to respect his arm and contain his legs. Jackson’s status on the Ravens’ first injury report of Week 7 could swing this line later on Wednesday afternoon. Injury updates on other key players, including trade acquisition Cam Jurgens, may not move the market, but they will still be plenty relevant on Sunday. In his Ravens debut, Jurgens will face the Bengals’ strong defensive tackle duo of Dexter Lawrence and Jonathan Allen, provided he can clear concussion protocol in time to play. If Jackson misses another game, Ravens head coach Jesse Minter will have his toughest test yet slowing down Joe Burrow, Ja’Marr Chase, and Tee Higgins, who have tortured Baltimore in the past and will be looking for revenge for last year’s shutout. In the last two games, his “best at our best when the best is needed” mantra has really showed up. In Atlanta, the Ravens decisively won the game’s last four drives to come back from an eight-point deficit for the third time that night and win in overtime. In Cleveland, the offense opened the fourth quarter with a missed field goal and a fumble and squandered subsequent redemption opportunities with three-and-outs. The defense dominated for most of the game, but could not keep the Browns out of the end zone after of the fumble and gave up a 33-yard completion on third-and-five to set up the game-winning field goal. Unfortunately, it is not hard to envision the Ravens stuffing the Bengals on early downs only to allow chain-moving, back-breaking completions to Chase and Higgins on third down. Cincinnati’s season average of 25.6 points feels like a tough target for Huntley unless Baltimore’s new-look O-line gels right away. If Jackson plays, well, he’s Lamar Jackson. With Ja’Kobi Lane, a proper center, and the team’s best guard back at his natural position, he could be primed for a comeback performance. Ravens Flock, game day is better on the SB Nation app! title: Winners and losers from Ravens’ Week 6 loss to the Browns
summary: The Baltimore Ravens lost the AFC North lead with a 13-10 loss to the Cleveland Browns in Week 6. As usual, there is plenty of blame to go around, though several positives still stood out in the losing effort. Winners Nnamdi Madubuike: After a year of uncertainty about whether Madubuike would play football again due […]
full_text: CLEVELAND, OHIO - OCTOBER 18: Trey Hendrickson #91 of the Baltimore Ravens sacks Deshaun Watson #4 of the Cleveland Browns during the first quarter of the game at Huntington Bank Field on October 18, 2026 in Cleveland, Ohio. (Photo by Jason Miller/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Baltimore Ravens lost the AFC North lead with a 13-10 loss to the Cleveland Browns in Week 6. As usual, there is plenty of blame to go around, though several positives still stood out in the losing effort. Winners Nnamdi Madubuike: After a year of uncertainty about whether Madubuike would play football again due to his neck injury, the former All-Pro defensive tackle is back and performing like he never left. Madubuike was officially credited with just half a sack on Deshaun Watson, but he was wreaking havoc in the backfield throughout the game. The 28-year-old finished with five pressures and a pass rush win rate of 15.2% on 22 pass-rushing snaps. Trey Hendrickson: Hendrickson was a consistent force of pressure in his first game back from hand surgery with a pass rush win rate of 13.3%. He recorded one sack officially, but finished with a team-high six pressures on 20 pass snaps. Kyle Hamilton: Hamilton makes his presence felt every week, and he did so on Sunday with a number of hard hits, including one that blew up a screen. The All-Pro safety finished with seven total tackles, three being tackles for loss, while allowing just seven yards on four targets. Calais Campbell: Campbell had the first of the team’s five sacks on Watson when he brought him down on third down on Cleveland’s first drive, resulting in a three-and-out. Campbell finished with five pressures on 16 pass snaps, according to PFF. Trenton Simpson: Simpson continues to stack strong games in a contract year. He finished with eight total tackles on Sunday while earning a team-high 90.2 PFF grade. Keyon Martin: Martin replaced rookie Chandler Rivers in the slot this week and made the most of his opportunities. The second-year undrafted cornerback single-handedly ended a Browns’ drive with a pass breakup on second down and a sack on the ensuing third down. He finished with a 71.2 PFF grade, good for fourth on the defense. Martin was flagged for a questionable pass interference that extended Cleveland’s drive on third down, leading to a game-tying touchdown, but that does not wipe away his strong day. Ja’Kobi Lane: The preseason darling made his long-awaited return to the field after a broken wrist suffered in Week 1 landed him on injured reserve. Lane did not disappoint in his first game back, catching four passes for 40 yards, with all four receptions being first downs. Lane also had a nice block to spring a 17-yard run on the opening drive. His 79.7 PFF grade was the highest among offensive players. Josh Cuevas: Cuevas was another rookie with a strong showing in Week 6. The fifth-round tight end had his best game of the season so far, catching four passes for 44 yards and the first touchdown of his career on the opening drive. With Mark Andrews in a slump and Durham Smythe out for the season with an Achilles tear, Declan Doyle may need to rely on his pair of rookie tight ends more as the season progresses. Ryan Eckley: The highlight of the day for the rookie punter was a punt that was downed at the one-yard line. Eckley averaged 49.4 yards on seven punts, with three landing inside the 20 and a long of 64. Keondre Jackson: Jackson seems to show up on special teams every week, and he did so again with an impressive play to keep a punt out of the end zone, downing it at the one-yard line instead. Marlon Humphrey: Humphrey had a strong game on Sunday, allowing just one catch for 17 yards and a passer rating of 53.5 on three targets, according to PFF. Nate Wiggins: Wiggins had a solid game as well on the other side of the defense, allowing two catches for 24 yards and a passer rating of 68.8 on four targets. Rookie Denzel Boston entered the game averaging a league-high 20.6 yards per reception, but the combination of Humphrey and Wiggins held the promising receiver to just one catch for 15 yards on five targets. Losers Derrick Henry: It was an uncharacteristically rough day for the future Hall-of-Fame back on Sunday. Henry’s fumble in the fourth quarter gave the Browns the ball at the 35-yard line, leading to their lone touchdown of the day to tie the game. Aside from the backbreaking turnover, Henry struggled to get anything going after a strong first quarter. He finished the game with just 58 yards on 17 carries for 3.4 yards per carry. While much of the run game’s failures could be attributed to other factors, it was still a game that Henry would like to forget. Offensive line: The offensive line struggled to give Henry much running room on Sunday as he was consistently hit behind or near the line of scrimmage. Henry averaged less than one yard before contact while being tackled for a loss on four of his 17 carries. Rookie Vega Ioane also had a poor snap that resulted in a fumble, effectively killing the drive despite being recovered by the offense. Tyler Huntley was sacked three times while being pressured 17 times per PFF, with one of the sacks and 12 pressures being credited to the line. Tyler Huntley: Huntley was the hero of the week after a magnicifent final two drives to win the game against the Falcons in Week 5, but that momentum sadly did not last long for the backup quarterback. Huntley struggled to move the ball through the air against Cleveland’s defense while putting the ball in harm’s way multiple times despite not ending up with an interception. Huntley’s limitations as a passer were on full display Sunday as he failed to push the ball down the field, ending the game with 5.3 yards per attempt. Mark Andrews: Andrews needed a bounce-back performance after a poor display in primetime against Atlanta, but it looks like he will be waiting at least another week to do so. The veteran tight end caught just one pass for four yards while also dropping a ball on three targets. Andrews also had a false start penalty that helped stall a drive. Tyler Loop: Loop failed to extend the lead to 10 in the fourth quarter with a 49-yard missed field goal in a game that was later lost by three points. Loop’s leash appears to be rather short, as kicker Jake Moody has re-signed to Baltimore’s practice squad since Sunday’s game. Rasheen Ali: After a fumble recovery and touchdown drive to tie the game seemed to finally swing momemtum Cleveland’s way in the fourth quarter, Ali made matters worse by muffing the ensuing kickoff, setting the Ravens up at the 16-yard line. Mike Green: Green failed to build off his previous pair of strong performances once Hendrickson rejoined the lineup. Green had just one pressure on 13 pass snaps, according to PFF. Both Green and Hendrickson appear to be most effective rushing on the right side of the defense, which is a puzzle Jesse Minter and Anthony Weaver will have to figure out in order to get the most from the pass rush.
author: Dustin Cox

title: Ravens re-sign K Jake Moody after another Tyler Loop miss in Cleveland
summary: Update, 4:00 p.m. ET: The Ravens also waived linebacker Carl Jones Jr. from the 53-man roster. He will likely re-sign to the practice squad on Wednesday with two elevations remaining for the rest of the season. The Baltimore Ravens re-signed Jake Moody to the practice squad on Tuesday, according to the NFL’s daily transaction notice, […]
full_text: LANDOVER, MARYLAND - DECEMBER 20: Jake Moody #16 of the Washington Commanders attempts a field goal against the Philadelphia Eagles in the first quarter at Northwest Stadium on December 20, 2025 in Landover, Maryland. (Photo by Greg Fiume/Getty Images) | Getty Images Update, 4:00 p.m. ET: The Ravens also waived linebacker Carl Jones Jr. from the 53-man roster. He will likely re-sign to the practice squad on Wednesday with two elevations remaining for the rest of the season. The Baltimore Ravens re-signed Jake Moody to the practice squad on Tuesday, according to the NFL’s daily transaction notice, once again adding competition for kicker Tyler Loop after two misses inside 50 yards in the last three weeks. Moody, 26, first signed in Baltimore on September 1 following Loop’s uneven preseason. But the second-year kicker went seven-for-seven on his kicks in Week 1, including a career-long 57-yard field goal, reviving team confidence and leading to Moody’s release a few days later. Loop continued to perform to start his sophomore campaign. A 49-yard attempt was blocked in Week 2, but he hit all six of his kicks in Rio, including a 56-yard game-winner, the first of his career, to cap off the Ravens’ seven-second miracle. The 25-year-old then crushed a 64-yard field goal in Week 4 that overshadowed a bad miss from 40 yards that seeemed to be an operational issue. Loop knew the assignment in Atlanta in Week 5 with Lamar Jackson sidelined. He nailed two field goals from 50-plus, bringing him to five-for-five on such kicks for the year. But in Cleveland on Sunday, he pulled a fourth-quarter 49-yard attempt wide left, and the Ravens lost by three points. Loop’s 76.9% field goal conversion rate is now well behind his 88.2% mark as a rookie. His success from long-distance has been remarkable after last season’s one-of-four showing, but three misses inside of 40 yards is unacceptable. The 2025 sixth-round pick obviously has the leg for the NFL, but his inconsistency is maddening. Moody has dealt with his share of struggles since entering the league in 2023 as a 49ers third-round pick. He was relatively reliable as a rookie, but his play fell off a cliff in 2024, though a whopping 20 of his 34 attempts came from 40 yards or longer. Last year, he made 19 of his 23 attempts while playing for three different teams. Notably, he went 10-for-11 in Washington to close out the year but could not beat out a rookie for the Commanders’ kicking job in training camp. It would likely take a calamitous Week 7 showing from Loop to motivate the Ravens to make a change, but if misses keep stacking over the next few weeks, Jesse Minter may have no choice but to give Moody a shot.
author: Nikhil Mehta

title: Baltimore’s best things to do, see, and eat before heading to a Ravens game
summary: Welcome to Baltimore! Whether you’re a Ravens fan coming home or a visiting fan following your team on the road, Maryland’s biggest city has plenty to offer for all ages and interests with an underrated food scene and plenty of local charm. The centerpiece of your visit will be, of course, M&T Bank Stadium, the […]
full_text: Photo by: Robert Knopes/Education Images/Universal Images Group via Getty Images Welcome to Baltimore! Whether you’re a Ravens fan coming home or a visiting fan following your team on the road, Maryland’s biggest city has plenty to offer for all ages and interests with an underrated food scene and plenty of local charm. The centerpiece of your visit will be, of course, M&T Bank Stadium, the newly renovated home of the Ravens. It is located in Camden Yards right next to Oriole Park, giving it a unique feel of being a pure sports neighborhood. The area is accessible via walking, driving, or taking public transit with no shortage of food and entertainment options in and around the stadium. Beyond M&T Bank Stadium, Baltimore has plenty of history and science to explore. The cuisine, specializing in seafood (read: crab cakes), can please any palette, and the locals are proud of their city and their football team. We hope you enjoy exploring Baltimore, and be sure to ask any questions you have in the comments! Places to stay in Baltimore Federal Hill If you’re going to M&T Bank Stadium, grabbing a rental in the Federal Hill neighborhood might be your best bet for lodging. The area is virtually devoid of hotels, but it is walkable to bars, restaurants, the stadium area, and the Inner Harbor. The city also offers a free GEICO Gameday Shuttle that goes through Federal Hill, making your gameday transit even easier. Fells Points For more local charm, stay in Fells Point , a cobblestone waterfront neighborhood established in 1763. Historic lodging in the area include The Pendry and The William Fell Inn , two brick-facade hotels that are worth a visit, even if you don’t spent the night. Fells Point has dozens of artisan shops and standout restaurants with access to the Inner Harbor and Federal Hill via water taxi. Harbor East If you’re looking for more modern, upscale accommodations, look no further than Harbor East . Situated between the Inner Harbor and Fells Point, it is home to the Four Seasons and the Baltimore Marriott Waterfront , which have some of the best views of the city. The area also has plenty of luxury shopping and fine dining. Inner Harbor/Camden Yards The biggest cluster of traditional hotels within walking distance of M&T Bank Stadium are near the Inner Harbor and Camden Yards . You’ll find most of your big chains with nearby light-rail access to the stadium. This is less of a signature Baltimore stay, but offers the most flexibility and geographic centrality. Things to do in Baltimore Inner Harbor Baltimore’s Inner Harbor features a diverse array of activities for all interests and ages. My personal favorite is the National Aquarium , which features thousands of animals and hundreds of different species. It’s not your typical underwater fare, either. The National Aquarium might be best known for Shark Alley, a 225,000-gallon, ring-shape shark tank that allows guests to walk down a spiral ramp alongside sharks of all shapes and sizes, but it also features a rainforest habitat and an exhibit of Australia’s extreme biomes. Other top Inner Harbor activities include the Maryland Science Center – which boasts full-size dinosaur skeletons as well as a planetarium and Maryland’s biggest IMAX screen – and the Reginald F. Lewis Museum , the largest African-American museum in Maryland. The Inner Harbor is also home to several historic ships, including the 19th-century sloop-of-war USS Constellation . A few blocks away is Power Plant Live! , an entertainment district featuring live music venues and dozens of food options at regular events throughout the year. More Baltimore activities: Visit the birthplace of “The Star-Spangled Banner” at Fort McHenry . Honor the Ravens’ namesake at the Edgar Allan Poe House & Museum , featuring the 19th-century poet’s grave. If you’re around between late November and New Year’s, check out Miracle on 34th Street , Baltimore’s best holiday lights (with several dining options nearby). For museum-lovers: American Visionary Art Museum : highlights self-taught, ‘outsider’ artistry with a focus on social justice B&O Railroad Museum : the birthplace of American railroading, in an 1884 roundhouse with the largest U.S. collection of 19th-century locomotives Walters Art Museum and Baltimore Museum of Art : the city’s best (and free!) art museums Babe Ruth Birthplace and Museum : the house where MLB legend Babe Ruth was born featuring the history of all sports in Maryland. Best places to eat in Baltimore Local Signatures First things first: If you’re coming to Maryland, you have to try a crabcake. The ‘best’ crabcake is subject to fierce debate among locals; my personal favorite is served by G&M Restaurant , which is located outside of the city but well worth the trip. Seafood from the Chesapeake Bay comprises the foundation of Baltimore’s local cuisine, and there’s a restaurant for any vibe: The Rusty Scupper : a classic, upscale waterfront experience on the Inner Harbor True Chesapeake : fresh, local, and restoratively-farmed oysters with innovative takes on seafood classics Nick’s Fish House : classic Baltimore seafood haunt where you can learn to pick steamed crabs Maryland-style Baltimore’s other signature dish is barbecue pit beef. It’s a popular menu item around the city, but I find it tastes best while tailgating or watching the game – fresh off the grill, thinly sliced, topped with Tiger sauce (mayonnaise and horseradish) and raw onions. Cross Street Market If you’re in Baltimore on game day, Cross Street Market is your one-stop destination for virtually any food need. It contains 16 food vendors that can cover nearly any dietary need. Pizza di Joey serves up jumbo slices that require two plates with a signature crispy bottom that make it an excellent grab-and-go option on the way to the stadium. Stick around for a beer and you’ll be entered to win a whole pizza that you can pick up after the game. They also offer a sausage and onion slice on game days along with pepperoni, cheese, and my personal favorite, Buffalo chicken. Theo’s Rolls and Bowls offers a variety of Vietnamese bánh mì sandwiches as well as their dynamite Bang Bang shrimp. I recommend the pork belly and Filipino-inspired adobo bánh mì in particular. Ramen might be an unconventional game day choice, but nothing is better before or after a cold winter football game. Dashi’s ramen will heat you right up on your way to or from M&T Bank Stadium. They also offer Asian-inspired twists on classic bar food, including phenomenal pastrami egg rolls. Here are some other highlights from Cross Street Market: Chicken Lab ’s chicken sandwiches come in a variety of flavors as another classic game day meal. Order like a Raven at Taco Joint! Super Bowl XXXV champion Femi Ayanbadejo recommends the surf and turf and chicken tacos. Grab a scoop of Taharka Bros.’ signature Honey Graham ice cream – or one of their many other flavors. You really can’t go wrong with anything in Cross Street Market. For a full list of their offerings, click here. A few of my favorite things Chicken wings: Delia Foley’s , smoked fresh and available with over a dozen sauces Ice cream: Pitango Gelato , specifically the mojito sorbet Pizza: Ledo Pizza , a local chain with a signature sauce and flaky pie crust Sushi: Shoyou Sushi and Nanami Cafe , a pair of casual spots with high-quality fish and creative rolls Sandwiches: Attman’s , serving freshly sliced meat piled high since 1915 Mexican: Barconina and Blue Agave , speciality tacos and tasty margaritas Fine dining: Charleston and Josefina , helmed by James Beard-recognized chefs M&T Bank Stadium parking, rideshare, and transit options Public Transit Baltimore’s devotion to its sports teams has made it easier to get to Ravens games without breaking the bank. The light rail runs from BWI Airport to M&T Bank Stadium with stops at Camden Yards (near Ravens Walk) and Hamburg Street (right outside the gates). A one-way ride is $2, and a $4.60 day pass…
author: Nikhil Mehta

title: Ravens discussion: should Eric DeCosta make a trade with the Colts?
summary: The Indianapolis Colts fired general manager Chris Ballard on Monday after a 2-4 start to the 2026 season, stirring speculation that the team could engage in a fire sale before the trade deadline. Baltimore Ravens general manager Eric DeCosta already made one blockbuster trade, sending a second-round pick to the Philadelphia Eagles in exchange for […]
full_text: KANSAS CITY, MISSOURI - NOVEMBER 23: Quenton Nelson #56 of the Indianapolis Colts runs onto the field before the game against the Kansas City Chiefs at Arrowhead Stadium on November 23, 2025 in Kansas City, Missouri. (Photo by Kathryn Riley/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Indianapolis Colts fired general manager Chris Ballard on Monday after a 2-4 start to the 2026 season, stirring speculation that the team could engage in a fire sale before the trade deadline. Baltimore Ravens general manager Eric DeCosta already made one blockbuster trade, sending a second-round pick to the Philadelphia Eagles in exchange for center Cam Jurgens. But the Colts have their own treasure trove of players to offer, particularly in the trenches where DeForest Buckner and Quenton Nelson can change games on their own. Should DeCosta call up Colts assistant GM Chris Dodds and make another deal? Nikhil Mehta If the Ravens want to move on from John Simpson as their starting left guard, they will have to stomach paying him $17.5 million for roughly half a season of work. Quenton Nelson would no doubt be a massive upgrade, but he is due for a substantial raise once his contract expires after the season. He would also cost premium draft capital – if Jurgens went for a second-round pick, Nelson is probably worth a first. It just does not make sense for Baltimore. Buckner, though, I have coveted for years. Officially, he already has four sacks and four tackles for loss through six games, and according to Pro Football Focus, he ranks ninth among interior defenders with 19 pressures. His pass rushing opportunities have also been somewhat limited by the Colts trailing for most of their games to open the year. This is another expiring contract in an expensive market, though, so a premium Day 3 pick would be the most I would offer for a half-season rental. Dustin Cox As much as I love the idea of adding Quinton Nelson to the Ravens, I simply do not think it is feasible given the combination of draft capitol required to pry him away from the Colts and the need to pay him a new contract. Nelson will surely demand another top-of-the-market deal and I am not sure if the Ravens are in a spot to hand one out, given their future cap situation and players such as Roger Rosengarten and Nate Wiggins who will be eligible for extensions next year. A player such as DeForest Buckner may make more sense, but Baltimore already has big-contract players on the defensive line in Nnamdi Madubuike and Travis Jones. Already giving up a 2028 second-round pick for Cam Jurgens means Eric DeCosta may not be as willing to part with another Day 2 pick. If a trade is to be made before the deadline, I expect DeCosta to flip a mid-round pick for a solid player instead. Zach Canter The Ravens should absolutely be calling to see the asking price on Quinton Nelson and DeForest Buckner. Both are north of 30 and on expiring contracts that the Colts should be looking to offload. I could see the Ravens passing on Buckner cause they have both Nnamdi Madubuike and Travis Jones signed long-term. Jesse Minter has struggled to get the most out of his pass rush, particularly with Trey Hendrickson and Mike Green failing to produce at the same time. Another disruptive interior would boost the pass rush and offer the flexibility for Madubuike to flex outside as a jumbo edge rusher. Nelson is a guy the Ravens shouldn’t be outbid for. There are a ton of resources now tied up in the offensive line: a first round pick in Ioane, the trade for Jurgens (and his contract), and veteran deals for John Simpson and Ronnie Stanley. Roger Rosengarten is eligible for an extension next spring and should be in line for a substantial raise. But with Stanley on an expiring contract and Vinson looking plausible as a future left tackle, there’s no reason for the Ravens to not go all in on building the wall this year and the future. There’s a very possible future that includes Nelson, Jurgens, Ioane, and Rosengarten the core of the OL for the next couple of years. Restructure a couple contracts, throw John Simpson in the deal, extend Lamar Jackson this offseason, and there’s a way to make the cap space for both Nelson and Rosengarten to get extensions. If the Ravens want to be a contender this year, it’s a move they should absolutely make. As the L.A. Rams say, F them picks. Kevin McNelis The Colts are in significant disarray at the moment, and Chris Ballard’s firing seems to signify that they’re ready to head in a new direction. With that in mind, I agree that Baltimore should see what the asking price is for Quenton Nelson and/or DeForest Buckner. The earlier acquisition of Cam Jurgens for a future second-rounder seems to signify that Baltimore is willing to deal at a high price to try to win now; the question is what kind of price they’re willing to pay for either of these guys, considering that they’d be short-term rentals under their current contracts. My gut says the Colts stand pat for at least a few more days while they try to figure out who is handling any trade considerations, especially given EDC’s track record of swooping in like a hawk to go after embattled franchises at moments of vulnerability. If I had to pick one target over the other, I’d see what the Colts want for Quenton Nelson since he would shore up the line basically everywhere barring another injury. Q is one of the most reliable guards in the league and has been for many years, so if you could line up LJ’s return with reinforcements along his line, this offense could get a huge, much-needed boost. I don’t know that I see the Ravens actually pulling the trigger to go after of these guys, but I’ve been surprised before (the Roquan acquisition comes to mind).
author: Dustin Cox

title: Examining Buffalo Bills 3rd down defense woes
summary: The Buffalo Bills haven’t had any difficulty whatsoever when it comes to scoring points. Which is wild, because us fans have seen them leave meat on the bone (a Cardinal WNY sin when it comes to wings). Yet at 5-1, they’ve won nailbiter after nailbiter thanks to a defense that doesn’t seem to particularly enjoy […]
full_text: The Buffalo Bills haven’t had any difficulty whatsoever when it comes to scoring points. Which is wild, because us fans have seen them leave meat on the bone (a Cardinal WNY sin when it comes to wings). Yet at 5-1, they’ve won nailbiter after nailbiter thanks to a defense that doesn’t seem to particularly enjoy sitting on the bench. It’s kind of them to allow Josh Allen to catch his breath, but would another third down stop here or there kill them? I mean, it’s bad. Real, real bad. And getting worse rather than better… Some stats to ponder I think all football fans can agree that whenever possible, it’s preferable for your favorite team to get a stop on third down. If you can believe it, there’s a good correlation between third-down stops and points allowed by NFL defenses. Therefore third down stops are a good thing as they help your team prevent points which is of course correlated with winning. Complicated math lesson aside, let’s set a baseline and then stack up some Bills numbers. The current NFL average 39.29% for allowing third down conversions. We’ll call that the perfect average (aka the “mean”) for purposes of discussion. If we treat “average” as a cluster of teams and apply my rule of four so I can skip all sorts of calculations I don’t care about doing tonight, the average line is anything below 43.371% (set by the Green Bay Packers in the 9th worst spot for the metric). OK then. That means you don’t want to allow greater than 43.37% or risk me saying you’re bad or terrible. Where do the Bills currently sit? They’re the fifth worst team in the league at 45.00%. That’s already bad, but I have worse news. They’re getting worse! Against the Houston Texans they allowed 43.75%. Against the Detroit Lions, they allowed 36.36%. Against the Los Angeles Chargers it was 40.00%, then 41.67% against the New England Patriots, then 50.00% against the Los Angeles Rams, and most recently 58.33% against the Raiders. Want even worse news? No one allows more third downs than the Dallas Cowboys, and even they only do so at a 54.67% rate. Sure I’m comparing the Bills’ worst day to Dallas average day, but it helps add perspective on just how bad it was against the Raiders. Bills fans expected growing pains, but the idea is that it leads to improvement over the course of the season and in this key metric, it just ain’t happening so far this year. Let’s check the film then! What we have is every single third down the Raiders faced against Buffalo. The official stat sheet has them going 7 of 12 to get that 58.33% conversion rate noted above. That said, the one by penalty and the one field goal are not counted in those totals. Do with that information what you will. pic.twitter.com/KHl8pskmjv — Kuebiko (@Kuebiko_Kami) October 21, 2026 I don’t have the time tonight to break down every single play in narrative format without jeopardizing my ability to do my fulltime job due to sleep deprivation so here’s my short version… There’s a little bit of hope. Remember that it’s NORMAL to give up around 40% of conversions. The 22.22% the Minnesota Vikings allow would of course be great, but we don’t need exceptional right yet as we’re setting our sights on “mediocre” first. To get to that level, Buffalo would have needed two less conversions allowed in this game. Honestly, I think they were close on a few. There are several lowlights in that short, depressing, awful film I have above that are due to a bit of confusion which created reaction lag. A little more time and understanding of the system could pay off. We also have Tre’Davious White to look forward to. If he sees the field, I do think recognition of the play could be a major advantage compared to what we see in the clips. Physical speed is great, but as we see on plays like the 3rd & 8 about a quarter of the way into the video, it’s the confusion that can kill. Even with the growing pains, there are several play in this game where small improvements give the defense a chance at a stop. If they can make those little changes, perhaps they can reverse the decline and get back to their middling ways .

title: Buffalo Bills fans grade the signing of CB Tre’Davious White
summary: Welcome to SB Nation Reacts, a survey of fans across the NFL. Throughout the year we ask questions of the most plugged-in Bills fans and fans across the country. The Buffalo Bills’ bye week is upon us, and there’s plenty to discuss in the absence of a game this coming weekend. The Bills share a […]
full_text: DENVER, COLORADO - JANUARY 17: Tre'Davious White #27 of the Buffalo Bills celebrates during an NFL divisional playoff football game against the Denver Broncos at Empower Field at Mile High on January 17, 2026 in Denver, Colorado. (Photo by Perry Knotts/Getty Images) | Getty Images Welcome to SB Nation Reacts, a survey of fans across the NFL. Throughout the year we ask questions of the most plugged-in Bills fans and fans across the country. The Buffalo Bills’ bye week is upon us, and there’s plenty to discuss in the absence of a game this coming weekend. The Bills share a lead as the NFL’s top scoring offense through six weeks, averaging 32.8 points per game. The offense is also currently ranked first in pass yards per play, and second in yards per play, as well pass yards per play. Things haven’t missed a beat on that side of the ball following Joe Brady’s promotion to head coach. It’s Buffalo’s defense that could stand to improve, currently ranked 28th in points given up per game, plus 31st in both yards given up per game and pass yards given up per game. Despite improvements against the run and an eye test in Week 6 that revealed an improved pass defense, the Bills have a lot of work to do before even thinking about the playoffs. In giving up nearly 29 points per game, Buffalo’s defense currently needs quarterback Josh Allen and the offense to put up almost 33 points a game just to walk off the field with a win. It’s not sustainable, and hardly a winning formula in the postseason. It’s interesting to think how good the offense may be with wide receiver DJ Moore healthy, and tight end Dalton Kincaid able to avoid the myriad of injuries that occasionally sideline him. Yet wide receiver Keon Coleman has really stepped up where needed, functioning well as the team’s leading receiver in recent weeks, and as a true complement to wide receiver Khalil Shakir. The Bills did make a move to bring back cornerback Tre’Davious White following the win in Las Vegas this past weekend. White, now 31, brings plenty of experience once again to One Bills Drive, but the system is entirely new under defensive coordinator Jim Leonhard. White will eventually be signed to the team’s 53-man active roster, once he’s acclimated and ready for game speed. Will White’s addition pay needed dividends for the Bills’ defensive backfield? title: Buffalo’s best things to do, see, and eat before heading to a Bills game
summary: For Buffalo Bills fans, game day is about much more than four quarters of football. It’s about the people, the traditions, the food, and the unmistakable energy that takes over Western New York when the Bills are playing at home. Whether you’re making your first trip to Buffalo or returning for another season, there’s plenty […]
full_text: Photo by Bryan Bennett/Getty Images | Getty Images For Buffalo Bills fans, game day is about much more than four quarters of football. It’s about the people, the traditions, the food, and the unmistakable energy that takes over Western New York when the Bills are playing at home. Whether you’re making your first trip to Buffalo or returning for another season, there’s plenty to experience before you ever set foot inside Highmark Stadium. Buffalo has a personality all its own. From legendary chicken wings and neighborhood taverns to waterfront attractions, historic landmarks, and some of the most passionate football fans in the NFL, the Queen City offers visitors a little bit of everything. And while the Bills may be the reason for your trip, you’ll quickly discover there’s a lot more to Buffalo than football. We’ve put together a guide to help visiting members of Bills Mafia make the most of their time in Western New York. Whether you’re flying in for a weekend, planning a family trip, or checking another stadium off your NFL bucket list, here’s where to stay, what to see, where to eat, and everything you need to know before heading to a Bills game. Places to stay in Buffalo One of the first decisions you’ll need to make is where to stay. While Highmark Stadium is located in Orchard Park, approximately 20 minutes south of downtown Buffalo without game-day traffic, there are several areas worth considering depending on what you’re looking to do during your visit. Downtown Buffalo: If you’re planning to turn your Bills trip into a full weekend getaway, downtown Buffalo is a great place to establish your home base. You’ll find hotels, restaurants, bars, entertainment, and attractions within walking distance or a short drive. Canalside and the waterfront: For visitors who enjoy waterfront views, restaurants, and easy access to downtown attractions, the Canalside area is worth exploring. Staying near the waterfront also puts you close to KeyBank Center and several popular destinations. Amherst and the airport area: This is my favorite go-to area. Hotels near Buffalo Niagara International Airport and Amherst are often convenient for travelers flying into town. You’ll have access to shopping, restaurants, and major highways while staying outside the busiest downtown areas. Orchard Park and Hamburg: If your priority is being closer to the stadium, consider accommodations in Hamburg or the surrounding Southtowns. Hotel options are more limited near the stadium itself, so another option could be to check out an Air BnB. One thing to keep in mind: Buffalo home games bring thousands of visitors to Western New York. Hotel availability can tighten quickly, particularly for prime-time games and divisional matchups. Things to do in Buffalo If you’re traveling to Buffalo for a game, consider arriving early. Western New York has plenty to offer, and some of the area’s best attractions are worth making time for. Niagara Falls: Just a short drive north of Buffalo, Niagara Falls is one of the region’s most recognizable attractions. Whether you’re visiting for the first time or returning after several years, the views never get old. Explore Niagara Falls State Park, walk along the observation areas, or take a boat tour when operating seasonally. Canalside: Located along Buffalo’s waterfront, Canalside offers walking paths, public spaces, seasonal activities, and beautiful views of the waterfront. It’s also a great place to explore nearby restaurants and attractions. Explore downtown Buffalo: Take some time to appreciate the city’s historic architecture, including Buffalo City Hall, the Guaranty Building, and the Richardson Olmsted Campus. Buffalo’s history is visible throughout the city, and many of its architectural treasures are worth seeing up close. Visit the Buffalo AKG Art Museum: For fans interested in art and culture, the Buffalo AKG Art Museum features an impressive collection and is located near Delaware Park. Explore Elmwood Village and Allentown: These neighborhoods are filled with locally owned shops, restaurants, coffee houses, and bars. They’re ideal for visitors looking to experience Buffalo beyond the typical tourist destinations. Experience another Buffalo sporting event: Depending on the schedule, visitors may be able to catch a Buffalo Sabres game at KeyBank Center or explore other local sporting events during their stay. And if it’s available take a tour of the new stadium! This gives you an opportunity to explore, learn about the stadium, see things you otherwise would not, a walk the trail around the stadium without worrying about it disrupting your game-day tailgate experience. Best places to eat in Buffalo You can’t write a guide to Buffalo without talking about the food. And while Buffalo is best known for its wings, the local food scene offers much more than wings covered in delicious sauce. Chicken wings: The Buffalo essential If this is your first visit, eating wings should be near the top of your list. Forget the ranch dressing. In Buffalo, wings traditionally come with blue cheese and celery. Bar-Bill Tavern: My absolute favorite and a favorite among locals and visitors alike, known for its crispy wings and signature sauces. Cajun Honey Butter BBQ is my go to! Gabriel’s Gate: Located in Allentown, this restaurant has earned a loyal following for its wings. Duff’s Famous Wings: Another iconic Buffalo establishment, particularly popular with visitors looking for traditional Buffalo-style wings. Anchor Bar: Famous for its place in Buffalo wing history and a popular destination for first-time visitors. Nine-Eleven Tavern: A South Buffalo favorite with a strong local reputation. WingNutz: For those who like a breaded wing. They have a location in Amherst and a new location is now available near the airport. They have wing flights available to sample different flavors! Beyond the wings Buffalo’s food culture extends well beyond its most famous dish. Beef on weck: A Western New York staple featuring thinly sliced roast beef served on a kummelweck roll with salt and caraway seeds. Charlie the Butcher and Schwabl’s are two places worth considering. Buffalo-style pizza: Buffalo has its own distinct pizza style, generally featuring a thicker, airy crust, generous cheese, and cup-and-char pepperoni. Picassos, La Nova, Bocce Club Pizza, and Imperial Pizza are well-known local names. Ted’s Hot Dogs: A Buffalo institution known for charcoal-broiled hot dogs, particularly when paired with fries and a Loganberry drink. Riverworks: Located along the river in the city’s historical industrial district, Buffalo’s RiverWorks is one of the area’s most unique entertainment destinations. Sponge candy: If you’ve never tried this Western New York favorite, stop by Watson’s Chocolates or another local candy shop for a sweet souvenir. And for those who enjoy exploring neighborhood bars and restaurants, Buffalo has no shortage of independently owned establishments where the conversation will almost certainly turn to the Bills. Highmark Stadium parking, rideshare and transit options Getting to Highmark Stadium requires a little planning, particularly for fans unfamiliar with Orchard Park. Unlike stadiums located in major downtown areas, the Bills’ home is surrounded by residential neighborhoods, local businesses, and parking lots that transform into a sea of red, white, and blue on game day. My biggest suggestion: have a car. Whether it’s the game day experience or just your weekend in Buffalo altogether, having a car makes your experience much more convenient. Stadium parking: Official Bills parking lots and surrounding private lots offer different options depending on how early you plan to arrive and what kind of tailgating experience you’re looking for. Parking lots open 4 hours prior to kickoff and have to be pre-purchased so check Ticketmaster for resale tickets. There are important tailgating rules for the Bills owned lots so come prepared. title: NFL trade deadline: Buffalo Bills trade candidate – Derwin James
summary: As soon as we know it, the NFL trade deadline will be here, and the rumors will have been running rampant for weeks regarding who the Buffalo Bills might acquire via trade. To adequately prepare you for every possibility on this front, I’m launching a series that will profile all the potential Bills trade candidates […]
full_text: As soon as we know it, the NFL trade deadline will be here, and the rumors will have been running rampant for weeks regarding who the Buffalo Bills might acquire via trade. To adequately prepare you for every possibility on this front, I’m launching a series that will profile all the potential Bills trade candidates ahead of the deadline. With the Week 7 bye approaching for the Bills, this is the perfect time to start this series. I’ll sprinkle these templated profiles onto the site up until the actual trade deadline until November 10, which is 21 day from now, and lands after Week 9. First up, Chargers safety Derwin James. Age: 30 He’s been a first-team All-Pro twice — after the 2018 (as a safety) and 2021 seasons — and a second-team All-Pro four times — after the 2018 season (as a defensive back), in 2022, 2024, and 2025. In short, he’s long been viewed as arguably the best strong safety / slot corner hybrid in the NFL. Ironically, James has not played since Week 3’s loss in Orchard Park. He’s dealing with a hamstring issue. What’s noteworthy about his start to 2026 — James had the highest missed tackle rate (16.7%) of his career, and throws in his coverage vicinity have netted a passer rating of 126.9, the highest rating he’s surrendered on those throws in a season as a professional. James is still one of the most physically imposing, genuinely versatile safeties in football. The first three games of this season have indicated he’s started to decline. Although the entire Chargers defense has struggled mightily in the club’s 0-6 start. 2026 snap splits Box: 37.3% Slot corner : 36.7% Free safety: 15.5% Defensive line: 9.3% Wide corner: 1% How he’d fit with Bills James’ presence in Buffalo’s lineup would create a ripple effect in the safety room, because of the type of safety he is. Entering the bye, Cole Bishop has played close to half of his snaps in the box and has spent a fourth of the time at free safety. Because of that there’d need to be some responsibility change and pre-snap alignment deviation for either him or Bishop. I’d guess James would likely move into a more predominant slot corner role, to deal with larger receivers in that position or tight ends deployed there. Financial obligation for Bills to trade for him 2026 salary: $11.5M If the Bills trade for James after Week 9, they’d be on the hook for $5.75M in prorated base salary. His 2027 salary is $17.5M (fully guaranteed), and in 2028 it’s set to be $24.6M. Remember though, upon acquiring any player via trade, the new team can agree to a completely different contract with the player. That’d likely be the route Buffalo would like to follow if James was added. What also must be considered here — per Spotrac , the Bills are allocating the fourth-lowest collective cap hit on the safety position in 2026. Next season, it’s the league’s seventh-lowest figure at $6.92M, and Bishop will be entering the final season of his rookie deal in 2027. Projected cost to acquire Using Syndicate32.com’s trade machine , given the Chargers venturing into a fire-sale situation, the projected cost to trade for James is a 2027 Round 2 pick. Even that feels a little high given his age and slow start to 2026. His current injury doesn’t exactly elevate his trade value either. Should the Bills trade for Derwin James? I respect the hell out of what James has brought to the field for the entirety of his NFL career. I was flabbergasted on draft night 2018 when he wasn’t selected until pick No. 17, and he’s been a downright stud in a truly hybrid role over the past eight-plus seasons now. Even if the draft-pick compensation to acquire James is less than a second-rounder, this fit doesn’t feel right to me. Sure, an argument could be made that the Bills defense simply needs more talented players on it, and James is undoubtedly a freaky specimen. However, Cole Bishop hasn’t been spectacular, he is locked into the strong-safety/blitzer/slot defender role AND maybe just as importantly, Buffalo has two young, reasonably large safeties behind him who may very well start to see the field sooner than later in Jalon Kilgore and second-year pro Jordan Hancock. I’m high on both of them as they grow in this defense in a James-like role. If James was playing in 2026 on an expiring contract, had a tiny base salary, or little-to-no future guaranteed dollars left on his deal, I could be persuaded here. None of those financial components are true. And as a reigning All-Pro, I doubt James would agree to ripping up his current Chargers deal and signing a cheap contract in Buffalo. I wouldn’t blame him for refusing to do that. For as fun of a player as James is, even at 30, I’m out on this trade candidate for the Bills. What do you think?

title: Bills Mafia hits the red carpet as ‘Just One Before I Die’ prepares for Tubi debut
summary: Bills Mafia is trading tailgate lots for the red carpet this evening as Just One Before I Die: The Story of Buffalo Fans celebrates its premiere ahead of its Wednesday, October 21 debut on Tubi. From legendary tailgate traditions to personal journeys, some of Bills Mafia’s most recognizable personalities are stepping into the spotlight as a new […]
full_text: Bills Mafia is trading tailgate lots for the red carpet this evening as Just One Before I Die: The Story of Buffalo Fans celebrates its premiere ahead of its Wednesday, October 21 debut on Tubi. From legendary tailgate traditions to personal journeys, some of Bills Mafia’s most recognizable personalities are stepping into the spotlight as a new a new five-part documentary series celebrates what makes Buffalo Bills fandom unlike any other. The premiere brings together the documentary’s creators, featured fans, and special guests to celebrate the stories and traditions that have helped make Bills Mafia one of the most recognizable fan bases in professional sports. Buffalo Bills fandom is unlike anything else in the world of sports. It’s a community built on decades of loyalty, unforgettable traditions, friendships, heartbreak, and an unwavering belief that someday, the Buffalo Bills will finally bring home a Super Bowl championship. Several years ago, Buffalo-raised filmmakers Kevin Polowy and Addison Henderson set out on a journey to capture that passion and tell the stories of the people who make Bills Mafia what it is today. On Wednesday, October 21, their vision becomes a reality when Just One Before I Die , a five-episode documentary series, premieres on Tubi. All five episodes will be available to stream free of charge. But before the documentary makes its streaming debut, the cast, creators, and members of Bills Mafia will gather Tuesday evening for a special red-carpet premiere in Buffalo. Meet some of faces For anyone who has spent time around a Buffalo Bills tailgate, some of the personalities featured in the documentary need little introduction. Others have built their communities through social media, charitable initiatives, and their dedication to the team. Among the familiar faces featured in the series: Kenny “Pinto Ron” Johnson: One of Buffalo’s most recognizable tailgate legends, famous for the ketchup-and-mustard ceremony and the traditions surrounding the Red Pinto Tailgate. Del Reid: Co-creator of the “Bills Mafia” movement and founder of 26 Shirts, a charitable apparel company that has turned Buffalo sports fandom into a powerful force for giving back to the community. 2023 Bills Fan of the Year. Frank “HannaBill-Lecter” Barber: A school principal who transforms into one of Bills Mafia’s most recognizable characters on home game days, dressing up and painting his face to show his unwavering support for the Bills. Joanie “Mama J” Podkowinski DeKoker: With more than 260 consecutive Bills games under her belt, Mama J is a familiar face throughout Bills Mafia. Her signature cowboy hat, adorned with Bills pins collected over the years of attending games, maybe as recognizable as she is. Kristen Kimmick: Founder and president of Bills Mafia Babes. She founded the group in 2016 to create a welcoming community where female Bills fans could discuss football without judgement. Sara “Shades” Larson: A dedicated Bills fan whose consecutive-game attendance streak has taken her across the country and the pond, following the team through wins, losses, and everything in between. The “Sara Shades” nickname was given by production as a lighthearted joke that has kind of stuck. Norm “Torpedo Dan” Brumfield: A Bills Mafia staple known for attending tailgates in his signature Speedo, even when the temperatures drop well below freezing. Sirr “SirrBaby” Woods: A recognizable Bills Mafia creator whose personality and journey are featured in the documentary. Though originally from Texas, he gained widespread popularity amongst the Bills community celebrating Buffalo football culture. John “Elvis” Lang: One of the fan base’s most recognizable personalities, bringing his unmistakable Elvis-inspired game-day appearance to the stands. 2022 Bills Fan of the Year. Norm and Poo, “The Chefs”: very familiar faces within the Bills Mafia tailgate community and often seen at games with their chef hats on. 2024 Bills Fan(s) of the Year. The documentary also features Ché Noir, Michael and Chuck Skelly, Kris Rose Brown, Keita Nakagawa, Jay Gatz, Steve Biegner, Kimberly Kaliszewski, Renee De Wald, Donna Hartnett, Damsel ’N Disdress, Becky Rice-Kane, and many more. While the costumes, traditions, and larger-than-life personalities may be what initially catch your attention, Just One Before I Die takes viewers beyond the surface to discover the people behind them. Bills Mafia has never been defined solely by wins and losses. It’s the traditions, friendships, travel, dedication, and generations of fans who continue showing up for a team still chasing that elusive Super Bowl championship. Just One Before I Die brings some of those stories to the screen, offering viewers a look at the individuals who make this fan base unlike any other. For many of us, the series is also a tribute to those of us who lost someone along the journey who never got the opportunity to witness JUST ONE. A Buffalo story brought to life by an extensive creative team At the heart of the documentary are creators, directors, writers, and producers Addison Henderson and Kevin Polowy, who spent years bringing the project to life. The production also includes co-creator and executive producer Clayton Polowy, with executive producers including former Buffalo Bills wide receiver Andre Reed, Chad Michael Murray, Mac Cappuccino, Marty Polo, Amy Elizabeth, Kayme Crowell Gianatasio, Jose Padin, Jamal Henderson, and Maverick Carter. Additional members of the production team include producer Leah Lynette Cohen-Mays, co-producer Trent Boling, associate producer KJ Zielezinski, directors of photography Andy Morin and Stephen Gerard Kelly, and composer Christy Carew. The series represents years of work dedicated to sharing the stories of a fan base whose connection to its team extends far beyond the football field. Bills Mafia rolls out the red carpet On Tuesday, October 20, the documentary’s creators, featured personalities, and special guests will gather in Buffalo for the red-carpet premiere of Just One Before I Die . For many involved in the project, the premiere marks the culmination of years of filming, storytelling, and capturing the moments that define Bills Mafia. It’s also an opportunity to celebrate the community that made the documentary possible before the series reaches audiences nationwide. The credits roll, but the party is just getting started Following the premiere, Bills Mafia is invited to keep the celebration going at the official Buffalo After Party, hosted at Southern Tier Brewing Co. in downtown Buffalo. The event promises signature draft beer, cocktails, exclusive behind-the-scenes content, giveaways throughout the evening, and a chance to celebrate alongside fellow Bills fans. Best of all, it’s a party with a purpose. A portion of sales will benefit the Andre Reed Foundation, which supports children through literacy, mentorship, and youth programming. Buffalo After Party details Date: Tuesday, October 20, 2026 Time: 9 p.m. to 2 a.m. Location: Southern Tier Brewing Co. Address: 7 Scott Street, Buffalo, NY 14203 Tickets: General Admission: $35 VIP Open Bar: $85 The event is sponsored by Seneca Nation, INGRAM Micro, Epson, Dave & Adam’s Card World, Big Indian Drift Pit, Kiss 98.5, WGR 550 Sports Radio, and Southern Tier Brewing Company. Grab your tickets now! Join Bills Mafia tonight at Southern Tier Brewing Co. for the official Just One Before I Die after-party. Purchase tickets: JustOneParty.Eventbrite.com⁠ How to watch ‘Just One Before I Die’ The wait is almost over. All five episodes of Just One Before I Die premiere Wednesday, October 21, on Tubi , where the entire series will be available to stream for free. title: Christian Benford’s play has returned to normal in Jim Leonhard’s defense
summary: Christian Benford remains one of the most underrated cornerbacks in the NFL, and he’s started to round into form for the Buffalo Bills the past two weeks. And his spike in performance has ironically occurred after he missed a game with a turf toe injury. Let’s track Benford’s 2026 season thus far. In Week 1, […]
full_text: Christian Benford remains one of the most underrated cornerbacks in the NFL, and he’s started to round into form for the Buffalo Bills the past two weeks. And his spike in performance has ironically occurred after he missed a game with a turf toe injury. Let’s track Benford’s 2026 season thus far. In Week 1, he followed Nico Collins. Shadowed him, really. He was the primary coverage defender on 91.4% of the Texans receiver’s routes, and the results weren’t fantastic but were far from brutal for Benford. He allowed six catches for 66 yards and a touchdown on 32 routes in coverage on Collins. Then, in Week 2, Benford covered the super-slippery, mostly-slot specialist Amon-Ra St. Brown on 13 routes. He yielded two grabs for 23 yards and a score. Better. The predominant coverage assignment for Benford in that game, Isaac TeSlaa, whom the Bills cornerback followed on 60.6% of his routes, only had one catch for 20 yards in those matchups. In Week 3, Benford did not shadow anyone. He moved around throughout the game and surrendered three catches for 40 yards to Quentin Johnston and just one snag for 11 yards to Ladd McConkey on 14 total coverage snaps. He missed Week 4’s game with that turf toe injury. In Week 5, Benford covered Puka Nacua and Davante Adams on more than 67% of those receivers’ routes. On those 30 routes, the Bills top cornerback allowed six catches for a mere 44 yards without a score. In Week 6, Benford really settled into a groove. He covered Raiders phenom tight end Brock Bowers on 18 of his routes and gave up two catches for 23 yards. Bowers first catch in the game didn’t happen until there was less than five minutes to go in the third quarter. Altogether, Benford has five pass breakups and 28 tackles in five contests to date this season. The former sixth-round pick is back to playing his normal brand of football. And although he doesn’t have the blue-blood college pedigree or a freaky combine performance on his resume, he’s acclimated well to Jim Leonhard’s scheme. All stats courtesy of Fantasy Points Data*

title: Buffalo Bills HC Joe Brady voices support for S C.J. Gardner-Johnson
summary: Without question, it’s been a tough start to the season for Buffalo Bills safety C.J. Gardner-Johnson. His frustration boiled over in Week 6 during Buffalo’s road game at the Las Vegas Raiders, which led to his being flagged for a personal foul and ejected from the game for spitting in the direction of tight end […]
full_text: INGLEWOOD, CA - OCTOBER 12: C.J. Gardner-Johnson #22 of the Buffalo Bills lines up before the snap during an NFL football game against the Los Angeles Rams at SoFi Stadium on October 12, 2026 in Inglewood, California. (Photo by Cooper Neill/Getty Images) | Getty Images Without question, it’s been a tough start to the season for Buffalo Bills safety C.J. Gardner-Johnson. His frustration boiled over in Week 6 during Buffalo’s road game at the Las Vegas Raiders, which led to his being flagged for a personal foul and ejected from the game for spitting in the direction of tight end Brock Bowers. On the heels of that incident, Gardner-Johnson has been handed a one-game suspension . Despite all that, head coach Joe Brady isn’t blinking in the face of adversity and the court of public opinion. During his most recent media availability on Monday following the team’s win in Vegas, Brady explained that Gardner-Johnson “knows that can’t happen, that’s inexcusable, that’s not the standard that we’re gonna have and play with,” and that despite their intent to “toe the line, we can’t cross the line.” Brady then also gave a vote of confidence in Gardner-Johnson, saying that no additional discipline or action will happen beyond the league punishment. He also acknowledged there’s plenty of room for improvement as a player and member of the locker room. When asked point-blank if Gardner-Johnson has a starting job when he returns, Brady said: “Yeah, I mean, look, C.J.’s a member of the Buffalo Bills. We brought him here for a reason and we know that he — he knows that he has to play better. He knows he has to be better for this team. You know, just like, like everybody else. Right? We gotta learn from this stuff, and we have to improve, and find ways to get better as the season goes. You know, no different than — it’s different , right? — Jimbo fumblin’, you know. We have to continue to find ways to get better, and he (Gardner-Johnson) knows that he has to be better. And, you know, it’s just an opportunity for him — look, it’d be an opportunity for someone else to, you know, play in the week and step up — but it’s an opportunity for him grow and be better as a better teammate and a better football player, you know, when his opportunity comes up again.” Gardner-Johnson’s actions will cost him an opportunity to suit up and play in the team’s Week 8 matchup against the Baltimore Ravens, their first game back following the bye week. Bills Mafia will have to wait to find out what Brady meant by stating “when his opportunity comes up again.” For his part, Gardner-Johnson owned his mistake and expressed a willingness to “ take my consequence as it is, my fine, whatever it may be .” Here's C.J. Gardner-Johnson's full postgame comments after being ejected from today's game. #Bills safety says he let emotions get the best of him. CJGJ apologized to the team after the game. pic.twitter.com/NrtXXS9ek6 — Jon Scott (@JonScottTV) October 19, 2026
