title: Buffalo Bills defense not better, but certainly different, in 2026
summary: The Bills were always going to look different on defense in 2026. From the time the firing of former head coach Sean McDermott was announced in the early parts of 2026, we all knew that Buffalo Bills owner Terry Pegula was pointing to coaching for a reason, and it wasn’t the performance of the team’s […]
full_text: The Bills were always going to look different on defense in 2026. From the time the firing of former head coach Sean McDermott was announced in the early parts of 2026, we all knew that Buffalo Bills owner Terry Pegula was pointing to coaching for a reason, and it wasn’t the performance of the team’s offense. So when new head coach and former offensive coordinator Joe Brady hired Jim Leonhard to be his defensive coordinator, everyone knew that qualitatively, what the Bills looked like on defense in 2026 would be very different than what the fans had been used to seeing from that unit for the previous nine years. Through six weeks of the 2026 regular season, the Bills defense has absolutely looked different than it has in previous years. It’s also objectively been worse (data from Fantasy Points Data Suite). The Buffalo defense thus far in 2026 is: 30th in EPA per play allowed 28th in EPA per drop back 25th in EPA per rush 28th in success rate against 28th in explosive play rate against To put this in perspective, in 2025 in the same categories, the Bills were: 14th in EPA per play allowed 8th in EPA per drop back 31st in EPA per rush 11th in success rate against 25th in explosive play rate against When your eyes tell you that the team has been a little better against the run than in 2025, your eyes are right. Everything else in terms of resultant defensive metrics is not just worse, but bad. How did we get here? What’s different stylistically in 2026 versus previous years? The biggest and most glaring departure for the 2026 is that the Bills, for a decade one of the most nickel-stubborn teams in the National Football League, are now running base personnel 36.2% of their defensive snaps (9th in the NFL), up from single digit base defense percentages in most years of the Sean McDermott era. The increased base defensive percentage also leads to the Bills having an average box count of 7.13 (5th in the NFL), compared to 6.87 in 2025 (19th in the league) and 6.52 in 2024 (27th in the league). This heavier phenomenon is a contributing factor to the slightly increased effectiveness against the run, but it’s also a factor in the decreased effectiveness against the pass. the McDermott Bills were well-noted to be a team that refused to be dictated to in terms of defensive personnel, and former nickel defender Taron Johnson was the centerpiece of that philosophy that has changed under Jim Leonhard. The next defensive characteristic that has changed significantly in 2026 on defense is the Bills coverage splits on defense. We live in a cover 3 league meta right now (current league average for cover 3 usage is 32.7%, the largest plurality of all coverage groups), but the Bills play cover 4 an astounding 26% of the time in 2026 (#1 in the league) while also being above league average in cover 3 usage (34.4% for Buffalo), which means over 60% of the time, the Bills are running either cover 3 or cover 4. Compare this to 2025, when the Bills ran cover 3 at a mark below the league average with cover 4 right at the league average and cover 2 and cover 1 above the league average. This shows that coverage diversity was far more present in 2025 versus 2026. So the Bills are running a lot more base defense with heavier boxes and a lot more cover 3 and cover 4 (the most cover 4 in the league, even). You may think this is a more aggressive lean, but the Bills are pressing at least one receiver less in 2026 (14.1%, 28th in the league) than the “maligned for ‘soft coverage’” Sean McDermott’s defense in 2025 (30.2%, 7th in the NFL). “Maybe they’re blitzing more”, you say. I mean, a little bit. Buffalo is 20th in the NFL in blitz rate in 2026 (27.9%) and was 23rd in 2025 (24.3%), so not a statistically significantly difference. If you have a team that is: running heavier defensive personnel running heavier boxes running the most cover 4 in the league running a less diverse selection of coverages pressing a lot less still not blitzing much You have the 2026 Bills defense compared to the previous and most recent versions of it. And the results make sense: they’ve seen a slight uptick in run defense due to heavier boxes and heavier personnel, but they’re running a lot of cover 4 to prevent explosives, which might get them there if the communication in the back seven wasn’t leading to blown coverages, allowing explosive plays in the pass game despite the cover 4 calls. They’re not blitzing, they’re not pressing, they’re not diversifying, and they’re not disguising (26.3% disguise rate, 28th in the NFL), so quarterbacks aren’t holding the ball (2.68 average time to throw against, 11th in the NFL). Being able to stop the run from two high is the holy grail of NFL defenses (the Bills are top 12 in both two-high and base personnel usage), so you can see the outcome the Bills are trying to generate, but it’s not happening for them through six weeks. The Bills were trying to get over the hump when they fired Sean McDermott, and they elected to hire a rookie head coach and a rookie defensive coordinator. You can’t do that and then logically not provide any grace for rookie mistakes from your rookie coaches, but the Bills are fortunate to be 5-1 going into their bye week with the defensive generating results this poor. Let’s hope we come out of the bye with a clear identity of how Jim Leonhard and the defense will get where we all want them to go. …and that’s the way the cookie crumbles. I’m Bruce Nolan with Buffalo Rumblings. You can find me on Twitter and Instagram @BruceExclusive and look for new episodes of “The Bruce Exclusive” every Thursday on the Rumblings Cast Network — see more in my LinkTree!

title: Buffalo Bills records and milestones from Week 6
summary: Well, that one was a little closer than we would have liked, but the Buffalo Bills get to head into the bye with a win. That’s definitely going to make the next two weeks a little more enjoyable while we wait to see them back on the field.  There’s been plenty of criticism of the […]
full_text: Well, that one was a little closer than we would have liked, but the Buffalo Bills get to head into the bye with a win. That’s definitely going to make the next two weeks a little more enjoyable while we wait to see them back on the field. There’s been plenty of criticism of the Bills’ play — and rightfully so — but not everything has been a cause for concern. So, let’s take a look at a few Shout!outs for the things that went right this week. _____________________________________________________________________________ Josh Allen just passed Russell Wilson. Allen’s 9-yard touchdown pass to Khalil Shakir was the 317th total touchdown of his career, moving him past Russell Wilson for the second-most touchdowns by a player in his first 10 NFL seasons. Allen, of course, is only six games into season No. 9. Josh Allen’s 9-yard TD pass to Khalil Shakir marked Allen’s 317th total TD. Allen (playing in his 6th game of his 9th season) has now passed Russell Wilson (316) for the second-most total TDs in a player’s first 10 seasons. pic.twitter.com/boWs38DKT5 — Buffalo Bills PR (@BuffaloBillsPR) October 18, 2026 Of course, we know that in the third quarter of the game, Allen tied Hall of Famer Jim Kelly atop the Bills’ franchise record as well. You can read about that here. With that 12-yard TD pass to Keon Coleman, Josh Allen now has 258 passing TDs (including playoffs). Allen is now tied with Jim Kelly for the most in team history. pic.twitter.com/zh6CefDawU — Buffalo Bills PR (@BuffaloBillsPR) October 18, 2026 Joe Brady is in some pretty good company. Through his first six games as a head coach, Brady’s Bills are averaging 32.8 points per game. That’s the second-highest average in the Super Bowl era for a coach’s first six career games. The only man ahead of him? Mike Martz, whose 2000 Rams averaged an absurd 43.7 points. The Bills 32.8 points per game under Joe Brady mark the second-most in the Super Bowl era through a head coach’s first 6 career games. Only Mike Martz (Rams – 43.7 in 2000) averaged more points. https://t.co/5DPssggUKp — Buffalo Bills PR (@BuffaloBillsPR) October 19, 2026 Tyler Bass has found his groove. Remember when every field goal attempt felt like an adventure? Bass has now made 18 straight dating back to 2024, tying Rian Lindell for the longest streak by a Bills kicker since Lindell put together 18 consecutive makes in 2007. Tyler Bass has made 18 straight field goals dating back to 2024. He is tied for the longest streak by a Bills kicker since Rian Lindell with 18 (10/21/2007-12/09/2007). pic.twitter.com/sxfoQYH5c0 — Buffalo Bills PR (@BuffaloBillsPR) October 18, 2026 Keon Coleman is making a habit of finding the end zone. Coleman has caught a touchdown pass in three straight games, becoming the first Bills wide receiver to do that since Gabe Davis scored in four consecutive games back in 2023. All four of Keon Coleman's catches today have been for first downs (including TDs). 15 of his 19 catches this year have gone for first downs. https://t.co/P38jXFxxqH — Buffalo Bills PR (@BuffaloBillsPR) October 19, 2026 And one more for the defense. Dorian Williams picked off Kirk Cousins for the first interception of his NFL career. It might not be history-making, but your first career interception deserves a Shout! James Cook is up to 627 rushing yards this season. Only O.J. Simpson has had more in their first 6 games of a season in Bills history (868 yds in 1973 and 911 yds in 1975). pic.twitter.com/jPzKUo0KeL — Buffalo Bills PR (@BuffaloBillsPR) October 18, 2026 _____________________________________________________________________________ The Bills have plenty to work on, but there are some pretty good things happening in between the things that make us yell at our televisions. And with Allen rewriting record books, Brady collecting wins (whether they’re pretty or not is not for us to judge here), and Bass doing his job without giving us a collective heart attack, we’ve got plenty of reasons to keep Shout! ing.

title: Charlotte’s best things to do, see, and eat before heading to a Panthers game
summary: The Carolina Panthers have started to make themselves worth seeing in person once again. Dave Canales, Dan Morgan, and the rest of the front office have the team moving in the right direction, and the games have been enjoyable to watch. You might find yourself thinking that it’s high time you made it back out […]
full_text: Photo by Marcio Machado/Eurasia Sport Images/Getty Images | Getty Images The Carolina Panthers have started to make themselves worth seeing in person once again. Dave Canales, Dan Morgan, and the rest of the front office have the team moving in the right direction, and the games have been enjoyable to watch. You might find yourself thinking that it’s high time you made it back out to Bank of America Stadium, or maybe even pay it a visit for the first time. The stadium is situated right in the heart of Uptown Charlotte, which has its pros and cons. On the one hand, there are all sorts of things to do within walking distance of the stadium as part of your game-day experience. On the other hand, parking is not exactly the easiest thing to do. If you’re new to attending a Panthers game, visiting Charlotte, or if you’re just looking to change up your game-day routine, this post is for you. There is so much to do and see and eat in Charlotte that we won’t be able to get to everything, but hopefully this at least gets you started. Places to stay in Charlotte The best places to stay depend on how you’re trying to experience the city and what kind of temporary living accommodations you want. If a hotels are your thing, you’ll find that most of them are concentrated in the middle of the city, the airport, and Southpark while several smaller options sit along the highways. Uptown options tend to be a bit more high-end but are very convenient for actually getting to the game and partaking in the other activities that area has to offer. You’ll be within walking distance of lots of bars and restaurants for non-game activities and also within walking distance of the stadium, which is a plus given how difficult transit can sometimes be. If you want to get out of the hustle and bustle of the inner city but are still looking for a higher-end place to stay, Southpark has some great options. There are a few hotels in the area which are all very close to swanky restaurants and Southpark mall. If you’re looking for a more budget option, there are hotels in the University area in the north and Carolina Place Mall area in the south that are just a short drive or rideshare rides away from park and ride lots for the light rail into Uptown (more on that in the parking section). There aren’t a lot of hotel options in the other more walkable areas of Charlotte. If you do have access to a vehicle, hotels and rental houses in the Ballantyne area put you in the safest part of the city while surrounded by all sorts of retail space if you’re into shopping or eating. You’ll generally find that most of the south to southeastern part of the city is the quietest part of town if you’re looking for a more laid-back experience with a more routine day-to-day. Things to do in Charlotte If you’re making a Panthers game part of a more extended stay in Charlotte, there are plenty of other things to do to keep you busy when you’re not screaming your lungs out on thirrrrrrd down. If the outdoors are your thing, you can’t come to Charlotte and not pay a visit to the Whitewater Center . It has the world’s largest manmade whitewater river to give people of all abilities a whitewater rafting experience. There are also zip lines, rope courses, and dozens of miles of mountain biking and hiking trails. The trails are free access, and the other activities can be accessed with a day pass. They also transform one of the ponds to an ice skating rink in the winter. For racing aficionados, the NASCAR Hall of Fame sits just about half a mile away from Bank of America Stadium. It has a Hall of Honor like you’d expect from a Hall of Fame, as well as a number of exhibits to vary the experience, including a couple that are interactive. There are exhibits showing the evolution of the cars and tracks and the history of the sport. There is a pit crew challenge where you test how quickly you can change a tire and refuel the car like a NASCAR pit crew, and a racing simulator to see how well you can actually drive a race car. The whole experience is very highly regarded both by NASCAR fans and non-fans alike. For nights out on the town, there are two distinct options. For a more chill, artsy vibe, check out Plaza Midwood or NoDa on the east side of the city. Both areas feature a wide variety of dining options, bars, and breweries in easily walkable areas. If you want more of a party atmosphere, Southend , just south of uptown, offers a more high energy alternative with dance clubs, bars, and trendy restaurants that appeal to a younger crowd. Best places to eat in Charlotte Given the transit options, there are nearly limitless options for dining before making your way to the stadium. Lots of the park and rides for public transit (covered below) have nearby dining options, so you could always swing by a restaurant outside the heart of the city for a quick bite to eat before catching the bus or train into the city for the game. One of the most popular places for this is Optimist Hall in NoDa . It has dozens of food options with shared dining spaces, and it’s a short walk away from the Parkwood light rail station. If you want to enjoy some food in the uptown area within walking distance of the stadium, there are options for just about any food preference and budget. If you like the idea of a singular area with multiple food and drink options like Optimist Hall but want something nearer to the stadium, the Alley at Latta Arcade and the adjacent Brevard Court might be your thing. It’ll be very crowded in the hours leading up to a game, but it will be full of Panthers fans and form almost a tailgate-like environment. The whole complex is only a few blocks from the stadium, so it’s a short jaunt to the game once you finish your food and beverages. There are a number of standalone restaurants in the stadium’s vicinity that offer more traditional dining options. For hibachi and sushi, there’s Hasaki Grill & Sushi ( a Chuba Hubbard favorite ) about a block from the stadium. Next to it is Mellow Mushroom for pizza, Chex Grill & Wings for some standard American fare, a Rhino Market deli, and Tikka Shack for Indian food (and they have a pizza and wings deal for game days). If you want a more upscale dining experience in the area of the stadium for either the night before the game or in the evening after, Fogo de Chão and Chima Steakhouse are catty-cornered from one another in the middle of uptown. Not far away is an STK Steakhouse . Outside of the center city in the Southpark area is a more middle tier option and one of my personal favorites, Cowfish . They serve sushi, burgers, and a combo of the two (burgushi, if you will). Bank of America Stadium parking, rideshare, and transit options Bank of America Stadium does not have its own parking, so don’t expect to pull up to the stadium and find a place to park. Instead, parking is entirely done in various parking garages, lots, and open spaces scattered in the area surrounding the stadium. It’s very hit and miss on which lots have availability if you’re showing up on a whim. It can also be difficult to navigate the area due to heavy traffic, both vehicle and pedestrian. If you intend on driving to the game, it’s highly recommended that you get into the area as early as possible to make finding open parking areas as easy as possible. You can also plan and book parking early through Ticketmaster or SpotHero . Given how difficult commuting by car can be, the team and city have combined to offer several game day specific public transit options. The light rail (Blue Line) is a train service that runs from South Boulevard near 485 through uptown Charlotte all the way to the campus of UNC Charlotte. There are several park and ride locations along the route, particularly towards either end of the route. You can see the park and ride stations here . The Brooklyn Village station is the closest one to the stadium. It’s about a four block walk to the stadium from the station. Just be prepared to…

title: Panthers vs Eagles game review: Milestones
summary: They can’t all be pretty. In fact, almost every game the Carolina Panthers have participated in this season has had a certain quality that only their fans can love. While the product on the field may have been ugly, there’s a certain aesthetic that having more wins than losses has that I think we can […]
full_text: PHILADELPHIA, PENNSYLVANIA - OCTOBER 18: Bryce Young #9 of the Carolina Panthers looks to pass against the Philadelphia Eagles during an NFL football game at Lincoln Financial Field on October 18, 2026 in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania. (Photo by Michael Owens/Getty Images) | Getty Images They can’t all be pretty. In fact, almost every game the Carolina Panthers have participated in this season has had a certain quality that only their fans can love. While the product on the field may have been ugly, there’s a certain aesthetic that having more wins than losses has that I think we can all appreciate. While taking down the Philadelphia Eagles in their own building was the main goal, the Panthers set some personal records while a handful of players also made some history. For this weeks game review, let’s take a look at some of the records, milestones, and other notable marks that were reached. Prior to kickoff, the Panthers social team put out a few things to watch with most coming to fruition. Some @Panthers notes and milestones to watch for in Week 6 at the Eagles. #KeepPounding pic.twitter.com/F4p2YsuibD — Carolina Panthers Football Communications (@PanthersFBComms) October 16, 2026 Bryce Young became the first quarterback in team history to have at least 250 passing yards and a touchdown pass in seven consecutive games and the first player in the NFL since 2013 to throw for at least 280 yards and a touchdown in the first five games of the season. The last two of three quarterbacks to accomplish the same feat won MVP – Aaron Rodgers in 2011 and Peyton Manning in 2013. Bryce Young in rarified air pic.twitter.com/XvFmHHeSxW — PFF (@PFF) October 19, 2026 On that note, the Young-led offense has score 146 points so far this season. This is the highest total through 5 games in team history, surpassing the old record of 135 set by Cam Newton and the 2015 Panthers on route to an MVP season and SB 50. Tetairoa McMillan’s six receptions has him tied with Kelvin Benjamin as the second fastest player in team history to reach 100 career receptions. While not my favorite career-trajectory comparison, it is impressive nonetheless. Speaking of great stats with frightening names tied to them, Ryan Fitzgerald’s first field goal of the afternoon made him the first kicker since big-legged Joey Slye to make the first 10 attempts in a season. Also, yes, Slye did also miss two extra points in that time. Of course, there was also JJ Jansen setting the record for most games played by a long snapper in NFL history. Only another 100 more games to go until breaking the record for most games played in NFL history . J.J. Jansen is now the all-time leader in games played for a long snapper! (282 games) 👏 @Panthers | #KeepPounding pic.twitter.com/wzwXEvR0ZC — NFL+ (@NFLPlus) October 18, 2026 Of course, it can’t all be positive. The Panthers also set the team record for most penalty yardage given up in a single game. A worrying trend as the team has been near the top in penalties for the entire season and after a bye week they decided that wasn’t enough. The #Panthers have set a new franchise for penalty yards in a game (144). Previous high was 120 against the Bucs in Week 2 of 2003. — Mike Kaye (@mike_e_kaye) October 18, 2026 One last one to close out the fun. For the schadenfreude enjoyers: by beating the Eagles, the Panthers contributed to the NFC East being the first division in NFL history to have all their teams go winless in back-to-back weeks. NFC East made history, going two straight weeks without a win. https://t.co/xMtbduIJio — Adam Schefter (@AdamSchefter) October 20, 2026 It’s hard to ignore the positive vibes permeating the team and their performance. A history of disappointment is sure to keep a sliver of nagging doubt in the back of the mind, but when the team is making history – the good kind, not the tragic kind – it’s bound to get people excited. Let’s see how things play out when the Panthers take on the division rival Tampa Bay Buccaneers next week. Until then, keep pounding.

title: Carolina Panthers 2027 NFL Draft Prospect Profile: Jamari Johnson
summary: The 2027 NFL Draft feels like forever away, and we’re all caught up in the start of the NFL season. Regardless, it’s never too early to look ahead to the Draft. This weekly series will take a closer look at some of the prospects the Carolina Panthers could select in the 2027 iteration of the […]
full_text: LOS ANGELES, CALIFORNIA - SEPTEMBER 26: Tight end Jamari Johnson (9) of the Oregon Ducks makes a one handed catch of the football in action during a game between the Oregon Ducks and the USC Trojans at Los Angeles Memorial Coliseum on September 26, 2026 in Los Angeles, California. (Photo by Robin Alam/ISI Photos/ISI Photos via Getty Images) | ISI Photos via Getty Images The 2027 NFL Draft feels like forever away, and we’re all caught up in the start of the NFL season. Regardless, it’s never too early to look ahead to the Draft. This weekly series will take a closer look at some of the prospects the Carolina Panthers could select in the 2027 iteration of the Draft. In this series, we’ll only be looking at prospects the Panthers could seriously consider. This week our profile will focus on Oregon Ducks tight end Jamari Johnson. Bio Johnson (6’5”, 257 lbs.) was originally a high school quarterback who showed the versatility to play other positions, including receiver, running back, and defensive end. A fairly highly touted four star recruit, he originally joined the Louisville Cardinals for a couple years before transferring to Oregon. Despite sharing the spotlight with fellow tight end and eventual first round pick Kenyon Sadiq, Johnson managed to put up some solid numbers while providing good run blocking as an inline and slot option. He missed a couple games due to injury so far this season, but has still managed 17 catches for 224 yards and a couple scores in just four games played for the Ducks. Strengths/Weaknesses Johnson has elite size and enough athleticism to be a problem in the passing game. He has the speed and wiggle to average 16 yards per catch in 2025, making him one of the best downfield threats at tight end in the Draft. He is a willing and able run blocker and even showed reliability as a pass protector when called upon. Johnson has some versatility, lining up inline or flexed and consistently moving around the offense. While he does give good effort in the run blocking game, Johnson doesn’t get a whole lot of push. He’s mostly able to hold his ground, but he’ll need to improve his strength and technique at the point of attack in order to be a true three down, inline tight end at the next level. Johnson also benefits from Oregon’s offensive scheme, with almost none of his targets being classified as “contested” or “in traffic.” NFL defenders are able to make those windows smaller, so he’ll have to show he can make those types of plays with defenders in his personal space. Projection Jamari Johnson has the size, speed, and catch radius to be a problem over the middle of the field, especially in the intermediate and deep ranges. He’s not especially twitchy, but manages to get open and is a massive target. His blocking needs to improve, and his route tree is a bit limited, but the potential for a three down move tight end is definitely there. The Carolina Panthers have truly run a tight end by committee so far this season, with both Darren Waller and Tommy Tremble notching multi touchdown games. With Waller being on a one year deal and turning 34 last month, the Panthers could look to add to that room with another massive weapon for Bryce Young to target over the middle and in the redzone. Right now, Johnson is seen as a late first/early second round prospect by most outlets, though he could obviously shoot up boards with some big games and a good showing at the Combine in February. What do you think, Panthers fans? If Jamari Johnson is available when the Panthers select in the 2027 NFL Draft, should they take him? Sound off in the comments!
author: Daniel Belton

title: Hot Take Tuesday: Chicago Bears’ Offense is Real, and it’s Spectacular
summary: Week one already feels like a long time ago. You remember it, right? When the Chicago Bears dropped 59 points on the Carolina Panthers and made a statement to the league that they were for real. And then, Caleb Williams got hurt in the slop bowl, and the Bears have just kind of slipped into […]
full_text: ATLANTA, GEORGIA - OCTOBER 18: Caleb Williams #18 of the Chicago Bears celebrates a touchdown against the Atlanta Falcons during the first quarter of the game at Mercedes-Benz Stadium on October 18, 2026 in Atlanta, Georgia. (Photo by Kevin C. Cox/Getty Images) | Getty Images Week one already feels like a long time ago. You remember it, right? When the Chicago Bears dropped 59 points on the Carolina Panthers and made a statement to the league that they were for real. And then, Caleb Williams got hurt in the slop bowl, and the Bears have just kind of slipped into the mix of other really good football teams but not uniquely great ones that deserve extra attention from fans and the media. A 31- 23 win over the Atlanta Falcons may not seem like a statement win, but it certainly showed that the Bears, with Caleb Williams back, are indeed that team you don’t want to cross. When Caleb Williams plays, they are simply a different team. They go from a good team to a great team. They go from a team that can make the playoffs to a team that can make some noise in the playoffs. In weeks 1 and 6, when Caleb Williams is healthy and plays a full game in good conditions, the Chicago Bears average 45 points per game. In the games without him (not even including the Minnesota game), they average 19 points per game. Think about that. The Bears are averaging a 26-point differential with or without Caleb Williams. Packers fans and other critics still want to criticize Caleb Williams. That’s getting tougher to do. If you set the qualifying number at 90 attempts so Caleb qualifies, he is currently first in completion percentage, third in QBR, 9th in yards per attempt, sixth in success rate, and 1st in completion percentage over expected. He’s 5th in EPA per play and 7th in adjusted EPA per play. When you look at the numbers, there’s no question: Caleb Williams is one of the top 10 QBs in the league. The question at this point is: will he be a top 5 QB by the end of the year? Some of us (myself included) may have bought into Ben Johnson’s wizardry a bit too much. We thought perhaps his offense was still good enough to beat the Green Bay Packers with Tyson Bagent. But I (and many others) learned our lesson. Ben Johnson is elite. Caleb Williams is elite. But Ben Johnson needs Caleb Williams and Caleb Williams needs Ben Johnson. Tom Brady had Bill Belichick. Drew Brees had Sean Payton. Brett Favre had Mike Holmgren. John Elway had Mike Shanahan. Dan Marino had Don Shula. The list goes on and on. You can go back to the early parts of the league. Sid Luckman had George Halas, Otto Graham had Paul Brown, Bart Starr had Vince Lombardi, and so on, and so on. A great coach and a great QB need each other to become legends. The Bears have the combo. Now the only question is, will they eventually become legends? It’s way too early to say, but the early returns certainly look promising. We are starting to see the vision for winning this year: control the clock and choke the life out of the opponent. Ben Johnson is approaching these games like a boa constrictor. In the Bears’ victories, they are averaging a whopping 38:30 in time of possession. Even in their two losses, they still held the ball more than their opponent at 31:10. The Bears want to run the ball, keep the clock moving, and keep their defense off the field. That’s going to give the opponents less chance to exploit the more questionable unit and keep them fresh and ready to attack the opposing offenses as well. At this point, the Bears offense isn’t going to set any NFL records because of those games that Caleb Williams missed, but they can still absolutely become the highest-scoring team in Chicago Bears history, and they can still absolutely be the best offense in the NFL. The Bears’ 2026 season is going to go by how this offense goes. And as far as I can tell, with Caleb Williams back, the Bears offense is real, and it’s spectacular.

title: Chicago Bears week 7 power rankings roundup
summary: The season is rolling on, and the good and the bad teams are separating themselves. For the Chicago Bears, it was great to get Caleb Williams and Kyler Gordon back. Who knew difference-making players impact games? The Bears have a quick turnaround — facing the New England Patriots at Soldier Field Thursday. The Patriots themselves […]
full_text: ATLANTA, GEORGIA - OCTOBER 18: Caleb Williams #18 and D'Andre Swift #4 of the Chicago Bears celebrate a touchdown against the Atlanta Falcons during the second quarter of the game at Mercedes-Benz Stadium on October 18, 2026 in Atlanta, Georgia. (Photo by Kevin C. Cox/Getty Images) | Getty Images The season is rolling on, and the good and the bad teams are separating themselves. For the Chicago Bears , it was great to get Caleb Williams and Kyler Gordon back. Who knew difference-making players impact games? The Bears have a quick turnaround — facing the New England Patriots at Soldier Field Thursday. The Patriots themselves have bounced back from a slow start to start to the season and find themselves moving up the rankings too. Let’s dive into this week’s rankings. WCG – Aaron Leming 10. Chicago Bears (4-2) Trending: Up (Caleb Williams is back) Chicago is now 2-1 with Caleb Williams as their starting quarterback, and 2-1 with their backups. Some might look at that as an indictment of Williams, but a deeper dive into the offensive numbers tells a much different story. Assuming he can stay healthy, the primary concern will be the defense. They’ve been about as Jekyll and Hyde as it gets through six weeks. The talent is there, but the consistency has lacked. The Athletic – Chad Graff and Josh Kendall 8. Chicago Bears (4-2) Last week: 11 Sunday: Beat Falcons 31-23 Fantasy focus: Luther Burden No team has had a more frustrating group of pass catchers for fantasy managers than the Bears. There was preseason optimism about tight end Colston Loveland and wide receivers Rome Odunze and Luther Burden, but none ranks higher at the moment than Burden, who is 77th in fantasy points per game (12.2). The good news is Caleb Williams is back, and Burden had eight catches for 95 yards on Sunday. NFL.com – Nick Shook 11. Chicago Bears (13) Caleb Williams was stellar in his return to the offense, opening up everything that was trapped behind padlocks in Green Bay. With the Iceman at the controls, everyone ate: Colston Loveland caught a touchdown pass, D’Andre Swift scored twice, Roschon Johnson bullied his way into the end zone, and the Bears could not be denied. That said, they need to clean up their penalties (12 for 133 yards on Sunday) and finish games more comfortably than they did in Atlanta. Pro Football Talk – Mike Florio Bears (No. 15; 4-2): A franchise quarterback makes all the difference. CBS Sports – Pete Prisco 13. Chicago Bears (15) Bouncing back from the loss to the Packers by winning on the road at Atlanta is a good look for this team. Of course it helps to have Caleb Williams back. ESPN NFL Nation – Courtney Cronin 9. Chicago Bears (4-2) Week 6 result: Beat the Falcons 31-23 Week 6 ranking: 13 Biggest issue on offense: Penalties Quarterback Caleb Williams being back under center alleviates a lot of the issues the Bears struggled with in his absence, such as red zone execution, third-down efficiency and their downfield passing attack. One area that can stand to be cleaned up more is offensive penalties, which accounted for seven of the Bears’ infractions Sunday. Those offensive penalties helped generate Chicago’s most penalty yardage in a game since 2016 (133). The Bears are tied for the third-most offensive holding penalties (10). That’s an area they’ll want to fix so it doesn’t derail drives. — Courtney Cronin Yahoo Sports – Frank Schwab 6. Chicago Bears (4-2, LW: 8) The 31-23 win over the Falcons wasn’t really that close. The Bears let down in the fourth quarter, turning a 31-7 lead into a one-score game. That’s not ideal but the way they played through three quarters in Caleb Williams’ return was impressive. Cornerback Kyler Gordon’s odd 2026 took a positive turn. Gordon had missed the offseason and the first five games due to a calf injury, prompting questions about his future with the team. In just 17 snaps on Sunday, Gordon had three sacks and two forced fumbles. He’s the first Bears defensive back with three sacks in a game since Todd Bell in 1983. He’s just the second defensive back in NFL history with three sacks and two forced fumbles in a game, joining Rod Kush of the Houston Oilers in 1985, according to the Bears’ site. His playmaking will be welcomed on the Bears’ defense. What do you think of the Bears’ rankings this week? Fair or no?
author: Sam Householder

title: 10 Thoughts on the NFL: Eagles failed Jalen Hurts, Travis Hunter Emerges, Bad QBs, and more
summary: 1. Even if this story wasn’t personal for you—and it unfortunately is for me—you should be infuriated with the Philadelphia Eagles for allowing Jalen Hurts to risk his life for a football game in London two weekends ago. They reportedly flew him to London with a superficial clot in his left calf, then kept him […]
full_text: London, United Kingdom - October 11: Jalen Hurts of Philadelphia Eagles looks on during the NFL match between Philadelphia Eagles and Jacksonville Jaguars at Tottenham Hotspur Stadium on October 11, 2026 in London, United Kingdom. (Photo by Vince Mignott/DeFodi Images/DeFodi via Getty Images) | DeFodi Images via Getty Images 1. Even if this story wasn’t personal for you—and it unfortunately is for me—you should be infuriated with the Philadelphia Eagles for allowing Jalen Hurts to risk his life for a football game in London two weekends ago. They reportedly flew him to London with a superficial clot in his left calf, then kept him awake for 36 hours for fear of the clot traveling to his lungs and potentially killing him, then allowed him to play a football game in which hard contact to his leg could’ve dislodged that clot and killed him anyway. Whether a doctor works for a football team or not shouldn’t matter. The oath says, “Do no harm.” That sometimes means making those hyper-competitive humans take a seat for their own well-being. They’re lucky their decision to green-light him to play only cost Hurts’ season, maybe his career, rather than his life. Regardless, someone needs to be held accountable for this. 2. Passing charts have turned into the new box-score watching for quarterback evaluation, and Caleb Williams’ game on Sunday is just the latest example. Except that, even if you didn’t watch the game, you should be able to see the difference between Williams going 30-for-26 for 305 yards and a touchdown versus Bo Nix barely topping 107 yards on 27 throws, right? There are multiple ways to have a really good game as an NFL quarterback. Taking risks and throwing the ball into tight windows down the field—something Williams has proven time and again he can do—is one way. Taking what the opposing defense gives you when they’re clearly trying to take away the deep part of the field, which is what Williams did yesterday, is another. The bottom line: if you don’t like a guy and want to see him fail, just say so. Don’t pretend to be objective. In the end, you’re mad that Williams now leads the league in completion percentage, which means you can’t use that argument against him to defend your fav. Cry more. 3. Personally, I have no problem with what Ryan Fitzpatrick said about Nix after the Broncos quarterback’s Thursday night performance in an overtime win against Seattle. And sure, maybe it is a little biased because I never thought highly of Nix coming into the league, plus he might still be rounding into form after the injury he suffered last year. But pretending he’s doing anything else but playing objectively terrible football is just wrong right now. If this were any other third-year quarterback averaging 174 passing yards a game, we would say that guy isn’t an NFL starter, record be damned. Why should Nix get a pass? 4. Y’all might find this mean, but I don’t care: L.J. Collier celebrating after recovering a fumble and getting tackled on that Rams two-point conversion attempt makes me mad. You cost your team two points because you wouldn’t give the ball up to a faster player who would’ve scored, and you’re happy about it? Someone lower his Madden Awareness rating to -2. That man’s lucky those two points didn’t come back to bite his team. 5. Remember back when Chris Ballard and Ryan Pace were both up for the Chicago Bears general manager job all those years ago? Wild to see Ballard finally out in Indianapolis after all that time, with the Colts just relieving him of his duties after their latest loss. This isn’t to disparage either of those two or Pace’s successor, Ryan Poles, but to point out the truth in something Ballard pointed out after Andrew Luck’s retirement: hitting on the quarterback is everything. Pace failed at it with both Mitchell Trubisky and Justin Fields. Ballard struggled to replace Luck but ultimately squeezed enough out of veterans to keep him employed until this year. And Poles arguably would’ve been fired already if not for landing Caleb Williams, which has helped people forget his misses at other positions. Remember that. 6. Thanks to the aforementioned Colts, there will be no 0-17 season this year. And I really do mean “Thanks to the Colts,” because the Tennessee Titans’ offense putting up 26 points on 186 yards of total offense is just offensive. Cam Ward’s 102 passing yards marked the fewest this season for a winning starting quarterback who played the entire game. There’s so much wrong with that team that it’s hard sometimes to parse between Ward being bad and everything else around him being awful. At least they know they’re not about to make the wrong kind of history. 7. In other news: maybe Ben Johnson and the Bears offense really are that good (when healthy). Remember that 59-point outing they put on the Carolina Panthers in Week 1 that had us all questioning what planet we were living on? Turns out Carolina has literally been one of the best units in the league since that point, holding opponents to just 16 points per game following that season opener. The NFL can change so dramatically from week to week that any one game can’t be taken as a complete picture of what a team is. For example, that next week against the Vikings on a rainy day, the Bears looked disgustingly bad. But who doesn’t want to believe the Bears could just randomly drop 60 on any defense they choose? 9. Count me among the people who questioned whether Travis Hunter could legitimately be a factor as a cornerback and wide receiver after starring in both roles at the University of Colorado a few years ago. As it turns out…he can. And is. According to NFL Communications, Hunter is the third player since 1970 with a touchdown reception and interception in the same game, joining Pro Football Hall of Famer Brian Dawkins (Sept. 29, 2002 with Philadelphia) and Roy Green (Sept. 20, 1981 with the St. Louis Cardinals). Shoutout to Liam Coen for having the gumption to actually use him in both roles and being creative enough to pull it off. What a player. 10. Question for the group: when’s the last time you saw a player fall off harder than Justin Herbert? And no, you don’t get to say “he was always bad,” because he wasn’t. Nothing approaching this, certainly. I’m having a hard time thinking of anyone. But we don’t have to ask that question about coaching falloffs, because Jim Harbaugh does it every four years. His flamout just arrived a year early this time.
author: Khari Thompson

title: Chicago’s best things to do, see, and eat before heading to a Bears game
summary: The Windy City, Chi-Town, the Second City, the City of Big Shoulders, the Chi — no matter what you call it, Chicago is one of the world’s greatest cities, and any trip to watch the Chicago Bears play at Soldier Field deserves that you at least make a long weekend of it. Come in early […]
full_text: Photo by Joseph Weiser/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The Windy City, Chi-Town, the Second City, the City of Big Shoulders, the Chi — no matter what you call it, Chicago is one of the world’s greatest cities, and any trip to watch the Chicago Bears play at Soldier Field deserves that you at least make a long weekend of it. Come in early or stay late and take in some of the attractions and dining experiences that are unique to Chicago. Places to stay in Chicago There are several places to stay in the Chicagoland area, but if you want to be in the city, here are a few to consider. The Marriott Marquis is connected to McCormick Place and is minutes from Soldier Field. It may also be a good place to stay if you want to bump into some players. Hilton Garden Inn Chicago Central Loop is just a few miles from Soldier Field. The Blackstone Hotel is just a 20-minute walk to Soldier Field. The JW Marriott is in the Loop and near plenty of fun things to do. The Westin Chicago River North is, you guessed it, near the Chicago Riverwalk, and it’s also a few blocks from the Chicago Theatre District and next to the House of Blues. Soldier Field has a hotel guide if you want even more information. Things to do in Chicago The aforementioned House of Blues is more than just the Blues, so go catch a show, music, or some comedy. The Chicago Theater District has plenty of entertainment options, but plan ahead when you get your Bears tickets so you don’t miss showtimes. Do some vintage shopping on Milwaukee Ave. in Wicker Park, or take some photos at Promontory Point. The Bean is one of Chicago’s iconic tourist sights, and a trip to the Fulton Market District offers something for everyone, with shops, restaurants, and nightlife. Take a Lake Michigan or Chicago River tour to learn more about the city and its architecture, and a visit to Navy Pier is always a fun time. The NFL season overlaps with other major professional sports leagues, so time your trip to see the Cubs, White Sox, Bulls, Blackhawks, or Sky. The Northwestern Wildcats in nearby Evanston also just opened a new football stadium. Best places to eat in Chicago No trip to Chicago is complete without a classic Chicago hot dog or a deep-dish pizza, but I also highly recommend an Italian Beef and a Maxwell Street Polish Sausage. Chicago is known for its steakhouses, and Asador Bastian in River North is one of the best. If you truly want to treat yourself, make a reservation at the 2025 Best Steak Restaurant in North America. The Armitage Alehouse is a leveled-up traditional neighborhood pub located in Lincoln Park, but you’ll swear you were in London circa 1926. MCCB (Modern Chinese Cook Book) offers its take on authentic dishes in its own creative way. If you want some sass with your hot dog, then you can’t miss the experience at the Weiners Circle . If thin-crust pizza is more your speed, Vito & Nick’s has one of the best. Whatever cuisine you like, Chicago has you covered. Soldier Field parking, rideshare, and transit options There are plenty of options for getting to Soldier Field, but public transportation and/or rideshare is the best way to go. Some parking lots offer a shuttle service, while others require a walk to the stadium. On that walk, be sure to start a Green Bay Sucks chant, but don’t bring alcohol with you. More info on parking and transportation options can be found here . Tailgating at Soldier Field Tailgating is allowed before and after the game, but you must follow specific guidelines. Bring your own setup or hang out at one of several hosted tailgates. More info on tailgating can be found here . The Soldier Field Experience Soldier Field is dedicated to the men and women of the armed services, so be sure to take in all the monuments around the stadium. You can also book a behind-the-scenes tour of Soldier Field. Every out-of-towner must take a trip up to the West Loop, grab a burger at Au Cheval or The Loyalist , and take a picture in front of the Caleb Williams mural on Halsted. Check the Bears’ website for policies and procedures, the latest on parking, and, as always, give yourself plenty of time to get to your seats before kickoff.

title: Stock up, stock down: Chicago Bears-Atlanta Falcons review
summary: It’s good to be back on the winning side. The Chicago Bears took care of business in Atlanta and must quickly pivot to their Thursday Night Football game. The Bears dominated most of the game against Atlanta, save for a couple of drives by the backups in the fourth quarter. It was a fun game […]
full_text: CINCINNATI, OH - AUGUST 22: Chicago Bears punter Tory Taylor (19) punts the ball during the preseason game between the Chicago Bears and the Cincinnati Bengals at Paycor Stadium on August 22, 2026 in Cincinnati, OH. (Photo by Ian Johnson/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images It’s good to be back on the winning side. The Chicago Bears took care of business in Atlanta and must quickly pivot to their Thursday Night Football game. The Bears dominated most of the game against Atlanta, save for a couple of drives by the backups in the fourth quarter. It was a fun game on both sides of the ball and with the return of star players, it should make for a good review. Let’s get into it. Stock up Kyler Gordon, DB – How many of us wrote off Gordon after the summer of zero updates or participation? I know I thought it was a lost cause. Fans and media questioned his motivation after he got paid, compared him to Nate Davis, and openly debated whether we would ever play for the Bears again. It’s fair to say he shut up a lot of those voices Sunday. Three sacks, two forced fumbles, three tackles-for-loss and two QB hits. Spider-Man is a menace and he was incredible for the defense. I hope he stays healthy and can continue to contribute like this. Caleb Williams, QB – The offense looks so different with the QB1. Williams controlled the operation with precision from the first play. 83.3 percent completion percentage. 305 yards. One touchdown. It was a performance that made you simultaneously glad he was back, while also making you sad or mad for what we missed without him. Tory Taylor, P – Taking a punter in the fourth round is always unpopular. Tory Taylor can’t help where he was drafted. It put a lot of pressure on him. And honestly, the performance has been inconsistent most of his first two seasons. But I think it’s fair to say he’s finally turned a corner. Drawing muffed punts isn’t a stat, but Taylor is very good at it. He’s become a legitimate weapon on special teams and not just for his so-called banana balls. He’s finding consistency pinning opponents deep and using a lot of different types of punts to give opponents fits. Stock down Garrett Bradbury, C – Bradbury did not have a great game against Atlanta’s defensive line. He gave up a lot of inside pressure. He’s been solid, if unspectacular this season, but this was really the first game since the Vikings where he struggled. Cairo Santos, K – After a miss Sunday, Santos is now 1-for-3 on his last three kicks. Not a huge sample size, but he’s only at 72.7 percent field goal percentage this season. Is kicker a concern or is this just a blip? Hopefully the latter. Jahdae Walker, WR – Jahdae is becoming a core special teams player. He is also a willing blocker with a nice role on offense. He played fairly well on Sunday, but his two penalties were costly. He was called for roughing the kicker, allowing the Falcons to continue a drive. Later, he lost his cool and ended up getting ejected. It doesn’t seem like this is going to be an ongoing issue for Walker, more of a learning moment- but he deserves to get docked for the week. Who is up and down in your world this week? Let me know in the comments.

title: NFL Week 7 Power Rankings: Teams Trending Up or Down?
summary: With the conclusion of Week 6, we are inching closer and closer to the midway point of the season. While the league’s elite and bottom-feeders have started to identify themselves, there’s still plenty to be learned in the coming weeks and months about how the NFL’s playoff picture will start to take shape. With six […]
full_text: SANTA CLARA, CALIFORNIA - OCTOBER 19: Christian McCaffrey #23 of the San Francisco 49ers celebrates after scoring a touchdown against the Washington Commanders during the second quarter of the game at Levi's Stadium on October 19, 2026 in Santa Clara, California. (Photo by Thearon W. Henderson/Getty Images) | Getty Images With the conclusion of Week 6, we are inching closer and closer to the midway point of the season. While the league’s elite and bottom-feeders have started to identify themselves, there’s still plenty to be learned in the coming weeks and months about how the NFL’s playoff picture will start to take shape. With six weeks in the books, it’s time to take a stock-watch approach to each team’s season so far and see how it’s trending against preseason expectations—and more in our Week 7 installment of WCG NFL Power Rankings. 1. San Francisco 49ers (6-0) Trending: Up Whew, what a game on Monday night, huh? The only thing stopping some from fully buying into this team is their rash of injuries that just won’t stop. That said, they’ve kept winning, and usually have done so convincingly. This is a very well-rounded team, albeit one of the oldest rosters in the league. With a three-game lead in the division, it’s hard to imagine a scenario where the 49ers aren’t at least in the NFC Championship game, barring a major step back. 2. Kansas City Chiefs (5-0) Trending: Up Six weeks and five games in, it’s safe to say t025 was the outlier and the Chiefs’ window hasn’t closed. While many expected a bounce-back, few saw a perfect 5-0 start coming. Quarterback Patrick Mahomes has looked good coming off a torn ACL, and running back Kenneth Walker has been a game-changer. With the Raiders fading and the Broncos’ offensive issues, the AFC West looks like theirs for the taking. 3. Buffalo Bills (5-1) Trending: Up It hasn’t always been pretty, and there are still plenty of questions remaining on the defensive side of the ball, but the Bills continue to find ways to win games. Even though the Patriots have rebounded from a slow start, the Bills look like the perennial contender that they are, especially if they can get the defense playing at a higher level. One thing is for sure: having an MVP-caliber quarterback in Josh Allen helps, and he continues to make mind-boggling plays for his team each week. 4. Minnesota Vikings (5-0) Trending: Up No matter how the offense has performed to this point, a 5-0 start is about as much of a dream come true as anything Vikings fans could have asked for. Their defense under Brian Flores continues to play at an elite level. If they can become more productive and consistent offensively, this will be a very dangerous team. Their schedule is about to tighten up, so we’ll see how “for real” their undefeated start proves to be. 5. New England Patriots (4-2) Trending: Up At 1-2 and Drake Maye struggling, it must have felt like the sky was falling in New England. A three-game winning streak later, and the Patriots are just one game out of first place heading into a Thursday night showdown in Chicago. The talent is there, but health has been an issue. We’ll see if they can keep building on their current streak or come back down to earth in the coming weeks. 6. Jacksonville Jaguars (4-2) Trending: Up Overall, the Jaguars have been one of the league’s more impressive teams. That said, they tend to play down to their competition, which has led to a few tight games. The talent is there, even if the defense isn’t as good as they showed last year. Quarterback Trevor Lawrence has picked up where they left off, but it’s hard not to feel like they blew an opportunity to really run away with the NFC South on Sunday in London. 7. Green Bay Packers (4-2) Trending: Up After a shaky 1-2 start, the Packers have found their stride over the past two weeks, dominating both the Bears and Cowboys at home. Their schedule tightens with matchups against the Lions, Panthers, Patriots, Vikings, and Rams over the next six weeks. If they continue to play as they have, there’s reason to believe they’ll come out of that stretch with a winning record. 8. Detroit Lions (3-2) Trending: Up (if they can figure out their defense) There’s no questioning the offense at this point, but will the return of Brian Branch be enough to get their defense back on the right track? The NFC North is a gauntlet, and Detroit is the only team that hasn’t played a divisional game yet. That changes over the next two weeks with games against the Packers and Vikings. Their matchup against Green Bay will challenge this defense. We’ll see how they respond. 9. Baltimore Ravens (4-2) Trending: (Slightly) Up The Ravens are an odd team to track. On paper, they should be much more dominant than they are, but because of an injury to quarterback Lamar Jackson and their defensive inconsistencies, they’ve produced an up-and-down product so far. On paper, they are the best team in the AFC North. So far, they haven’t consistently played like it. Once Jackson is back, I expect them to round into form. 10. Chicago Bears (4-2) Trending : Up (Caleb Williams is back) Chicago is now 2-1 with Caleb Williams as their starting quarterback, and 2-1 with their backups. Some might look at that as an indictment of Williams, but a deeper dive into the offensive numbers tells a much different story. Assuming he can stay healthy, the primary concern will be the defense. They’ve been about as Jekyll and Hyde as it gets through six weeks. The talent is there, but the consistency has lacked. 11. Cincinnati Bengals (3-2) Trending : Up (With some questions) The defense is clearly improved, and their two losses were against a pair of 4-2 teams. The issue is that their wins have come against teams with a combined 3-14 record. The talent is there, but so far, the weekly consistency hasn’t been. The Bengals remain one of the league’s more intriguing teams. 12. Seattle Seahawks (3-3) Trending : Down Coming into the season, Seattle was one of the more overlooked Super Bowl winners in recent history. Despite a strong start to the season, quarterback Sam Darnold has been turning the ball over at a highly concerning rate. The defense also hasn’t been nearly as dominant. It’s clear they miss running back Kenneth Walker, but the offense needs to figure it out soon if they plan to keep pace with San Francisco in the NFC West. 13. Denver Broncos (4-2) Trending : Teetering (without better QB play) The Broncos were a Bo Nix injury away from making it to the Super Bowl and at least being competitive. That feels weird to say, especially given how this season has started, but the offense has been an issue in almost all six of their games. It starts with quarterback play, but the run game has left a lot to be desired. It’s quite remarkable that they’ve been able to win four games playing like this, but it goes to show just how well-rounded this roster is. If Nix can figure it out, they might ultimately be the favorites in the AFC. 14. Cleveland Browns (4-2) Trending : Up (The league’s biggest surprise… So far) As usual, a few teams are surprises, and a few weeks ago, my vote would have been for the Raiders. That said, the Browns defense has continued to play at a high level without Myles Garrett, and their offense is doing just enough to win them games. No matter how the season ends, sitting at 4-2 and in first place is an outstanding start to the Todd Monken era. 15. Pittsburgh Steelers (4-2) Trending : Up (Somehow) Even without Mike Tomlin, this team feels eerily similar to the last 10 Steelers teams we’ve seen. Quarterback Aaron Rodgers continues to hang around and play well enough, and overall, they are getting enough from their aging roster to have a winning record. That said, I’m just not convinced this lasts over 17 games. We’ll see if they can last. 16. Carolina Panthers (3-2) Trending : Up Is Bryce Young a legitimate MVP candidate? It sure feels like it. In a weak NFC South, the Panthers are set up well to repeat. Really, the…

title: 3 Reasons Why the Chicago Bears Won vs. the Falcons
summary: The Chicago Bears traveled to Atlanta this week to take on the Falcons and imposed their will from start to finish. Here are my top three reasons Chicago won the game. Let’s get to it! 1. Competitive Fire Call it competitive fire, juice, edge, ‘want-to,’ whatever works for you. From the opening kickoff through the […]
full_text: ATLANTA, GA - OCTOBER 18: Chicago cornerback Kyler Gordon (6) reacts during the NFL game between the Chicago Bears and the Atlanta Falcons on October 18th, 2026 at Mercedes-Benz Stadium in Atlanta, GA. (Photo by Rich von Biberstein/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The Chicago Bears traveled to Atlanta this week to take on the Falcons and imposed their will from start to finish. Here are my top three reasons Chicago won the game. Let’s get to it! 1. Competitive Fire Call it competitive fire, juice, edge, ‘want-to,’ whatever works for you. From the opening kickoff through the closing seconds, the Chicago Bears simply wanted this game more than Atlanta. Despite what many people realize, that matters even at this level. Chicago came out to play in this one, and you could tell it meant something to them in all three phases. I’d be remiss not to mention the masses of Bears fans that traveled to Atlanta for this one too. From the kickoff teams blowing up ball carriers, to the punt team perfectly executing some “Banana Balls” to Caleb Williams igniting the offense on the field or defense on the sidelines, these Bears were going to go down swinging. An encouraging sign after last week’s defeat at Lambeau. Zavier Scott looks like an absolute keeper on this team, and his juice on special teams stands out. Daniel Hardy had himself a game both in the third phase AND on Defense with Montez Sweat out. Noah Sewell made his presence felt as well and the contrast between what Kalif Raymond brings to what his predecessor Olamide Zacchaeus brought is night and day – and that’s only the reserve players! When you have your stars putting forth that same selfless effort to win games (spoiler alert – like the two guys listed below) then you have a fighters chance every week. And when your stars are as talented as they are in Chicago, good things can happen. REALLY good things. I might even call them super. 2. Iceman Caleb heard all the noise, yes. But in my opinion, his biggest motivating factor is and has always been winning ball games as starting quarterback and leading his team to new heights. Well, he made quite the impression Sunday, completing over 80% of his passes with zero turnovers and 1 TD pass, in addition to a career-best mark for consecutive completions with 12 straight complete throws. And that doesn’t count the multiple throw aways he had either. Caleb was on fire. When he is healthy and playing like that, this offense will be hard to stop. Remember, Chicago didn’t even have their RB1B in Kyle Monangai this week either. I said it on Bears Over Beers last week that I hoped he learned from Case Keenum how explosive this offense can be even without him playing Superman in the pocket and not only did he allude to it leading up to this game, but it showed on the field. Chicago has playmakers at each position. All he has to do is get it to them. On Sunday, he did just that with EIGHT players securing at least 2 catches. Caleb is back, people. Cannot wait to see him at home this week against last year’s MVP runner-up and fellow 2024 rookie classman, Drake Maye. Expect fireworks. 3. Spidey Not to be outdone by the epic return of Caleb Williams AKA Iceman, Kyler Gordon AKA “Spider Man” or “Spidey” had arguably the most impressive performance of the afternoon. Easing back into full-time action this week, Spidey played only 16 defensive snaps. In those snaps, he accumulated 4 tackles, 3 sacks, 3 tackles for a loss, 2 forced fumbles, and 2 QB hits. Spider Man is an absolute terror for opposing offenses, and we didn’t really even get to see him in coverage, where he is equally as dangerous. After all he’s been through with the public outcry over missing so much action and reports of tension in the locker room, it was huge to see his performance this week and earn himself a game ball from Ben Johnson postgame. With the struggles this defense has had to start the season, particularly in the secondary, Gordon’s return couldn’t have come at a better time as Chicago has the Patriots, Seahawks, and Buccaneers before the Week 10 BYE – and ALL in Primetime. What about you? What stood out most in your mind when watching The Beloved come away with the win?

title: Bengals News: Zac Taylor Hot Seat Watch
summary: The Cincinnati Bengals are coming out of their Week 6 bye and are set to travel to Baltimore for their second division game of the 2026 season. They’re 3-2, but they’ve been a mixed bag so far. The offense, despite the star power, has struggled with consistency. The defense has shown progress in some ways, […]
full_text: The Cincinnati Bengals are coming out of their Week 6 bye and are set to travel to Baltimore for their second division game of the 2026 season. They’re 3-2, but they’ve been a mixed bag so far. The offense, despite the star power, has struggled with consistency. The defense has shown progress in some ways, but they haven’t shown themselves to be among the league’s top-ranked units. After three straight seasons of missing the playoffs following two consecutive trips to the AFC Championship and one Super Bowl appearance, head coach Zac Taylor’s leash may finally be starting to get tight. With the Bengals still very much in the mix in the division, it’s too early to say Taylor could be on his way out, but some think the process could be accelerated with a bad showing against the Ravens . The Bengals under Taylor have been notoriously slow starters. The offense, with Ja’Marr Chase and Tee Higgins, has looked mediocre at times, and the defense, after a good start, has struggled over the last couple weeks. Burrow and the weapons around him have a finite amount of time in the league to win a championship, and they can’t afford to waste any more time. This weekend could tell us a lot about what happens next. Here’s what else is going on: Bengals Get Encouraging Injury News on Key Playmaker Ahead of Ravens Game “He’s looked as good as he’s looked in a long time,” Taylor said. “I think last week he had a good week on what he could handle from a rehab perspective. So this week to get him back involved, he looked good running around today. I think it’s good to finally get him back and feel like he’s closer to 100% health.” Bengals Urged to Trade for 19-Sack Defender “I would say Yaya Diaby because you could extend him and make him a part of your d-line of the future,” said Liscow on why he is so high on the Bengals adding Diaby. “I think that would be one of the more expensive options on the list, especially when you factor in the extension required there. But pairing him with Dexter Lawrence and with Boy Mafe gives you three really good players on that defensive line to build around.” Bengals may have a green light to trade for Colts 3-time Pro Bowler after Chris Ballard’s firing, but an obstacle needs to be addressed There’s no question Taylor is the better tailback compared to Brown, and his production from this season is enough of an argument on its own. Taylor has 492 yards and seven touchdowns on 122 carries through six games. Over 80% of his yardage has come from under center concepts, and he’s averaging 4.4 yards per carry on those runs. He would be an obvious upgrade over Brown as the lead back in Cincinnati’s run game. The Bengals used their bye to look inward. Here’s what stood out “I think certainly we’ve had our moments in all three phases that you feel like this is who we’re going to be,” Taylor said. “And now it’s just putting the complete game together in all three phases.” Who Dey! title: 3 things we learned from the Bengals’ first 5 games
summary: After five games, the Cincinnati Bengals stand at a disappointing 3-2. The bye week couldn’t have come at a more perfect time. As Joe Burrow said, the team has to be better everywhere and avoid the little mistakes that cost them two games by a combined eight points. Here are three things we learned: 1. […]
full_text: MIAMI GARDENS, FLORIDA - OCTOBER 11: Ollie Gordon II #0 of the Miami Dolphins is tackled by Boye Mafe #53 of the Cincinnati Bengals during the fourth quarter at Hard Rock Stadium on October 11, 2026 in Miami Gardens, Florida. (Photo by Carmen Mandato/Getty Images) | Getty Images After five games, the Cincinnati Bengals stand at a disappointing 3-2. The bye week couldn’t have come at a more perfect time. As Joe Burrow said, the team has to be better everywhere and avoid the little mistakes that cost them two games by a combined eight points. Here are three things we learned: 1. The defense is improved, but they can’t stop the run Let’s be fair here. Last year, the Bengals had one of the worst defenses in the league, giving up 380.9 yards and 28.9 points a game. This year, they’re only giving up 21.8 points per game, good for 11th best. They’re also forcing a lot more turnovers, including four against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers. And they’re getting to opposing quarterbacks consistently, including 41 pressures against the Houston Texans. Boye Mafe and Jonathan Allen have been successful at generating pressure. NFL EDGE Production through 5 weeks There are 3 truly elite guys in the league right now. Boye Mafe has been a nice signing for the Bengals. pic.twitter.com/jno3VNX1Mp — Gridiron Grading (@GridironGrading) October 14, 2026 But the centerpiece (figuratively and literally) is Dexter Lawrence, who has exceeded the very high expectations that came with being traded for the 10th overall pick in the 2026 Draft. NFL iDL Production through 5 weeks Alim McNeill has quietly had a dominant start to the season. The Seahawks and Bengals have had the strongest duos in the league to this point. pic.twitter.com/sSVM9IMHuB — Gridiron Grading (@GridironGrading) October 15, 2026 Jonathan Allen and Dexter Lawrence in the same interior defensive line. Pack a lunch. It's going to be a long day. pic.twitter.com/fm2tvW4hgt — Doug Farrar ✍ (@NFL_DougFarrar) October 14, 2026 Thanks to Lawrence, the Bengals went from the NFL’s lowest run stuff rate in 2025 to the highest through Week 5 of this season. The problem is when runners get past Lawrence. Over the last three weeks, Cincinnati is allowing an average of 155.3 rushing yards per game. The result was back-to-back losses and a game against the Miami Dolphins that was closer than it should have been. If Lamar Jackson plays on Sunday, the Bengals’ run defense could be in for a long day. 2. Burrow and Chase are still holding up the offense The passing game is working, accounting for 260 yards per game (seventh in the NFL). Burrow has 11 touchdowns in five games, and he’s just warming up. Ja’Marr Chase suffered a concussion against the Jacksonville Jaguars, but he’s still making eye-popping plays when he’s on the field. Tee Higgins has been outstanding as well. And they even have an elite right tackle in Amarius Mims, who very rarely allows a QB pressure. The problem is twofold: those big passing plays are coming off incredible athleticism or playmaking from the receivers and Burrow. And the running game is not making things easier (outside the Miami game). Currently, the Bengals are 26th in the league at 82.8 rushing yards per game. Against the Jaguars, Burrow threw 54 times and made a costly mistake in the fourth quarter. That’s what happens when you become too one-dimensional in the NFL. Then Samaje Perine got more involved against the Dolphins, and the run game turned around. Samaje Perine vs. Miami 14 carries for 68 yards (4.9 YPC) 2 catches for 10 yards and a TD 1 magnificent beard pic.twitter.com/DESX3nT5WB — Bengals & Brews (@BengalsBrews) October 13, 2026 It’s not clear if the 31-year-old veteran running back can continue getting double digit carries or not. But that game did show that Cincinnati needs a bigger, more traditional runner to lead the rush attack instead of Chase Brown. (I am very much in favor of trading for Jonathan Taylor, for what it’s worth.) 3. The Bengals’ biggest opponent has been themselves The two losses this year were completely avoidable. The game in Pittsburgh was largely decided by two special teams disasters. And against Jacksonville, Burrow made a shockingly bad read that took the Bengals out of scoring position and set the Jaguars up for a touchdown in the fourth quarter. Additionally, Cincinnati had some sloppy plays against Miami, including two personal fouls, a foul on a field goal (that then turned into a touchdown), two red zone fumbles, and a kickoff caught at the 4-yard-line. The bye week is the perfect time to take a deep breath, reevaluate, and get your focus back if you’re Zac Taylor and the Bengals. Once they’ve done that, they’ll have to prepare for Derrick Henry and the Ravens. We previewed that game with HOF Bengals coach Jim McNally and Ravens YouTuber Engraven in the video below.

full_text: The Cincinnati Bengals announced Tuesday that they signed safety Russ Yeast from the practice squad to the active roster. In addition, the team released safety Isaiah Nwokobia from the practice squad. Finally, the Bengals signed linebacker Emany Johnson and tight end Josh Kattus to the practice squad. Yeast, a third-year player, was elevated from the practice squad to the active roster for two games this season and has recorded three tackles. Nwokobia, an undrafted rookie from SMU, signed to Cincinnati’s practice squad on Sept. 29 and spent the past two games there. Kattus, an undrafted rookie out of the University of Kentucky, was originally a college free agent signee of the Bengals in May and spent the offseason and training camp with Cincinnati. He was waived by the Bengals on Aug. 30 and was not with a team for the first six weeks of the regular season. Johnson, a first-year player out of the University of Nevada, was signed by Dallas as a college free agent in 2024. He spent his rookie season on the practice squads of the Cowboys and Los Angeles Chargers, then spent the entire 2025 season on the Chargers’ practice squad. He was not with a team for the first six weeks of this season.
