title: The Day After The Day After: Houston Texans beat Jacksonville Jaguars 34-31 in London
summary: The Day After the Day After…when the raw, immediate emotions from the aftermath of a game diminish into the realm of clarity and the proverbial (or literal) hangover no longer haunts the mind. With that, a review of Week 6 Love Defense? This was not your game: Neither Matt Burke nor Anthony Campanile had a […]
full_text: LONDON, ENGLAND - OCTOBER 18: The players of the Houston Texans celebrate victory at full-time in the NFL London Series match between Houston Texans and Jacksonville Jaguars at Wembley Stadium on October 18, 2026 in London, England. (Photo by Julian Finney/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Day After the Day After…when the raw, immediate emotions from the aftermath of a game diminish into the realm of clarity and the proverbial (or literal) hangover no longer haunts the mind. With that, a review of Week 6 Love Defense? This was not your game: Neither Matt Burke nor Anthony Campanile had a great flight back after this game. Consider: 65 combined points, 618 combined yards passing, 220 combined yards rushing, 8 total touchdowns (7 passing), 52% 3rd Down conversion rate, only 2 INTs (both in the end zone) and ZERO, yes, ZERO sacks! Granted, few quarterbacks are playing as well as Trevor Lawrence and CJ Stroud, but with the respective defensive talent on the field, especially with pass rushers like Danielle Hunter, Will Anderson Jr., Travon Walker and Josh Hines-Allen, you figured someone would’ve gotten one sack. Houston’s Rushing Attack: Jacksonville came into this game with a historically good run defense. They had yet to allow a single rusher to gain more than 40 yards in five game. They had the #1 rushing defense in the league. So of course, the Houston Texans and their 31st ranked rushing offense, which had only broken 80 combined rushing yards in a game once all season, managed to outgain the Jags on the ground with 114 combined yards. Houston’s top RBs went for over 40 yards each (Marks 56 on 15 carries, Jordan 43 on 6 carries). You could argue that Marks has been the more explosive back for the Texans’ attack vs. Montgomery, who seemed a bit more tentative before his injury in Week 5. Jordan offered just as much explosiveness as a rusher, especially on his 25-yard TD rush in the 3rd Quarter. Houston must really hope this is a trend and not a fluke. The Kicks for the Kickoffs were good. The coverage, uh, well…it was: On a day with so much scoring, the kick coverage units got a lot of work. For the Texans, it seems that Fairbairn has been working on landing his kicks short of the end zone to force a return. Only one of his six kickoffs was a touchback, and that was the kick at the end of the 1st half. That was the good news. The bad news was that of five Jacksonville kick returns, three started past the JAX 35, including one in Houston territory. All three of those drives got to the Houston red zone, with 2 TDS and one end zone INT. Yes, Ameer Abdullah is a quality kick returner, but that is not exactly the standard Houston fans have come to expect from a Frank Ross unit. THE CRITICAL PLAY: 4th Quarter (2:24), JAX Ball @ HOU 48, 1st and 10; Trevor Lawrence pass for TE Brenton Strange incomplete. S Calen Bullock on the pass defense In this game, most of the big plays came on offense, from Jaylen Noel’s 50-yard reception inside of a minute left in the 1st half that secured Houston a TD to the Woody Marks’ catch-and-run setting up Fairbairn’s walk-off FG. However, we will consider a defensive play. After the Stroud INT, the Jags had moved the ball 32 yards to Houston’s side of the field on three straight Lawrence completions. On this play, Lawrence was looking to TE Strange, who had a solid game to this point, down the intermediate middle of the Houston defense. However, the pass was nearly picked off by Calen Bullock, who couldn’t quite wrap up the ball. Yet, it stemmed Lawrence’s momentum. An incompletion and short pass later, the Jags settled for a tying FG. This gave Houston the ball back with plenty of time to win it, which they managed to do. Given how Houston has lost three games with a lead inside of the final two minutes with teams and given how neither defense was making all that much an impact, Bullock’s near INT was enough to hold Jacksonville and set up the Texans for the win. FUN WITH NUMBERS: 8: Number of 4th Quarter/OT game-winning drives led by Stroud for Houston : That number could and should be higher this season. Stroud has done this twice against Jacksonville, the other happening in 2024, when he led Houston to a win via a last-second TD pass to RB Dare Ogunbowale. 1388: Days between a CJ Stroud/Marvin Harrison, Jr. reception: Prior to the second quarter of the London Game, the last time that Marvin Harrison Jr caught a pass from CJ Stroud, it was in the first half of the 2022 Peach Bowl/CFB semi-final between Ohio State and Georgia. Georgia would win that game 42-41, but a “what if?” that haunts Ohio State fans is what if Harrison hadn’t left the game after a concussion. Harrison and Stroud were slicing up the Georgia defense (Harrison: 5 receptions/106 yards/2 TDs), but when Harrison went out of the game, Georgia was able to get back into contention and eventually took the lead for good. 60: Distance of Longest FG ever made against the Texans: When Cam Little got all of that kick to tie the game at 31, he set a record against Houston. The previous long, 59, happened in 2020, when the-then Jags kicker, Josh Lambo, made his kick to end the 1st half of a game in Jacksonville (also against Houston). GAME BALLS: QB CJ Stroud: Great numbers (24-of-34 for 312 yards, 3 TDS, 1 INT, 0 sacks) and rebounded from a bad INT to lead a game-winning drive. WR Jaylin Noel: Noel continues a breakout run with this day at the office: 4 receptions/107 yards/1 TD; 2 kickoff returns/74 yards.; 1 punt return/2 yards LT Aireontae Ersery/LG Keylan Rutledge: In a game where Houston rushed for over 100 yards against the top rushing defense in the league, as well as not surrendering a single sack, a lot of credit must go to the Texans offensive line. In particular, Houston had most of their success running along the left side of the offensive formations (70 of their 114 rushing yards). These two youngsters did much of the heavy lifting to make this game work. OC Nick Caley: If you are going to slam him for the bad, gotta give credit for the good. The critical 3rd down conversion for the Texans on the final drive when Stroud hit Marks for a catch-and-run was one of his best calls. SHOULD BE FORCED TO EAT NOTHING BUT BRITISH COOKING FOR THE REST OF THE WEEK WHILE LISTENING TO DUUUVAAALLLL CHANTS IN A BAD BRITISH ACCENT ON REPEAT S Reed Blankenship: The rough start for the once-lauded free agent signing continues. Jags TE Brenton Strange was feasting on Blankenship’s coverage in the 1st half, and Blankenship missed a key tackle on a Jags TD. To top off the bad trip, he left the game due to a concussion. MJ Stewart replaced him in the lineup, and while the defense still had a tough day, Stewart seemed to play a bit better. TE Brevin Jordan: Not entirely fair, but if you sat through the entire Texans game Sunday and just stayed seated, you had more receiving yards than Brevin Jordan. He had more receptions (1 to 0), but you had more yards (-1 to 0). Wembley Groundskeepers: Few stadiums are as venerated as Wembley. The host of the 1966 World Cup Final, the 2012 Olympics and tons of other massive events, you would think that the groundskeepers would be among the best in the world. Uh, about that. The field seemed unnecessarily slick, which cost the game its umpire early in the 1st quarter due to slippage/leg injury. Additionally, Dalton Schlutz could not maintain his footing on a key 1st half reception on a third down, forcing Houston to punt. A key talking point throughout the game as it impacted both teams. With that win, Houston moves to 2-4, two games back of Jacksonville for the AFC South. They return home to face the New York Giants of New Jersey. Kickoff is this Sunday at noon CDT at Reliant Stadium.

title: How much is DeForest Buckner worth on the trade market?
summary: This is the second part of a three-article series looking at the hypothetical trade value of three of the Colts’ biggest stars. This one is about DeForest Buckner. You can click here to read the previous one on Jonathan Taylor. As with Taylor, this is not an argument that Indianapolis should trade Buckner. The Colts […]
full_text: PITTSBURGH, PENNSYLVANIA - OCTOBER 11: DeForest Buckner #99 of the Indianapolis Colts celebrates during the third quarter of the game against the Pittsburgh Steelers at Acrisure Stadium on October 11, 2026 in Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania. (Photo by Lauren Leigh Bacho/Getty Images) | Getty Images This is the second part of a three-article series looking at the hypothetical trade value of three of the Colts’ biggest stars. This one is about DeForest Buckner. You can click here to read the previous one on Jonathan Taylor . As with Taylor, this is not an argument that Indianapolis should trade Buckner. The Colts probably should not be looking to move any of these players unless the season falls apart or another team comes calling with an offer that is too good to ignore. The point of the series is simply to determine what these players would realistically be worth if serious trade interest developed around the deadline. Buckner is an interesting case because the player is still very good, but almost everything surrounding him works against his value. He is 32 years old. His contract voids after this season. Any team acquiring him would be doing so primarily for the stretch run and playoffs, with no guarantee he would remain there beyond February. That makes this much more complicated than simply asking how good DeForest Buckner is. Buckner is still really good The easiest part of this evaluation is determining whether Buckner can still play. He definitely can. Through six games, Buckner has four sacks, eight quarterback hits and 18 pressures. He consistently ranks amongst the highest interior defensive linemen in these categories. That is especially important considering the state of the Colts’ defensive front. Indianapolis has struggled badly to consistently pressure quarterbacks this season, yet Buckner continues to create problems from the interior. At 32 years old, he is still arguably the most dependable pass rusher on the roster. There has been no dramatic falloff where we are evaluating Buckner based on what he used to be. He is still collapsing pockets, still winning inside against the top interior offensive linemen and still capable of ruining a drive. That puts him in a different category from the typical veteran defensive lineman available at the deadline. The two trades that make sense as comparisons There have been plenty of defensive tackles traded over the last decade, but very few are particularly useful here. The best comparison is Leonard Williams. Seattle acquired Williams from the Giants at the 2023 trade deadline for a second-round pick in 2024 and a fifth-round pick in 2025. Williams was 29 and in the final year of his contract. Through eight games with the Giants that season, he had only 1.5 sacks. The Seahawks were 5-2, believed they could make a run and paid a significant price for a high-end interior defender. The other useful comparison goes back to 2017, when Seattle acquired Sheldon Richardson from the Jets. The Seahawks sent a second-round pick and Jermaine Kearse while the teams also swapped seventh-round selections. Richardson was 26 at the time and coming off a season with 1.5 sacks, although he had already made a Pro Bowl and had an eight-sack season earlier in his career. Both trades tell us that teams will pay substantial draft capital for an impact interior defensive lineman when they believe they are close to winning. From a performance standpoint, Buckner belongs in that conversation. He has already doubled Williams’ pre-trade sack total in three fewer games this season, and Richardson was coming off one of the quieter statistical seasons of his career when Seattle acquired him. The problem is that Williams was 29 and Richardson was 26. Buckner is 32. That is an enormous difference when assigning trade value, even if Buckner is playing just as well or better than either player was at the time. The contract makes him a potential rental This is probably the biggest factor dragging Buckner’s value down. His contract voids in February, which means a team trading for him would only control him for the remainder of the 2026 season unless it negotiated another deal. That could be eight or nine regular-season games plus the playoffs. The financial cost for this season would not be particularly difficult to handle. Buckner has a $13 million base salary in 2026. The Colts already paid his $10 million roster bonus, and the prorated signing-bonus money would remain Indianapolis’ responsibility. A team acquiring him around the halfway point of the season would therefore be taking on roughly half of that $13 million salary, somewhere around $6.5 million depending on the exact date of the trade. Most contenders can find a way to absorb that, but the larger issue is what happens afterward. There is no cheap year of team control waiting in 2027. There is no franchise-friendly contract that makes him a multi-year asset. The team either lets him reach free agency or has to negotiate a new contract with a player who will turn 33 next season. That has to significantly reduce the return compared with Williams and Richardson. How much does Buckner have left? Age is a legitimate concern, but I would not assume Buckner is approaching the end. Defensive tackle is one of the positions where elite players can remain productive well into their 30s. Cameron Heyward might be the most obvious example. He is 37 years old and was still one of the best defensive linemen in football last season. At age 36, PFF gave him the highest grade of any interior defender in the league at 90.4, and he earned another All-Pro selection. Heyward is obviously an extreme example, not the standard everyone should be expected to follow. Calais Campbell is still playing the position at 40! Defensive tackle is a position that relies a lot on strength, technique and instincts and those 3 things don’t age. All of this shows that 32 is hardly ancient for a great defensive tackle. Buckner’s game also lends itself to aging relatively well. He is 6-foot-7, incredibly long and wins with power, technique and an ability to use his frame inside. He does not need to rely entirely on explosive athleticism to remain effective. I would be comfortable saying Buckner has at least a few quality seasons left if he remains healthy and if he decides he wants to play that long. There have been rumours about him retiring the last couple of seasons, so that also plays a factor into things. A contender acquiring him would be doing so for the current playoff run first, but there is a legitimate possibility that the relationship could continue beyond that. If Buckner finishes the year playing at his current level, it would not be surprising at all to see him sign another multi-year contract. The uncertainty simply means a team cannot value those future seasons as part of the trade itself. Who could use Buckner? Unlike Taylor, where only certain contenders have an obvious need at running back, the market for Buckner could be fairly broad. Almost every playoff team could use another interior defender who can rush the quarterback, but 4 stand out to me. Detroit would probably be the most interesting fit. The Lions are 3-2 and clearly still view themselves as a championship contender. Aidan Hutchinson gives them a premier edge rusher, while Alim McNeill is a good interior player, but Detroit lost veteran nose tackle D.J. Reader during the offseason. Adding Buckner would give the Lions another proven interior pass rusher and allow them to build a defensive front capable of creating pressure without constantly blitzing. For a team with legitimate Super Bowl aspirations, Buckner is exactly the type of veteran addition that makes sense in October. San Francisco would be the funniest destination for obvious reasons. The 49ers traded Buckner to Indianapolis in 2020 because they did not want to give him the enormous contract he eventually received. Six years later, they could theoretically bring him back for…

title: Evaluating Colts veteran trade chips who could be on the move soon to jumpstart rebuild
summary: After longtime general manager Chris Ballard was fired Monday, it’s a reasonable expectation right now that the Indianapolis Colts (at 2-4) may look to trade off some of their veteran players to recoup lost draft compensation. As you may recall, the Colts currently do not have a 2027 first round pick, as theirs went to […]
full_text: INDIANAPOLIS, IN - OCTOBER 12: Indianapolis Colts guard Quenton Nelson (56) congratulates Indianapolis Colts running back Jonathan Taylor (28) on his nice run during and NFL game between the Indianapolis Colts and the Arizona Cardinals on October 12, 2025 at Lucas Oil Stadium in Indianapolis, IN (Photo by Jeffrey Brown/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images After longtime general manager Chris Ballard was fired Monday, it’s a reasonable expectation right now that the Indianapolis Colts (at 2-4) may look to trade off some of their veteran players to recoup lost draft compensation. As you may recall, the Colts currently do not have a 2027 first round pick, as theirs went to the New York Jets, along with other pieces, in last year’s trade deadline deal for shutdown cornerback Sauce Gardner. Newly appointed interim general manager Ed Dodds may be tasked with trying to trade some sought after Colts veterans ahead of this year’s trade deadline in early November. Let’s look at some of the Colts top trade candidates, that have value to other teams and could realistically be on the move for a clearly rebuilding team: DeForest Buckner Look, no one wants to trade Buckner, who’s consistently embodied what it means to be a member of the Horseshoe about as well as anyone during his entire tenure in Indianapolis. However, Buckner is 32-years-old coming off neck surgery, entering the last year of his current contract, and was publicly frustrated after Sunday’s brutal loss. If the price is right, it makes sense to trade him to a title contender for the last stretch of his standout playing career, perhaps back to the San Francisco Bay where it all started for him. It makes sense to me that a contender could be interested in the still highly productive veteran pass rushing defensive tackle, similarly to when the Colts traded a 2nd round pick for Anthony ’Booger’ McFarland of the Tampa Bay Buccaneers which helped galvanize their interior run defense for a Super Bowl run—along with the return of starting safety Bob Sanders of course. Buckner has 26 tackles (9 solo), 4.0 sacks, 18 QB pressures, 3 passes defensed, and a fumble recovery during all 6 starts in 2026. Trade Compensation: 2027 2nd round pick Possible Trade Suitors: Buffalo Bills, Los Angeles Rams, and San Francisco 49ers Quenton Nelson Unless the future Hall of Famer goes to interim Colts management or ownership and explicitly states, “I want out,” the pending free agent should remain in Indianapolis for the remainder of his playing career prime through a new lucrative contract extension, regardless of who the next general manager is calling the shots—and that should come from a mandate above by team ownership. Simply put, “Lock up Nelson for life!” Since being selected by the Colts with the 6th overall pick of the 2018 NFL Draft, Nelson has been a perennial NFL All-Pro and one of the best offensive guards in all of football. He’s still playing at a very high Pro Bowl level again, and at age 30 is still young enough to outlast a short rebuild with productive football still left in him—as great offensive guards can still age pretty gracefully until at least their mid-thirties. Particularly one with great technique and fundamentals like Big Q, who should be a future Ring of Honor player for the Colts franchise, when his Canton-bound career is all said and done. Nelson has started all 6 games for the Colts and has a +84.3 overall grade via PFF, having allowed 0 sacks and just 7 total QB pressures during his 248 total pass blocking snaps. Trade Compensation: 2027 first round pick Possible Trade Suitors: Detroit Lions, Minnesota Vikings, Seattle Seahawks Grover Stewart Buckner’s longtime running mate at defensive tackle, Grover Stewart, has been a consistent run stopping force in the middle of the Indianapolis defensive line and like Buckner, another longtime veteran leader of their defense. At 32-years-old, he’s also starting to get a bit long in the tooth at defensive tackle for Indianapolis and while his play has dipped a bit this season, perhaps a change of scenery and playing for a contender could motivate ‘Big Grove’ to find his vintage run stuffing self again during a serious playoff push. There has to be a legit playoff hopeful, who’s looking to shore up their run defense, and Stewart could be that guy for them in the short-term as another pending free agent. On the 2026 campaign, Stewart has 20 tackles (5 solo), 0.5 sacks, and a pass defensed during all 6 starts. Trade Compensation: 2027 4th Round Pick Possible Trade Suitors: Dallas Cowboys, Green Bay Packers, Las Vegas Raiders. Jonathan Taylor Look, I can certainly understand the rationale for trading Taylor at this time, he’s 27-years-old with a lot of mileage on his tires, and NFL running backs typically do not age all that gracefully into their early thirties, unless apparently you’re freak of nature Derrick Henry. To me, this is similar to Nelson though, where unless Taylor asks out via a trade, I think the Colts would look to keep the star workhorse for the remainder of his playing career prime here—as another future Ring of Honor guy and NFL Hall of Famer, when it’s all said and done. Plus, you still want to give fans a reason to go to Colts games and have stars they can be proud of and root for on Sundays, if the expected trade return isn’t going to be all that worth the while. On the season, Taylor has 122 carries for 492 total rushing yards (4.0 ypc avg.) and 7 rushing touchdowns during all 6 starts in the 2026 season. Trade Compensation: 2027 2nd round pick Possible Trade Suitors: Denver Broncos, Green Bay Packers, Minnesota Vikings Charvarius ‘Mooney’ Ward With a myriad of injuries, including multiple concussions, since joining Indianapolis in the 2025 offseason, it’s hard to see much of a robust market for the 30-year-old cornerback, who’s had some up-and-down play this year. While Ward clearly hasn’t played up to his current Colts lucrative contract, he has no guaranteed money for next year, meaning a contending team with a clear need for a proven veteran cornerback could potentially kick the tires on Mooney Ward finding his familiar self down the season’s stretch as a rental to shore up their secondary. Ward has 18 tackles (12 solo) and 4 passes defensed during all 6 starts, with a +64.7 overall grade via PFF—including a +62.8 coverage grade. Trade Compensation: 2027 5th round pick Possible Trade Suitors: Detroit Lions, Kansas City Chiefs, Pittsburgh Steelers, San Francisco 49ers
author: Luke Schultheis

Giants releasing RB Najee Harris, source says | ESPN Harris, who is second on the team behind Cam Skattebo in rushing yards with 99 this season, got the start Sunday but had just four carries for 2 yards. title: Chiefs are reportedly signing rookie LB Aiden Fisher to the practice squad
summary: On Tuesday, the Kansas City Chiefs brought in rookie linebacker Aiden Fisher, a teammate of left tackle Kahlil Benson at Indiana last season, for a workout. Jason Anderson of 810 Sports was the first to report that he was expected to sign with the Chiefs’ practice squad, and NFL Insider Jordan Schultz backed that up […]
full_text: (Photo by John Byrum/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images On Tuesday, the Kansas City Chiefs brought in rookie linebacker Aiden Fisher, a teammate of left tackle Kahlil Benson at Indiana last season, for a workout. Jason Anderson of 810 Sports was the first to report that he was expected to sign with the Chiefs’ practice squad , and NFL Insider Jordan Schultz backed that up by reporting that he will be signing with Kansas City . Sources: The #Chiefs are signing former #Texans LB Aiden Fisher to their practice squad. The rookie 7th-round pick was an All-American last season en route to helping Indiana win a national championship. https://t.co/6tiiKUIUma pic.twitter.com/SQ3NKkCV4x — Jordan Schultz (@Schultz_Report) October 20, 2026 Fisher, a seventh-round pick this year, was released by the Houston Texans last week after playing solely on special teams over three games this season. He recorded a tackle in the Week 2 loss to the Cincinnati Bengals . Fisher played the 18th-most snaps among Texans special-teams players this year. Listed at 6 feet 1 inch and 231 pounds, Fisher was the 13th-ranked linebacker in the 2026 NFL Draft, according to draft expert Dane Brugler of The Athletic . He projected Fisher to be drafted in the fifth round. This was Dane’s takeaway from watching Fisher’s film. “Fisher looks small at times on film, but he is equal parts athletic and tough, and his play personality should make him an easy sell in a war room. He projects as a low-end NFL starter, similar to Drue Tranquill.” Fisher spent two years at James Madison before transferring to Indiana, following head coach Curt Cignetti. During his time with the Hoosiers, Fisher totaled 215 tackles, 16 tackles for loss, six sacks, two interceptions, one forced fumble and five passes defended. The comparison to Tranquill speaks to Fisher’s potential as an all-around linebacker who can make plays against the pass and run. The Chiefs will look to develop the National Champion from the practice squad, and reserve linebacker Jeffrey Bassa could face that competition on the depth chart sooner rather than later.
author: Ron Kopp Jr.

title: The Chiefs’ schedule gets a lot tougher starting in Week 7
summary: It’s hard to deny that the (5-0) Kansas City Chiefs had a favorable schedule to begin the 2026 regular season. The best opponent so far has been the (4-2) Denver Broncos, who were clearly caught off guard by the Chiefs’ shift in offensive identity in the season-opening beatdown on “Monday Night Football.” It’s reasonable to […]
full_text: (Photo by Ethan Miller/Getty Images) | Getty Images It’s hard to deny that the (5-0) Kansas City Chiefs had a favorable schedule to begin the 2026 regular season. The best opponent so far has been the (4-2) Denver Broncos , who were clearly caught off guard by the Chiefs’ shift in offensive identity in the season-opening beatdown on “Monday Night Football.” It’s reasonable to believe Denver would have put together a more competitive game with even just one game of this year’s film to study. The team’s other four opponents have a combined 5-18 record going into Week 7. The Chiefs have taken care of business on a light schedule, as shown by the second-best point differential in the NFL (+57). Only the (6-0) San Francisco 49ers (+67) are better at this point. That’s what elite teams do, but the schedule will get a lot harder from here. The road trips So far, the team has hit the road to play the winless Miami Dolphins and to play the Las Vegas Raiders at “Arrowhead West,” where Chiefs head coach Andy Reid is the venue’s winningest coach. Starting in Week 7, the road trips get longer and more difficult. The “Sunday Night Football” road game against the (3-3) Seattle Seahawks will feature a defending Super Bowl champion and its roaring crowd, who could feel like they’re backed into a corner with a .500 record after six weeks. The Chiefs can expect an A-game from Seattle in every phase, including the drive to shut down the NFL’s leading rusher, Kenneth Walker. He was the Super Bowl MVP for the Seahawks less than a year ago, and has been the driving force for Kansas City’s success on offense this year. After the primetime game on the West Coast, the Broncos will welcome the Chiefs to Mile High for a pivotal matchup. Let’s say Kansas City drops its first game of the season in Seattle while Denver takes care of the (2-4) Arizona Cardinals in Week 7. Suddenly, Week 8 could put the AFC West teams at the same level in the standings. If the Chiefs emerge from the next two road games still unbeaten, they will have built up a lot of margin for error for the next significant stretch of away games: starting on Thanksgiving night in Week 12, Kansas City will play the (5-1) Buffalo Bills , (2-4) Los Angeles Rams — on “Thursday Night Football” — and (3-2) Cincinnati Bengals before finally returning to Arrowhead four days before Christmas. Six of the team’s next eight games are on the road. The strength of opponents Going into the season, we knew the Chiefs’ schedule got a lot tougher starting in Week 7. From this point on, the team will face seven teams that made the postseason last year. Between now and the Week 17 rematch with the Chargers, only four teams currently have losing records — and one of them is a sleeping giant in the Rams. Kansas City still has to play the undefeated 49ers, the one-loss Bills and three other teams with only two losses in the AFC playoff race: the Broncos, Bengals and the New England Patriots . This all happens before the final two-game stretch against the Chargers and Raiders. The bottom line The Chiefs are clearly one of the best teams in the NFL this season, ranking top-10 in points and yards on both sides of the ball. However, they’ve faced a much lighter schedule than Kansas City will face for the rest of the season, with no bye week to rest in the middle of a postseason run. The team has built up some margin for error with an undefeated start, but it will need to keep winning to earn the sole bye week in the AFC playoff bracket.

title: Kansas City’s best things to do, see, and eat before heading to a Chiefs game

Built in 1972, the iconic and legendary stadium has hosted everything from AFC Championship games, the Pro Bowl, iconic concerts, and most recently; six games of the […]
full_text: Photo by: Michael Siluk/UCG/Universal Images Group via Getty Images One of the great places to visit in the NFL, and a stadium which should be on every football fan’s bucket list—is Arrowhead Stadium in Kansas City, Missouri. Built in 1972, the iconic and legendary stadium has hosted everything from AFC Championship games, the Pro Bowl, iconic concerts, and most recently; six games of the 2026 FIFA World Cup. Arrowhead Stadium is home to the four-time Super Bowl Champion Kansas City Chiefs, and holds the Guinness World Record for loudest stadium in the world. When visiting Arrowhead, visitors are unable to forget they are in the loudest stadium in the world. From visual reminders all around the stadium, to Chiefs’ fans screaming until their voices are gone; fans are in for a world class experience with a visit to Arrowhead. Arrowhead Stadium is consistently ranked as one of the top venues to see a football game across the NFL, and for good reason. There is more to see, do, and experience in Kansas City than just a trip to Arrowhead Stadium, however. Located smack dab in the middle of the United States, Kansas City has blossomed from its “cow town” or “flyover country” perception into a world-class Midwestern city. Although Kansas City is the seventh-smallest market in the NFL, it can easily entertain travelers or families of all budgets and interests for a weekend. Places to stay in Kansas City One of the downsides to Arrowhead Stadium is the distance from other attractions and amenities in Kansas City. The stadium is about a 15-20 minute drive from downtown and other attractions in Kansas City, without much to do around the stadium. Depending on your itinerary, you may want to stay further from the stadium and drive to the stadium on game day. Mid-range: Best Western Plus Kansas City Sports Complex Hotel is located within walking distance of Arrowhead Stadium. If looking for something closer to city center but still relatively close to the stadium, Stoney Creek Hotel is a 15 minute drive in Independence. It offers free hot breakfast, as well as an onsite restaurant. Luxury: Loews Kansas City Hotel is located in downtown Kansas City. It offers modern amenities and great views of the Kansas City skyline. Several restaurants are located in the hotel, including 1587 Prime, the steakhouse co-owned by Chiefs’ quarterback Patrick Mahomes and tight end Travis Kelce. Things to do in Kansas City There are an abundance of entertainment options to fill almost any person’s interests in Kansas City. Whether looking for something the whole family can enjoy; or interested in history, art, or nightlife; Kansas City has it. Fun can be had across the city, without breaking the bank. For the family The Kansas City Zoo and Aquarium : The zoo is over 200 acres (be prepared to walk) and could fill an entire day of your itinerary. A state of the art aquarium opened in 2023 and a new giraffe exhibit opened in the spring. Union Station : Kansas City’s historic Union Station boasts Science City, a planetarium, shopping, and restaurants. There is currently a special exhibition on the Berlin Wall. Negro Leagues Baseball Museum : One of the premier destinations for any sports fan visiting Kansas City. Revisit the history of the Negro Leagues in the historic 18th and Vine District. Right next door to the American Jazz Museum! Arrowhead Stadium Tour : A great option to get behind the scenes looks at areas many fans don’t see on game day. This includes looks at suites, private clubs, the locker room, the Hall of Honor, broadcast booth, a stop on the field, and more. For the history buff National World War I Museum and Memorial : The official and largest museum in the United States dedicated to the Great War. Several hours or an entire day could be spent here. Don’t stop at just the museum. Visit the iconic Liberty Memorial on the grounds for a fantastic view of Union Station and downtown. Harry S. Truman Presidential Library and Museum : The nation’s 33rd president lived in Independence, a suburb of Kansas City. Visit his home, presidential library, and museum to learn more about the influential politician and Missourian. Plan several hours for this stop. Nightlife Kansas City Power & Light District : In the past decade, Kansas City has revitalized downtown. The Power & Light District is a great option for dining, shopping, and bars for any visitor to the city. It does get busy on game weekends. KC Live is a great venue to catch any game. Westport or the Crossroads : Both neighborhoods contain many dining or entertainment options to satisfy any taste bud. Highlights include Kelly’s or The Landing in Westport, and Up-Down and The Brick in the Crossroads. Best places to eat in Kansas City The first thing that comes to mind when someone thinks of food in Kansas City? Barbecue. And rightfully so, as Kansas City is home to some of the best barbecue in the United States. There are over 100 barbecue restaurants in Kansas City, so there is no way to try them all. You can’t go wrong with finding something delicious in almost every barbecue restaurant in the city. Here are some of my favorites: Joe’s Kansas City Bar-B-Que Char Bar Q39 Slap’s BBQ If interested in more than barbecue on your visit to Kansas City, there’s plenty of other options as well. There are options across the city for any budget, and for any taste bud. Here are some of my non-BBQ favorites: The Peanut Lula Southern Cookhouse Garazzo’s Tay’s Burger Shack Pizza Tascio After eating at these delectable eateries, you may be thirsty. There are plenty of unique and fun places to parch your thirst: Boulevard Brewing Company KC Bier Co Messenger Coffee Company The Roasterie Arrowhead Stadium parking, rideshare, and transit options Arrowhead Stadium has ample parking, the reason being it is a tailgating mecca. Parking at the stadium is cheapest if you purchase online ahead of time, and runs at $57. There are parking options around the stadium at various businesses or homes which offer parking spots at a cheaper rate. This just requires a bit more walking to get to the stadium. Parking lots typically open about four and a half hours prior to game kickoff. There are rideshare options, with drop-off and pick-up being at the Missouri Welcome Center on Blue Ridge Cutoff between Gates 1 and 2. Visit the official website for maps and further information on ride share. The other transit option for transportation to and from the stadium is the Ride KC bus service on the 47 Broadway Line. Visit RideKC.org for more information. Tailgating at Arrowhead Stadium Consistently ranked as one of the best overall game-day experiences in the NFL, Arrowhead Stadium is the premier tailgating experience. From the moment you step foot in the parking lot, the smell of barbecue is wafting in the air. Smoke from grills can be seen in the atmosphere for what feels like miles. While the stadium being separated from the city may limit lodging and on-site restaurants or bars, the expansive parking lot surrounding Arrowhead Stadiums allows the fans to make game day special. Tailgating at Arrowhead Stadium is a religious experience for some. Fans line up in their vehicles hours before the parking gates open in order to park and begin tailgating as soon as possible. This is how some fans spend their vacation money and a hefty portion of their grocery budget. Even if wearing an opposing team’s jersey, you’ll still find a welcoming group of Chiefs fans waiting to offer you some food or a beer—as long as you can take some friendly ribbing. The Arrowhead Stadium Experience Beyond tailgating and being the loudest stadium in the world, Arrowhead is also known for its national anthem. The Arrowhead faithful welcome visiting fans and players with a vibrant, “home of the Chiefs!” at the end of the national anthem. On special game days, the national anthem also ends with a flyover of the stadium, often with aircraft from nearby Whiteman Air Force Base. The Chiefs Hall of…

title: Checking in on former Chiefs players who moved on this offseason
summary: The strong start to the (5-0) Kansas City Chiefs’ season is proof that the organization made some effective changes this offseason. Still, with plenty of recent Super Bowl memories, Chiefs Kingdom likes to check in on players who once wore red and gold. Let’s take an early-season look at how the players the team moved […]
full_text: (Photo by AAron Ontiveroz/The Denver Post) | Denver Post via Getty Images The strong start to the (5-0) Kansas City Chiefs ’ season is proof that the organization made some effective changes this offseason. Still, with plenty of recent Super Bowl memories, Chiefs Kingdom likes to check in on players who once wore red and gold. Let’s take an early-season look at how the players the team moved on from this offseason are performing in 2026: CB Trent McDuffie New team: Los Angeles Rams Stats: 16 tackles (2 for loss), 1 interception and 7 passes broken up in five games The Chiefs traded McDuffie to the Rams this offseason for a haul of draft picks, and he has been a vital part of Los Angeles’ secondary this season. That’s why his groin injury in practice was so significant, forcing him to miss the Week 6 matchup against the Arizona Cardinals ; the Rams lost, falling to 2-4. So far this season, McDuffie has spent the majority of his time on the perimeter for the Rams being a lockdown corner. He has played only 14% of his defensive snaps in the slot. According to Pro Football Focus , he has allowed only five catches over 18 targets, generating a 21.1 passer rating. CB Jaylen Watson New team: Los Angeles Rams Stats: 17 tackles (2 for loss), 1 interception and 5 passes broken up in five games Watson joined McDuffie in Los Angeles and has been the starter opposite McDuffie on the outside. He’s arguably made just as big an impact in as many games; Watson dislocated his shoulder in Week 3, forcing him to miss Week 4. He has since returned to the lineup, including an interception against the Buffalo Bills in his first game back on the field. He has allowed 12 catches over 20 targets, generating a 71.5 passer rating. Chiefs Kingdom will see McDuffie, Watson and the Rams in Week 13 on “Thursday Night Football” in Los Angeles. S Bryan Cook New team: Cincinnati Bengals Stats: 17 tackles, 1 forced fumble and one fumble recovered in four games Cook has been a staple in Cincinnati’s back end through the 3-2 start, although he missed the Week 4 game due to an ankle injury. He returned to the field against the Miami Dolphins in a full-time role with five tackles. Outside of the forced fumble in Week 1, Cook hasn’t made many splash plays for the Bengals. He has pressured the quarterback twice over four blitzes, but has a 12% missed-tackle rate ( PFF ). Cook and Cincinnati will welcome the Chiefs in for a matchup in Week 14. LB Leo Chenal New team: Washington Commanders Stats: 18 tackles (1 for loss) in three games Unfortunately, the Chiefs’ former hybrid linebacker has already seen his season come to an end after a scary collision in the Week 3 game against the Seattle Seahawks , which led to season-ending neck surgery. He shared that “surgery went well” on X , so we’ll look forward to getting more positive updates on Chenal moving forward. RT Jawaan Taylor New team: Atlanta Falcons Stats: 10 quarterback pressures (2 sacks) allowed over 186 pass blocks in six starts Taylor has missed just a handful of snaps for the Falcons this season, manning the right tackle spot and the blind side for quarterback Michael Penix. He has been called for two penalties this season, although one was either declined or offset. Taylor and Atlanta will welcome Kansas City in for a game in Week 10. WR Hollywood Brown New team: Philadelphia Eagles Stats: 12 rushing yards over two attempts Brown has only been on the field for 17 snaps for Philadelphia’s offense this year and hasn’t seen a pass thrown his way. Brown has missed time due to an ankle injury this season, but ahead of Week 6, he had no game designation, pointing to him being a healthy scratch. DE Charles Omenihu New team: Washington Commanders Stats: 1 tackle, 1 quarterback hit and a pass defended in four games The big veteran defensive end has played 45% of the defensive snaps for the Commanders when he’s been on the field, but he suffered groin and ankle injuries in Week 4 and hasn’t been back in action since. CB Joshua Williams New team: Tennessee Titans Stats: 3 tackles and 2 passes defended in one game In his first game of the season, a start in a Week 6 win over the Indianapolis Colts, Williams played every defensive snap and broke up two passes. DT Jerry Tillery New team: Indianapolis Colts Stats: 13 tackles (2 for loss), 1 QB hit over six games (three starts) After one year in Kansas City, Tillery has found a role in the Colts’ defensive line rotation, playing 38% of the snaps and starting three games this year. TE Robert Tonyan New team: Pittsburgh Steelers Stats: 1 catch for 2 yards over six games Tonyan has seen the field with his old friend quarterback Aaron Rodgers just 22 times this season; he has played more special teams (35 snaps) for Pittsburgh this year. DE Malik Herring New team: Miami Dolphins Stats: 8 tackles (2 for loss) in five games played Herring has found a spot in Miami’s defense; he plays 39% of the defensive snaps and produced four quarterback pressures over 55 pass rushes so far. DE Mike Danna New team: Buffalo Bills Stats: 1 game played Danna appeared in just one game for Buffalo (Week 2, 8 defensive snaps) before he was cut on October 12th; he was brought back to the team a couple of days later. RB Isiah Pacheco New team: Detroit Lions Pacheco was put on the Reserve/Injured list after undergoing back surgery during the first week of the season. According to CBS Sports , at the time, Pacheco had a 12-week recovery timeline and “could return in December.” RB Dameon Pierce New team: Philadelphia Eagles Stats: 23 carries, 49 rushing yards and one touchdown, along with six catches for 13 yards in two games Pierce has been forced to step up with the Eagles due to injuries to Saquon Barkley and other running backs, seeing more time already than he ever did with the Chiefs. QB Gardner Minshew New team: Arizona Cardinals Minshew has been the third-string quarterback in Arizona all year, presumably behind both the starter Jacoby Brissett and the rookie Carson Beck. 2025 Chiefs not currently on a team Wide receiver Juju Smith-Schuster Defensive tackle Derrick Nnadi Running back Kareem Hunt Running back Clyde Edwards-Helaire

title: NFL Power Rankings Week 7 Roundup: Chiefs settle into No. 2 spot
summary: The 2026 NFL regular season’s Week 6 featured the Kansas City Chiefs beating the Los Angeles Chargers to push their unbeaten record to 5-0. Let’s see how the national media tweaked their opinion on the Chiefs over the weekend in this week’s sampling of power rankings: ESPN: 2 (No change) Biggest issue on offense: Offensive […]
full_text: (Photo by Jamie Squire/Getty Images) | Getty Images The 2026 NFL regular season’s Week 6 featured the Kansas City Chiefs beating the Los Angeles Chargers to push their unbeaten record to 5-0. Let’s see how the national media tweaked their opinion on the Chiefs over the weekend in this week’s sampling of power rankings: ESPN : 2 (No change) Biggest issue on offense: Offensive tackle health The Chiefs have done an admirable job protecting quarterback Patrick Mahomes, especially since left tackle Josh Simmons, their 2025 first-round pick, has been out because of a bulging disc in his lower back. Coach Andy Reid suggested Simmons won’t be ready for Sunday’s showdown against the Seahawks. Plus, right tackle Jaylon Moore sustained a concussion against the Chargers. Reid might have to continue altering the Chiefs’ playbook if undrafted rookies Kahlil Benson (left tackle) and Joshua Ezeudu (right tackle) are the starters. — Nate Taylor The Athletic : 2 (No change) Fantasy focus: Kenneth Walker III The Chiefs won six games last year. They signed Walker to a three-year, $43 million deal in the offseason. On Sunday, they won their fifth game. Walker is second in the league in fantasy points per game (27.6) after being drafted 16th on average. He had 19 carries for 128 yards against the Chargers and leads the league with 665 rushing yards. — Chad Graff and Josh Kendall Pro Football Talk : 2 (No change) Super Bowl MVP Kenneth Walker III is the NFL MVP so far. — Mike Florio CBSSports.com : 2 (No change) Coming out of the bye, they dominated the Chargers. The same formula worked: Run it with Kenneth Walker and timely throws by Patrick Mahomes, who is doing more and more each week. — Pete Prisco Yahoo! Sports : 2 (No change) It’s hard to believe that an offense with Patrick Mahomes at quarterback has been turned over to another player, but Kenneth Walker III’s impact on the Chiefs can’t be understated. Walker had another 128 yards and two touchdowns on the ground as the Chiefs easily beat the Chargers 22-6. Walker leads the NFL with 665 rushing yards, even though Kansas City has already had its bye. His 133 rushing yards per game puts him on pace for 2,261 rushing yards. Since 1984, Eric Dickerson has held the NFL’s single-season record with 2,105 yards. Walker’s candidacy for MVP will be discussed, but it’s still a long shot because voters have turned it into a quarterback award. Adrian Peterson was the last non-quarterback to win and that came in 2012. The MVP has gone to a quarterback 18 of the last 19 seasons. But if Walker can get to 2,000 yards, it might give him a chance. — Frank Schwab USA Today : 2 (No change) Andy Reid is now 23-5 in the regular season following bye weeks. Sure looks like he might get the opportunity to coach after another bye a few months from now. — Nate Davis Sports Illustrated : 2 (Up from 3) Asking this seriously: Kenneth Walker is the best free agent signing through six weeks of an NFL season since…Peyton Manning and the Denver Broncos? Walker is averaging one hundred and thirty three yards and more than twenty attempts per game. That’s just wild stuff. — Conor Orr Sporting News : 1 (No change) Kenneth Walker III is now averaging 133 rushing yards per game and is up to 6.3 yards per carry with his 8 TDs. He’s on pace 2,261 yards, which should already put him in the MVP discussion as one of the best-ever free-agent pickups. — Vinnie Iyer FOX Sports : 2 (No change) Is it possible that the Chiefs are actually under the radar for most of the NFL? Or maybe we just all take their greatness for granted? But there sure isn’t a lot of chatter or hype about what might be the best team in the league. And Patrick Mahomes , just 10 months removed from tearing his ACL, is quietly on pace for his best season since 2022 — when he won league MVP and the Chiefs won the Super Bowl. Maybe Mahomes belongs in the early MVP conversation, too? The Chiefs play at Seattle and at Denver these next two weeks, so the noise about K.C. is about to get a lot louder. — Ralph Vacchiano

summary: The Kansas City Chiefs secured their fifth win of the season against the Los Angeles Chargers in Week 6, and middle linebacker Nick Bolton made history. He led the team with 11 tackles, surpassing one of the team’s all-time greats and setting a franchise record. Download the SB Nation app on your mobile device! For […]
full_text: (Photo by Brooke Sutton/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Kansas City Chiefs secured their fifth win of the season against the Los Angeles Chargers in Week 6, and middle linebacker Nick Bolton made history. He led the team with 11 tackles, surpassing one of the team’s all-time greats and setting a franchise record. Chiefs Kingdom, bring the noise to the SB Nation app! Join fellow Chiefs fans to react to every explosive play and game-changing moment in real time. Chat live throughout the game Browse with fewer ads Easily jump between communities Enjoy faster commenting and posting Download the SB Nation app on iOS or Android . Download the SB Nation app on your mobile device! For Apple devices, click here . For Android devices, click here . The latest Kansas City Chiefs news Nick Bolton reacts to securing an all-time Chiefs record vs. Chargers | Chiefs Wire “I knew going into the Colts game. I missed a couple of tackles and didn’t deserve it then,” Bolton said, “but it’s pretty cool being in the echelon with those guys. A lot of linebackers came before me who laid the groundwork, and being part of history with them is a special moment for me.” Bolton recorded 11 tackles (three solo) in Sunday’s victory. With 10+ tackles, Bolton reached his 26th 10+ tackle game, the most in franchise history. He recently passed Chiefs Hall of Famer Derrick Johnson for the team’s all-time mark. Latest injury update on Kansas City Chiefs’ Josh Simmons, Jaylon Moore raises big offensive tackle questions for Week 7 vs. Seahawks | A to Z Sports Asked about his potential status for Sunday’s game against the Seahawks, Reid was hesitant to overpromise. The team will continue to ramp up Simmons’ workload and see how he responds as he returns from injury. “Josh (Simmons) is still probably going to be ramping up as we go,” Reid said. “Rashee (Rice), we’ll have to see. I haven’t seen Rashee today, but he’s been here every day, and he’ll be coming in here in a minute. So, we’ll see where he’s at.” 10 Quick Facts Following the Chiefs Week 6 Win Over Los Angeles | Upon Further Review | The Mothership The Chiefs moved to 3-0 in the AFC West this season. Kansas City is now 3-0 vs. the AFC West through just six weeks, joining the San Francisco 49ers (3 wins) for the most victories against divisional opponents for any team so far this season. The Chiefs own a 39-12 record vs. the AFC West since 2018, which marks the best record for any team against their own division in that span. A 5-0 record now secured through the first six weeks of the year, Kansas City will aim to stay perfect this upcoming weekend with a prime-time showdown against the Seattle Seahawks on deck. Ex-Teammate Praises Travis Kelce for Not ‘Milking That Ankle Injury’ After Chiefs’ 5th Straight Win | Yahoo! Sports Dieter posted on X early Monday to praise the tight end’s toughness, penning, “Kelce is a dawg! They don’t make em like him anymore. Anyone else would be milking that ankle injury.” Kelce hurt his ankle on a screen pass during the opening drive. He had it taped on the sideline. He got medical tape put on his ankle, went back into the game and later returned to the sideline to get more tape wrapped around it. Former NFL team doctor David Chao wrote on X, “By video, mild right high eversion ankle sprain. Possible to tape and return.” The Chiefs Have a Harrison Butker Problem, Whether They Care to Admit It or Not | Sports Illustrated Instead, the club is paying Butker more on a per-year basis ($6.4 million) than all but three kickers in NFL history to provide negative value. Doing so while denying that is even worse. The three-time Super Bowl champion is now several years removed from his last legitimately good effort. In 2023, he drilled 94.3% of field goals and didn’t miss an extra point. In 35 regular-season outings since then, though, those respective accuracy marks are 84.2% and 91.4%. Last year saw the former seventh-round pick finish just 1.2% above the league average on field goals and 7.3% worse on PATs. Around the NFL Terry McLaurin leaves in cart, ruled out of Commanders-49ers game with knee injury | The Athletic McLaurin went down away from the play, in front of the team’s bench and without contact, after a Commanders’ third-and-long that resulted in a sack of quarterback Jayden Daniels. McLaurin grabbed his left knee in pain and his leg was placed in a large air cast. McLaurin hobbled onto a cart as players from both sides came over to pat him on the helmet before he was whisked away. Jalen Hurts expected to miss season after blood clots discovered in QB’s lungs | ESPN Hurts will undergo treatment involving blood thinners that is expected to sideline the three-time Pro Bowler for at least three months, sources informed of the diagnosis told Rapoport and Schefter. Hurts’ agent, Nicole Lynn, and the Eagles released a statement Monday detailing Hurts’ condition. Lynn and the Eagles said Hurts has deep vein thrombosis and bilateral pulmonary emboli, meaning a blood clot traveled from his legs to his lungs. 49ers’ Mike Evans ruled out with Achilles injury after leaving game late in first half | CBS Sports Head coach Kyle Shanahan noted this week that Evans was dealing with Achilles soreness. The wideout did not practice at all this week, which left his status for Week 6 firmly up in the air for a big NFC matchup. Evans did not practice at all this week, with reports noting that he was mostly working off to the side. The 33-year-old has a history of playing through injuries and has not missed a contest to this point despite missing time in practice. Last week, Evans missed Thursday’s practice with his rib injury, but ended up playing in the Week 5 win over Seattle. That said, this is the first time all season that Evans missed the entire week of practice. In case you missed it on Arrowhead Pride 5 things we learned from the Chiefs’ Week 6 victory over the Chargers Over five games, Walker has 665 rushing yards and averages 6.2 yards per carry, with eight total touchdowns. For reference, the last time a non-quarterback won the NFL MVP was in 2012 when Minnesota Vikings running back Adrian Peterson won the award. That season, Peterson rushed for 2,097 yards and 13 total touchdowns, averaging six yards per carry. Before Peterson won the award, you have to go back to 2006 to find the next season a non-quarterback won the MVP. Chargers running back LaDainian Tomlinson won that year. Interestingly, in 2005, Seattle Seahawks running back Shaun Alexander also won MVP. title: Chargers Power Rankings Roundup: Bolts hit rock bottom after 0-6 start
summary: While there was still three different winless teams in the NFL, the Chargers were able to stay out of last place of the league’s various power rankings thus far. After the Titans earned their first win Week Six, and the Chargers once again setting a new low bar for their offense against the Chiefs, some […]
full_text: KANSAS CITY, MISSOURI - OCTOBER 18:Head coach Jim Harbaugh of the Los Angeles Chargers applauds for a defensive stop against the Kansas City Chiefs in the third quarter at Arrowhead Stadium on October 18, 2026 in Kansas City, Missouri. (Photo by David Eulitt/Getty Images) | Getty Images While there was still three different winless teams in the NFL, the Chargers were able to stay out of last place of the league’s various power rankings thus far. After the Titans earned their first win Week Six, and the Chargers once again setting a new low bar for their offense against the Chiefs, some analysts just couldn’t find a remaining reason to keep them any higher. This is the first 0-6 start to a season for the Chargers since 2000, a year they finished 1-15. With the Rams and Texans up next after the bye, this franchise is going to have to wait a bit longer to finally see that light at the end of the tunnel. Let’s go ahead and see just how bad the damage is after their latest loss. ESPN – #31 “ The Chargers’ offense under new offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel is a major reason they’re winless. The Chargers’ average points dropped to 15.0 per game with Sunday’s loss, which ranks 30th in the NFL. They are averaging 287.2 yards (26th). Quarterback Justin Herbert has a league-worst eight interceptions and the lowest QBR (29.9). And the team has consistently struggled to put together sustainable drives. Case in point? They had four three-and-outs against the Chiefs to go along with two turnovers. Whatever light is at the end of the tunnel is pretty dim.” – Anthony Gharib USA Today – #31 “By most relevant metrics, Justin Herbert has been one of the NFL’s worst quarterbacks this season. Maybe he was a tad overrated to begin with, but he certainly was never, ever this bad. Hi s downfall lies mainly at the feet of Mike McDaniel, which, in turn, also reflects poorly on Jim Harbaugh, who chose to bring in the offensive coordinator in the first place. In other words, the winless Chargers have entered “the finger-pointing” phase of their nightmare season. It won’t end well for anyone.” – Robert Zeglinski Bleacher Report – #31 “ The Los Angeles Chargers entered 2026 with high expectations after back-to-back 11-win seasons. They head into the bye week one of two remaining teams in the league who have yet to win a game. ” “Simply put, the Chargers aren’t doing anything well. Los Angeles ran the ball 22 times Sunday—for 73 yards. Justin Herbert barely cracked 200 passing yards and hsn’t thrown multiple touchdown passes in a game yet this season. The offensive line is in shambles. No team in the league has turned the ball over more.” “ While addressing the media after the game, head coach Jim Harbaugh said changes are coming over the bye week. ” “‘Definitely, offensively, we need to evaluate,’ he said. ‘We need to look at it all — everything we’re doing, how we’re doing it.’” “I hope embattled offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel is renting.” – Brad Davenport Yahoo Sports – #31 “ The Dolphins and Chargers are the last winless teams. While it seems like the Chargers are far better than the Dolphins and won’t seriously challenge Miami for the first overall pick in the 2027 NFL Draft, maybe they are as bad as they’ve looked. The Chargers are 31st in DVOA, and a distant 32nd in EPA (expected points added) per play on offense. They are ninth in EPA per play allowed on defense, which provides more hope. But overall the Chargers are as bad as their record. ” ‘‘The offense is at -0.209 EPA per play, and the Titans are the next worst at -0.133. It wouldn’t be a surprise if offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel, a popular offseason hire, is removed from that role soon. ” – Frank Schwab The Athletic – #32 “ Ranking the most disappointing part of the Chargers’ season so far would be tough, but we’ll go with Hampton. The second-year back was drafted 15th on average and is 133rd in scoring (9.6 ppg). He has topped 60 rushing yards in a game only once, and he’s averaging 3.6 yards per carry. Amazingly, the most valuable Charger from a fantasy perspective this year is quarterback Justin Herbert, who is 109th in scoring at 10.4 per game. ” – Josh Kendall and Chad Graff Pro Football Talk – #32 “Has any team ever failed so badly to live up to their preseason expectations?” – Mike Florio

title: Did Davante Adams play his final game with the Rams?
summary: After Davante Adams went on injured reserved for an expected 6-10 weeks on Monday, it’s fair to wonder if he suits up for the Los Angeles Rams again. If Adams’ recovery takes the full 10 weeks, that puts the Rams in Week 16 or 17. If L.A. hasn’t turned their season around, what is the […]
full_text: After Davante Adams went on injured reserved for an expected 6-10 weeks on Monday, it’s fair to wonder if he suits up for the Los Angeles Rams again. If Adams’ recovery takes the full 10 weeks, that puts the Rams in Week 16 or 17. If L.A. hasn’t turned their season around , what is the point of Adams suiting up for a meaningless game? If Adams can come back this year, that’s very exciting for him and the Rams. Still, how healthy will he be? How hindered or recovered will he be from his ruptured hamstring? Fair questions with no answers. The 33-year-old Adams was on a nice pace for L.A. in 2026 with 480 yards and four touchdowns, but his injury puts him at risk of basically missing the rest of the season, and missing his remaining time with the Rams. Rams HC Sean McVay told reporters that WR Davante Adams ruptured his hamstring and now will be sidelined 6-10 weeks. — Adam Schefter (@AdamSchefter) October 19, 2026 What’s next for Davante Adams? Adams hits free agency in 2027. Unless a new deal is worked out, or unless Adams comes back and plays in 2026, then Adams’ last game with the Rams was this past Sunday against the Arizona Cardinals. It would be a disappointing end to his tenure in L.A. As far as where Adams goes from here, it will depend on his recovery, if he still wants to play and if a team would be interested. Then there is the contract to work out. The future of Adams in the NFL isn’t certain. Davante Adams actually ruptured a hamstring tendon on this play. Rams saying he’ll miss 6-10 weeks but if surgery is needed, I would anticipate this being on the longer end of missed time. https://t.co/UYfl9Sbw2Q — Jeff Mueller, PT, DPT (@jmthrivept) October 19, 2026 Was Adams a success with the Rams? Adams was signed as a missing piece to the offense in 2025 and he was. He scored 19 touchdowns his regular seasons and postseason combined after joining up with Sean McVay and Matthew Stafford. Adams was/is past his prime, and he still was (is?) very good for McVay and the Rams. He came in to functionally replace Cooper Kupp as a veteran wide receiver who could produce, and he did that. He added to his Hall of Fame resume when he led the NFL with 14 receiving scores in 2025. Davante Adams’ 14 touchdowns this season. pic.twitter.com/yNavTNmzbY https://t.co/Qdej886dEt — Football Performances (@NFLPerformances) December 1, 2025 But Adams came to L.A. to win a Super Bowl , and that doesn’t look likely to happen. As of October 2026, the Rams sit at 2-4 with a real chance to miss the playoffs . Funnily enough, Kupp won the Super Bowl in 2025 with the Seattle Seahawks. Not Adams. Six weeks into 2026 and another NFC West team is vying for the Super Bowl, but it’s the San Francisco 49ers, not the Rams. Was Adams time in L.A. a success? Yes. Did his time in L.A. deliver what he and the Rams wanted? Unless they win the Super Bowl in 2026, then not exactly. Adams has been to the NFC Championship Game five times, but the Super Bowl zero. Five NFC Championship losses are both something to be disappointed in, and something to be proud of. Will Adams get the chance to reach a sixth? Unless something changes, it won’t be with the Rams. That ship may have sailed , and his time playing days for the Rams, may be behind him.

title: How does Rams’ depth chart look post-injuries?
summary: Just when fans were getting hopes up for a return of Myles Garrett, the Los Angeles Rams were hit with a wave of injuries unlike anything they’ve seen in a single week since 2022. Garrett is not going to return this week and Sean McVay can’t give any updates on when he might return, while […]
full_text: Just when fans were getting hopes up for a return of Myles Garrett, the Los Angeles Rams were hit with a wave of injuries unlike anything they’ve seen in a single week since 2022. Garrett is not going to return this week and Sean McVay can’t give any updates on when he might return, while Terrance Ferguson isn’t going to come back to practice yet either. Trent McDuffie’s status is unclear. The Rams announced once clear replacement for one of those injuries, which is Brandon McManus as the new kicker to replace Blake Grupe . How else will the Rams look different when they face the Las Vegas Raiders? WR Davante Adams – OUT WR Konata Mumpfield – IN Nobody is saying that Mumpfield will “replace” Adams in a production or value sense, and nobody’s saying that McVay should not increase snaps or reps for Tutu Atwell and other options, including C.J. Daniels. But merely on the depth chart, player to player, Mumpfield is the next man up to start in place of Adams moving forward. Konata Mumpfield needs to be a PRIORITY on waivers this week. He’s my No. 2 target heading into Week 7. 112 routes this season. 3rd among Rams WRs. 50+ ahead of the next WR. When Puka Nacua missed time against Denver in Week 3? 8 targets 4 catches 93 yards 1 touchdown… pic.twitter.com/2iMwLZprvP — PeteNova (@SuperrNova38) October 20, 2026 Adams gave Mumpfield a shoutout in the offseason as a receiver to watch out for, and now the second-year wideout gets to prove himself in that exact role. A seventh-round pick in 2025, Mumpfield has 127 yards on eight catches. 48 of those yards came on a play where it didn’t even feel like he was covered, he just juked someone out of position a little bit and the wheel route was on. Mumpfield has 178 snaps compared to 107 for Jordan Whittington. Expect Atwell to be active, but what about Daniels? Or is Daniels active but not Atwell? Don’t put any decision past McVay. DT Kobie Turner – OUT DT Tyler Davis – IN Davis should be stout against the run, but won’t provide the same pass rushing presence as Turner. He has limited moves in his arsenal and below-average length. The depth of the Rams' defensive front is what's staggering … • Myles Garrett, Byron Young, Josaiah Stewart on the edge. • Aaron Donald, Kobie Turner, Braden Fiske as attacking interior d-linemen. • Poona Ford and Tyler Davis as capable run-stuffing nose tackles. — Albert Breer (@AlbertBreer) August 30, 2026 The Rams went into the season as a “super group” on the defensive line. Now they’re down to Byron Young as perhaps the only healthy player with a good track record who is having a good season. Davis has played 146 snaps this season and he has 15 tackles. He had 43 tackles last season and he has 1.5 sacks in 2.5 years. The Rams must continue to seek other options on the defensive line. NT Poona Ford – OUT NT – Ty Hamilton- IN Hamilton is another defensive lineman with a reputation for run defense, but not pass rushing ability. At least in this case, he’s replacing another player who can’t rush the passer. In fact, Ford might be the worst pass rusher at the nose tackle position in the entire league. Hamilton has great power and leverage but he has limited pass rushing moves and is known to over-pursue when he gets the chance to play, which is rarely. Ty Hamilton is a DT prospect in the 2025 draft class. He scored a 9.21 RAS out of a possible 10.00. This ranked 160 out of 2022 DT from 1987 to 2025. https://t.co/9QBkjJTkPP pic.twitter.com/OJqyWZePkF — RAS.football (@MathBomb) April 1, 2025 The Rams also have Larrell Murchison but he’s only appeared in one game. That’s sure to change. On the practice squad, the Rams have Bill Norton and Jaxson Moi.

summary: The Los Angeles Rams’ third kicker of this season is veteran free agent Brandon McManus. McManus […]
full_text: The Los Angeles Rams’ third kicker of this season is veteran free agent Brandon McManus. Technically, McManus will be the fourth because punter Ethan Evans kicked a PAT last week after Blake Grupe tore his ACL, but in any case the Rams continue to cycle through kickers like most people go through Brita filters. McManus is signing with the L.A. Rams immediately after he beat out Matt Prater in an audition for the job on Tuesday. He is set to be the Rams’ kicker against the Las Vegas Raiders on Sunday. The #Rams are signing veteran kicker Brandon McManus, per me and @MikeGarafolo , the latest in Los Angeles’ kicker saga. He worked out today, along with FA K Matt Prater. McManus most recently kicked for the #Packers and #Broncos . pic.twitter.com/eyzO9QmQjt — Ian Rapoport (@RapSheet) October 20, 2026 This will officially be the 13th season of McManus’s career. An undrafted free agent out of Temple in 2014, McManus spent his first nine years with the Denver Broncos, and he made 81.4% of his field goal attempts. He kicked for the Jacksonville Jaguars in 2023, then the Green Bay Packers in 2024 and 2025. He was 20-of-21 over 11 games with Green Bay in 2024, then 24-of-30 in 14 games last season. McManus immediately replaces Grupe and the recently-released Harrison Mevis. If he fails or gets injured, it looks like Prater could be the next man up and fans shouldn’t put it past L.A. to continue making moves at kicker this season. The only question is, when will this madness be settled with a real kicker?

title: What are the logistics of a Matthew Stafford trade?
summary: The Los Angeles Rams can not only still make the playoffs, their odds of being a wild card are not as bad as most people think despite being 2-4. However, if the Rams lose to the Las Vegas Raiders on Sunday, that likely ends the hope that most fans have for a successful season and […]
full_text: The Los Angeles Rams can not only still make the playoffs, their odds of being a wild card are not as bad as most people think despite being 2-4 . However, if the Rams lose to the Las Vegas Raiders on Sunday, that likely ends the hope that most fans have for a successful season and then the “fire sale” talk will really heat up. The top name on that list is Matthew Stafford. But could the Rams even trade Stafford if they wanted to? Stafford has to agree It doesn’t matter if Matthew Stafford has or doesn’t have a no-trade clause in his contract (the answer is unclear) because he could just refuse to go somewhere if the Rams trade him. He’s rich enough and accomplished enough at this point to just not show up. So if the Rams trade Stafford to the Browns, he may decide he doesn’t want to play in Cleveland. However, if he goes to the Vikings, Stafford may like the idea of reuniting with Kevin O’Connell and pairing with Justin Jefferson for a team that is 5-0. The Rams can’t just trade Stafford anywhere. It’s hard to believe he’d play for any team that he doesn’t want to play for at this point. Financials Stafford makes just under $1 million per game, so the acquiring team would be on the hook for a prorated portion of his $16 million base salary. He’s owed about $11 million for the rest of the season. The Rams would save that money, but they’d also get off the hook for the money they owe Stafford in 2027. That would be very beneficial for L.A. given the extraordinary number of 2027 free agents on the roster. Draft Pick Compensation The Rams don’t have a first-round pick in 2027 because of Myles Garrett. L.A. wouldn’t need to get a quarterback in return for the trade because they already have Ty Simpson and Stetson Bennett. The Rams would just want draft picks, probably starting with a first. If the Vikings feel that they’re going to reach the playoffs and make a decent run, then would it be worth it to give up pick 28 or 30 for a quarterback like Stafford? Minnesota probably isn’t thinking about replacing Kyler Murray right now though. That could change. The Giants were very interested in Stafford last year. Would he be willing to go play for John Harbaugh and pair with Malik Nabers? Would Stafford be open to playing for the Eagles, a recent Super Bowl winning team? Would he go back to the state of Georgia to help the Falcons and Kevin Stefanski? Or the Denver Broncos and Sean Payton? There are teams that should consider Stafford, but who would make the best offer? A first-round pick would likely have to be the starting point even if Stafford has struggled this season . Is it possible? It sure seems that way. The Rams are setup for a trade if they end up 2-5 or 2-6 because they already drafted Simpson and should pave the way for him in that case . However, should they do it? You can answer that question yourself by voting: Welcome to SB Nation Reacts, a survey of fans across the NFL. Throughout the year we ask questions of the most plugged-in Rams fans and fans across the country. Should the Rams trade Stafford? Are you confident in the Rams? Sign up here to participate in the weekly emailed surveys:
