title: Los Angeles’ best things to do, see, and eat before heading to a Rams game
summary: There are few NFL gameday experiences that can match the excitement of watching the Los Angeles Rams at SoFi Stadium. Located in the heart of Inglewood, California, the Rams’ home venue offers more than just football, providing fans with an opportunity to experience everything that Los Angeles has to offer. Whether you’re a lifelong Rams […]
full_text: Eric Thayer / Los Angeles Times via Getty Images There are few NFL gameday experiences that can match the excitement of watching the Los Angeles Rams at SoFi Stadium. Located in the heart of Inglewood, California, the Rams’ home venue offers more than just football, providing fans with an opportunity to experience everything that Los Angeles has to offer. Whether you’re a lifelong Rams fan making the trip to Southern California or a visiting supporter looking to experience an NFL game, planning ahead can make all the difference. Los Angeles is a city filled with entertainment, culture, and diverse attractions, giving fans plenty of ways to enjoy their weekend beyond the football field. From exploring popular destinations and experiencing the city’s nightlife to discovering the best neighborhoods to stay, there is no shortage of activities to fill your itinerary. The area’s diverse dining scene also provides countless options, ranging from iconic local restaurants to popular pregame destinations. Getting to SoFi Stadium requires some preparation, making transportation an important part of the gameday experience. Fans can also explore tailgating opportunities, connect with fellow supporters, and enjoy the electric atmosphere before kickoff. Once inside, SoFi Stadium delivers a state-of-the-art experience with impressive architecture, modern amenities, and unique features that make it one of the NFL’s premier venues. From weekend activities and accommodations to dining, transportation, tailgating, and stadium highlights, this guide covers everything Rams fans need to know to make the most of their gameday experience in Los Angeles. Things to do in Los Angeles Hollywood Park Casino is a convenient entertainment option for Rams fans staying near SoFi Stadium. Located in Inglewood, just minutes from the stadium, the casino offers table games, poker, dining, and a lively atmosphere before or after the game. Its location makes it an easy addition to a game-day weekend itinerary, particularly for visitors looking to stay close to the action. Fans can enjoy some entertainment without traveling far from SoFi Stadium, making Hollywood Park Casino a natural stop for those exploring the area around the Rams’ home. Santa Monica and the iconic Santa Monica Pier should be near the top of any Rams fan’s Los Angeles itinerary. Located along the Pacific Ocean, Santa Monica offers beautiful beaches, oceanfront views, shopping, entertainment, and a relaxed Southern California atmosphere. The historic pier is perhaps the area’s biggest attraction, featuring the famous Ferris wheel, amusement rides, games, restaurants, and spectacular views of the coastline. Visitors can walk along the pier, enjoy the beach, or explore the Third Street Promenade nearby. Whether you have a few hours or an entire afternoon, Santa Monica provides a memorable experience away from the football stadium. One of the reasons @J_Rey_11 loves LA? “You can make a vacation out here while you’re living out here.” Take on the Santa Monica Pier with We Love LA! | @AmericanAir pic.twitter.com/1BuWJKzmr5 — Los Angeles Rams (@RamsNFL) July 23, 2019 Venice Beach and Abbot Kinney Boulevard offer visitors a unique look at Los Angeles’ laid-back, eclectic culture. Venice Beach is famous for its sandy shoreline, lively boardwalk, street performers, Muscle Beach, and colorful atmosphere. Just a short distance away, Abbot Kinney Boulevard provides a different experience, featuring trendy restaurants, boutique shops, coffee houses, art galleries, and local businesses. The combination makes Venice an ideal destination for Rams fans looking to explore Southern California before or after gameday. Griffith Observatory is one of Los Angeles’ most iconic attractions and a great stop for Rams fans exploring the city. Located on the southern slope of Mount Hollywood, the observatory provides spectacular views of the Los Angeles skyline, Hollywood Sign, and surrounding area. Inside, visitors can explore fascinating exhibits focused on astronomy and space, while the facility’s telescopes offer opportunities to look toward the stars. The surrounding Griffith Park also provides hiking trails and scenic overlooks. For visitors wanting a combination of sightseeing, science, and unforgettable views, Griffith Observatory is a must-see destination. Plan your ultimate LA trip to Griffith Park! 🏔️ Home to 14 scenic peaks like Mount Hollywood, iconic film spots from La La Land & Rebel Without a Cause, and free entry to the Griffith Observatory grounds! 🔭 Stay close at Hollywood Stars Inn! 🏨 https://t.co/WVK4ToQwVF pic.twitter.com/QjjZjHy1m6 — Hollywood Stars Inn (@HwdStarsInn) September 30, 2026 The Getty Center is a must-see destination for visitors looking to experience Los Angeles’ art, architecture, and stunning scenery. Perched in the Santa Monica Mountains, the center features an impressive collection of European paintings, sculptures, photographs, and decorative arts. Beyond the galleries, visitors can enjoy beautifully landscaped gardens and panoramic views of Los Angeles. Its combination of world-class art, remarkable architecture, and breathtaking surroundings. Where to stay in Los Angeles If looking for convenience, the LAX hotel corridor around Century Boulevard offers a large selection of chain hotels and is particularly convenient for fans flying into Los Angeles. It’s also relatively close to SoFi, making it a practical choice for a short Rams weekend. El Segundo is one of my favorite choices for a Rams weekend. It offers restaurants, breweries, a walkable downtown, and proximity to both LAX and SoFi. You get more of a neighborhood feel than the airport corridor while remaining relatively close to the stadium. If you’re turning the Rams game into a full Southern California vacation, Manhattan Beach is an excellent option. You’ll have access to the beach, pier, restaurants and a classic South Bay atmosphere. The trade-off is a longer trip to SoFi on gameday. Manhattan beach, California pic.twitter.com/zHncUOwgPy — ✶ (@echoesofworld) March 29, 2026 Santa Monica is farther from SoFi, but it’s arguably the most appealing choice if you want the beach, restaurants, shopping and iconic Los Angeles attractions to be a major part of your trip. Just plan considerably more time for gameday transportation. Where to eat in Los Angeles Three Weavers Brewing Company is a popular Inglewood destination for Rams fans looking to enjoy a local craft beer before or after the game. Located near SoFi Stadium, the brewery offers a welcoming taproom and a rotating selection of beers brewed on-site. Its convenient location makes it an easy stop for visitors exploring the area around the stadium. Fiesta Martin Bar and Grill is a popular Mexican restaurant in Inglewood that can be a convenient dining option for Rams fans visiting SoFi Stadium. The restaurant offers a lively atmosphere alongside a menu filled with traditional Mexican favorites, making it a solid choice for a pregame meal or a casual stop during a game-day weekend. Its proximity to SoFi Stadium makes it especially appealing for visiting fans who want to enjoy a meal without venturing far from the action. With flavorful food, drinks, and a festive environment, Fiesta Martin helps capture the energy of an Inglewood game day. Roscoe’s House of Chicken and Waffles , known for its signature combination of crispy fried chicken and fluffy waffles, Roscoe’s has been serving hungry Angelenos for decades. The casual, welcoming atmosphere makes it an excellent option for breakfast, lunch, or a late-night meal. For visitors wanting to experience an iconic piece of Los Angeles food culture, Roscoe’s delivers a memorable and uniquely local dining experience. Dulan’s Soul Food Kitchen is a Los Angeles favorite for Rams fans looking to experience authentic Southern cooking. Known for generous portions and comforting classics, the restaurant serves dishes such as fried chicken, oxtails, macaroni…

title: Rams’ division title odds crushed after Monday night
summary: The Los Angeles Rams were already facing an uphill battle in the playoff picture after opening with a 2-4 record, but the San Francisco 49ers made those odds even slimmer after beating the Washington Commanders on Monday night. According to the latest playoff odds by ESPN, the Rams have a 35% chance to make the […]
full_text: The Los Angeles Rams were already facing an uphill battle in the playoff picture after opening with a 2-4 record, but the San Francisco 49ers made those odds even slimmer after beating the Washington Commanders on Monday night. According to the latest playoff odds by ESPN , the Rams have a 35% chance to make the postseason, and 34% of those odds come as a wild card. L.A. has less than a 1% chance to win the NFC West after starting 2-4 and the 49ers starting 6-0 with a win over the Rams. Perhaps the only silver lining is that the Rams still have better playoff odds than seven other teams in the NFC, with a large lead over the New York Giants, the closest team to them with worse odds at 16%. With San Francisco undefeated through six games, Los Angeles cannot afford any more setbacks if it hopes to claim a playoff spot. The Rams have 11 games to turn things around, but the 49ers’ fast start has made winning the NFC West a unlikely option. That means Los Angeles may need to shift its focus toward the NFC’s three wild-card spots. The expanded playoff format gives three non-division winners a postseason berth, but the competition is expected to be fierce as the season progresses. Teams that stumble early can quickly find themselves chasing multiple contenders for one of those coveted positions. The Rams must win in Week 7 against the Las Vegas Raiders. A victory would move Los Angeles closer to .500 and help prevent the gap between the Rams and the current NFC’s playoff contenders from growing any wider. Playoff chances for the NFC West, per @NextGenStats : 1. 49ers (5-0): 96% 2. Seahawks (3-3): 58% 3. Cardinals (2-4): 4% 4. Rams (2-4): 43% Are the Rams' chances … too high?! pic.twitter.com/f5L0qbNSQJ — Henry McKenna (@henrycmckenna) October 18, 2026 Current NFC Standings… #1 Seed: San Francisco 49ers (6-0) The 49ers are controlling the physicality of the NFC with a top 5 offense and defense. #2 Seed: Minnesota Vikings (5-0) The Vikings have a strong grip on the NFC North, with a two game lead over the Detroit Lions. The Vikings have divisional wins over the Bears and Packers. #3 Seed: New York Giants (3-2-1) The NFC East is a laughing stock as the the current starting quarterbacks are Jameis Winston, the often-hurt Jayden Daniels, Tanner McKee, and Dak Prescott. I foresee the Cowboys winning the division in the long run. If they don’t, Dak Prescott and the Cowboys may find themselves separating after the year. #4 Seed: Carolina Panthers (3-2) Carolina should be able to win the NFC South unless they suffer some sort of significant injury and Atlanta can gain ground. #5 Seed: Green Bay Packers (4-2) The Packers have heated up in the last three weeks but their SOS is only .457 and SOV is .375. #6 Seed: Chicago Bears (4-2) Chicago is probably the best team in the NFC North and it’ll be a matter of time to see if the Vikings can hold on in the NFC North once they play tougher teams. #7 Seed: Detroit Lions (3-2) The Lions have the easiest strength of schedule in the NFL so they will probably grab one of the three wild card spots. The Rams will need the Packers, Bears, or Seahawks to drop out out of the picture to grab the 6th or 7th seed. #8 Seed: Seattle Seahawks (3-3) The defending champions are on a two game slide after losses to the 49ers and Broncos. Next on tap for Seattle is Kansas City and Chicago… #9 Seed: Atlanta Falcons (2-4) #10 Seed: New Orleans Saints (2-4) #11 Seed: Philadelphia Eagles (2-4) #12 Seed: Dallas Cowboys (2-4) #13 Seed: Arizona Cardinals (2-4) #14 Seed: Los Angeles Rams (2-4) The Rams have not gotten out to a great start for the fourth consecutive year but they had to face a brutal first five game schedule (.712 SOS) that included a 18 hour trip to Melbourne, Australia. The road is much lighter in the middle of their schedule and should allow them to pick up steam. Even despite that, the Rams offense proves to be one of the best in the NFL while Aaron Donald and Myles Garrett get up to full speed by the midway point. San Francisco may in fact win the division because of their easy schedule but Los Angeles has their work cut out for themselves to earn the #5, #6, or #7 seed in the NFC.
author: Steven Ridings

title: Rams ‘dream season’ being derailed by poor play and injuries
summary: The Los Angeles Rams traded for Myles Garrett and Trent McDuffie not to be 2-4 through six weeks, but to compete for a Super Bowl. But the Rams plans have been derailed by poor play, penalties and injuries as the Rams continue to lose key pieces. Garrett hasn’t suited up since Week 1, McDuffie missed […]
full_text: INGLEWOOD, CA - OCTOBER 12: Davante Adams #17 of the Los Angeles Rams looks on from the sideline during the national anthem prior to an NFL football game against the Buffalo Bills at SoFi Stadium on October 12, 2026 in Inglewood, California. (Photo by Cooper Neill/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Los Angeles Rams traded for Myles Garrett and Trent McDuffie not to be 2-4 through six weeks, but to compete for a Super Bowl. But the Rams plans have been derailed by poor play, penalties and injuries as the Rams continue to lose key pieces. Garrett hasn’t suited up since Week 1, McDuffie missed week 6, Davante Adams is hurt, Aaron Donald has missed time, Jaylen Watson has missed time, Puka Nacua has missed time and more. Alaric Jackson was suspended so we’ll file that one under poor decision making. Either way, the Rams had a plan, and they are punching themselves in the mouth and need to come up with the new one. I am not saying the season is over, it’s not, but it’s currently being derailed, and it’s up to the Rams to get themselves back on track. Can they do it? Yes. Will they do it? We have to keep watching to find out. Rams star Kobie Turner likely going on IR due to groin injury (ramswire) “On top of that, star defensive lineman and team captain Kobie Turner will likely have to go on injured reserve , keeping him out of action for the near future. Turner injured his groin and will be out 4-6 weeks, according to Michael J. Duarte of the California Post. Turner played in only 23 snaps during Sunday’s loss to the Arizona Cardinals . That was the second-lowest out of the position group, with Ty Hamilton’s 18 snaps rounding out the count.“ Cardinals Have Sent Rams Into Full-Blown Meltdown After Week 6 Upset (sports.yahoo) “”Throughout the McVay era, beating the Cardinals was about as ‘sure’ as it gets. This was supposed to be a ‘get right’ game and start a run going into the bye. Instead, they lose 18-16 to a Cardinals team that had waved the white flag on this season,” wrote Rams On SI’s Blaine Grisak. The national stories aren’t about an incredible achievement from Arizona, who saw Mike LaFleur emerge as the second coach in NFL history to have his first two wins come on the road at the same stadium, but rather about how things are going sideways quickly in Los Angeles:“ Full list of Rams’ terrible injury updates following Week 6 loss (ramswire) “Davante Adams, Poona Ford, Kobie Turner and Blake Grupe all got injured in the game and will miss extended time, ranging from a few weeks to the rest of the season. When it rains, it pours, and it is torrential in Los Angeles right now. Here’s a full list of injury updates from McVay following Monday’s press conference.“ Davante Adams set for lengthy layoff as LA Rams rocked by injury blows (aol.com) “In his 13th NFL campaign, the 33-year-old wide receiver has recorded 30 catches for 480 yards and four touchdowns this year. Adams previously missed three late-season contests with a hamstring issue last year before coming back for postseason play. “It’s significant when you don’t have a player like Davante, but we have to be able to adjust,” McVay said. “His contributions can’t be measured. You don’t replace somebody like him, and so what you’ve got to do is you’ve got to be able to figure out what’s the next right thing? What does that look like in terms of our vision? We’ll have to adjust and adapt.” NFC West update: LA Rams in injury crisis mode with several long-term absences (fieldgulls) “It bodes well for Seattle, who—like Los Angeles have dropped back-to-back games and have looked like a shell of themselves as of late. However, it certainly helps one of the most dangerous forces in the NFC has as well. Despite the injury news, the Rams are set to take on the Las Vegas Raiders, Los Angeles Chargers, Washington Commanders and the Cardinals over their next four games—a favourable upcoming stretch of games by all means. Given the star power on their roster, it’s difficult to count Los Angeles out of the playoff picture, even nearing the halfway mark of the season, but there’s certainly work to be done if they want to keep up in the NFC race.“ What has gone wrong for the 2-4 Rams after ‘superteam’ hype? Can they fix it? (espn.com) “Well, the alarms are now going off in Los Angeles. On Sunday, the Rams lost 18-16 at home to a 1-4 Cardinals team , the sort of defeat that inspires soul searching and painful self-reflection. Any team can lose when the turnovers don’t bounce its way or an injury unexpectedly costs it a key player, but neither of those were the case against Arizona. And while the Rams lost new kicker Blake Grupe to an early-game knee injury , special teams weren’t really to blame for the loss, either. Are the 2-4 Rams, who were the prohibitive favorites to win the Super Bowl after acquiring Myles Garrett and Trent McDuffie and bringing Aaron Donald out of retirement this offseason, just not very good? Do we know enough after six games to say with confidence that the superteam Rams we expected to see heading into the season aren’t ever going to show up on the field in 2026? Is it time to write them off as Super Bowl contenders? One thing I can say for sure: To live up to the preseason hype and win the Super Bowl, the Rams will have to do something no NFL team has ever done before. If the Rams even make it to the Super Bowl, they would be the first team in NFL history to post a losing record through six weeks and still manage to win its conference in the Super Bowl era. Playing in an era with a 17-game regular season and 14 playoff teams makes a potential turnaround a little easier for the Rams, but they would have to break 60 years of precedent to overcome this slow start.“ 3 takeaways from Rams’ rash of major injuries suffered in Week 6 (ramswire) “With all their losses, here are three takeaways on what they mean for the Rams. Nacua needs to be at his absolute best Puka Nacua will be called upon even more with Adams being out for an estimated 6-10 weeks . In the last year of his deal, Nacua has found his form in recent weeks and is making the ultimate push to become the NFL’s highest-paid non-quarterback.“ Legendary band to play Rams-Packers halftime show on Thanksgiving Eve (sports.yahoo) “Netflix announced on Tuesday that legendary rock band U2 will play the halftime show during the Los Angeles Rams ‘ game against the Green Bay Packers on Thanksgiving Eve. That game takes place at SoFi Stadium in Inglewood, bringing the iconic band to the Rams’ house for a special performance. It’s the NFL’s first game ever on Thanksgiving Eve, and it comes after the Rams’ Week 11 bye. Kickoff is set for 8 p.m. ET and will be streamed live on Netflix, just as the Rams’ season opener against the 49ers was. U2, led by Bono and The Edge, have won 22 Grammy Awards, including Best Album for The Joshua Tree in 1987.“ Rams’ devasting wave of Week 6 injuries might be the final blow (ramblinfan) “Defensive tackle Kobie Turner: groin injury. Out four to six weeks, per ESPN’s Adam Schefter. Kicker Blake Grupe: torn ACL. Done for the year. title: Raiders overreaction to 33-30 loss to the Bills
summary: If you’re expecting a the season is over, fire everyone and trade the draft picks for a player to be named, you’ve come to the wrong place. In the last three games against the Kansas City Chiefs, the New England Patriots and the Buffalo Bills, the Las Vegas Raiders’ offense has put up an average […]
full_text: (Photo by Christian Petersen/Getty Images) If you’re expecting a the season is over, fire everyone and trade the draft picks for a player to be named, you’ve come to the wrong place. In the last three games against the Kansas City Chiefs, the New England Patriots and the Buffalo Bills, the Las Vegas Raiders’ offense has put up an average of 24.66 points. Defensively, they have allowed an average of 36 points. While many will point to needing more offense, the real problem lies in protecting the quarterback, opening holes for the running back and defending the line of scrimmage. Four plays that cost them the game Obviously, the backhanded flip for a touchdown from Buffalo Bills quarterback Josh Allen to Keon Coleman, where he shook every man on the defensive line at least twice before all defenders abandoned their responsibilities. Was a thing of beauty where as a fan of the sport you just have to acknowledge that Allen is a bad bad man. The play-action pass to James Cook in the flat, where every defender keyed on the misdirection from the Bills offensive line and completely vacated one sideline of the field. This allowed him a free pass all the way down to the three-yard line. Where the Bills would score on a three-yard run after pushing the entire defense into the end zone. Kirk Cousins’ interception, thrown into the robber look. On a play where he clearly expected the linebacker to trail Brock Bowers in man coverage. When the defender squatted in his zone, the pass meant for Michael Mayer was thrown right to him. The last one was a pass at the goal line to Cody White, which was too low and ultimately resulted in the Raiders having to kick a field goal instead of getting a touchdown. Losing out on four extra points which stands out in a three-point loss. Coaching matters but execution matters more Against the Bills, once again, the game plan was nearly flawless on both sides. Bend but don’t break was the approach taken by Raiders defensive coordinator Rob Leonard. His defense forced the Bills into four field goals and 4/11 on third-down conversions. The only real legitimate gripe that leapt out was the inexperience and on-the-job learning of the young defensive backfield. Experience is only acquired one way, they have to go through it to get to it. On the defensive line, you saw the Raiders play Allen and Cook about as well as anyone in the league has done all season. The defensive line fenced off the pocket and kept Allen inside of it. He ran the ball five times for 1 yard, was sacked twice, was under constant pressure and threw off his back foot a lot. In 22 rushes, the reigning rushing leader, Cook, was held under 100 yards on the ground. As a team they collected 103 total rushing yards. Offensively, the mixing and matching of the running backs was beneficial and the running game started to show signs of life for the Raiders. Once again, Mike Washington Jr. proved he should be the number one back from now until Ashton Jeanty is 100%. He ran the ball nine times for 43 yards, featuring runs of 14 and 18 yards. Tre Tucker has proven that not only can he catch the football diving to the ground, but he can also run past defenders if you throw it far enough. His diving catch for a 44-yd touchdown on the Cousins’ best pure throw of the season was marvelous. Michael Mayer had his best game of the season, catching seven of nine targets for 95 yards and an average of 13.6 yards per catch. Nearly every catch he made was a third-down conversion. He was the garbage man out there, cleaning up the field. Final thoughts The Raiders are going to beat the teams that they should, and find ways to come up just short of beating teams with better superstars. As a team, the Raiders are playing damn good ball, but when they run up against the league’s best, who just find ways to do the unimaginable, they just haven’t quite figured out ways to stop it yet. Left guard is more of a position to be experimenting with, not the right guard. Kolton Miller had a better game, but Caleb Rogers had some struggles on the right side, as well as some successes. This ended up being another winnable game for the Raiders that they just couldn’t figure out how to win. Playing good teams tough and being in it until the end sounds cool and all, but moral victories don’t count.
author: Philip Robinson

title: Kirk Cousins draws praise in Week 7 NFL Power Rankings roundup despite Las Vegas Raiders’ 3-game losing streak
summary: The Las Vegas Raiders are in the midst of a three-game losing streak after falling to the Buffalo Bills 33-30 on Sunday. However, that didn’t impact the Raiders’ standing in the Week 7 NFL Power Rankings roundup, as many in the media are giving quarterback Kirk Cousins his flowers. Bleacher Report 18. Las Vegas Raiders […]
full_text: (Photo by Cooper Neill/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Las Vegas Raiders are in the midst of a three-game losing streak after falling to the Buffalo Bills 33-30 on Sunday. However, that didn’t impact the Raiders’ standing in the Week 7 NFL Power Rankings roundup, as many in the media are giving quarterback Kirk Cousins his flowers. Bleacher Report 18. Las Vegas Raiders Last Week: 18 Here’s how most people expected this season to go for the Raiders: Kirk Cousins would open the season as the starter under center, but as the losses mounted, the reins in the offense would be handed to rookie No. 1 overall pick Fernando Mendoza. The Raiders have dropped three straight, but don’t hold your breath waiting for Mendoza to take over. For the second time in three weeks, the Raiders gave an AFC heavyweight all they could handle in Week 6. Cousins was a big reason why, lighting up the Bills for 313 passing yards. It’s going to come down to the Raiders’ priorities. Once the team’s unlikely postseason hopes have been dashed, then odds are we’ll see Mendoza take over. But given how feisty these Raiders have been to date, those playoff aspirations may be around a while longer than we thought. — Gary Davenport Davenport is correct in that the 3-0 start has altered the timeline (or at least expectation) of when the rookie will take over behind center in Las Vegas. But it does feel like this weekend could be a swing game, even though the team would only be one game below .500 and still in playoff contention if it doesn’t leave Los Angeles with a win. A loss to a struggling and hobbled Los Angeles Rams would make it four in a row for the Raiders, meaning they aren’t able to beat the best teams they’ve played even when Cousins is playing well. At that point, the postseason odds become very bleak, and it might be time to start focusing on 2027 and beyond for the rest of 2026. The Athletic 18. Las Vegas Raiders Last Week: 17 Fantasy focus: Kirk Cousins The 38-year-old quarterback just keeps hanging on, but the calls for No. 1 pick Fernando Mendoza will get louder after the Raiders dropped their third straight game Sunday. That’s not necessarily Cousins’ fault, though. He is 29th in fantasy scoring (18.5 ppg) after being drafted No. 264 overall. Tight end Brock Bowers is once again pacing the Raiders offense. He’s 13th in scoring (20.6 ppg). — Josh Kendall, Chad Graff This basically reiterates the point above. Cousins is playing well, but at some point, the organization’s and coaching staff’s focus needs to shift to the future. Getting over the hump and taking down the Rams this Sunday will buy the veteran quarterback and the Raiders’ playoff hopes some time, but the club has used up all of its moral victories when it comes to the current starting lineup and the outlook for the 2026 season. Sports Illustrated 19. Las Vegas Raiders Last Week: 16 Piggybacking on [the Browns potentially trading for a quarterback], an interesting thought experiment: What if the Raiders decided that Fernando Mendoza was ready? Would the Browns be at all interested in having Cousins back up/challenge Deshaun Watson for snaps down the stretch, especially if Cleveland keeps gutting out victories? — Conor Orr In my opinion, this feels more like a fantasy idea than a trade that can actually happen. I have a hard time seeing Kubiak sending away Mendoza’s mentor right after making the rookie the starter. Part of the reason Cousins was brought in was to add a veteran voice to the quarterback room, giving Mendoza another person to turn to for advice. In other words, Cousins would still provide value to the team even if he isn’t on the field. Also, while Watson isn’t exactly lighting it up in Cleveland, I have a hard time seeing the Browns trade for a quarterback and have that quarterback pick up Todd Monken’s offense quickly enough to make a change, especially since the team is winning. NFL.com 18. Las Vegas Raiders Last Week: 19 Another tough loss marked the Raiders’ third straight defeat, dropping them from a 3-0 start to 3-3 after six weeks. For some teams, this might be a sign of crisis. These Raiders, however, have proven competitive in two of those three losses, going blow for blow with two AFC titans in the Chiefs and Bills. This is part of the process of evolving from cellar-dweller to aspiring contender, in which the upstart learns how to win the close battles against proven teams. Las Vegas has received a couple of good lessons in this department recently, while Kirk Cousins continues to thrive. There are no moral victories, but there are degrees of losses, and this one appears more favorable than others. — Nick Shook I like this assessment of where the franchise is heading. Would it have been better to pull off upsets instead of losing by three points to the Chiefs and Bills? Absolutely, no one is arguing that. But the Silver and Black are at least making strides and are clearly a better team than they were last year. Rome wasn’t built in a day, and remember, Kansas City took pity on Vegas in the first meeting last season. The Chiefs didn’t even throw the ball in the fourth quarter and took a knee before the two-minute warning, and that was a bad Chiefs team for their standards. ESPN 18. Las Vegas Raiders Last Week: 17 Biggest issue on offense: Run blocking Las Vegas signed center Tyler Linderbaum with the expectation that he would fix the team’s run-blocking issues from last season. Instead, those have continued, especially Sunday, when the Raiders totaled just 65 rushing yards. The unit struggled containing the Bills’ offensive line; Linderbaum had a hard time blocking defensive tackle Deone Walker. Caleb Rogers, who started at right guard over Jackson Powers-Johnson, also whiffed on a block that led to Ashton Jeanty being stopped for a 3-yard loss at the goal line in the fourth quarter. — Ryan McFadden Fair or not, Linderbaum was supposed to be the catalyst to solve this problem, hence the record-setting contract. Instead, the results are about the same, and the center has been average to slightly above average. But don’t take my word for it; take his. Linderbaum was very candid about his performance against the Bills and said he “has to play better for the team.”

title: Las Vegas’ best things to do, see, and eat before heading to a Raiders game
summary: The Raiders are considered one of the “nomads of the NFL” for good reason. The franchise has moved four times and called three different cities home (Oakland, Los Angeles, Oakland again, and now Las Vegas). The Las Vegas Raiders have spent seven seasons in their new location, which happens to be one of the biggest […]
full_text: Kyle Terada-USA TODAY Sports | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The Raiders are considered one of the “nomads of the NFL” for good reason. The franchise has moved four times and called three different cities home (Oakland, Los Angeles, Oakland again, and now Las Vegas). The Las Vegas Raiders have spent seven seasons in their new location, which happens to be one of the biggest tourist destinations in the country. Whether it’s Raiders fans from Oakland, Los Angeles, another part of the world, or opposing fans looking to attend an away game, that leads to many circling a date to visit Las Vegas in the fall. But where should you stay, what is there to do, where should you eat, and how do you get to the game in the “Entertainment Capital of the World”? Places to stay in Las Vegas The Strip is the most convenient choice. Allegiant Stadium technically isn’t on The Strip, but it’s right off of it. If you’re the fancy type, Mandalay Bay is a good choice since it’s close to the stadium, while the Luxor and Excalibur are in the same vicinity but are more budget-friendly options. However, just about any hotel on The Strip is going to get pricey during a game weekend. So, you might want to look into places like the Holiday Inn Express or Staybridge Suites, which are off The Strip to help save some money but still within walking distance to Allegiant. If you want to escape the hustle and bustle of Las Vegas, the M Resort in Henderson is actually the official team headquarters hotel for the Raiders. It’s a lot quieter and near the team’s practice facility, though you will need a car to get to the game. The M also has a Raiders-themed restaurant in it. Another thing to consider: The Strip is considered a “tourist trap”. Most locals stay away from it because everything is marked up, including the table minimums at the casino. There’s a lot more going on there, but you’re going to pay a premium for it. Things to do in Las Vegas Well, it’s Vegas, baby! Of course, there are casinos everywhere you look. Even if you aren’t a gambler typically, there is a “when in Rome” type of vibe to Las Vegas where people put at least a few bucks on the table or in a slot machine with the hopes of paying for their trip and/or bringing home some extra cash. Just remember, those palaces weren’t built on winners! Also, there are plenty of shows to catch if you’re looking for something on the entertainment side. You can find pretty much any sort of live entertainment that you can think of, ranging from the acrobatics of Cirque du Soleil to comedy and magic. Additionally, the Sphere is a newer venue that typically has some type of concert, live event or movie going on . It just depends on what they have scheduled during your visit. So, there’s a chance what’s going on at the Sphere during the time of your visit isn’t something you’re interested in. But the venue and experience itself is worth checking out, and it’s more family-friendly than the casino or most shows. On that note, the Mandalay Bay hotel has an aquarium , and Circus Circus has a theme park in it if you’re traveling with and looking for something to do with your kids. Additionally, there are several different options to tour the Grand Canyon , which is about a two- to two-and-a-half hour drive from Vegas, or the Hoover Dam , a 45-minute to an hour drive. To be honest, you’d have to try pretty hard to be bored in Las Vegas… Best places to eat in Las Vegas If you’re on the Strip, you can find just about any type of restaurant you’re looking for. Not only does it cover every cuisine (sushi, BBQ, Italian, etc.), but it also ranges from recognizable fast food options to local steakhouses. Granted, it might be some of the most expensive fast food you’ll ever pay for, but that’s just the Strip. If it’s your first time out west, it’s a requirement to stop at In-N-Out for a burger. There’s a location on the Strip, as well as a handful in the surrounding areas. My go-to order is a three-by-three (three patties and three slices of cheese) with grilled onions and extra spread (their 1000 Island-like sauce), fries and a chocolate-strawberry milkshake. I will say In-N-Out’s fries are underwhelming, but the burgers and shakes are top-notch. Sometimes, I’ll skip the fries and just do two burgers. Also, make sure to check out the “ not so secret menu ” and ask for well-done fries if you like them crispy. Additionally, there are plenty of buffets. The go-to, in my opinion, is the one at the Bellagio . However, it’s only open from 8:00 a.m. to 2:00 p.m. during the week and dinner is only available on the weekend — Saturday Seafood dinner ($69.99) and Sunday ($59.99). A weekday brunch will run you about $45 a person, and it’s about $50 on the weekend. Children under five get in free, and six to 11 are half off. That’s expensive for a buffet, but it isn’t your typical buffet food, and it has cuisine options from all over the world. In the mood for something fancier? Gallagher’s Steakhouse in the New York New York hotel is my top choice. I’ve also heard good things about TENDER Steakhouse in the Luxor (which is a more affordable option for a steakhouse), and SW Steakhouse in the Wynn (one of the pricier options). If you want to get away from the Strip (and save some money), Eater has 18 places to eat that are away from the touristy part of town. Two of the more popular options are Esther’s Kitchen and Herbs & Rye . Allegiant Stadium parking, rideshare, and transit options It depends on where you’re staying, even if you’re on the Strip, since it’s over four miles long. Allegiant Stadium is on the very South end of the Strip. So, if you’re at Mandalay Bay, Luxor, Excalibur, MGM Grand or Aria, it’s an easy walk. Also, there are several pedestrian bridges to make the trek safer and avoid traffic. You can’t miss them either, as the bridges are right in your face. If you’re staying in the middle or the north end of the Strip, the Las Vegas Monorail is a great option to get to the game. Its final station on the south side is at MGM, where you just have to make that short walk, and there are seven stations where you can catch it along the Strip. Children under five years old can ride for free, and single rides for everyone else start at $5. You can also just buy a full-day pass if you want to use the monorail to explore the city, too. If you’re not on the Strip at all, check the RTC website for a few options to take a bus to the game. They have pickup and return options throughout the surrounding areas, including at the M Resort mentioned above, North Las Vegas and near Summerlin. It’s only $4 for a round trip and drops you off right at the stadium. Otherwise, there are always plenty of Ubers, Lyfts or taxis available to get you there. Just be aware of surge pricing. Tailgating at Allegiant Stadium To be honest, the Raiders sacrificed a good tailgate scene when the franchise moved from Oakland to Las Vegas. The B Lot barbeques are a thing of the past, and there simply isn’t enough real estate where Allegiant Stadium is located to have an old-school tailgate. The Raiders do have a ‘ Modelo Tailgate Zone ’ that’s free to enter and has different activities going on, a variety of food and beer/cocktail options, and NFL RedZone playing if you want to hang out in the stadium parking lot before the game. But it’s not nearly the party Oakland tailgates were back in the day. To put it in perspective, the Oakland Coliseum has about 10,000 parking spaces while Allegiant has just 2,700. Essentially, the move to Vegas swapped out a traditional tailgate experience for a unique one with the casinos on the Strip. The Allegiant Stadium Experience If you’re looking to enhance your experience at the game, Allegiant Stadium has several premium clubs and lounges available . They vary from field-level experiences to 200-level options with table seating. You just have to be willing to open up your wallet pretty wide to have those experiences. When you get hungry and/or…

title: Foster Moreau comes up big in crazy Houston Texans win
summary: Week 6 had the Las Vegas Raiders dropping their third straight game, falling to the Buffalo Bills 33-30. But let’s see how the weekend fared for a few old friends: Foster Moreau, Davante Adams and Tre’von Moehrig. Foster Moreau Score: 34-31 Texans win Stats: 2 catches, 7 yards, 2 TDs This was a crazy game […]
full_text: (Photo by Johnnie Izquierdo/Getty Images) | Getty Images Week 6 had the Las Vegas Raiders dropping their third straight game , falling to the Buffalo Bills 33-30 . But let’s see how the weekend fared for a few old friends: Foster Moreau, Davante Adams and Tre’von Moehrig. Foster Moreau Score: 34-31 Texans win Stats: 2 catches, 7 yards, 2 TDs This was a crazy game across the pond to get Sunday started, with the Houston Texans getting a huge divisional win to keep their hopes of an AFC South title alive. Moreau was a big part of that, hauling in a pair of scores as a red zone threat. Granted, those were his only targets in the game, as the 2019 fourth-round pick continues to be a blocking tight end in Houston. Including Sunday, Moreau has 11 catches for 72 yards and three touchdowns this season. Maybe I only find this interesting but the Jags call timeout just before the snap and CJ Stroud still throws it to Foster Moreau and he casually catches the ball with one hand. And then they run the real play after the timeout… pic.twitter.com/eDaDKDmM3Z — Goodberry (@JoeGoodberry) October 18, 2026 Davante Adams Score: 18-16 Rams lose Stats: 3 catches, 39 yards It’s been a while since we’ve checked in on Adams, and now feels like a good time to see how the campaign is going for the wideout. Short answer: not well. The Los Angeles Rams are easily the NFL’s biggest disappointment at 2-4, and dropping a game to the Arizona Cardinals on Sunday feels like the icing on that cake. Meanwhile, Adams had a productive two-game stretch in Weeks 2 and 3, with 23 catches for 332 yards and two touchdowns in those contests. However, he’s been held below 55 yards in every other game. On top of that, Adams ruptured a hamstring and will be out for the next six to 10 weeks, according to The Athletic’s Nate Atkins , meaning the former Raider will miss next week’s revenge game. Tre’von Moehrig Score: 25-14 Panthers win Stats: 4 tackles, 0.5 sack, 1 TFL, 2 QB hits This was a big win for the Carolina Panthers, taking down the Philadelphia Eagles to move to 3-2 and sit atop the NFC South standings. Meanwhile, Moehrig managed to make an impact in a few areas of the defense. He’s been having a solid year, collecting 17 tackles in five games and two run stuffs. The 2021 second-round pick has yet to record a PBU or interception in 2026, though.

full_text: (Photo by Christian Petersen/Getty Images) | Getty Images Here is a look at how the Las Vegas Raiders’ 2026 draft class (eight of the 10 picks are on the 53-man roster) fared in a 33-30 home loss to the Buffalo Bills on Sunday and what to look for Sunday at home against the Los Angeles Rams. Washington had 43 yards on nine carries and had two runs of 10-pus yards. Getting Washington more involved is key to igniting the Raiders stagnant running game. Dalton Johnson: The fifth-round pick safety was inactive for the fifth team in six games. Zeke Masses: The fifth-round pick played is definitely not a starter anymore, losing his job to Darien Porter, who began the season as a starter before losing his job to Masses briefly. Masses played just 19 percent of the snaps after playing 33 percent in Week 5. He was mostly in dime packages against Buffalo and was benched after pass interference call. Let’s see how much he plays against the Rams. Malik Benson: The sixth-round pick played played just eight offensive snaps with no targets. The training camp star has two catches for 12 yards on eight targets this season.

full_text: ATLANTA, GEORGIA - OCTOBER 26: Storm Duck #36 of the Miami Dolphins lines up against the Atlanta Falcons during the second quarter of the game between the Miami Dolphins and Atlanta Falcons at Mercedes-Benz Stadium on October 26, 2025 in Atlanta, Georgia. (Photo by Kevin C. Cox/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Miami Dolphins’ roster continues to be in constant flux under the leadership of new general manager Jon-Eric Sullivan. On Tuesday, the team signed a new kicker — Zane Gonzalez — while releasing incumbent Riley Patterson. In addition to that roster shuffle, the team also released a familiar name who hadn’t seen the field in 2026, but played a significant role in the team’s defensive backfield rotation in past years. Cornerback Storm Duck was released from Miami’s physically unable to perform list after practicing fully for the past two weeks. In early 2025, Duck suffered a major knee injury which cost him most of last season. He was still working his way into playing shape when the Dolphins gave him his walking papers Tuesday morning. After signing with Miami as an undrafted free agent ahead of the 2024 NFL season, Duck played 14 games for the Dolphins as a rookie. He totaled 35 tackles and four passes defensed during his first season with the club. Last year, Duck played in just two games before his season-ending knee injury, making two tackles and having one pass defense during that stretch. In addition to Miami’s move at kicker, the team announced that they waived EDGE Andre Jones Jr., while signing rookie EDGE Rodney McGraw to the active roster from the team’s practice squad.

title: Miami’s best things to do, see, and eat before heading to a Dolphins game
summary: Are you heading to your first Miami Dolphins game? Have you been to many, but maybe never explored the South Florida area? It is time to help you get a better idea of what to expect in and around Miami, as well as give you some tips to make sure you have a great time. […]
full_text: MIAMI GARDENS, FL - FEBRUARY 02: A general view of Hard Rock stadium is seen in game action during the Super Bowl LIV game between the Kansas City Chiefs and the San Francisco 49ers on February 2, 2020 at Hard Rock Stadium, in Miami Gardens, FL. (Photo by Robin Alam/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Are you heading to your first Miami Dolphins game? Have you been to many, but maybe never explored the South Florida area? It is time to help you get a better idea of what to expect in and around Miami, as well as give you some tips to make sure you have a great time. Where should you stay? What is there to eat or do outside of the game? We take a look at some of the best areas around Miami and the surrounding region to give you an idea of how to turn a Dolphins game into a great weekend – or longer – in South Florida. If you are local to the area or have been to several Dolphins games and want to share your ideas, feel free to jump into the comments and help your fellow Dolphins fans get the best information for an epic experience. Oh, and before we get into anything else about your travel to a Dolphins game, let me give you one major piece of advice. Do not fly into Miami International Airport. Just do not do it. It is a poorly designed airport with way too many people, and it needs upgrades. Use Fort Lauderdale-Hollywood International Airport instead. You are north of the stadium, but the distance from Hard Rock Stadium to both airports is almost the same, and avoiding Miami International is worth it. Even if you plan to stay in Miami, using Fort Lauderdale-Hollywood is still the right move. Places to stay in Miami The first thing to know about traveling to a Dolphins game is that Hard Rock Stadium is not in Miami. It is in Miami Gardens, northwest of Miami itself. It is about 20 miles from Miami and places like South Beach and Miami Beach. Depending on your travel plans and your goals for the trip will determine where you want to find a hotel. Miami Gardens and Hard Rock Stadium If your focus is solely on the game, staying near Miami Gardens can simplify the weekend and help you avoid Miami and the beach area’s congestion. You will trade off some of the culture and food of being down in Miami itself. The Stadium Hotel, about a mile north of the stadium, is a convenient option. It is listed as a three-star hotel, but it exceeds expectations. You can walk to the stadium from here, which saves on parking, which we will discuss later. A little further down the road, about 3.5 miles from the stadium, there are a Hampton Inn & Suites and a SpringHill Suites, both listed as Fort Lauderdale/Miramar if you look them up. These are decent, affordable options that get you close to the stadium Fort Lauderdale This is my go-to when I travel for a game: stay in Fort Lauderdale and drive down to Miami Gardens. It is a little further away, but I have found it fairly simple. Even going over toward the beachside, it is pretty quick to get down to the stadium. The area has plenty of options for all budgets. Whether you want a smaller, local hotel or a larger brand-name stay, you can find it. Of course, I have to mention the experience of staying in the area. The Seminole Hard Rock Casino in Hollywood, Florida, about midway between Fort Lauderdale and Hard Rock Stadium, is an amazing option. It is going to push your budget (a lot), but the Guitar Hotel is iconic and it is an option out there for you. Aventura and Sunny Isles Beach North of Miami, east of Miami Gardens, the Aventura and Sunny Isles Beach area mixes a football-focused weekend with a Miami vacation that includes football. You have beaches, shopping, restaurants, and the waterfront, while being about 10 miles from the stadium. Traffic will, of course, pick up ahead of the game, but it is a good compromise for trying to do everything that Miami offers. Aventura is good for shopping and dining options. Sunny Isles Beach can provide you with oceanfront views and beach experiences. You can also check out condominiums along with standard hotels in the area. Downtown Miami and Brickell If you want a Miami weekend, you should probably stay in Miami. You can still get to Hard Rock Stadium, but expect there to be an increased travel time. You are probably around 15 miles south of the stadium now. You will have more restaurants, cocktail bars, and entertainment options than you can use. This is a great area for a group trip, with something for everyone. Brickell has upscale dining options and plenty of entertainment. You can also quickly move around all of the diverse neighborhoods of Miami, as well as head over to the beaches. Miami Beach If you have never been to the area and want the “Miami” experience that you have seen on TV and in the movies, you are probably going to want to head over to Miami Beach. This is where you will get the white sand beaches, Art Deco buildings, oceanfront dining, and everything you think of when you think Miami. You will be right in the middle of the tourist area, close to the beaches, and where all the action is. Especially if you are around South Beach. If you want to stay in the area but find something a little quieter, head north to Mid-Beach. You are probably out closer to 20 miles from the stadium now, and you will see the travel time tick up. Things to do in Miami Miami is unique, with a cultural blend of many different people, and it offers just about anything you want. From the beaches to the nightlife, there is so much to do in Miami and the surrounding area that you could build an entire itinerary for the weekend, and still come up short on seeing everything you wanted to see. Beaches The beaches are, of course, a major draw. South Beach will be the starting point for many first-time visitors to the area, but do not be afraid to explore other, probably less crowded, beach options. That said, a walk around the Art Deco District around South Beach is worth visiting. Little Havana Moving out to Little Havana brings you into the Cuban heritage that shapes so much of Miami. The food, the music, the art- it could be the highlight of your Miami visit, aside from the Dolphins game, of course. Get some coffee – but be careful. Cafecito is…strong. Maybe do not drink several of them. Wynwood and the Design District Northeast of Little Havana is Wynwood. Have you ever seen pictures or TV shows that highlight the murals on walls in Miami? That is Wynwood. Absolutely a beautiful art exhibition on outdoor murals. Plus, the causal dining in the area is great and you are going to get amazing pictures of your trip. Continue north to the Design District. Public art continues here, but the architecture adds a little more, so the pictures will be amazing. It is going to feel a little more upscale and polished than Wynwood, plus there is some great shopping in the area. If you want to get away from the beach, Wynwood and the Design District (and Little Havana) are definitely places to visit. Biscayne Bay But if you want the waterfront, Biscayne Bay is an amazing option. You can take boat tours to see the Miami skyline and celebrity homes. You can go snorkeling or scuba diving. You can jet ski. You can head over to Biscayne National Park – essentially an underwater national park. You can just walk around the area. Nightlife Clubs, lounges, rooftop bars, dinner, parties on the beach, music, dancing, whatever you want to do, Miami can provide it. Wherever you choose to stay during your trip, there is going to be plenty to do. Other options If you are staying in the area for more than just the Dolphins game and you want to explore Florida, here are some other options to consider. Florida Keys – heading out to the Keys, whether you go to Key Largo (about 90 minutes from Hard Rock Stadium) or all the way to Key West (3.5 hours from HRS), the Keys have bars, beaches, and photo oppotunities. Orlando – A trip north to Orlando takes about 3 hours, but it offers all the…

title: Tuesday Miami Dolphins Thoughts With The Earl
summary: The Miami Dolphins got a HUGE win this week by not losing to anyone.  It’s a small victory in a season that will lack them, but it’s one we’ll have to take.  The Dolphins will be coming off the bye hoping to get healthy, stay healthy, and build some momentum in the development of the […]
full_text: MIAMI GARDENS, FLORIDA - OCTOBER 11: Malik Willis #2 of the Miami Dolphins warms up before a game against the Cincinnati Bengals at Hard Rock Stadium on October 11, 2026 in Miami Gardens, Florida. (Photo by Carmen Mandato/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Miami Dolphins got a HUGE win this week by not losing to anyone. It’s a small victory in a season that will lack them, but it’s one we’ll have to take. The Dolphins will be coming off the bye hoping to get healthy, stay healthy, and build some momentum in the development of the young players. Since there were no game observations this week, I thought I would take a look at the roster and compare each position group to where they were at the beginning of the season to now and whether they are trending up or down. QUARTERBACK – TRENDING DOWN The struggles of Malik Willis have been documented far and wide. I think this video explains it best . RUNNING BACK – TRENDING UP The Dolphins lost superstar De’Von Achane, but Ollie Gordon II has stepped up to fill the void. The sophomore runner is averaging 5.0 YPC and has 3 rushing TDs on the season, one in each game he has started or played a prominent role. The Dolphins will continue to be a run-oriented team, and the success of that venture will be determined by OG2. Wright has struggled in limited reps and needs to step up. The Dolphins also acquired Kaytron Allen from the Commanders via the waiver wire. He is another physical, downhill runner which may indicate the Dolphins have a type at RB. WIDE RECEIVER – TRENDING EVEN Caleb Douglas had a breakout game in week 1 but was lost with an ankle injury in week 2 and hasn’t been seen since. His absence was felt as the passing game didn’t have a go-to player. Fellow rookie Chris Bell has had his moments but has been inconsistent. Kevin Coleman Jr. has started getting more reps and was the first of the 3 rookies to score a TD. The reason this group isn’t trending down is the play of Malik Washington. He’s not a star player, but he has been doing his job, even if it only shows up on the tape and not in the box score. He should have had a couple of scores already but was simply missed by the QB. TIGHT END – TRENDING DOWN I predicted that Greg Dulcich would surpass 1000 yards this season . He’s on pace for less than 500 yards. I am utterly shocked that the TE position has been underutilized as much as it has. Dulcich is tied with Kevin Coleman in targets with 17, but with the QB struggling, this position could offer some help. Will Kacmarek is a forceful blocker and has added some receptions. But that’s it. Perhaps after the bye, they can start incorporating more targets to receiving TEs Seydou Traore and waiver wire addition Justin Joly. There is some potential in this group, but it isn’t materializing. OFFENSIVE TACKLE – TRENDING EVEN Patrick Paul is trending up. He’s had some rough moments in games, but he is tied for 12th in pass block win rate at 90%. He is turning the corner to becoming a franchise left tackle. Austin Jackson has been abysmal to this point and is trending down. He has been a complete liability in pass protection. His issues in the past were about injuries. He has played every snap thus far but played them mostly poorly. The Dolphins may shop him at the trade deadline to see what they can get. I’m not sure if Caedan Wallace is ready, but we all know that Jackson is not the answer and will not be a Dolphin past 2026. OFFENSIVE GUARD – TRENDING UP The weakness of the offensive line in recent years is turning into a strength. Rookie Kadyn Proctor is a people mover and is getting better each week. Sophomore Jonah Savaiinaea has been much improved. He unfortunately went down with an ankle injury in the last game, but it sounds like he’ll be ready to go. However, waiver wire OL Jarrett Kingston stepped right into the RG role after Savaiinaea left and the OL didn’t miss a beat. Quality starters at OG and good depth? What are you gonna say next… dogs and cats living together ? CENTER – TRENDING EVEN Aaron Brewer isn’t playing at an All-Pro level, but he is playing like a very good center. Nothing much to add here. INTERIOR DEFENSIVE LINE – TRENDING DOWN This group gets a vote downward due to the overall lack of pass rush. They have a good yards per carry against rate at 3.7, which is top ten, but they are still allowing 110.6 yards per game, which is right smack in the middle. Sieler has 2 sacks on the season, but the rest are at 0 and aren’t adding much in terms of pressure. Kenneth Grant just returned from IR and will hopefully add some juice to the pass rush mix. At worst, he should maintain the run defense. EDGE RUSHER – TRENDING UP This group seems like it should be going the other direction, but the edge guys have stepped up. The issue is they just aren’t getting home with the sacks. Chop Robinson missed a week due to concussion stuff, but he is tied for 1st in pass rush win rate at 36% . He has won 20 reps out of 55. That’s a good start and it won’t be long before the wins start paying off. Uche has been solid also. Malik Herring has been a decent run defender from the edge group. They likely need one piece to make this group more fearsome. Perhaps that can come from rookie Trey Moore upon his return. LINEBACKER – TRENDING UP This one is all about rookie Jacob Rodriguez. He is currently 3rd in the league in total tackles with 57. The 2 players ahead of him have played 6 games vs. the 5 for Rodriguez. He is always around the ball and while he hasn’t had success punching the ball out, he does have an INT on the season. Brooks is playing well and the Dolphins look like they have a quality LB duo for seasons to come. Willie Gay Jr. has not been great so far, but once Moore returns, those reps will go to the rookie. CORNERBACK – TRENDING EVEN I really wanted to make this a trending-up, but the completion percentage stat is a problem. The Dolphins are allowing a league worst 76.6% CP to their opponents while also allowing a 7.8 YPA. In the past two games, the Dolphins have still allowed the QB to complete 70% of the passes, but they did so with a sub 7.0 YPA allowed. In other words, they are allowing the short completions and keeping everything in front of them. There are questions as to whether this issue comes from the coverage schemes. They have some tough matchups coming up and if they can start to reverse the CP issue, then they’ll certainly be moving up. Individually, the players are moving in an upward trend, with Chris Johnson looking like a 1st round pick should look. Juju Brents has been solid. The surprise has been Jason Marshall Jr. as the other starter. He has played the 5th most snaps thus far and he looks like an NFL starter. He gave up a TD to Chase in the last game, but the rep showed what he is becoming. He was in tight coverage, but the All-Pro WR just made a better play. I won’t go so far as to say that JMJ is pushing CB down the needs list, but that’s the way it’s headed. The depth is improving as veterans Darrell Baker Jr. and Storm Duck are possibly coming off PUP soon. The Dolphins could do a lot worse than having those guys come off the bench. SAFETY – TRENDING UP I want to keep this one in the “even” category but given the dearth of talent at the beginning of the season, they have made great improvements. Rookie Michael Taaffe is the primary safety in terms of snaps played. Sophomore Dante Trader Jr. didn’t start the season playing much but has moved into the opposite starting role. Both have been decent in coverage, and both have generated an INT. Now, they aren’t GOOD yet. There are still some issues that need to be worked out. But at the beginning of the season, this was arguably the worst position group in the NFL and it has been surprisingly better than expected. The depth is solid too with Zayne Anderson, who is a solid player. Kyle Louis was going to be the big nickel safety, but had a stint on IR. He could be coming back soon. If he can play solid coverage on TEs,…

title: Dolphins to make move at kicker amid Riley Patterson struggles
summary: Miami Dolphins kicker, Riley Patterson, is having a tough season. As a result, the team is reportedly moving in a new direction at the position. According to NFL insider Jordan Schultz, the Dolphins are expected to sign kicker Zane Gonzalez after a workout that also included former Baltimore Ravens kicker Justin Tucker. The move comes […]
full_text: MIAMI GARDENS, FLORIDA - JUNE 09: Zane Gonzalez #45 of the Miami Dolphins speaks to media after OTA Offseason Workouts at Baptist Health Training Complex on June 09, 2026 in Miami Gardens, Florida. (Photo by Megan Briggs/Getty Images) | Getty Images Miami Dolphins kicker, Riley Patterson, is having a tough season. As a result, the team is reportedly moving in a new direction at the position. According to NFL insider Jordan Schultz, the Dolphins are expected to sign kicker Zane Gonzalez after a workout that also included former Baltimore Ravens kicker Justin Tucker. The move comes after the team’s bye week this past weekend. Sources: The #Dolphins are signing K Zane Gonzalez after a workout today that I’m told also included 7× Pro Bowler Justin Tucker. Gonzalez is set to join Miami pending a physical. pic.twitter.com/TFxpkE0Tm8 — Jordan Schultz (@Schultz_Report) October 20, 2026 Patterson has attempted just seven field goals this season, but has missed two of them. He has also missed an extra point and struggled to execute proper kickoff technique according to his coaches. Gonzalez last kicked for the Atlanta Falcons in 2025. That season he made 19 of 22 field goal attempts and 17 of 18 point after tries in 9 games played. During his seven-year career, the 31-year old has made 115 out of 142 field goal tries (81%) and 163 of 171 point after kicks. Gonzalez was with the Dolphins during training camp, but was released with an injury settlement following an undisclosed ailment that kept him out of action. The signing is dependent on Gonzalez passing a physical with the Dolphins’ medical staff. UPDATE: Miami finalized Gonzalez’s signing and released kicker Riley Patterson to make room for the addition.

title: How Sustainable is the Vikings’ Success This Season?
summary: The Minnesota Vikings are the biggest surprise among undefeated teams this season among pundits nationally. A little over a month ago before the season began, the Vikings had an over/under win total of 8.5 and were clear favorites to finish last in the NFC North division. Now the Vikings are the clear favorites to win […]
full_text: CLEVELAND, OHIO - AUGUST 17: Defensive coordinator Brian Flores of the Minnesota Vikings talks with head coach Kevin O'Connell during the second half of a preseason game against the Cleveland Browns at Cleveland Browns Stadium on August 17, 2024 in Cleveland, Ohio. (Photo by Nick Cammett/Diamond Images via Getty Images) | Diamond Images/Getty Images The Minnesota Vikings are the biggest surprise among undefeated teams this season among pundits nationally. A little over a month ago before the season began, the Vikings had an over/under win total of 8.5 and were clear favorites to finish last in the NFC North division. Now the Vikings are the clear favorites to win the division, and their over/under win total has moved up to 11.5, win a bias toward the under. The prevailing view among pundits nationally was that while Kyler Murray may lead to a slight improvement in the Vikings offense, the Vikings defense would probably slip back some and offset whatever gains Murray might make in the offense- hence the roughly the same win total as the Vikings had last season. There was skepticism that Kyler Murray was the guy to significantly improve the Vikings’ offense over that of a season ago led by J.J. McCarthy, Carson Wentz, and Max Brosmer. Some questioned the fit with Kevin O’Connell’s offense while others felt essentially that Kyler Murray peaked years ago and still others questioned whether he’ll stay healthy for the whole season. So far this season that view is mostly vindicated, as the Vikings offense hasn’t really improved that much statistically over last season and Kyler Murray hasn’t been healthy- missing essentially two games with a concussion. Defensively, the prevailing view among pundits was that the Vikings would take a step back from last season, maybe still be a fringe top ten unit, but closer to average than top five. Trading Jonathan Greenard and releasing Jonathan Allen and Javon Hargrave figured into that calculation, along with questions about whether Harrison Smith would return. That view has proved to be entirely wrong as the Vikings defense has improved to be the top unit in the league by most major metrics, including points allowed, EPA, and DVOA. The Vikings have also emerged as the top special teams unit so far, with All-Pro Will Reichard perfect on the season and Myles Price upping his game as both a punt and kick returner, including taking one to the house. Isaiah Rodgers also had a blocked field goal attempt which added to the Vikings’ special teams prowess. Overall, the Vikings are tied with the also undefeated 49ers for the top EPA/play, which has become the analytics community’s go-to measure of efficiency, across all three phases after five weeks: Nevertheless, the betting markets view the Vikings as among the most likely potential frauds in the league after five weeks, from the standpoint of projected regular season record vs. average for a team with their current (5-0) record. What this chart is saying is that the average team that starts 5-0 is expected to finish 13-4 whereas the Vikings are currently projected to finish 11-6, 2 games below that average. Given the projections for the rest of the NFC, that would still make the Vikings NFC North division champions and the second seed in the NFC playoff tournament but also implies that the Vikings will go just .500 the rest of the season. Part of the ‘fraud’ implied here isn’t necessarily that the Vikings are a bad team and should really be 2-3 at this point (although that’s what was expected just before the season started), but rather that the Vikings have played a relatively easy schedule measured by average DVOA of past opponents and play a relatively difficult schedule by the same measure going forward. The Vikings played the 29th most difficult schedule so far by average total DVOA of opponents and have the 4th most difficult schedule going forward. By contrast, the 5-0 49ers have played the 26th most difficult schedule so far and have the 23rd most difficult schedule going forward. The other part of the ‘fraud’ implied from the Vikings projected season record is how the Vikings have performed in each phase- offense, defense, and special teams- and how that is perceived. Offense Typically More Important and Predictive than Defense or Special Teams At this point in the season, the league and pundits are just starting to figure out who the real contenders are, which teams are fringe playoff teams, and which teams will be picking early in next year’s draft. There are still probably more questions than answers at this point and pundits that have been around for a while will remind people that come December, nobody will remember or care how teams played in September and October. At the same time, the analytical community will note that early season performance tends not to be particularly predictive, but offensive efficiency (measured by EPA or DVOA) tends to be more predictive and at an earlier stage in the season than either defensive or special teams performance, and for that reason is more important. Fans also tend to focus on offense more than defense, and that includes Vikings fans who were much more excited about the 2024 Vikings’ 5-0 start, which featured a more productive offense, than the 2026 Vikings’ 5-0 start, which has featured a more anemic offense. All of these analytical topics are covered in a good clip on whether defense wins championships or not below: The bottom line on whether defense wins championships is more of a qualified ‘sort of’ rather than something more definitive as top offenses tend to make the playoffs more than top defenses, but once in the playoffs, the vast majority of Super Bowl winning teams won the turnover battle, which at least in part depends on having a defense that can produce takeaways. That said, there are definitely teams that won the Super Bowl with a defense that carried the team. The 2015 Broncos, the 2002 Bucs, and the 2000 Ravens are the clearest examples, but there are several others that at least leaned more on their defense to make it through the playoffs unbeaten. You could make a good argument that the last three Super Bowl champions- the Seahawks, Eagles, and 2023 Chiefs – won based more on their defense than offense over the course of the season and playoffs. That said, even 2015 Broncos, 2002 Bucs, and 2000 Ravens had at least average offenses in terms of points and yards. The Vikings offense has a way to go yet before they would have average rankings in those two metrics. So How Much More Can the Vikings Lean Into Their Defense and Special Teams? The Vikings offense has shown improvement, particularly over the past five quarters, but there probably isn’t much more runway for them to become a solid unit without blemishing the loss column. Here’s why. The Vikings defensive unit is currently #1 in the league in most major efficiency metrics, including points allowed and points allowed per game, but after the Colts this weekend face a tougher slate of offenses. The Lions, Bills, and 49ers (3 of the next 4 games) currently rank 2nd, 1st, and 3rd in points scored. The Packers are the 4th team and have been looking better offensively in the last couple weeks. So, it’s holding the opposing team to 13 points on average, which the Vikings defense has done so far this season, is likely to get tougher. The Vikings’ special teams units, led by All-Pro kicker Will Reichard and returner Myles Price, is currently leading the league in DVOA. In fact, if they were to maintain their current DVOA (+13.6%) they would be the best special teams units in the league going back to the 1970s and possibly earlier. Will Reichard hasn’t missed a kick and Myles Price leads the league in combined return yardage and has the only special teams TD. I wouldn’t be surprised if both Reichard and Price continue at a high level, but odds don’t favor them maintaining this level all season. So, at some point in the next couple weeks, the Vikings…
