With its distinct profile and raucous crowds, a trip to the Twin Cities to take in a football game is one that you and your family will definitely remember. The fact that the Minnesota Vikings […]
full_text: Photo by Stephen Maturen/Getty Images | Getty Images More than a decade since it opened, U.S. Bank Stadium is still one of the crown jewels of NFL stadiums. With its distinct profile and raucous crowds, a trip to the Twin Cities to take in a football game is one that you and your family will definitely remember. The fact that the Minnesota Vikings are pretty good helps, too. But if you’re coming to the Minneapolis/St. Paul area for more than just a football game, you’re going to need to find some other things to fill your time with while you’re in town. After all, the Vikings game is only a three-hour block of time on a Sunday afternoon (or whatever evening you’re in town for, if you’re here for a primetime game). There are plenty of other things to do in the Twin Cities while you’re waiting for kickoff, and we want to share some of our favorites with you. Places to stay in Minneapolis If you’re planning on making a Vikings-centric trip to the Twin Cities into something for the whole family, the Great Wolf Lodge in Bloomington is certainly a place that you could set up shop. Honestly, you could do an entire weekend at Great Wolf Lodge without even leaving the building, considering that it has multiple restaurants, numerous kids’ activities, free events for all ages, and. . .oh, yeah. . .a 75,000-square-foot indoor water park that’s open year-round and kept at a balmy 84 degrees for everyone’s enjoyment. With rooms and suites that can accommodate eight or nine people, just about any size family can crash at Great Wolf Lodge for a weekend. If it’s just you and your significant other, check out Hotel Ivy , which is situated in the historic Ivy Tower on South 11th Street. With a full-service spa that you can spend quality time at together and three different restaurants, it’s a place where a couple can take some time away from everyday life and relax. It’s also pet-friendly if you simply can’t leave your furry friends at home, and it even has an outdoor area called Thor Lounge. It’s practically begging Vikings fans to come visit, isn’t it? Of course, maybe hotels aren’t your scene at all. Maybe you just want a place where you can hang out for a few days, come and go as you please, and not have to worry about parking or dealing with. . .well, anything. There’s always the option to hit up Airbnb , find yourself a place as close to (or as far away from) the heart of the Twin Cities as you’d like, and plan your activities accordingly. Obviously, it’s best to book these things as far out as you’re able for maximum flexibility, but it works for last-minute trips as well. Things to do in Minneapolis Sure, I could recommend the Mall of America , but everybody recommends the Mall of America, and you were probably going to go there anyway. Let’s go in a couple of different directions, shall we? I’m going to give you a different shopping center for an entirely different reason: Eden Prairie Center . Why? Have you heard of and/or seen the movie Mallrats ? Well, Eden Prairie Center is the mall from that movie. Sure, it looks a little different now, both inside and out, and you’re probably not going to run into Jay or Silent Bob (or Ben Affleck, for that matter), but if you’re a fan, you can at least say that you’ve been there. There are plenty of shopping and dining options to be had, as well, though I understand that the Fashionable Male location has been closed for some time. If you’re looking for something to do with your little ones, we recommend the Minnesota Children’s Museum . With three floors of exhibits and activities, you can find things to do for children of just about any age. There are all sorts of different interactive exhibits and things to do to get your kids active and spark their imaginations. A couple of things to be advised of: The museum recommends bringing an extra pair of shoes and a change of clothes for your kids, as some of the exhibits do involve water, and if you buy your tickets in advance, it’s cheaper than buying them at the door. If you’re in a couple or a part of a group and you want to take a look at Minneapolis from a different perspective, you can take a trolley tour of the city . These tours run year-round, and there are several different themes to choose from, including a regular sightseeing tour, a candlelight ghost tour, and a true crime tour that runs on the weekends. If you go in December, there’s even a holiday light ride that comes in “naughty” and “nice” versions. The “naughty” version is for people 21 and over only because, you guessed it, there’s alcohol involved. Book in advance to make sure you have a seat, and if you’re prone to motion sickness, you should probably avoid this one. Best places to eat in Minneapolis Sometimes, you just want a good steak. If that’s what you’re looking for, point yourself in the direction of Manny’s Steakhouse . Manny’s has sort of become the unofficial steakhouse of the Vikings because. . .well, whenever free agency comes around and the team is courting a big-name player, that’s always where dinner seems to be. With its outstanding service, top-notch entrees, massive side dishes, and incredible atmosphere, Manny’s is at the top of the list of Twin Cities restaurants for a reason. Of course, it comes with a premium price tag, but if you’re willing to go all out, a trip to Manny’s will not leave you disappointed. If you want a family meal out that doesn’t involve a play area and pizza that tastes like someone slapped tomato sauce on top of some cardboard, check out the Market at Malcolm Yards . It’s hard enough to get everyone to agree on what they want, and the Market has nine different options for everyone to choose from under one roof. You’ll find your regular food court-style fare like burgers, chicken tenders, and pizza, and even less traditional fare like dumplings, empanadas, and sushi. It’s hard to believe that anyone would be unsatisfied after a trip here for lunch. “But what about a date night option?” you might ask. Well, since we already gave you a place that you could go for a really expensive date if you wanted to go that route, let’s go the opposite direction. Ladies and gentlemen, I give you the Bryant Lake Bowl and Theater in Uptown Minneapolis. Yes, a bowling alley. Well, it’s more than a bowling alley. It’s got a theater that features acts such as improv comedy and local musical talent, and a menu that features traditional bar fare like burgers and tacos, and they even serve breakfast food until 3 PM. If you’re looking for something a little more relaxed, Bryant Lake Bowl and Theater is your destination. U.S. Bank Stadium parking, rideshare, and transit options While U.S. Bank Stadium does not directly operate its own public parking, there are numerous lots available near the stadium that fans are able to make use of on game days. The Vikings have partnered with ParkWhiz to give fans the opportunity to reserve parking at the lot of their choice prior to an event, complete with pricing options so they can find anything they’re comfortable with, budget-wise. Fans also have the option to use rideshares such as Lyft and Uber to make their way to the stadium. There are two specific locations that the Vikings have set aside as drop-off points for rideshare patrons. One is on 9th Avenue South between 6th Street South and 7th Street South, and the other is on 3rd Street between Park Avenue and Portland Avenue. Be advised that, as you can imagine, traffic is going to get a little congested the closer you get to game time, so time your ride accordingly. You can also make use of the Minneapolis light rail system to get to and from U.S. Bank Stadium on game day, allowing you to park at venues as far away as Fort Snelling or the Mall of America and head to the stadium. Both the Blue and Green Lines make stops at U.S. Bank Stadium, so you can plan your trip accordingly. You can see maps of the routes here . Again, when it comes time to leave the stadium and get back on the light…

title: Could the Vikings Get Flexed to Sunday Night Football In Week 8? Maybe, But. . .
summary: With recent changes to the NFL’s scheduling rules, the ability for the league to flex games around the schedule comes much earlier than it has in previous seasons. With a prime time game coming up that no longer looks particularly appealing, the Minnesota Vikings could, potentially, find themselves getting a game against one of their […]
full_text: MINNEAPOLIS, MN - DECEMBER 25: Minnesota Vikings running back Aaron Jones (33) spins into the end zone from 1-yard out for a touchdown and Detroit Lions linebacker Malcolm Rodriguez (44) defends during the first quarter of a NFL game between the Minnesota Vikings and Detroit Lions on December 25, 2025, at U.S. Bank Stadium in Minneapolis, MN. (Photo by Nick Wosika/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images With recent changes to the NFL’s scheduling rules, the ability for the league to flex games around the schedule comes much earlier than it has in previous seasons. With a prime time game coming up that no longer looks particularly appealing, the Minnesota Vikings could, potentially, find themselves getting a game against one of their division rivals moved into a Sunday Night Football slot in a couple of weeks. But there’s a catch. The Week 8 Sunday Night Football matchup is currently slated to pit the 2-4 Philadelphia Eagles against the 1-4-1 Washington Commanders. Now, under most circumstances, the league would rather perform a root canal sans Novocain on themselves than take an all-NFC East game out of prime time, but with Jalen Hurts now out for the season and neither of those teams looking particularly great, the league may be looking for other options. One of those options could come from the NFC North, where the (currently) 5-0 Minnesota Vikings will be facing off with the (currently) 3-2 Detroit Lions at Ford Field in Week 8. If the season ended today, the entire NFC North would find themselves in the NFC playoff field, which could potentially make this an enticing matchup for the league to move to NBC. There are two potential problems with this idea. The first problem is that the league has to give twelve days notice before flexing this matchup to Sunday Night Football, which means they would have to make that decision. . . checks calendar . . .today. So, if it’s happening, we’ll know very soon. The other , and potentially larger, issue, is that the league has a rule that mandates that at least one of the two home-and-home games in each divisional rivalry has to take place in one of the noon Sunday windows during the season. The reason that this is a problem is that the Vikings and Lions are already slated to meet in one prime time game in Week 15 when the two teams play one another at U.S. Bank Stadium. That’s already a scheduled Sunday Night Football matchup. So, if the league wants to move the Week 8 Vikings at Lions matchup into a Sunday Night Football spot, they would have to move the Week 15 Lions at Vikings matchup out of the Sunday Night Football spot into the Sunday noon window that week and find another game to move into Sunday Night Football for Week 15. Got all that? Like I said, we should know relatively soon whether or not the league is flexing any game into the Week 8 Sunday Night Football spot to move Eagles/Commanders out of it. Of the Week 8 matchups, the Vikings/Lions game does appear to be the best potential option. It would also give the Vikings three prime time games in the stretch of four weeks: Week 8 on Sunday Night at Detroit, Week 9 on Monday Night against Buffalo at home, and Week 11 on Sunday Night against San Francisco in Mexico City. If the league does decide to shift the Vikings’ schedule around, we will let you know as soon as the news drops.

title: Vikings Trade Deadline Targets: Buckner, Taylor, Bynum & More
summary: The Minnesota Vikings are 5-0 and reportedly ready to be aggressive at the trade deadline. Who should they target? That’s the question driving the latest episode of The Real Forno Show, where host Tyler Forness and producer Dave Stefano fired up the brand-new A to Z Sports Trade Simulator to break down every realistic target […]
full_text: MINNEAPOLIS, MINNESOTA - SEPTEMBER 13: General manger Nolan Teasley of the Minnesota Vikings looks on before a game against the Green Bay Packers at U.S. Bank Stadium on September 13, 2026 in Minneapolis, Minnesota. (Photo by Stephen Maturen/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Minnesota Vikings are 5-0 and reportedly ready to be aggressive at the trade deadline. Who should they target? That’s the question driving the latest episode of The Real Forno Show, where host Tyler Forness and producer Dave Stefano fired up the brand-new A to Z Sports Trade Simulator to break down every realistic target — from DeForest Buckner to Saquon Barkley to Cam Bynum. “If the Vikings want to truly make a Super Bowl run they should make a couple of trades and fortify the roster,” Forness said, pointing to past champions like the 2021 Rams adding Odell Beckham Jr. and the Seahawks acquiring Rashid Shaheed as proof that late-season additions matter. GM Nolan Teasley comes from an aggressive organization and has been calling around. “We’ve heard Nolan Teasley’s calling around,” Forness noted. “All the beat reporters like the Vikings are going to add people.” Key points from the episode: DeForest Buckner is the #1 target. “I think the number one player I wanna bring in of anybody that I think could realistically be available is DeForest Buckner,” Forness said. Beyond the playoff push, he sees Buckner as a developmental mentor for rookie Caleb Banks due to their similar builds (6’6″+, 34-35″ arms) and leverage techniques. Likely cost: a third-round pick plus a token sixth. Justin Herbert doesn’t fit. Despite tantalizing arm talent, Forness has major concerns: “I have concerns that he doesn’t fit this offense.” He questioned whether three first-round picks is worth it for a QB thriving in Sean Payton/Joe Lombardi systems, not Kevin O’Connell’s anticipatory West Coast offense. Quenton Nelson is a risky rental. Stefano noted Nelson is “the fourth-ranked guard in PFF right now” and “a Pro Bowl guard,” but Forness pushed back on spending two thirds for a 30-year-old rental when Donovan Jackson is expected back for the playoffs. Jonathan Taylor carries too much tread. With 2,599 carries since college vs. Jordan Mason’s 859, Forness cautioned: “Tread on the tires matters with running backs. It, we don’t want it to, but it does.” Likely cost: a second-round pick. Cam Bynum reunion makes sense. With Theo Jackson struggling, Forness explained: “This is a PhD level defense where rookies don’t often get a lot of playing time.” Bynum already knows Brian Flores’ system, eliminating the learning curve. Proposed deal: a third, a fifth, and Theo Jackson for Bynum and a fourth. Saquon Barkley is within reach. A third-round pick plus a fifth could land the Eagles star, creating a devastating trio with Aaron Jones and Jordan Mason. Pass rush is the priority. “Pass rush, defensive line, I think that should be the priority,” Forness said, noting Jalen Redmond, Andrew Van Ginkel, and Dallas Turner are all playing 80-90% of snaps. Kevin O’Connell isn’t going anywhere. “You are not going to find better as a head coach if you fire him,” Forness said bluntly. Listen: Or on your favorite podcast aggregator. Watch: Whether it’s Buckner anchoring the defensive line, Bynum steadying the secondary, or a surprise running back addition, the Vikings have the capital and urgency to make a Super Bowl push. For the full breakdown with trade simulator point values, salary analysis, and player comparisons, watch The Real Forno Show — a Minnesota Vikings podcast from Vikings 1st & SKOL on the Bleav Network. Tyler Forness and Dave Stefano deliver the most comprehensive trade deadline analysis in the Vikings ecosystem. Fan with Us!!! Tyler Forness @TheRealForno of Vikings 1st & SKOL @Vikings1stSKOL and A to Z Sports @AtoZSportsNFL , with Dave Stefano @Luft_Krigare producing this Vikings 1st & SKOL production, the @RealFornoShow found at the @BleavNetwork . So here’s a question for you: Which trade target would you prioritize, and would you give up the draft capital to get it done?

title: Corey Kiner’s clock-killing carries are what’s great about football
summary: Football really is the ultimate team sport. There’s something so poetic about how often the fortunes of the largest figures in the sport are shaped by players no one knows before they are suddenly thrust into the limelight. Just ask Malcolm Butler. Nothing reminded me of this truth more than watching the end of last […]
full_text: Football really is the ultimate team sport. There’s something so poetic about how often the fortunes of the largest figures in the sport are shaped by players no one knows before they are suddenly thrust into the limelight. Just ask Malcolm Butler. Nothing reminded me of this truth more than watching the end of last Sunday’s game during a picture-perfect autumn afternoon at Gillette Stadium. The Patriots had the ball up by one score midway through the fourth quarter against the Jets in an important AFC East contest. New England’s offense is led by a quarterback who narrowly missed winning the MVP a season ago. His top target is a three-time All-Pro with a Super Bowl title to his name. And yet, with the game on the line, Josh McDaniels turned to a cast of cast-offs to seal the win. As the clock ticked under six minutes to go in the ballgame, McDaniels needed to make that clock keep ticking faster and faster. To make that happen, he turned to his run-game personnel package. That group included a trio of players no one wanted: wide receiver Efton Chism, tight end Cameron Latu, and running back Corey Kiner. The Foxboro Faithful are familiar with Chism after his heroics in Buffalo a few weeks ago. No one wanted him in the 2025 NFL Draft, but that didn’t stop him from carving out a spot on the roster and earning playing time. When Mack Hollins went down with an injury, Chism was there to help fill in for his run-blocking presence despite being roughly half the size. Latu and Kiner are less familiar to the fans. With multiple tight ends banged up coming out of camp, the Patriots claimed Latu off waivers when he didn’t make the cut in Philadelphia. He made his presence felt earlier in this game on special team with a thundering hit on a kickoff return, and he’s be out there to help the Patriots put the game away. After the team’s camp competition for a third running back left people wanting. New England swung a future seventh-round pick to Arizona for the running back buried on the depth chart behind the guy they took third overall this spring and the veteran free agent they signed shortly before that. Like Chism, Kiner also went undrafted in 2025. Little did they know, this group would decide the outcome. McDaniels called Kiner’s number eight times in a row. Kiner answered by picking up three first downs and 42 yards, taking almost four minutes off the clock as it ticked down to the two-minute warning. The longest run of the drive, one that went for 12 yards, was aided by a Latu kick-out block. The second longest, an eight-yarder, got some help from Efton Chism blocking out Minkah Fitzpatrick. View this post on Instagram Of course, the running game can’t do what it needs to do without the offensive line. Down three starters, the Pats were forced to turn over the interior of the line to two more players most fans had never heard of. When the Patriots took the field for that game-sealing drive, it was Walter Rouse at left guard and Matt Pryor at right guard. Rouse ended up in New England one day after Kiner. He was moved from Minnesota for a day-three pick swap to help give the Patriots some depth. Meanwhile, Pryor was with the Cardinals on their practice squad until being signed by the Patriots at the start of the month and admitted after the game that he still does not know the playbook. On the first of Kiner’s right consecutive runs, the running back follows a lead block from Rouse on a power concept to pick up 12 yards. McDaniels went back to the same concept two plays later for five more yards, with Kiner breaking it back to run behind Pryor as he squared up five-time All-Pro DeMario Davis. And when Kiner cut one back two plays after that, Rouse provided one of the key blocks to create a lane. No one would have predicted two months ago that this cast of characters would be on the field together to help finish out an AFC East victory for the Patriots. And yet, here they are, making plays when called upon and helping the team win. Isn’t that a little bit romantic?

title: Examining the roster ties between Patriots, Bears ahead of Week 7
summary: The connections extend beyond coaches Thomas Brown, Ashton Grant, Jason Houghtaling, Charles London and Isaiah Ford. Between the active rosters, practice squads and reserve lists, three former New England Patriots and four former Chicago Bears find themselves in the fold Thursday’s primetime meeting at Soldier Field. Here’s a glance through those on-field ties heading into […]
full_text: CHICAGO, ILLINOIS - SEPTEMBER 28: Joe Thuney #62 of the Chicago Bears celebrates after a touchdown during the third quarter of an NFL football game against the Philadelphia Eagles at Soldier Field on September 28, 2026 in Chicago, Illinois. (Photo by Kevin Sabitus/Getty Images) | Getty Images The connections extend beyond coaches Thomas Brown, Ashton Grant, Jason Houghtaling, Charles London and Isaiah Ford. Between the active rosters, practice squads and reserve lists, three former New England Patriots and four former Chicago Bears find themselves in the fold Thursday’s primetime meeting at Soldier Field. Here’s a glance through those on-field ties heading into the 8:15 p.m. ET kickoff. CHICAGO Joe Thuney, guard — A future inductee into the Pro Football Hall of Fame, Thuney’s NFL run began in Foxborough in the third round of the 2016 draft at No. 78 overall. The North Carolina State All-American earned Super Bowl LI and LIII rings during his versatile stay on the offensive line and made the cut for the Patriots’ All-2010s and All-Dynasty teams. A five-year deal brought Thuney to the Kansas City Chiefs as an unrestricted free agent in 2021 after playing on the franchise tag. And last March, after adding Super Bowl LVII and LVIII rings to his collection, the 33-year-old ironman was traded into quarterback Caleb Williams’ pass protection and signed a two-year extension. Thuney has started 167 games in the regular season and 23 games in the postseason during his career. The four-time Pro Bowler and five-time All-Pro stands as the reigning NFL Protector of the Year and a captain. Garrett Bradbury, center — Before NFL free agency opened in March, Bradbury’s stay at Gillette Stadium reached its end with one year remaining on his contract. The Patriots agreed to trade the 31-year-old center to the Bears in exchange for a fifth-round draft choice in 2027 on the heels of Pro Bowler Drew Dalman’s retirement. Bradbury had started every game for the reigning AFC champions from September into February, handling 98 percent of the offensive snaps. Signing in 2025 after being released by the Minnesota Vikings, he received the organization’s Ron Hobson Good Guy Award on the way to Super Bowl LX. The former Rimington Trophy winner out of North Carolina State has started all 111 of his appearances in the regular season since being selected in the first round at No. 18 overall in 2019. Jamree Kromah, defensive end — A 26-year-old former transfer from Rutgers to James Madison, Kromah entered the NFL with Chicago as an undrafted rookie in 2024. The defensive end agreed to depart from the Bears’ practice squad for a spot on the Patriots’ 53-man roster in September of his rookie campaign. And after spending three weeks among the team’s inactives, which marks the league’s minimum requirement for poaching, he was waived and soon circled back to his previous club. Kromah made initial 53-man roster for the first time out of training camp and debuted last Sunday. NEW ENGLAND Lorenz Metz, offensive tackle — The Patriots signed the 29-year-old Metz to the practice squad ahead of the AFC divisional round in January. A futures contract followed. And after the 53-man roster deadline passed in August, so did a return to the practice squad as an exempt 17th member via the NFL International Pathway. Born in Bavaria, Germany, the offensive tackle played collegiately at Cincinnati and went undrafted in 2023. The Bears marked his first stop in the league. After being waived at the start of his rookie training camp, Metz went on to spend two campaigns on the practice squad of the Tampa Bay Buccaneers. Matt Pryor, guard — Signed off the practice squad of the Arizona Cardinals, Pryor landed on the 53-man roster in Foxborough as the calendar turned to October and checked in at guard last week. The veteran out of Texas Christian has appeared in 111 games, including 40 starts, since being selected by the Philadelphia Eagles in the sixth round of the 2018 NFL draft at No. 206 overall. He has also been an Indianapolis Colt and a San Francisco 49er. And in 2024, Pryor became a Bear on a one-year deal. The 31-year-old saw action in every game that campaign in the NFC North while making 15 starts. Kindle Vildor, cornerback — After serving as a standard elevation amid attrition at cornerback, the Patriots signed Vildor to the 53-man roster in early October. The 28-year-old’s time in the AFC East has included six tackles, including one for loss, to go with one pass deflection and one forced fumble. Signed in March and retained on the practice squad in August, Vildor originally entered the league with the Bears in the fifth round of the 2020 draft at No. 163 overall. The Georgia Southern product spent time with five other organizations before heading to Foxborough. Through 83 appearances, including 27 starts, he has had a hand in 146 tackles, one sack, two forced fumble and two interceptions. Kevin Byard III, safety — Voted a team captain following the preseason, the 33-year-old Byard reunited with a familiar staff in March after leading the NFL with seven interceptions with the Bears in 2025. A three-time Pro Bowler and first-team All-Pro, he has appeared in 170 games and made 161 starts since entering the league out of Middle Tennessee State in the third round of the 2016 draft. Setting out with head coach Mike Vrabel’s former Tennessee Titans before being dealt to Philadelphia ahead of the 2023 trade deadline, the veteran safety has amassed 998 tackles, 36 interceptions, six sacks, four forced fumbles, six fumble recoveries and two touchdowns off turnovers to the tune of 424 return yards.

title: Patriots Power Rankings Week 7: Win streak sends message from the mess
summary: The way the experts see it, the Patriots’ stunning turnaround has them clawing their way up from irrelevance, back from being a disconcerting mess and asserting themselves as a credible threat in the AFC… until injuries and offensive line health threaten to derail them this week in Chicago. Nate Davis from USA Today actually knocked […]
full_text: Oct 18, 2026; Foxborough, Massachusetts, USA; Fans cheer in the first half between New York Jets and New England Patriots at Gillette Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Bob DeChiara-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The way the experts see it, the Patriots’ stunning turnaround has them clawing their way up from irrelevance, back from being a disconcerting mess and asserting themselves as a credible threat in the AFC… until injuries and offensive line health threaten to derail them this week in Chicago. Nate Davis from USA Today actually knocked them down two spots because they might lose Thursday night. Didn’t realize the rankings were based on what might happen in games that haven’t been played yet. I’m not that pessimistic. The 4-2 Bears are a good team with a good quarterback and a solid defense. As a team, they’re not going to make Jets-like mistakes. Here’s hoping Brown has been spending quality time with either Drake Maye or his favorite Jugs machine. Bears are favored by 3.5 but my Monopoly money is on the Patriots to “Advance to GO, collect a win in Chicago and earn some much needed rest. GO PATS!! AFC East: Buffalo Bills (5-1) – Bye Week New England Patriots (4-2) at Chicago Bears (4-2) New York Jets (2-4) vs. Miami Dolphins (0-5) AFC Matchups: Kansas City Chiefs (5-0) at Seattle Seahawks (3-3) Cleveland Browns (4-2) at Tennessee Titans (1-5) Jacksonville Jaguars (4-2) – Bye Week Pittsburgh Steelers (4-2) at New Orleans Saints (2-4) Denver Broncos (4-2) at Arizona Cardinals (2-4) Baltimore Ravens (4-2) vs. Cincinnati Bengals (3-2) Las Vegas Raiders (3-3) vs. Los Angeles Rams (2-4) Indianapolis Colts (2-4) at Vikings (5-0) Houston Texans (2-4) vs. New York Giants (3-2-1) Los Angeles Chargers (0-6) – Bye Week 5th – Vinnie Iyer (Sporting News): Patriots have now improved their rushing total to 784 yards in 6 games, a clip of 131 rushing yards per game – a huge number that doesn’t get enough credit for their offensive success. They are up from 129 yards per game last year and it’s helped them get Drake Maye out of his slump . [+2] 5th – Ian Glenn (Full Press Coverage): Drake Maye threw three touchdown passes in a 26-19 victory over the Jets, giving New England three straight wins. The Buffalo upset and Raiders blowout now look like the start of a genuine run rather than isolated good Sundays. Pats are back among the AFC’s most credible threats . [+2] 7th – NFL Nation (ESPN): Biggest issue on offense: Offensive line health. The Patriots had three starters — right tackle Morgan Moses (ankle), left guard Alijah Vera-Tucker (hamstring) and right guard Ben Brown (knee) — get knocked out of Sunday’s game. And the only reason Brown was in the lineup was because opening-day starter Mike Onwenu (ankle) and his replacement Greg Van Roten (hip) were put on IR earlier in the season. The Patriots have started three different OL combinations in their first six games, and there will likely be a fourth Thursday in Chicago . — Mike Reiss [+2] 7th – Frank Schwab (Yahoo! Sports): The Patriots lost 13-10 at Seattle in the opener, when they were in position to kick a game-tying field goal at the end. If that turns out different, we’re having a much different conversation about the Patriots. They have blown out the Steelers and Raiders, who have had some good moments this season. They won at the Bills. The win over the Jets might not have been dominant but they were up 10 points going into the final minute. Of course, the Patriots’ season turned when Drake Maye started to heat up. Through three games he had 585 yards, one touchdown and six interceptions. In the three games since he has 878 yards, 10 touchdowns and one interception. A.J. Brown is back (though Romeo Doubs went on injured reserve with a shoulder injury) so the Patriots’ offense should continue to flouris h. [+4] 7th – Nick Shook (NFL): New England has transformed from a disconcerting mess into a professional outfit that is improving weekly on the defensive side and benefitting greatly from Drake Maye’s return to prominence. A.J. Brown was a bit rusty in his return, but I love the trajectory the Patriots are on right now . [+3] 8th – Mike Florio (ProFootballTalk): The injuries are piling up before a short-week trip to Chicago . [+1] 8th – Nate Davis (USA Today): Given all the injuries they sustained Sunday, gonna be tough to sustain a three-game winning streak with a trip to Chicago on Thursday night next up on the docket − especially if WR A.J. Brown drops four more balls . [-2] 9th – Pete Prisco (CBS Sports): They have turned their season around the past three weeks as Drake Maye has lit it up. The defense is also getting to the quarterback . [+2] 9th – Conor Orr (SI): While it’s a very, very small sample size, the A.J. Brown drop rate being on par with Quentin Johnston is not what you want. My bold prediction is that Drake Maye gets him into the end zone twice against the Bears on Thursday night . [+1] 11th – Ralph. Vacchiano (FOX Sports): Yawn! The Patriots beat the Jets. What else is new? But that’s three straight wins now for a team that was on the brink of disaster after Week 3. And more importantly, it was a third straight good game from QB Drake Maye. The turnaround is stunning. He averaged 195 passing yards and had one touchdown pass and six interceptions over the first three games. He’s since averaged 292.7 yards while tossing 10 touchdowns with just one interception. Maye may not get there because that terrible start could be an anchor, but he’s playing like an MVP contender again . [+2] AVG RANK: 7.6 [+1.7]

title: A.J. Brown’s recent struggles no cause for concern, says Drake Maye
summary: A.J. Brown’s return to the field last Sunday did not go as planned. Despite seeing a game-high 10 targets, the star wide receiver hauled in only three for 27 yards while struggling with a handful of drops. Quarterback Drake Maye, however, is not concerned about his top wide receiver moving forward. “It’s A.J. Brown,” said […]
full_text: A.J. Brown’s return to the field last Sunday did not go as planned. Despite seeing a game-high 10 targets, the star wide receiver hauled in only three for 27 yards while struggling with a handful of drops. Quarterback Drake Maye, however, is not concerned about his top wide receiver moving forward. “It’s A.J. Brown,” said Maye. “Last week is what it is. I wish I had some throws back and attempts I targeted his way, and I think it’s part of this league. You want to make a play so bad, you want to have plays back, and there are plays that I want back every week, and that’s part of it. It’s a short week, so we’ve got to get focused on Chicago.” The short week gives Brown an opportunity to quickly flush his performance against the Jets and turn his attention to the Bears. That has been his approach. “I just didn’t make the play. I’m not really going backwards because it’s over with now,” Brown said Tuesday. “I watched the film. I put it to bed, and I’m looking forward.” Brown played 52 snaps in his return and said his ankle was “feeling good.” He left Sunday’s game dealing with the usual bumps and bruises everywhere else, but his ankle was not an issue. The Patriots will need the three-time Pro Bowler to handle another significant workload Thursday night after placing fellow wide receiver Romeo Doubs on injured reserve this week. That leaves just Brown, DeMario Douglas, Efton Chism III and Kyle Williams as New England’s receivers on the active roster . New England will also need better production on the field from Brown while he continues to build chemistry with Maye. “We’re always trying to evolve,” Brown said. “Not just with him, but just with all the pass catchers and all of us trying to continue to grow in that area, and just go out here and make plays. It’s nothing to overthink. You throw it and catch it, you make the play. Simple as that. I’m gonna keep it very simple because it is, you know? And that’s how I approach the game, and you just gotta keep it pushing.”

title: Patriots waive wide receiver from injured reserve
summary: Jeremiah Webb will soon become a free agent after spending three months on injured reserve. The New England Patriots waived the wide receiver on Tuesday, according to the NFL transaction wire, allowing him the opportunity to catch on elsewhere in 2026. Webb, 25, had been placed on injured reserve just two practices into training camp […]
full_text: Jeremiah Webb will soon become a free agent after spending three months on injured reserve. The New England Patriots waived the wide receiver on Tuesday, according to the NFL transaction wire, allowing him the opportunity to catch on elsewhere in 2026. Webb, 25, had been placed on injured reserve just two practices into training camp in July after outside linebacker Gabe Jacas signed his rookie contract and began to count against the club’s roster limit. But the corresponding move is no longer season-ending. Instead, the former transfer from South Dakota to South Alabama will be subject to the league’s claiming period. Entering the NFL as part of the Patriots’ 2025 undrafted class, Webb caught six passes for 80 yards and one touchdown during his rookie preseason. He also broke off a 59-yard kickoff return and 22-yard punt return. The 5-foot-11, 198-pound wideout was waived at last year’s 53-man roster deadline and proceeded to join the organization’s practice squad at its formation after clearing waivers. Webb remained to serve as an inactive standard elevation for the AFC wild card in January and reached a futures contract following Super Bowl LX. With his exit, a dozen continue to reside on injured reserve in Foxborough. Wide receiver Romeo Doubs joined fellow veteran target Mack Hollins on the list this week due to a shoulder injury. The rest of the IR group includes running back Myles Montgomery, fullback Reggie Gilliam, tight end Julian Hill, offensive linemen Marcus Bryant, Mike Onwenu and Greg Van Roten, linebackers Quintayvious Hutchins and Khalil Jacobs, safety Dell Pettus and punter Bryce Baringer. The Chicago Bears host Thursday’s 8:15 p.m. ET kickoff at Soldier Field.

title: Caleb Lomu’s versatility comes into focus after Patriots O-line injuries
summary: With only two days to go until their Thursday night game in Chicago, it seems increasingly likely that the New England Patriots will be without both of their starting guards. According to head coach Mike Vrabel, both Alijah Vera-Tucker and Ben Brown are “probably” set to miss the game. If that indeed turns out to […]
full_text: With only two days to go until their Thursday night game in Chicago, it seems increasingly likely that the New England Patriots will be without both of their starting guards. According to head coach Mike Vrabel, both Alijah Vera-Tucker and Ben Brown are “probably” set to miss the game. If that indeed turns out to be the case — and practice participation thus far suggests so — the Patriots have multiple directions they could go in. One of them is inserting their first-round draft pick from earlier this year, Caleb Lomu. “I think that Caleb will have to be ready to go at multiple positions,” Vrabel told reporters on Tuesday. “We were getting ready for him to have to be able to pull the ball in the game, in another different scenario. Where that ends up being on Thursday — he’ll have to be ready for a couple of spots.” Lomu joined the Patriots as the 28th overall selection in this year’s draft after almost exclusively lining up at offensive tackle during his college career at Utah. As executive vice president of player personnel Eliot Wolf said during a press conference shortly after the pick was made, however, the team did see some versatility in him — versatility it continued to explore in the following months. Besides playing both left and right tackle in practice, the 6-foot-6, 308-pounder also saw some reps inside during training camp. The Patriots have not yet had to use him in that capacity during a game, but the injuries suffered on Sunday against the New York Jets might prompt them to reconsider. With Vera-Tucker and Brown unlikely to play due to their respective hamstring and knee injuries, Walter Rouse and Matt Pryor project as the next men up. The two were already inserted into the lineup down the stretch versus the Jets. If there should there be any hiccups against the Bears, however, the Patriots might just end up turning to Lomu. “Everyone’s got to prepare like a starter for those types of things that happen,” the 21-year-old said after the win over the Jets. “It’s terrible to see. It does happen, though, unfortunately, in this league.”

title: New England’s best things to do, see, and eat before heading to a Patriots game
summary: As the fall season officially settles in, few places offer a better way to experience the seasonal change than New England, where Sundays and primetime kickoffs bring fans to Gillette Stadium for Patriots football. Whether you’re making a day trip for a game or are a routine visitor familiar with the stadium, there is plenty […]
full_text: As the fall season officially settles in, few places offer a better way to experience the seasonal change than New England, where Sundays and primetime kickoffs bring fans to Gillette Stadium for Patriots football. Whether you’re making a day trip for a game or are a routine visitor familiar with the stadium, there is plenty to explore at Patriot Place and throughout the surrounding New England area. From weekend outings leading up to kickoff to weekday evening activities, the region offers plenty of options for visitors looking to make the most of their time in Foxborough, Mass. Places to stay near Foxborough, Mass. Patriot Place offers an on-site hotel at the Hilton Garden Inn, which sits between a row of shops and restaurants. With its close proximity to the stadium and other complexes at Patriot Place, its average nightly price is $155, allowing convenient access to the stadium at a reasonable price. Additionally, about three miles from Gillette Stadium in the neighboring town of Sharon, the Best Western The Inn at Sharon/Foxboro is another option with nightly rates of roughly $104. The hotel provides an affordable alternative for visitors who want to stay a short drive away from the action. However, if you’re planning to spend more of your time in Boston, there’s an array of staying options to suit your preferences. For reference, downtown Boston is a one-hour to one-and-a-half-hour long commute on the road to Gillette Stadium. Things to do in New England For those venturing into Boston, the New England Aquarium , located on the opposite side of Route 93 from the Boston Common, is a favorite local attraction while exploring the city. Apple picking and visiting local orchards in the region are some of the best New England fall activities as well, with many locations offering fresh apple cider products and other popular fall snacks. And if your Patriots tickets are for a winter matchup, there are plenty of stunning holiday light displays to visit. If you’re staying locally, a 15-minute drive will lead you to the Wrentham Village Premium Outlets for a diverse shopping experience, featuring over 170 brands. At Patriot Place , there’s also an abundance of accessible activities to check out, including the Patriots Hall of Fame , Showcase Cinema De Lux and the Bass Pro Shop s. Best places to eat in New England Remaining local, Tavolino rests next to the Hilton Garden Inn as a mid-range-priced Italian restaurant. While the establishment is best known for its pizza, the pasta options are a close rival. Also at Patriot Place is The Harp , a sports bar with a broad menu. Though for a quicker and more casual dining experience, Foxboro House of Pizza at 34 Central St. offers many combinations of slices and sandwich subs to order before or after a game. But if you’re in Boston, FiRE+iCE is an all-you-can-eat dining experience for a one-time payment. Customers can fill an empty bowl with whatever Latin, Italian, American and Asian-inspired foods they’d like. Gillette Stadium parking, rideshare, and transit options Traffic can be congested after events, so there are two recommended ways to approach the game-day parking situation: Pay up to $50 for official stadium parking or settle in the free gravel and dirt lots situated across Route One from the stadium. Fans using the free lot should expect a 10- to 15-minute walk to the ticket gates. After the game, traffic can cause delays of up to two or three hours. Leaving slightly before the game clock expires can significantly reduce that wait. On the other hand, official stadium parking allows a quicker walk and exit. For fans traveling from Massachusetts or northern Rhode Island, the MBTA commuter rail offers another way to reach the stadium, with a stop on the east side of the Patriot Place complex. Typically, round-trip game-day tickets can be available for around $20 per person. To find a station near you and check schedules, you can visit the MBTA website . Rideshare services also provide an alternative, though fares can rise as demand increases and drivers have to navigate stadium traffic. Tailgating at Gillette Stadium And finally, once it’s game day, fans can take part in the lively tailgating scene that fills the parking lots surrounding the stadium, with gatherings held in both stadium-side and off-site lots. While Route One splits half of the crowd, fans still find ways to bring the pregame atmosphere to both sides of the road. Groups set up tables and grills, filling the air with the aroma of steak tips, sausages, clam chowder and other game-day favorites as visitors make their way to their parking spots. Those gatherings also often feature backyard-style games. For fans planning to enjoy the pregame atmosphere, official lots open four hours before kickoff. The Gillette Stadium Experience Once fans pass through the gates, they can choose from a laundry list of concession stands located on every seating level of the stadium. Meal prices typically range from $10 and $12, with the cheesesteak and brisket sandwich among the venue’s most popular options. But if you want to skip those busy lines, Gillette Stadium also offers checkout-free concession locations for faster service, such as the Pepsi Grab & Go line. Fans can simply grab what they want, tap their card to pay while exiting and quickly continue with their game-day experience. There’s also the option of paying a more premium price to watch the game from the Cross Insurance Club, with lounges running along both sidelines. In the lounge, there’s a quickly accessible bar and stadium catering behind glass windows peering out to the field. Finally, once seated, you can take in the fall football atmosphere in person with the roaring New England crowd while Ozzy Osbourne’s “Crazy Train” echoes through the speakers as the Patriots exit the tunnel for game day.

title: Patriots vs. Jets snap counts from Week 6
summary: After missing the previous four games with an ankle injury sustained in the season opener, A.J. Brown made his comeback on Sunday against the New York Jets. Despite the New England Patriots beating their division rivals, it was a disappointing return for the 29-year-old. Brown caught just three passes for 27 yards, registered two drops […]
full_text: After missing the previous four games with an ankle injury sustained in the season opener, A.J. Brown made his comeback on Sunday against the New York Jets. Despite the New England Patriots beating their division rivals, it was a disappointing return for the 29-year-old. Brown caught just three passes for 27 yards, registered two drops (plus a third on an onside kick), and generally did not have the impact one would have hoped he would have. Still, it was not all bad. He did get open fairly regularly, and also managed to play a high number of snaps despite his one-month absence. When all was said and done, Brown had 52 of 68 snaps — the highest among all Patriots wide receivers. For head coach Mike Vrabel, the circumstances surrounding Romeo Doubs’ shoulder injury on the fifth offensive snap of the game played a role in that. “We were down to four guys, so I mean, somebody’s got to play in there,” he said when asked about Brown’s workload on Monday. “We like to have our best players available as much as they can be.” Here is our full snap count report from the Patriots’ 26-19 win . Brown* (52; 76%), TE Hunter Henry* (52; 76%), RG Matt Pryor (46; 68%), WR Efton Chism III (42; 62%), RB Rhamondre Stevenson* (41; 60%), WR DeMario Douglas (40; 59%), TE Eli Raridon* (39; 57%), WR Kyle Williams (25; 37%), LG Alijah Vera-Tucker* (22; 32%), TE Cameron Latu* (18; 26%), RB TreVeyon Henderson (16; 24%), LG Walter Rouse (14; 21%), RB Corey Kiner (12; 18%), RT Morgan Moses* (9; 13%), WR Romeo Doubs (2; 3%) Suffering respective knee and ankle injuries in Week 5 against the Jets, Will Campbell and TreVeyon Henderson were both questionable entering the Jets game. However, both showed no physical limitations. Whereas Campbell went wire-to-wire for all 68 snaps, Henderson played 16. Campbell’s availability in particular was crucial given that the Patriots needed all eight of the offensive linemen on their game day roster to play meaningful snaps. The reason for that is starters Alijah Vera-Tucker, Ben Brown and Morgan Moses all exiting the game due to injury at one point. In their place, Walter Rouse, Matt Pryor and Caleb Lomu took over at left guard, right guard and right tackle. Elsewhere on the team, Lomu played one snap as an H-back in an unbalanced short-yardage look; youngsters Efton Chism and Eli Raridon continued to be heavily involved; Corey Kiner served as the close-it-out back in the fourth quarter. title: New Orleans’ best things to do, see, and eat before heading to a Saints game
summary: New Orleans is a uniquely special city that always deserves a trip on its own, but Saints game days take that experience to a whole other level. With so many exciting places to eat at and visit, a few days in the Big Easy really aren’t enough. However, this game-day guide will help you not […]
full_text: by Chris Graythen/Getty Images | Getty Images New Orleans is a uniquely special city that always deserves a trip on its own, but Saints game days take that experience to a whole other level. With so many exciting places to eat at and visit, a few days in the Big Easy really aren’t enough. However, this game-day guide will help you not miss out on the things that are a must-see and do here. Places to stay in New Orleans: There are so many hotels within a few blocks or miles of the Superdome. Several located on Poydras and Canal streets will be your closest options. However, if you are looking for something more historic and lively, you can head to the French Quarter. Just a few of my recommendations include: NOPSI Hotel (Baronne Street) Housed in the former headquarters of New Orleans Public Service Inc., the historic downtown hotel offers space room accommodations, a rooftop pool and bar, and on-site dining. It’s in walking distance of the French Quarter, Caesars Superdome and many of the city’s top attractions. Royal Sonesta (Bourbon Street) The Sonesta has a beautiful courtyard, dining options and lively atmosphere which is just steps away from nightlife, restaurants and attractions in the heart of the French Quarter. Hotel Monteleone (Royal Street) Known for their famous Carousel Bar, the Monteleone gives their visitors a taste of classic New Orleans charm while being within walking distance of many French Quarter and Downtown attractions. Doubletree Hilton (Canal Street) Located at the end of Canal Street, the Hilton offers on-site dining and is within walking distance to Caesars Casino, the Filmore, Aquarium and Riverwalk. Ritz-Carlton (Canal Street) The Ritz is located in the historic Maison Blanche building and offers elegant accommodations, upscale dining, and live jazz music at the Davenport Lounge. Its prime location provides easy access to Bourbon Street, downtown attractions and the Superdome. Things to do in New Orleans: There is so much more to New Orleans than football, food and the French Quarter. Whether you’re a history buff, an animal lover or simply looking to experience the city’s unique charm, here are a few must-visit attractions. Audubon Zoo (Uptown) The zoo features wildlife from all around the world, beautiful grounds and family-friendly attractions. The National WWII Museum (Downtown) One of the city’s and the county’s most popular attractions, featuring immersive exhibits, historic artifacts and personal stories from World War II. Steamboat Natchez (Downtown) Experience New Orleans from the Mississippi River on an authentic paddlewheel steamboat, complete with live jazz and beautiful views of the city. Audubon Aquarium (Downtown) The recently renovated aquarium offers an up-close look at marine life, including sharks, penguins and white alligators as well as a beautiful butterfly garden in the Audubon Insectarium. Best places to eat in New Orleans: As a New Orleans native, this is honestly a tough one. There are so many incredible options for authentic Cajun and Creole cuisine, and a few days in New Orleans just isn’t enough time to sample them all. However, here are a few of my personal favorites throughout the Greater New Orleans area that I recommend trying to squeeze into your visit: Drago’s (New Orleans and Metairie) Domilise’s Po-Boys (New Orleans) Parkway Bakery (Uptown) Dooky Chase (New Orleans) Cafe Du’ Monde (Multiple locations) Giorlando’s (Metairie) Quarter View (Metairie) Caesars Superdome parking/rideshare options: Fortunately, the Superdome is in the heart of the city, so getting to and from there is super easy, and there are plenty of parking options available. There are two paid parking garages, plus Champions Garage on-site, as well as a few others within a few blocks of the Superdome. However, if you are staying at a hotel downtown or in the French Quarter, the Superdome is just about a 15- to 20-minute walk away, or you can use Uber or Lyft for just a few dollars. Tailgating at the Superdome: Unfortunately, tailgating around the Superdome has changed quite a bit in recent years. For a long time, fans could pay for an additional parking spot on the top level of the garages and set up their own tailgate. However, that is no longer permitted to allow for more parking spaces on game days. The good news is that there are still plenty of tailgating opportunities around the Superdome. You’ll find fans gathering beneath the Claiborne Avenue overpass and in various parking lots along Poydras Street and Loyola Avenue, keeping the tailgating tradition alive. Fans can also enjoy Champions Square; an outdoor entertainment area located next to the Caesars Superdome. The venue offers live music, food, drinks and a festive game-day atmosphere where Saints fans can come together, celebrate and get ready for kickoff. The Saints Game Day/Superdome Experience: This is where we get to the good stuff. There is no place like the Home Sweet Dome on Saints game days. I was a proud season ticket holder for 16 years and only gave up my tickets once I started covering the team, trading my plaza-level seat for one in the press box. Before I owned season tickets, I would occasionally buy tickets to individual games on eBay or from friends. I have literally sat everywhere, even in the suites, so I can honestly say there is not a bad seat in the house. The terrace level is the highest but also offers the cheapest seats. There is club-level seating that offers premium seats and food options. The lowest level is the plaza, which has tons of food options and two very large bar areas. Speaking of food and drinks, there is no shortage of good options. Some of the most popular include shrimp po-boys, chicken baskets and jambalaya. Of course, there are game-day must-haves like hamburgers, hot dogs and nachos, plus a variety of sodas, beers and cocktails. I highly recommend getting to the Superdome early on game days because traffic around the area can get crazy. The doors open two hours before kickoff, giving you plenty of time to eat, drink and get settled in before the game. From the moment you step inside, the excitement is contagious as thousands of Saints fans decked out in black and gold fill the Dome. On Sundays, the Superdome comes alive as a DJ pumps music through the speakers, the Saints Cheer Krewe gets the crowd fired up, and fans enjoy interactive games on the video boards, giveaways and plenty of other game-day entertainment. So arrive early and soak up every minute of the experience! From the electric atmosphere to the passion of the Who Dat Nation, there is truly nothing like a Saints game in the Superdome. It’s an experience every football fan should have at least once. I hope this guide helps you plan your next trip to New Orleans and enjoy everything that the city and game days have to offer. Laissez les bons temps rouler!

For the Saints, establishing an offensive rhythm early and getting consistent pressure on Rodgers could be the difference. With New Orleans sitting at 2-4, a victory overseas would provide a much-needed confidence boost and offer a sign that the team is beginning to turn its season around. title: A win is a win, but the Saints didn’t exactly inspire confidence
summary: For a moment, it looked like the New Orleans Saints were finally going to give fans a stress-free Sunday. Leading 34-10, the Saints appeared to have everything under control. Then, somehow, they turned a comfortable victory into another fourth-quarter nail-biter. New Orleans surrendered 17 unanswered points and barely escaped with the win. Sure, a win […]
full_text: EAST RUTHERFORD, NEW JERSEY - OCTOBER 18: Isaiah Likely #9 of the New York Giants is unable to make a catch against the New Orleans Saints during the fourth quarter at MetLife Stadium on October 18, 2026 in East Rutherford, New Jersey. (Photo by Caleb Bowlin/Getty Images) | Getty Images For a moment, it looked like the New Orleans Saints were finally going to give fans a stress-free Sunday. Leading 34-10, the Saints appeared to have everything under control. Then, somehow, they turned a comfortable victory into another fourth-quarter nail-biter. New Orleans surrendered 17 unanswered points and barely escaped with the win. Sure, a win is a win, but this performance left just as many questions as the last three losses have. The Saints might be one of the hardest teams in the NFL to trust right now, even when they have a commanding lead. And that is on Kellen Moore and his staff. It’s not easy to take a 24-point lead in this league. The offense did enough to put the game seemingly out of reach, and the Saints looked poised to take care of business. But instead of putting the Giants away, New Orleans allowed them to hang around long enough to make things uncomfortable. That’s the frustrating part. This wasn’t a game like we’ve seen recently, where the Saints have to claw their way back after being down considerably. They had the opportunity to control the game after overcoming an early 10 point deficit and nearly threw it away. Of course, nobody in New Orleans is going to complain about getting a win. After all, the standings don’t care how pretty a victory looks. But the way this game unfolded makes it difficult to walk away feeling entirely confident about what this team can accomplish moving forward. The Saints deserve credit for holding on, but they also need to figure out why that even happened in the first place and how to not let it happen again. For now, the Saints will take the win. But if they want to build momentum, they have to learn how to finish what they start.

Throughout the game, one player stood out and remained consistent, even while the team was riding a wave of inconsistency. That player was Martin Emerson Jr., who is the Canal Street Chronicles Game MVP. Emerson was able to get more reps as Kool-Aid McKinstry was sidelined with a migraine, and he did not disappoint. Emerson finished second on the team in tackles with seven, all of which were solo, and even recorded a tackle for loss. There was a point in the game when it felt like whenever the defense needed a play to be made, Emerson stepped up and made it happen. summary: Martin Emerson Jr. made his presence felt in the New Orleans Saints’ 34-27 victory over the New York Giants, putting together one of the defense’s most impressive individual performances of the season. Emerson finished with seven combined tackles, two interceptions, four passes defensed, one pressure and one tackle. His performance earned him an 88.4 overall […]
full_text: BALTIMORE, MARYLAND - SEPTEMBER 20: Martin Emerson Jr. #22 of the New Orleans Saints looks on against the Baltimore Ravens during an NFL football game at M&T Bank Stadium on September 20, 2026 in Baltimore, Maryland. (Photo by Michael Owens/Getty Images) | Getty Images Martin Emerson Jr. made his presence felt in the New Orleans Saints’ 34-27 victory over the New York Giants, putting together one of the defense’s most impressive individual performances of the season. Emerson finished with seven combined tackles, two interceptions, four passes defensed, one pressure and one tackle. His performance earned him an 88.4 overall defensive grade and a 90.2 coverage grade from Pro Football Focus, highlighting just how effective he was against the Giants. His two interceptions were the biggest difference-makers. Emerson picked off both Jameis Winston and J.J. McCarthy, and was inches away from a third interception late in the fourth quarter. For a Saints defense that’s been lacking consistent playmakers in the secondary, Emerson’s performance was exactly the type of showing that can change the conversation surrounding a unit. The Saints escaped with a seven-point victory after allowing the Giants to erase much of their early deficit. That late-game collapse overshadowed what was otherwise a productive afternoon for several New Orleans players, but Emerson’s performance deserves recognition. If he can build on this performance, Emerson could become an increasingly important piece of the Saints’ secondary moving forward.

summary: Good morning, New York Giants fans! Here are the stories you need to know as John Harbaugh get set to announce their starting quarterback for Sunday. There doesn’t need to be an immediate urgency for Giants’ QB decision | New York Post There must be urgency. A sense of urgency. An emphasis on urgency. Urgency […]
full_text: Good morning, New York Giants fans! Here are the stories you need to know as John Harbaugh get set to announce their starting quarterback for Sunday. There doesn’t need to be an immediate urgency for Giants’ QB decision | New York Post There must be urgency. A sense of urgency. An emphasis on urgency. Urgency for this upcoming practice. Urgency for the next game. The offense must have urgency. The defense must have urgency. Urgency for all. What is probably inevitable does not need to happen right now. What’s the urgency to replace Jameis Winston with J.J. McCarthy? The upcoming schedule offers a smarter option if a change is to be made. DJ Reader: Division is there for us to win "I think that's kind of how you've got to look at it – somebody's got to go take it and we should be the ones to go do that." DJ Reader talks about the Giants leading the NFC East and how important it is to take advantage of other teams losing: pic.twitter.com/HU3SKBw2TV — SNY Giants (@SNYGiants) October 20, 2026 Jameis Winston vs. J.J. McCarthy: Pros and cons of Giants ’ QBs | ESPN.com The element of the unknown is perhaps McCarthy’s most attractive trait. He has talent as a top-10 pick of the Minnesota Vikings in 2024, and who knows, there might be high-end quarterback play buried somewhere in there. At the very least, McCarthy flashed that potential in his short stint Sunday. It was impressive. So was McCarthy’s ability to throw the ball deep downfield. He went 3-of-4 for 119 yards with a touchdown and no interceptions on passes of 20 air yards or more. Winston did not attempt any such passes against the Saints. Harbaugh said he would judge the quarterbacks based on “performance.” And it’s hard to argue what McCarthy did leading the Giants on three scoring drives and close to a fourth even though it was in a helter-skelter football circumstance trying to rally in the final minutes. McCarthy could also provide a much-needed boost to the running game. The Giants designed an offense for Dart filled with zone-reads and quarterback rollouts. That’s better suited to McCarthy’s game than Winston’s. Harbaugh conceded that. Were Giants QB J.J. McCarthy’s late-game heroics real or a product of ‘desperation time’? | The Athletic McCarthy’s arm talent was never in doubt, and he delivered a highlight reel’s worth of impressive throws in a short period. But the Saints played very conservatively as they tried (unsuccessfully) to guard against big plays. They sent four rushers almost exclusively and played soft zone coverage. That was a change from the first half when the Saints crowded the line of scrimmage and mixed blitzes at Winston on passing downs. It will be much different if McCarthy has to play a full game against the Texans’ defense, which hasn’t played up to its standard but still has elite talent, led by All-Pro defensive ends Will Anderson and Danielle Hunter. A key factor in McCarthy’s favor is that he has enough athleticism that opponents must respect the quarterback runs that were a staple of the playbook with Dart. The struggle to establish the run has been a source of immense frustration for Harbaugh. Jameis Winston should be Giants’ starter, but John Harbaugh may go to J.J. McCarthy | New York Daily News Harbaugh needs to steady this ship, not keep running out a different captain every few weeks hoping the change will sprinkle magic pixie dust over the rest of the crew. The first-place Giants (3-2-1) have Sunday’s game against the Texans, a bye and then two NFC East tilts away at the Eagles (2-4) and at home against the Commanders (1-3-1 entering Monday night). Regardless of what happens in Houston, if the Giants beat Philly and Washington after the bye, they would be 3-0-1 in the division entering the back half of the regular season. Winning those division games should be the priority. And frankly, so far, Harbaugh has empowered Winston as this team’s North star since Dart’s season-ending injury. So pivoting hard to McCarthy this quickly could give this uncertain Giants locker room some whiplash at a time when they seem a bit fragile and beaten up. The 11 Biggest Overreactions After NFL Week 6 | Bleacher Report J.J. McCarthy Can Revive the New York Giants’ Offense. Seeing McCarthy on the field during a meaningful contest less than a month after he joined the team shows just how desperate the G-Men are. With Winston reverting to his turnover-prone ways—tossing a pair of picks that effectively put the game out of reach—the coaching staff elected to see what it had in the third-year backup. Although McCarthy racked up 243 passing yards in short order, he also struggled with accuracy (completing just 11 of 21 passes) and turnovers (tossing an interception on his first drive). Those same issues doomed McCarthy’s chances of leading the Minnesota Vikings and will prevent him from becoming a quality starter in the Big Apple. If McCarthy does usurp Winston as the starter going forward, the G-Men will remain a fringe playoff team at best with no real shot at contending for anything beyond a Wild Card appearance. McCarthy: @EvanRobertsWFAN pic.twitter.com/n9yyc7S2ou — WFAN Sports Radio (@WFAN660) October 20, 2026 Jameis Winston ’ s Super Surprise For Breast Cancer Survivors: ‘ Nothing Short Of Amazing ’ | FOX Sports Helping breast cancer survivors has become a passion for Winston, who has held an annual event at games since he was with the New Orleans Saints in the early 2020s. He was inspired by the stories of his Aunt Lois in Birmingham, Alabama, and his Aunt De-De and cousin Tonda in Louisville, Kentucky, who are all survivors of the terrible disease. “It’s one of the most rewarding things I get to do,” Winston told me. “We want to give these women a special experience, but every year I feel like I’m the one walking away blessed. full_text: ﻿New York Giants linebacker Trace Ford makes a tackle against the Washington Commanders. | Getty Images The NY Giants are signing edge defender Trace Ford to their 53-man linebacker, per a report from Dan Duggan . Ford, 25, was originally signed by the Giants as an undrafted free agent out of Oklahoma after the 2025 NFL Draft. He spent that year on the Giants practice squad and was signed to a reserve/futures contract for the 2026 season. Ford was elevated to the active roster in each of the last three games and was a part of an active rotation. Ford has been impressive in the preseason and has earned the trust of the Giants coaches. He was the first man off the bench to spell both Abdul Carter and Kayvon Thibodeaux against both the Arizona Cardinals and New Orleans Saints. Ford might not have the rare size-athleticism combination boasted by the Giants starting linebackers, but he’s solid in both categories and plays with a wide-open motor. Ford takes the place of veteran Jihad Ward, who was released by the Giants earlier on Tuesday.

title: New York City’s best things to do, see, and eat before heading to a Giants game
summary: There’s much, much more to going MetLife Stadium to watch the New York Giants play than simply filing into the stadium, finding your seat, and waiting for the action to start. There is, of course, the game itself as the main attraction, with the tailgating as the opening act. But the stadium sits in the […]
full_text: JERSEY CITY, NJ - SEPTEMBER 7: The sun sets on the skyline of midtown Manhattan as the Empire State Building is lit in blue to mark the New York Giants NFL home opener in New York City on September 7, 2024, as seen from Jersey City, New Jersey. (Photo by Gary Hershorn/Getty Images) | Getty Images There’s much, much more to going MetLife Stadium to watch the New York Giants play than simply filing into the stadium, finding your seat, and waiting for the action to start. There is, of course, the game itself as the main attraction, with the tailgating as the opening act. But the stadium sits in the shadow of one of the world’s greatest metropolises. New York City and New Jersey, where the stadium is actually locared, are home to more things to see, more places to eat (and get anything from anywhere), and places to stay than we can readily count. The Giants are one of the NFL’s flagship franchises, and New York itself is one of the greatest attractions in the world. How could you be bored? Places to stay in New York City It’s New York City! Stay anywhere that your budget allows. If you want to stay as close as possible to MetLife Stadium, there are a number of hotels on Paterson Plank Road actually within walking distance of the stadium. The Hampton Inn Carlstadt at The Meadowlands , Springhill Suites or Fairfield Inn in East Rutherford are all good options in an average price range, and if you want to go a little fancier, check out the World of Blue , a boutique experience right by the stadium. Things to do in New York City Again, it is New York City! You can find anything you want to do. Go to Times Square! The Empire State Building! Macy’s! Central Park! Whatever you want to do, you can find it. The best thing to do right near the stadium? Visit the American Dream mall. The second-largest mall in the country is basically next door to MetLife, and includes MUCH MORE than shopping. It includes an indoor theme park, water park, ski slope, and high-end luxury stores. For more information, please visit American Dream . In New York City, the Circle Line Tour of Manhattan is a must . They have a range of boat tours exploring Manhattan’s history and architecture. We highly recommend the sunset version so you can experience the city lights to their full effect. One of Circle Line’s boats was used for the water rescue when Captain Sully landed his plane in the Hudson River, so even the boat is a little famous. Best places to eat in New York City We keep saying it, but it’s New York City. It is just a few miles away, and it is an easy shuttle or rideshare away. Right near the stadium? Here are three options: Redd’s — Want a post-game or pre-game experience with fans within the shadow of the stadium? This is your place. Yard House — Located inside the American Dream mall. Offersan extensive menu of globally influenced dishes and the world’s largest selection of draft beer. Candlewyck Diner — Love the casual diner experience? The Candlewyck Diner is your place pre-game or post-game. It’s an easy drive to Paterson Ave., just a couple of miles from the stadium In New York City, check out Friedman’s for a massive menu with tons of allergy-friendly options and seven locations in the city. Their cheese blintzes are a revelation. We also recommend the Park Ave. Kitchen by David Burke for the best dry-aged steak you’ll ever have in your life . MetLife Stadium parking, rideshare and transit options The best way to get to MetLife Stadium for a game is to take advantage of the mass transit options. MetLife stadium suggests using either NJ Transit or taking a Coach USA bus. NJ Transit NJ TRANSIT will operate the Meadowlands Rail Service for events with anticipated attendance above 50,000. The Meadowlands Rail Service delivers guests directly to the front door of MetLife Stadium! To access the train while at an event, guests should exit from the MetLife or Verizon Gates. Most of NJ TRANSIT’s rail system connects at Secaucus Junction, allowing fans from the region to quickly and efficiently reach MetLife Stadium. Trains depart from Secaucus Junction, with rail service commencing a few hours prior to kickoff and continuing for a couple of hours after the conclusion of the match. Travel time between Secaucus Junction and the Sports Complex station is approximately 10 minutes. On select occasions, NJ TRANSIT may offer bus service between Secaucus Junction and MetLife Stadium. When this option is available, the NJ TRANSIT team will be on hand to direct you to the designated bus boarding areas. The travel time from the stadium to Secaucus Junction is approximately the same by train or bus. Coach USA bus Coach USA provides the 351 Meadowlands Express bus service from the Port Authority to the MetLife Sports Complex for NFL games and other large events at MetLife Stadium. The 351 bus service will begin two and one half (2 1/2) hours prior to the start of a game and will continue to run until one half hour (1/2) after the start of a game. The 351 bus line will be operational for approximately one (1) hour following the conclusion of the game. Bus drop-off/pick-up is in Lot K, near the Quest Diagnostics Performance Center, which may be accessed by exiting from the MetLife Gate. Please visit www.351express.com or call (800) 877-1888, Ext. 3 for more information. Tailgating at MetLife Gates open to the parking lots five hours before kickoff. You must have a parking pass. For NFL Games, parking is pre-paid and is available on a first-come, first-serve basis determined by parking tier. (i.e. Premium, Reserved, General, etc.) For those ticketholders who do not bring their own tailgating supplies, there are activity zones within the plazas adjacent to MetLife Stadium. A variety of food, games, entertainment, and activities for adults and children will be available in the plaza areas. The Bud Light Beer Garden will be open in Lot F. Please visit the MetLife Stadium Tailgating web page for more information. The Giants game-day experience If you want to do more than sit in the stands and watch the game, you have options. The stadium offers a wide variety of food and beverage options . The stadium features five hospitality clubs that can seat a total of more than 10,000 people.
