title: NY Giants could take advantage if Indianapolis Colts go into fire sale mode
summary: The Indianapolis Colts are 2-4 and fired general manager Chris Ballard this week. There is obvious speculation that the Colts could be in a break-it-down-and-start-over fire sale. The New York Giants could be a team to watch if the Colts go in that direction. Below are my top three targets for the Giants if the […]
full_text: Jonathan Taylor | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Co The Indianapolis Colts are 2-4 and fired general manager Chris Ballard this week. There is obvious speculation that the Colts could be in a break-it-down-and-start-over fire sale. The New York Giants could be a team to watch if the Colts go in that direction. Below are my top three targets for the Giants if the Colts decide to be aggressive sellers—and the NFC East-leading Giants aggressive buyers—before the Nov. 10 NFL Trade Deadline. RB Jonathan Taylor This is the most obvious possibility. Giants head coach John Harbaugh is pining for “ a Derrick Henry circumstance or a Saquon Barkley circumstance” at running back. The Giants ended their four-way timeshare at running back on Tuesday by releasing Najee Harris . That doesn’t mean that they have solved their running back issues. They don’t have a 20-yard run from a running back yet this season. Cam Skattebo has averaged 3.6 yards per carry with four fumbles, Tyrone Tracy 3.1, and Devin Singletary 3.0. Blocking has been part of the issue , but none of the backs have distinguished themselves. Enter Taylor. The 27-year-old is one of the game’s elite backs and would immediately give Harbaugh and the Giants the Henry/Barkley circumstance Harbaugh spoke about. Taylor has four 1,000-yard seasons over his first six NFL seasons, three Pro Bowl appearances, and a first-team All-Pro honor in 2021. Injuries limited him in 2022 and 2023, the only seasons he did not reach 1,000 yards. Taylor had 1,585 yards rushing and a league-best 18 rushing touchdowns in 2025. Taylor signed a two-year, $44 million contract extension with the Colts that runs through the 2028 season. He would cost an acquiring team the pro-rated portion of his 2026 salary, and roughly $34 million over the 2027 and 2028 seasons. His contract includes a 2028 out, with a $7.5 million roster bonus due on the fifth day of the 2028 league year. What would it take to acquire Taylor? SB Nation’s Stampede Blue believes a 2027 second-round pick and a 2028 third-round pick would be an appropriate price tag. Maybe that is an appropriate price tag. The Pro Football and Sports Network trade machine, though, thinks a fair price would involve the Giants surrendering a first-round pick in either 2027 or 2028 to go along with a Day 2 asset. DT DeForest Buckner The 32-year-old is a free agent-to-be who has been one of the better defensive linemen in the NFL ever since the San Francisco 49ers made him a first-round pick in the 2016 NFL Draft. It wouldn’t make any sense for the Colts not to make him available at the trade deadline. The Giants are having success with long-in-the-tooth defensive linemen D.J. Reader and Shelby Harris, but haven’t had much luck finding depth behind them. Buckner would take care of that issue. For now. Buckner seems tired of what has been going on in Indianapolis , and might welcome a new opportunity. There are two problems. If Buckner is available, there figure to be several suitors. The other is cost. A team acquiring Buckner would have to figure out how to fit the pro-rated portion of his $13 million base salary under their cap. I ran this through the PFSN trade simulator, and it told me that third-round picks in 2027 and 2028 AND Kayvon Thibodeaux might not be enough to get a deal done, and wouldn’t quite get the Giants, with just over $8 million in cap space, under the cap. That’s way too big of a price to pay. G Quenton Nelson This one is probably pie-in-the-sky. But, hey, we can talk about it. The 30-year-old eight-time Pro Bowler (every year of his career) and three-time All-Pro is perhaps the best guard in the game. He is going to be in the Pro Football Hall of Fame one day. He remains an elite run blocker and very good pass blocker. He is also in the final year of his contract. Nelson would provide a massive upgrade to a Giants offensive line that has been struggling to run block. Again, though, there are myriad problems in trying to trade for Nelson. Giants left guard Jon Runyan Jr. is a good pass blocker, but a poor run blocker. The Giants, though, gave him a two-year, $22 million extension through 2028 that guarantees him $19.5 million. That’s a lot of money to sit on the bench. The PFSN trade simulator says it would take a 2027 second-round pick and a 2028 first-rounder to get Nelson. It would also put them roughly $10 million over the salary cap, so they would have to figure that out. That is not a trade you can make without getting Nelson to sign a long-term deal, and perhaps considering the idea of transitioning Runyan to center. Are any of these trade possibilities appealing to you, Giants fans?

title: NY Giants release running back who complained about timeshare
summary: The New York Giants have released running back Najee Harris, a team source confirmed on Tuesday morning. After gaining just 2 yards on four carries Sunday against the New Orleans Saints, Harris had complained about not being able to get into a rhythm as the Giants were rotating four running backs during the game. Head […]
full_text: Najee Harris | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The New York Giants have released running back Najee Harris , a team source confirmed on Tuesday morning. After gaining just 2 yards on four carries Sunday against the New Orleans Saints, Harris had complained about not being able to get into a rhythm as the Giants were rotating four running backs during the game. Head coach John Harbaugh said he understood Harris’s complaint, but his message to all of the backs was to “do something” to “take the job” as the team’s No. 1 running back. Harris won’t be given another opportunity. The 28-year-old Harris had 1,000-yard rushing seasons in each of the first four years of his career, all with the Pittsburgh Steelers. He tore an Achilles tendon early in the 2025 season with the Los Angeles Chargers, and signed with the Giants as a free agent during the preseason. Harris had just 99 yards on 31 carries for New York, an average of just 3.2 yards per attempt. The Giants now have Cam Skattebo, Tyrone Tracy, and Devin Singletary at running back. The Giants also released veteran outside linebacker Jihad Ward on Tuesday. The Giants added Trace Ford to the 53-man roster to replace Ward.
author: Ed Valentine

title: NY Giants release veteran linebacker after just 2 games
summary: The New York Giants have released veteran outside linebacker Jihad Ward just three games after they poached him off the Minnesota Vikings’ practice squad. The news was first reported by NFL Network insider Mike Garafolo. Ward tied his career high with 5.0 sacks last season while playing for the Tennessee Titans, where current Giants defensive […]
full_text: Jihad Ward | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Co The New York Giants have released veteran outside linebacker Jihad Ward just three games after they poached him off the Minnesota Vikings’ practice squad. The news was first reported by NFL Network insider Mike Garafolo . Ward tied his career high with 5.0 sacks last season while playing for the Tennessee Titans, where current Giants defensive coordinator Dennard Wilson had that job. When the Giants needed a replacement on the roster for Brian Burns, out with the season due to a torn ACL, they signed the 32-year-old Ward. He was on the active roster for three games, playing in two. In 41 defensive snaps, Ward had just one tackle. Ward was also a Giant in 2022 and 2023. He was a second-round pick by the Raiders in the 2016 NFL Draft. Releasing Ward could be the precursor to adding outside linebacker Trace Ford to the 53-man roster. Ford, 25, is out of practice squad elevations after playing in the Giants’ last three games. In 49 defensive snaps, Ford has eight tackles. He has also played 78 special teams snaps.

title: Film review: 5 plays from NY Giants quarterback J.J. McCarthy
summary: The New York Giants were down 34-10 to the New Orleans Saints with 11:31 left in the game when they turned to backup quarterback J.J. McCarthy. Jameis Winston had just thrown his second interception, and the Giants’ offense was lifeless. McCarthy entered the game and threw an interception on a miscue to Malachi Fields (88): […]
full_text: J.J. McCarthy talking with running back Tyrone Tracy. | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Co The New York Giants were down 34-10 to the New Orleans Saints with 11:31 left in the game when they turned to backup quarterback J.J. McCarthy. Jameis Winston had just thrown his second interception, and the Giants’ offense was lifeless. McCarthy entered the game and threw an interception on a miscue to Malachi Fields (88): Make that 2️⃣ INTs for Martin Emerson Jr.! NOvsNYG on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/k7IrxOuk0n — NFL (@NFL) October 18, 2026 Fields was pivoting outward—a common route concept used by Matt Nagy—and McCarthy thought the rookie receiver would sit in the vacated window left by Pete Werner (20), who matched Devin Singletary’s flare route to the flat. The ball hit Martin Emerson Jr. (22) in the numbers. The game seemed all but over. Kellen Moore put Spencer Rattler into the game, but Jason Pinnock forced a fumble that was recovered by star rookie Arvell Reese, giving McCarthy the football back at midfield. McCarthy would lead a six-play, 52-yard drive that resulted in a 5-yard Tyrone Tracy Jr. touchdown, followed by a 2-point conversion to Isaiah Likely. This drive made the score 34-18 with seven minutes left in the game. The drive was highlighted by the throw below: Q4, 8:24: First-and-10 via GIPHY The Saints ran quarter, quarter, half ( Cover-6 ) against an 11 personnel clearout concept with a deep post from Fields with two deep crossing patterns from Charlie Jones (89) and Malik Nabers (1), with Tyrone Tracy Jr. (29) and Isaiah Likely (9) releasing to hold the middle hook defenders after helping in protection. The middle quarter defender, Julian Blackmon (23), carried Jones’ cross to the hash before transitioning off to Nabers underneath, but by that point, Blackmon was out-leveraged. The throw was hard and direct — it could have used more touch — and it forced Nabers to make a miraculous adjustment to secure the pass from the far-hash. An ideal throw with touch outside the numbers may have led to a touchdown, given how the Saints reacted to the passing concept. Still, McCarthy recognized the vulnerability and attacked for a 27-yard gain that set up Tracy’s touchdown. McCarthy also had a great pocket. Q4, 5:54 : First-and-10 via GIPHY via GIPHY The Giants forced a three-and-out, giving New York the ball back down 34-18. On the first play of the drive, McCarthy saw the Cover-3 look and gave Jones a chance against deep third defender Quincy Riley (29). New York ran two inside-leaning vertical routes to isolate the outside deep thirds in a one-on-one matchup. Blackmon — the middle-of-the-field-closed safety — followed Nabers over the top on his deep horizontal cross toward Fields, so McCarthy let it rip. McCarthy may not have made this throw in a neutral game script, but it made sense down multiple scores late in the fourth quarter. The ball was underthrown and identified by Riley, but the Saints’ cornerback knocked it into the air, and Jones somehow secured it for a 49-yard gain. Q4, 5:11: Second-and-10 Emerson Jr. almost came away with his third interception of the game on a well-defended play against Fields on first down; the ball hit the turf. McCarthy responded well by trusting his star tight end to make a play: via GIPHY The Giants were in shotgun 2×2, 11-personnel, with Nabers and Likely on the same side. Nabers ran a quick curl, which forced Likely’s defender to cover the deep third, as Jones and Fields ran deep dig routes to hold the center-field safety in place; Likely was isolated against safety Justin Reid (21), who had outside leverage, and the inside help was preoccupied with Jones and Fields, while Emerson was with Nabers on the numbers. McCarthy does an excellent job putting the ball high and inside, away from the defensive leverage, letting the tight end maximize his catch radius and secure the ball. This was a very difficult catch to make, but Likely secures it through contact. Q4, 3:29: First-and-15 via GIPHY via GIPHY J.J. McCarthy stepped into the pocket, set his feet, and fired a 46-yard strike to Malik Nabers pic.twitter.com/yzTHzK0eKq — Nick Falato (@nickfalato) October 19, 2026 The Giants were in shotgun — 12 personnel — from a 3×1 nub set with Thomas Fidone II (86) as the nub. Likely was the No. 3 to the far side, and he ran a deep horizontal crosser against Cover-4. Nabers ran up the seam to split the deep-fourth safeties, and he did an excellent job turning the hips of Blackmon with an excellent route where he leaned outward and exploded back to the inside. Fields ran a deep dig underneath the clearouts, and McCarthy had his eye on the isolated Nabers. Plays like these are exactly why McCarthy was drafted so high; not only did he step up and avoid the rush, comfortably setting his feet in a clean pocket, but he kept his eyes downfield and delivered an absolute strike that hit Nabers outside and away from Blackmon. The play design ensured that Reid would not be able to get outside his hash to help Blackmon out with the coverage. A great job by Nabers, McCarthy, the offensive line, and the Giants coaching staff to secure 49 yards. Q4, :40: Second-and-10 J.J. McCarthy layering the football over a Saints' defender to Isaiah Likely for a 20-yard gain. pic.twitter.com/rEHWASWahY — Nick Falato (@nickfalato) October 19, 2026 The Giants got the ball back with :57 left in the game, needing a touchdown. McCarthy scrambled for 28 yards, threw an incomplete pass, and then had this 20-yard completion to Likely with :40 left in the game. Again, 12 personnel nub with Likely as the No. 3 and Nabers as the No. 2. Nabers ran a deep corner; Fields on the outside ran a dig to replace what may have been vacated due to Likely’s horizontal crossing route. The Saints were in Cover-6, and Likely’s dig was to the half-field side. McCarthy used touch — something he doesn’t use consistently — to perfectly layer the throw over the middle hook defender. This is a high-level throw, and one that was inches away from being tipped by Werner. McCarthy threw this in a very high-level situation and gave the Giants a realistic shot to pull off the improbable comeback. Final thoughts McCarthy has now sparked questions about when he should be the starting quarterback for the Giants. The velocity and how the ball jumps out of his hand are undeniable. Is he perfect? No. Did he have mistakes? Yes. Would this have happened in a neutral game script? I don’t know! Still, was this an impressive performance? Of course it was! McCarthy will likely start sooner rather than later, and he’ll provide the Giants with an element that Jameis Winston can’t — mobility. McCarthy performed well, but it was just a little too late for the Giants.
author: Nick Falato

title: John Harbaugh to NY Giants RBs: ‘Do something … take the job’
summary: New York Giants head coach John Harbaugh has a clear message for the team’s running backs, stuck in a four-way timeshare that is not producing results anyone is happy with. “Do something.” After getting four carries for just 2 yards on Sunday against the New Orleans Saints despite starting the game, Najee Harris expressed his […]
full_text: Najee Harris | Getty Images New York Giants head coach John Harbaugh has a clear message for the team’s running backs, stuck in a four-way timeshare that is not producing results anyone is happy with. “Do something.” After getting four carries for just 2 yards on Sunday against the New Orleans Saints despite starting the game, Najee Harris expressed his frustration. “It’s hard to get in a rhythm with one or two plays. The first couple runs will be like, ‘OK, how are they playing it?’ And then the next ones will be, ‘OK, this is how you attack it.’ But if you’re getting a play here and then get taken out for a series, there’s nothing you could do. That’s why I’m saying, ‘I don’t know.’ I’ve never been through none of this before.” At the end of a Monday Zoom call with Harbaugh dominated by the impending decision regarding whether Jameis Winston or J.J. McCarthy will be the team’s starting quarterback , I asked Harbaugh if he understood Harris’s frustratio and what, if anything, he would do about the backfield timeshare. After the loss yesterday, Najee Harris expressed frustration with the Giants' running back usage approach: "It's hard to get into a rhythm with one or two plays…if you're getting a play here and then get taken out for a series, there's nothing you could do. I've never been… pic.twitter.com/DtA0eNqIcP — SNY Giants (@SNYGiants) October 19, 2026 “Do understand it. Respect it. Also understand that that’s earned,” Harbaugh said. “I would love for us to be in that kind of a circumstance. A (Baltimore Ravens running back) Derrick Henry circumstance or a (Philadelphia Eagles running back) Saquon Barkley circumstance or whatever it might be. That would be great, and we haven’t. Our run game hasn’t earned that yet, and none of those guys have.” Harbaugh had acknowledged on Sunday night that trying to split carries between four backs is not ideal . “Now you can argue that. You can say, well, I don’t like that. I don’t like you divvying up the snaps between four backs. And I can tell you, I don’t like it either,” Harbaugh said. “One of those guys needs to step up. Somebody needs to step up and be the back. And none of those guys have done that yet. And when one of those guys steps up to be the back, then they’ll be the back. That’s your answer.” The Giants are 22nd in the NFL averaging 3.8 yards per carry. Nearly all of their big plays in the run game have come from quarterbacks or wide receivers on jet sweeps or reverses. Cam Skattebo’s 19-yard run is the longest by a Giants’ running back this season. Here are the rushing numbers: Skattebo: 81 carries, 294 yards, 3.6 yards per carry Harris: 31 carries, 99 yards, 3.2 yards per carry Tyrone Tracy: 13 carries, 40 yards, 3.1 yards per carry Devin Singletary: 13 carries, 39 yards, 3.0 yards per carry “My advice would be to any player, and it’s all the guys, we had the same conversation. I’ve had the same conversation with all the running backs, the receivers, it’s no different than any position, but do the most you can with the opportunities you get,” Harbaugh said. “Make the most of those opportunities and you’re sure to get more opportunities. Do something. “So, I get it that you want to get out there and you want to get a rhythm, but that rhythm is earned, too, and it just hasn’t happened yet. Definitely want it to happen. A couple weeks ago, we kind of went that direction and the running game was no different than it was this last game.” Skattebo is the only back with double-digit carries in a game, and he reached that number in every game before being mostly sidelined and never touching the ball in Sunday’s loss to the New Orleans Saints. He has had mixed success, only averaging at least 4 yards per carry in one game without Jaxson Dart at quarterback. His four fumbles in five gamed led Harbaugh to look elsewhere against the Saints. Harbaugh did not take issue with Harris expressing his frustration. “I respect that he said that,” Harbaugh said. “I mean, I get it. Shoot, that’s how we all want it. That’s for sure and I respect that he would want that, too.” Who Harbaugh and the Giants turn to when they hand the ball off on Sunday against the Houston Texans is anybody’s guess. “I do know that each of the guys, because I’ve talked to all those guys, is they want to be that guy. They’re not advocating for the other guy to be that guy. They’re advocating for themself to be that guy,” Harbaugh said. “My advice is go out there and take the job when you get the ball. Take the job.”

title: Eagles-Commanders Week 8 game will NOT be flexed out of Sunday night
summary: The Philadelphia Eagles’ Week 8 road game against the Washington Commanders will remain on Sunday Night Football despite previous reporting that it was in consideration to be flexed. The NFL gave thought to moving the 1:00 PM start between the Pittsburgh Steelers and Cleveland Browns into that SNF slot before ultimately keeping Eagles-Commanders instead, according […]
full_text: PHILADELPHIA, PENNSYLVANIA - SEPTEMBER 13: Saquon Barkley #26 of the Philadelphia Eagles runs the ball against Quan Martin #20 of the Washington Commanders during the second quarter at Lincoln Financial Field on September 13, 2026 in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania. (Photo by Mitchell Leff/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Philadelphia Eagles’ Week 8 road game against the Washington Commanders will remain on Sunday Night Football despite previous reporting that it was in consideration to be flexed. The NFL gave thought to moving the 1:00 PM start between the Pittsburgh Steelers and Cleveland Browns into that SNF slot before ultimately keeping Eagles-Commanders instead, according to the Inquirer’s Rob Tornoe . It’s surprising that the league did not move this NFC East battle out of the primetime spotlight. The Eagles have lost four straight games to drop to 2-4 … while also losing starting quarterback Jalen Hurts for the season. The Commanders are 1-4-1 this season and 0-7-1 in Jayden Daniels’ last eight starts. It’s not exactly looking like a marquee matchup. Then again, the Eagles and Commanders are both very much alive in their very bad division. And if the Eagles beat the Dallas Cowboys in Week 7 (a big if considering they’re 4.5-point home underdogs), the Eagles can reach .500 with a win in Landover, Maryland. One would hope the Eagles won’t make us all stay up late just to watch them stink again.

title: NFLPA calls for “full investigation” into Jalen Hurts situation
summary: Earlier on Tuesday, the NFL concluded that Jalen Hurts being cleared to play with a superficial blood clot was “handled appropriately.” On Tuesday evening, the NFL Players Association pushed back on that assertion with an official statement: The NFLPA is not aware of any NFL investigation into the medical care provided to Jalen Hurts. In […]
full_text: CHICAGO, ILLINOIS - SEPTEMBER 28: Jalen Hurts #1 of the Philadelphia Eagles looks on during the National Anthem before the game against the Chicago Bears at Soldier Field on September 28, 2026 in Chicago, Illinois. (Photo by Todd Rosenberg/Getty Images) | Getty Images Earlier on Tuesday, the NFL concluded that Jalen Hurts being cleared to play with a superficial blood clot was “ handled appropriately .” On Tuesday evening, the NFL Players Association pushed back on that assertion with an official statement: The NFLPA is not aware of any NFL investigation into the medical care provided to Jalen Hurts. In fact, the league previously informed the union that it did not plan to review the care he received. Before conclusions are drawn about how this situation was handled, there must be a full investigation into what occurred. Determining the facts is essential to ensuring players receive the highest level of care and protection going forward. The NFLPA isn’t necessarily casting doubt on the NFL’s stance. They’re calling for more transparency, which they’re well within their rights to do. It’s not their function to merely take the league at their word. If everything was truly above board in how the Eagles handled Hurts’ medical situation, a “full investigation” into the matter should reveal as much. The team and the league should be fully cooperative with the NFLPA if they have nothing to hide. It’ll be interesting to see what comes of this request.

title: NFL Trade Rumors: Hollywood Brown expected to be available
summary: With the Philadelphia Eagles’ 2026 outlook not looking so bright at the moment, there’s been a lot of talk about the team being active as sellers ahead of the NFL trade deadline. Much of that focus revolves around key names, such as Saquon Barkley. But here’s talk of a more fringe roster player being available. […]
full_text: BALTIMORE, MARYLAND - AUGUST 15: Hollywood Brown #0 of the Philadelphia Eagles walks off of the field after an NFL preseason football game against the Baltimore Ravens at M&T Bank Stadium on August 15, 2026 in Baltimore, Maryland. (Photo by Perry Knotts/Getty Images) | Getty Images With the Philadelphia Eagles’ 2026 outlook not looking so bright at the moment, there’s been a lot of talk about the team being active as sellers ahead of the NFL trade deadline. Much of that focus revolves around key names, such as Saquon Barkley . But here’s talk of a more fringe roster player being available. Hollywood Brown is “a name that teams seeking [wide receiver] help believe could be traded in the coming weeks,” according to a report from NFL insider Jordan Schultz . This kind of report seems like an effort by Brown’s representation to get teams interested in him to find him a new NFL home with more opportunity than he has in Philly. At the same time, I’m sure Howie Roseman would love to get anything he can in a trade for him as opposed to just having to cut Brown. But I’m not so sure teams will be knocking down the Eagles’ door to make a deal happen. Brown mostly struggled during offseason practices, which explains why he was active but played zero snaps in Week 1. The Eagles then got him involved with some designed touches in Week 2 … but he still only played 17 snaps. Brown then missed the Eagles’ next three games due to an ankle injury. He was not listed on the Eagles’ final injury report entering Week 6 … but the team kept him inactive behind six active receivers (DeVonta Smith, Dontayvion Wicks, Makai Lemon, Darius Cooper, Elijah Moore, and Britain Covey) as a healthy scratch. So, it’s clear that Brown doesn’t have a role in Philly. And it’s clear that he would welcome a new NFL home. It’s hard to believe the Eagles will get much, if anything, for him in a trade. They might just have to cut a player they signed to a one-year, $5 million contract earlier this year.

title: Eagles roster moves include 4 running back transactions
summary: The Philadelphia Eagles officially announced five transactions on Tuesday evening. Here’s an overview: Let’s sort through this news on a player-by-player basis. CARSON STEELE Steele, a preseason fan favorite, recently got called up to the roster after beginning the season on the practice squad. With the Eagles missing their top three running backs due to […]
full_text: PHILADELPHIA, PENNSYLVANIA - AUGUST 28: Carson Steele #34 of the Philadelphia Eagles runs the ball during an NFL preseason game against the Cincinnati Bengals at Lincoln Financial Field on August 28, 2026 in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania. (Photo by Perry Knotts/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Philadelphia Eagles officially announced five transactions on Tuesday evening. Here’s an overview: RB Carson Steele was waived/injured. RB Jaydon Blue was waived from the roster. C James Brockermeyer and RB Ian Wheeler were released from the practice squad. RB Elijah Mitchell was signed to the practice squad. Let’s sort through this news on a player-by-player basis. CARSON STEELE Steele, a preseason fan favorite, recently got called up to the roster after beginning the season on the practice squad. With the Eagles missing their top three running backs due to injury, Steele entered Week 6 as RB2 behind Dameon Pierce. Steele suffered a shoulder injury on his first and only touch of the season, a reception for four yards. He re-entered the game after getting banged up but then left again. Bummer to see him get hurt just as he was getting an opportunity to play. If Steele clears waivers, he will revert to the Eagles’ injured reserve list. JAYDON BLUE The Eagles signed Blue, a fifth-round pick by the Dallas Cowboys in the 2025 NFL Draft, to their practice squad on the last day of August. They then signed him to their roster this past Friday to be a third running back behind Pierce and Steele. But even with Steele getting banged up early on, the Eagles did not trust Blue to play any snaps for them (offense or special teams). Maybe the Eagles will bring him back on the practice squad if he clears waivers. Maybe not. JAMES BROCKERMEYER The Eagles signed Brockermeyer to their practice squad earlier this month, right around when they traded Cam Jurgens to the Baltimore Ravens. He was around to provide more center depth. But with Drew Kendall presumably getting healthier, the team apparently deemed Brockermeyer expendable. IAN WHEELER The Eagles signed Wheeler to their practice squad last week to give them more running back depth in practice. But now they’re going with Mitchell, who offers more NFL experience, instead. ELIJAH MITCHELL Mitchell brings experience to the table with 327 career rushing attempts for 1,523 yards (4.7 average) and nine touchdowns. He was previously with the Eagles in training camp before getting hurt. The team placed him on injured reserve and later waived him with an injury settlement. Mitchell is now back in Philly to give the Eagles more running back depth. It’s currently unclear if Saquon Barkley will be ready to return from his hamstring injury in Week 7. If not, Dameon Pierce is currently the only healthy running back on the Eagles’ roster with Tank Bigsby and Will Shipley on injured reserve. Depending on Barkley’s status, Mitchell could be temporarily elevated from the practice squad to serve as RB2 or RB3 on Monday night against the Dallas Cowboys.

title: Report: NFL concludes Eagles allowing Jalen Hurts to play in Week 5 “was handled appropriately”
summary: The NFL does not believe there was any wrongdoing in the Philadelphia Eagles allowing Jalen Hurts to play in the team’s Week 5 London game, according to a report from The Athletic’s Jonathan Jones (not to be confused with the Eagles cornerback with the same name). The NFL has concluded that the process surrounding Philadelphia […]
full_text: CHICAGO, ILLINOIS - SEPTEMBER 28: Jalen Hurts #1 of the Philadelphia Eagles warms up prior to the game against the Chicago Bears at Soldier Field on September 28, 2026 in Chicago, Illinois. (Photo by Michael Reaves/Getty Images) | Getty Images The NFL does not believe there was any wrongdoing in the Philadelphia Eagles allowing Jalen Hurts to play in the team’s Week 5 London game, according to a report from The Athletic’s Jonathan Jones (not to be confused with the Eagles cornerback with the same name). The NFL has concluded that the process surrounding Philadelphia Eagles quarterback Jalen Hurts being cleared to play in Week 5 with a superficial blood clot “was handled appropriately,” a league source tells The Athletic. The source, speaking to The Athletic on the condition of anonymity because they are not authorized to discuss the matter publicly, says the NFL will not issue any punishment to the Eagles for its handling of the medical process, or for Hurts not being given an injury designation ahead of the game. Questions have been raised about the Eagles’ handling of this situation in the aftermath of Hurts being ruled out for the rest of the 2026 season due his condition worsening. Not to mention initial reports about Hurts playing against the Jacksonville Jaguars without sleeping for as many as 36 hours prior to the game, which have since been changed , as noted by Pro Football Talk. So, in the course of the same day, the reporting went from doctors telling Hurts not to sleep at all to Hurts eventually sleeping up to 7.5 hours at the hotel AND napping at the stadium. None of it makes sense, largely because the Eagles have yet to make anyone available to answer the questions that the media and the public have. Although Monday’s statement from the team mentioned “transparency,” the level of transparency has been selective and incomplete. Only coach Nick Sirianni has spoken to reporters, and his role was necessarily limited. If Hurts has no qualms about the issuance of statements detailing his health situation, he surely wouldn’t object to the doctor(s) who treated him talking about what happened, when it happened, how it happened, why it happened. But it appears that both the Eagles and the NFL hope to run out the clock until the next bright, shiny object captures the attention of our collective goldfish brain. For what it’s worth, NFL insider Tom Pelissero — who originally reported on Hurts’ lack of sleep before later walking that claim back — talked through a timeline of the Hurts situation during a recent appearance on The Ringer NFL Show : From the @ringernflshow on Jalen Hurts, the Eagles, sleep, the timeline and why everyone is on the same page. pic.twitter.com/exVxaD1a2T — Tom Pelissero (@TomPelissero) October 20, 2026 Transcript: “I think this is also a kind of microcosm of the general society, the media — that we’re a part of. I certainly played a role in it today. But anytime you have something unusual that happened, most people — from what I can tell — at least on social media, immediately search for who to blame. ‘It’s gotta be the Eagles! It’s gotta be their fault! How could they? How could they put him on the field?‘ Earlier in the week, it was ‘Jalen Hurts, maybe he doesn’t want to play.‘ Let me just take you inside this because this is a situation where everybody that I have spoken to, all parties are really on the same page here. Yes, it trickled out oddly going back to last weekend where you got one report that he’s not on IR, and then a few hours later he is going on IR. Before that, playing in the game, and then [Thursday] it’s announced that he’s out. And then we learn today that the blood clots have spread from what was initially in his calf, into his lungs, which can be a really scary and serious deal. So, the Eagles from the start have focused more on Jalen Hurts the person and his health than they have the player. So, let me just give you the timeline on what actually happened once they get to London. Remember, they fly over on Friday. Like most teams, the advice was ‘Hey, once you get to London, stay [awake]. Stay up all day, it’s the best way to beat the jet lag.‘ And so guys, all of us who have traveled to Europe, you know you don’t totally have your sea legs underneath you but the worse thing you can do is go and take a nap immediately because then you’re going to be out of whack the rest of the time. So all the players are going to bed, they did this kind of last minute. All the players are going to bed around 9 or 10 o’clock on Saturday night before the Sunday kickoff, which I think is 3:30 London time. It’s right about then that this calf issue, which stems from Jalen Hurts getting cleated a week prior, and then on Friday he was on the injury report but he was listed as a full participant. It’s that Saturday night that they start to realize there might be something more here. So, he ends up going to a clinic that is not exactly close by. Goes and gets an ultrasound, gets these various tests. He’s there until 2:00, 3:00, 4:00 in the morning. By the time he gets back to the hotel, they come to the conclusion that it’s a superficial blood clot. A superficial blood cot — and I’m not going to play doctor on any of this — but I asked doctors how you best explain it and it’s like if you ever see a bruise, like a deep bruise that just doesn’t go away and it’s kinda sitting there, it’s like that, except it’s in the vein. But it’s not something that would preclude you from going out, running around, getting hit, playing a football game. So, Jalen Hurts finally gets back to the hotel. Everybody is, again, on the same page, in the loop. Hurts did sleep. This is where there was a miscommunication among a variety of people and I take seriously my responsibility in relaying accurate information. Again, there were some things that were not communicated, um, as would’ve been ideal in this situation. He DID get some sleep. Once he got back to the hotel. Now, this is like in mid-morning, all of his teammates are getting up and they’re going through their day, he’s sleeping then. They then get him on the bus, they go over to the stadium next, they set aside a room, so he got another hour of sleep actually at the stadium. Which, now, if you walk that back, all those videos that came out from fans in the stands of, like, Jalen Hurts running onto the field … I don’t know if it was after the national anthem or right before — like, last minute, he’s coming out there. It’s because he was going through this whole process to get himself ready. But it was NOT — and I will reiterate this — it was NOT because they told him ‘don’t sleep.‘ There are things you want to do, motion-wise, for the blood clot. But it was not because they were scared it would turn into something more. It was just the logistics of the situation. So, he plays in that game, he played pretty well, they lose the game in absolute crazy fashion in the final seconds. But he threw for over 200 yards and a touchdown. You would not have known, I don’t think, other than he didn’t run a whole lot, that he was dealing with something. They get back [to Philadelphia], Wednesday he practices in full again, but he had a follow-up ultrasound scheduled and it was there that they realized the clot is moving. That’s when the announcement comes that he’s not going to play this week. He goes and gets additional scans. Saturday, they get back the information from another doctor in Boston … and this is after the initial report that was out there that he was not going on IR. Which, it was true at that time they hadn’t discussed IR because they didn’t have all the information, they were waiting for it. They get it back, he’s got what I was told is several blood clots that have moved up and are now in his lungs. That’s a very serious deal, because it had actually gotten into the body. At that point, it was OK, we’re shutting him down, he’s going to have to go on blood thinners. They consulted a…

title: Philadelphia’s best things to do, see, and eat before heading to an Eagles game
summary: It’s well known by everyone that Philadelphia is commonly referred to as “the Paris of the United States.” Well, maybe not. But it’s a pretty dang cool city in which to hang out. There are a ton of walkable parks if you enjoy touching grass, fantastic places to eat for every budget, wonderful places to […]
full_text: PHILADELPHIA, PA - JANUARY 29: People tailgate before the NFC Championship game between the San Francisco 49ers and Philadelphia Eagles at Lincoln Financial Field on January 29, 2023 in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania. (Photo by Hannah Beier/Getty Images) | Getty Images It’s well known by everyone that Philadelphia is commonly referred to as “the Paris of the United States.” Well, maybe not. But it’s a pretty dang cool city in which to hang out. There are a ton of walkable parks if you enjoy touching grass, fantastic places to eat for every budget, wonderful places to stay and, if you’re a history buff, an unending list of sites to visit. Philly’s reputation as a gruff, unwelcoming city couldn’t be further from the truth. Oh sure, we’re gruff, but it’s a friendly gruff, and we like to feed people. So, if you’re coming to the aptly named City of Brotherly Love, here’s a quick guide that can help you get started on a lovely time in the Paris of the U.S. Yeah, I’m trying to get that nickname to happen. Doesn’t feel like it’s got a good shot. Places to stay in Philadelphia If you’re on a budget, Sleep In Center City puts you right in the middle of downtown, next to the Convention Center, China Town and, most importantly, adjacent to Reading Terminal Market. You could spend your entire weekend in Reading Terminal Market, but we’ll get to that in a second. If you’re looking to spend around $150-250 a night, Penn’s View Hotel is right in the middle of Philly’s Old City Historic District, and the building itself carries some of that same charm. It dates back to 1828, with European-styled accommodations that make you feel like you’re someplace Europe-y. It also has its own Italian restaurant in the building, so you won’t have to go far for a delicious meal. And if you’re Mr. and Mrs. Moneybags from Wealthville, USA, you can’t go wrong with the Ritz Carlton or the Rittenhouse Hotel. But if you want to drop a little extra coin and stay someplace higher-end, the historic Bellevue-Stratford hotel is a 4-star luxury hotel that is extremely popular among visitors. It opened in 1904 and is nicknamed The Grande Dame of Broad Street (see, I’m not the only one trying to work the Paris angle in here, am I?). It even has a supper club. What more do you need? Things to do in Philly Well, if you’re reading this I’m assuming you’re a sports fan. So obviously, if you’re in town for an Eagles game, that will soak up most of your day. And if you’re in town for the Phillies, Sixers, Flyers or Union, that’s going to be Destination No. 1. But what else? If you’ve got kids, set half a day (or a whole day if you’ve got the stamina!) for The Franklin Institute . I have so many wonderful memories of Philadelphia’s best science museum, with hundreds of interactive displays and a huge movie theater that has to be seen to be believed. It never gets old, even as an adult. The National Constitution Center, nearby Liberty Bell and Constitution Hall should be mandatory stops as well. If you’re up for something a little different, check out Eastern State Penitentiary , a former prison that architecture buffs would enjoy. Al Capone was once housed there, if that does anything for you. They also do Halloween like no one else, so if you’re going to be in Philly within the next few weeks, check it out! And if you’re willing to leave the city limits by about 15 minutes, the Manayunk neighborhood is a great place for shopping, walking, eating, catching live music, and it’s all within a three-block walk. If you want something a little more traditional, head over to South Street , a place every Philly tourist should hang out at at least once. Best places to eat in Philly If you ate every meal at Reading Terminal Market , you’d be one step closer to Heaven. No seriously, your cholesterol level would shoot up about 100 points in a weekend, but you’d enjoy the experience! There is no place better in the city to get a taste of every kind of food Philadelphia has to offer. An indoor cavalcade of privately-owned restaurants and food stores, it… has… everything. If you’re dying for a cheesesteak, you can certainly get one there at any one of 5-10 places. But roast pork sandwiches are becoming all the rage and, while there are a slew of outstanding options from which to choose, John’s Roast Pork has turned up as the No. 1 spot in more of the lists I’ve seen than any other. As for fine dining, Philly has three Michelin-starred restaurants, all of which hold one star: Her Place Supper Club, Friday Saturday Sunday, and Provenance. But they’re far from the only good ones. I’m big on Italian food, so I’d recommend Vetri Cucina , in which you’re presented with a four-course tasting menu featuring local, fresh, seasonal ingredients. It also saves you the trouble of having to make any choices. Sometimes, you just want the chef to tell you what you should eat and then make it for you. Lincoln Financial Field parking, rideshare and transit options Lincoln Financial Field has a link to all these different options, but here they are in a nutshell. For public transportation: SEPTA Broad Street Line (Subway) is he most direct transit option. Take the southbound train to AT&T Station (NRG Station) at the sports complex. Connections are available from Center City, the Market-Frankford Line, Regional Rail, and the PATCO Speedline. If you’re driving to the game, the stadium is accessible via I-76 (Exit 349 for Sports Complex or Exit 350 for Packer Ave) and I-476 to I-76 East. Parking & Logistics: Parking generally opens three hours prior to kickoff with standard rates around $30 for cars and $60 for oversized vehicles. Full details are available at Lincoln Financial Field Maps and Parking . Accessible drop-offs are in Lot L and Lot J. And if you’re someone who likes to ridshare, the pick-up/drop-off location is at the northeast corner of Broad Street and Pattison Avenue . Tailgating at The Linc The tailgating experience at the Linc is something that one can only learn through experience. It cannot be explained. But there have been some changes to the tailgating locations and rules so if you haven’t been to the Linc for a little while, you may need to pay attention to this. According to the Linc’s website , “Parking areas are generally open four and a half hours prior to kick off. In conjunction with the safety directives of the NFL, all reserved parking areas are subject to a vehicle inspection prior to an event. Tailgating is not permitted in the parking lots north of Pattison Avenue and west of Darien Street (Lots Q-W and the lot near the Jefferson Health Training Complex.) Need a map? Here you go . Also, people are no longer allowed to drive into a parking spot and tailgate wherever they want. Some tailgaters would take up 4-6 parking spaces for their areas and the Eagles have decided they don’t want that to be a thing, anymore. So, attendants now direct vehicles into assigned spaces rather than allowing fans to freely choose or save spots next to each other. And you have an oversized vehicle, you will be restricted to designated sections (primarily Lots D and N) and have to pay $200 for four spaces, with options to purchase up to two additional spaces for $100 each. Standard cars are not allowed in oversized vehicle zones. Lincoln Financial Field game-day experience As this seemingly injury-plagued 2026 season continues, it’s entirely possible this will be one of the few seasons in which it will attainable for a non-season ticket holder to acquire tickets for games without having to take out a second mortgage on their house. The 2-3 Eagles have lost Jalen Hurts for an undetermined amount of time due to a blood clot in his leg. One Hall of Fame offensive lineman retired suddenly and another Pro Bowler was traded. A second one may be traded soon. The star WR and RB can’t stay healthy and it appears as though these Eagles are headed for a lost season. And while that may take a little of the juice out of going to the game, the…
author: John Stolnis

title: The Eagles left Nick Sirianni hanging
summary: They pushed him out there like he was supposed to know. Nick Sirianni did not know, nor was he about to speculate publicly as to what happened to his quarterback, Jalen Hurts, whose season was over when it was announced on Monday due to blood clots migrating to his lungs. Sirianni was out there front […]
full_text: PHILADELPHIA, PENNSYLVANIA - OCTOBER 04: Head coach Nick Sirianni of the Philadelphia Eagles looks on prior to the game against the Los Angeles Rams at Lincoln Financial Field on October 04, 2026 in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania. (Photo by Emilee Chinn/Getty Images) | Getty Images They pushed him out there like he was supposed to know. Nick Sirianni did not know, nor was he about to speculate publicly as to what happened to his quarterback, Jalen Hurts, whose season was over when it was announced on Monday due to blood clots migrating to his lungs. Sirianni was out there front and center looking relatively helpless while being asked about a serious medical situation during Monday’s press conference, which was dominated by a barrage of questions about Hurts’ condition—as it should have been. The assembled media asked the necessary questions. They did their jobs. The Eagles did not. Sirianni should never have been out there answering medical questions about Hurts. It was incredibly unfair to him. It was another botched play in a season full of botched plays for the Eagles. They’re 2-4. They’ve lost four-straight games for the first time in Sirianni’s tenure. Half the team seems like it is on the injured reserve list. The Sean Mannion experiment is failing. The quarterback under center is failing. The Eagles are 30th in the NFL in offense (255.5 yards a game). They are 29th in points per game (17.7)—and last in second half points per game (5.0), last in average points in the first quarter (0.5—yes, less than one point a game), and last in average points in the third quarter (1.0/per game). Hurts, 28, has a five-year, $255 million contract that runs through 2028. This is the caveat in the deal: His guaranteed salary falls from $51.5 million this season to $22 million next year, to zero in 2028. “I’m a football coach,” it seemed Sirianni kept repeating. Sirianni is a football coach, not a hematologist. “The health of our players are as always at the forefront of our mind and leave that up to the medical experts, but we always, always care deeply about our players, and that’s when you are completely focused on together and connection,” Sirianni said. “You’re always thinking about the wellbeing of your guys and that’s where we were in that situation.” Eagles’ general manager Howie Roseman was nowhere to be found. It is Roseman who oversees the medical department. Roseman should have stood next to his man Sirianni when all of this went down on Monday. Instead, Roseman and the Eagles’ franchise left Sirianni out there hanging in the wind. Sirianni was pressed about the team decision to allow Hurts to fly to and back from London with the blood clot injury. Sirianni hardly ever delves into injuries to begin with. “Again, I’m not a medical expert,” Sirianni said. “Same deal there. We get medical information from our guys, and we always put players’ health first and foremost in every situation. That’s where we were there.” You believe Sirianni genuinely cares about his players. And, it seems, his players genuinely care about him. “I’m a football coach,” Sirianni said. “I lean on our medical experts in every situation. I have full trust and full faith in them. It’s not just me who has major care for our players. It’s them as well. I’m glad to be part of an organization that cares about the guys the way our guys do.” Based on their actions, the Eagles do not seem to care right now too much about their head coach. Like him, dislike him, trust him, do not trust him, think he is a good coach or a bad coach, Sirianni deserved better—by his own team.
author: Joseph Santoliquito

title: It’s getting harder to see how the Eagles’ Jalen Hurts marriage ends well
summary: Without having all the facts at our disposal, the impression left by the fiasco surrounding Jalen Hurts’ blood clots, his ill-fated trip to London and the confusing and ever-changing circumstances surrounding it all certainly leads one to believe that the Eagles might have messed this whole thing up. While the narrative around how much sleep […]
full_text: Without having all the facts at our disposal, the impression left by the fiasco surrounding Jalen Hurts’ blood clots, his ill-fated trip to London and the confusing and ever-changing circumstances surrounding it all certainly leads one to believe that the Eagles might have messed this whole thing up. While the narrative around how much sleep Jalen Hurts received prior to taking the field in England is changing by the hour (he did not play the game on no sleep, but reportedly did get a few hours just prior to the game ), it still has the appearance of a less-than-ideal situation. Hurts was obviously not at his most rested, and in my mind, the decision to play him in that game remains a highly questionable one. Also, these international games are awful. They need to stop. Playing football is dangerous and exhausting enough without having to force players to fly over an ocean for 5-6 hours, re-acclimate their body clocks, and then risk their health. If a player suffers an injury serious enough that requires a hospital stay, they have to do it in a foreign country where it may not be safe for them to make a trans-continental flight for a few days. That’s probably what should have happened with Hurts, but that will be a matter for the league and the NFLPA to sort out. Nevertheless, here we all are, six weeks into a disastrous 2026 season that is over. There will be no playoffs and, even if the Eagles somehow win the NFC East with a losing record, anothe title is out of the question. Fans are watching the remnants of a Super Bowl championship roster crumbling before their very eyes, and it feels as though we’re witnessing the end of an era. The offensive line as we know it is gone. The wide receiving room is missing that game-breaking superstar, even with DeVonta Smith in the lineup. Saquon Barkley can’t run behind this line, and can’t stay healthy. They’re down to RB4. There is one tight end. The offensive coordinator looks overmatched. The defensive side of the ball is healthier, but not healthy. Vic Fangio is probably retiring after this season, and who could blame him? What becomes of the defense after he leaves? It would be hard to imagine any head coach being able to sustain a winning record with all these injuries and an incomplete roster, and maybe that has bought Nick Sirianni some time. Or, maybe it will be an excuse for Howie Roseman and Jeffrey Lurie to tear it all down and hire a head coach that can also be the team’s offensive coordinator and play caller. These are all fascinating questions that will be revealed in due course, but the biggest one of all is Jalen Hurts. And after this incident with the blood clots, it’s getting harder to see a future with him under center in 2027. It’s not because Hurts is a bad quarterback, because he clearly isn’t. But even when things looked their most optimistic, there were questions about whether the Eagles would hitch their wagons to Hurts long term after this season. Hurts’ contract extension only guarantees him $22 million following the 2026 season, and serves as an off-ramp for the team to change directions at that position if they want to. The 2026 season was supposed to determine whether Hurts would be able to play well enough to continue on in Sean Mannion’s offense. Unfortunately, we only saw five weeks of uneven play, with Hurts at times struggling to string together drives with an injury-plagued roster and a new offensive coordinator that is still getting his feet wet. And, Hurts also played one of those games on four hours’ sleep in another country after spending the previous night in the hospital because of concerns about blood clots. It’s virtually impossible to judge anything about Hurts’ future based on what’s happened on the field, so Roseman and Lurie will have to make a determination about Hurts’ future based on the circumstances the team is facing as well as the money involved. With Tanner McKee under center the rest of the way, it’s likely the Eagles are going to finish with a top-10 pick. Roseman is likely to start selling veterans at the NFL trade deadline to pile up more picks. In a way, the Hurts situation will make Roseman’s decision at the trade deadline much easier than it otherwise would have been. Saquon Barkley, Riq Woolen, Dallas Goedert, Landon Dickerson and Nolan Smith all should be dealt. The Eagles could pile up enough draft capital in this year’s and next year’s drafts to do whatever they want next April. It’s also perceived to be a solid draft class at quarterback. The opportunity for Roseman to grab a cost-controlled signal caller that can function better in the type of offense the Eagles want to run may be too good an opportunity to pass up. But first, the Eagles have to decide what they want to be. Do they want their offense to look like a Sean McVay/Kyle Shanahan type offense? If so, do they believe Mannion and Sirianni are a good combination to construct an offense like that? Is it too difficult to get someone to create and run an offense with Sirianni as the CEO head coach? That certainly seemed to be an issue last off-season as multiple experienced offensive coordinators turned down the Eagles’ job. The simplest and cleanest way to get the Eagles back on track just may be to get rid of everyone, strip the coaching staff and the roster down, and retool. With a ton of draft picks, the Eagles could rebuild their lines and get a new QB pretty quickly. A new head coach/offensive coordinator would be able to identify the QB he believes would be best suited to run his offense and work on building a new program, starting in 2027. Unfortunately, that would mean Jalen Hurts is traded this off-season. Make no mistake, Hurts is the best quarterback in franchise history . It would be very interesting to see how things would work out if Sirianni was gone and an offensive-minded head coach was brought in who would tailor an offense around Hurts’ strengths. But it would also require Hurts to run the ball more often than he has, and if he’s decided he’s not a running QB anymore, then Hurts’ value as a franchise player decreases tremendously. One also has to wonder if Hurts has lost trust in the organization and how they handled things in London. Sirianni was left hanging out to dry by Roseman and Lurie in his Monday press conference, forced to dance around questions concerning the process that took place. It was bad PR and made Sirianni look like the team was hiding information, although one would assume the ambiguity was done to avoid making statements that could be used against the team in a potential lawsuit and also to protect Hurts’ rights to medical privacy. So we’re left to speculate and guess, and it would appear from the outside that this was handled very badly. It has the appearance of the team prioritizing getting Hurts back on the field as opposed to being conservative and making his personal health the No. 1 priority. Again, that is speculation, but that is the appearance. And if that is all true, does Hurts even want to be an Eagle moving forward? There are so many decisions that will need to be made after these next 11 games are completed. Do the Eagles get rid of all the coaches and start over with a coaching structure that makes more sense? Does Fangio return and, if not, what does that mean for the defense? Which players will be dealt at the trade deadline? But the most important will be … is Jalen Hurts still the franchise quarterback of the Philadelphia Eagles? Right now, it’s getting harder to see how that will be the case in Week 1 of 2027.
author: John Stolnis

title: Eagles News: Jalen Hurts situation “shakes the foundation of what we think we know about how the team operates”
summary: Welcome to The Linc, the daily Philadelphia Eagles links roundup at Bleeding Green Nation! As the great Zach Berman has said, people will speculate in the absence of information. And the Eagles might not enjoy that speculation. But if the Eagles have permission from Jalen Hurts to share more about the specifics of his situation, […]
full_text: PHILADELPHIA, PA - OCTOBER 04: Philadelphia Eagles quarterback Jalen Hurts #1 looks on during the game between the Los Angeles Rams and the Philadelphia Eagles on October 4, 2026 at Lincoln Financial Field in Philadelphia, PA.(Photo by Andy Lewis/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Welcome to The Linc, the daily Philadelphia Eagles links roundup at Bleeding Green Nation! As the great Zach Berman has said, people will speculate in the absence of information. And the Eagles might not enjoy that speculation. But if the Eagles have permission from Jalen Hurts to share more about the specifics of his situation, it sure seems like they should. Let’s get to the Philadelphia Eagles news and links … Bowen: We still don’t know enough about Jalen Hurts’ situation, but we know the Eagles organization is reeling & looks incompetent – PHLY Eagles It’s irritating when coaches do this, because they know very well the medical staff is not available to answer anything. As one Sirianni questioner pointed out, Sirianni is the team spokesman here. It would be reasonable to expect him to be briefed by the medical staff before going out to answer questions. In fact, this was an occasion on which we might have expected to hear from Howie Roseman or even Jeffrey Lurie. Instead we got Sirianni repeating himself, starting multiple answers with “again,” as if all of this was just so repetitive and tiresome for him, hours after we learned the extent of the problem. “We put out a detailed statement for you guys to hear and to understand,” Sirianni said. The only thing Sirianni really made clear is that it wasn’t his decision, to play Hurts or to fly him home. He might get fired this season because of losing, but from what we know right now, I wouldn’t expect this matter to directly lead to Sirianni’s departure. (It could certainly do so indirectly, by exacerbating the losing.) Someone, maybe multiple someones on the team’s medical staff surely will have to have to answer for this, though. […] But it’s bad enough to cast doubt on Hurts’ future here, and by extension, on Sirianni’s future. The organization hasn’t been at a crossroads like this since Carson Wentz demanded to be traded. Even then, though, the Eagles had Hurts. I don’t see Tanner McKee taking the team to any Super Bowls. Overall, this is a shocking failure from an organization that prides itself on its professional standards. It shakes the foundation of what we think we know about how the team operates. Is there a trust issue between Jalen Hurts and the Eagles? – BGN One thing is for certain, some close to Hurts were not happy with how the Eagles dealt with the blood clot situation. They also felt Hurts should have been treated far better by the team this offseason by offering another contract extension. The Eagles never budged. With the perception of how the Eagles dealt with Hurts’ situation, coupled with the looming contract extension, it may not help the relationship. The Eagles Somehow Made the Jalen Hurts Situation Even Worse on Monday – SI This is purely my opinion: I am not sure what the Eagles would have ultimately gained by sneaking Hurts onto the field knowing he was suffering through a dire medical condition and then parking the franchise quarterback on an airplane to let the condition worsen. Again, doing this knowingly would be one of the most significant medical controversies in NFL history and would require firing an entire medical staff. As Mike Florio of Pro Football Talk noted, demand a reexamination of everything when it comes to the way we treat players. Certainly, there have been high-profile stories of team medical professionals acting negligently, and I am not naive to the fact that a doctor can make a horrible mistake. However, this would represent a multiperson, department-wide breakdown for which I don’t have a reference point. But if this were the case, wouldn’t Hurts’s agent be publicly warring against the Eagles on behalf of her client instead of collaborating on a statement with them? There are so many details about the nuances of the treatment, what was known at the time in London, what kind of testing equipment was available to the Eagles in another country before the team made a decision to play Hurts, and what, ultimately, was passed along to the person or people deciding it was O.K. for Hurts to play. We cannot have this narrative both ways: The Eagles seemed to be preparing for a rebuild and, weeks ago, traded one of their best remaining offensive linemen after the Johnson retirement. They also needed to win a game in the absolute destitute swampland that is the NFC East so badly that they would put a quarterback in a life-threatening situation? The Biggest Questions About Jalen Hurts’s Health, and Where the Eagles Go From Here – The Ringer What does this mean for Hurts’s future with the Eagles? Hurts was likely going to be one of the main characters of the 2027 offseason even before this blood clot issue. He’s under contract through 2028, but the bulk of the guaranteed money from the deal he signed in 2023 has already been paid out, and the team could get out of his contract after next season for just a $54.5 million dead cap hit. It’s also possible that Hurts could have been a trade candidate next spring, if the Eagles were interested in moving on, or, if this season had gone well, they might have considered extending him early, before the QB market explodes. Lamar Jackson, C.J. Stroud, and Bryce Young will be among the passers looking for new deals next offseason, just as the quarterbacks from the 2024 draft class—including Caleb Williams and Drake Maye—become eligible for second contracts. The Eagles often try to be ahead of the market—that was the case in 2023 when they got Hurts’s last extension done before Jackson’s new deal with Baltimore. Now, though, it’s not simply a question of timing or cost to keep Hurts, but Philadelphia needing to decide if he’s even still their long-term quarterback. The Eagles are currently on their third offensive coordinator/play caller in the last three years; the most recent change, from Kevin Patullo to Sean Mannion, a Matt LaFleur protege, brought an entirely new scheme for Hurts, one with increased time under center and more frequent use of play-action. The early results haven’t been great—though the injuries, particularly Barkley’s, and personnel changes along the offensive line have made it difficult to give the system a true evaluation. Siranni signed a contract extension in 2025 within months of the Eagles’ most recent Super Bowl title, but it’s hard to imagine that his job is super secure as yet another season spirals away. Playing the rest of this year without Hurts just makes all of those offseason questions more difficult to answer. Eagles QB Jalen Hurts’ blood clot diagnosis explained – ESPN Hurts was originally diagnosed with having a superficial blood clot, according to a team statement released on Oct. 15, which was discovered following an ultrasound in London before the Eagles’ Week 5 game against the Jacksonville Jaguars. It was deemed that mobility was important and Hurts could safely play in the game, per the statement. A follow-up ultrasound last Wednesday showed the blood clot had moved, the team said. Hurts was subsequently ruled out of Sunday’s Week 6 game against the Carolina Panthers and has since been put on injured reserve. ESPN spoke with Dr. Jordan K. Schaefer, associate professor of internal medicine at the University of Michigan specializing in disorders of hemostasis and thrombosis, for a better understanding of causes, treatments, and outlook for those with blood clots. Dr. Schaefer has not treated Hurts and is not involved with the Eagles. The conversation has been edited for brevity and clarity. Jalen Hurts is out for the season. Where do the spiraling Eagles go from here? – The Athletic The problem with this conversation? The worse the Eagles finish, the worse it is for…

title: Steelers’ Mike McCarthy named one of best new coaches
summary: After just over one-third in the NFL’s 2026 regular season, we’ve gotten a good look at the whopping 10 new head coaching hires across the league this year. And according to CBS Sports’ Garrett Podell, the Steelers’ hire of Mike McCarthy has been one of the best of the group. In a Tuesday piece grading […]
full_text: Photo by Joe Sargent/Getty Images | Getty Images After just over one-third in the NFL’s 2026 regular season, we’ve gotten a good look at the whopping 10 new head coaching hires across the league this year. And according to CBS Sports’ Garrett Podell, the Steelers’ hire of Mike McCarthy has been one of the best of the group. In a Tuesday piece grading and ranking every first-year head coach this season, Podell placed McCarthy in fourth place with a B- grade. “The Steelers are starting to find their groove under new head coach Mike McCarthy. Pittsburgh is averaging the fifth-most points per game (28.5) since Week 3, a major improvement after averaging the second-fewest points per game (11.5) in the league through the first two weeks,” Podell wrote . “Pittsburgh also just completed its largest fourth-quarter comeback (13 points, 16-3) since the 2002 AFC Wild Card Round against the Cleveland Browns in its 26-19 overtime road win at the Tampa Bay Buccaneers. McCarthy’s offense has added more life this season to the Steelers’ attack, and Pittsburgh is in a 4-2 bottleneck at the top of the AFC North as a result.” With that aforementioned 4-2 record, McCarthy is currently in a three-way tie for the most wins among newly-hired head coaches, with the Bills’ Joe Brady (ranked second) leading the way at 5-1. Interestingly, despite McCarthy ranking high on the list, he’s still last among the three new head coaching hires in the AFC North this year, with the Browns’ Todd Monken (4-2, ranked first) and the Ravens’ Jesse Minter (4-2 record, ranked third) coming in slightly higher, per Podell’s list. Currently, the Steelers are ranked second in the division, but with three teams at 4-2 and the Bengals not far behind at 3-2, the AFC North is shaping up to be one of the NFL’s best and most competitive divisions this season. Despite being a new face in the division, McCarthy is still by far the most experienced head coach in the AFC North, with 18 prior seasons in the role during his time with the Packers and Cowboys. Over that span, he won his division eight times, and has yet to finish in last place. Now 62, it’s unclear how long McCarthy will coach the Steelers. During his time in Pittsburgh, he’ll be trying to make NFL history as the first head coach to win a Super Bowl with two separate teams.

title: Steelers Week 7 power rankings roundup: Starting to believe yet?
summary: The Pittsburgh Steelers needed overtime to complete a comeback victory against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers on the road. Timely fourth-quarter interceptions by Jamel Dean and Daylen Everette helped the Steelers take the lead late, while Germie Bernard scored the game-winning touchdown in overtime. As always, let’s have a look around the internet to see where […]
full_text: (Photo by Logan Bowles/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Pittsburgh Steelers needed overtime to complete a comeback victory against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers on the road. Timely fourth-quarter interceptions by Jamel Dean and Daylen Everette helped the Steelers take the lead late, while Germie Bernard scored the game-winning touchdown in overtime. As always, let’s have a look around the internet to see where other media outlets have the Steelers ranked among the rest of the NFL in this week’s power rankings roundup. FOX Sports: No.15 (No. 17 Last Week) “I feel like I say this every week, but this is the most confusing team in the league for me. The Steelers look great, then they look terrible, and sometimes — like in their 26-19 overtime in Tampa on Sunday against the Baker Mayfield-less Bucs — they alternate between great and terrible within the same game. They were terrible for three quarters and trailed 16-3. But their defense kept them in it. Then Aaron Rodgers woke up a little. Then he went off in overtime (6 for 7, 51 yards and a TD). I don’t know. They’re 4-2, but the roller coaster is making me a little nauseous.” – Ralph Vacchiano The Athletic: No.16 (Last Week No.16) “The people who bet on Dowdle this season are not happy. The veteran running back was taken off the board 73rd on average, but he’s 215th in scoring (6.1) after Jaylen Warren has taken firm hold of the top spot in Pittsburgh. Warren is 42nd in fantasy scoring (17.1), the highest spot for any Steeler.” – Chad Graff and Josh Kendall CBS Sports: No.17 (Last Week No. 13) “At 4-2, they are tied atop the AFC North. But do we really know how good or bad they are? The defense showed up against the Bucs.” – Pete Prisco Pro Football Talk: No.13 (Last Week No. 12) “Time to get Le Torchon Terrible ready.” – Mike Florio NFL.com: No.17 (Last Week No.22) “It took them nearly all afternoon, but the Steelers finally did it: They found enough offensive production to win a game in an even-numbered week. An unrelenting fourth-quarter comeback effort saw Pittsburgh steadily chip away at Tampa Bay’s lead, taking its own lead late in regulation before asserting dominance in overtime with a 12-play, 70-yard touchdown drive that ended in a Germie Bernard touchdown catch from 6 yards out. The triumphant finish followed a frustrating first three quarters that were all too familiar to Steelers fans, but their ability to break free from their struggles suggests they might have finally unlocked what seemed buried in prior weeks — or at the very least, finally learned how to adjust in game enough to produce late-stage progress. Aaron Rodgers’ reliance on the quick passing game sparked the offense, and Bernard turned in his best rookie performance yet in a Pittsburgh win without significant output from Jaylen Warren. Perhaps these Steelers have some versatility after all.” – Nick Shook Yahoo! Sports: No.16 (Last Week No. 17) “Are the Steelers doing it again? Nothing about them is impressive … except their record. That’s a recurring theme for the Steelers in recent seasons. Pittsburgh trailed 16-3 through three quarters on Sunday and came all the way back to win in overtime. They won despite not having a play longer than 19 yards. They averaged 3.9 yards per play.” “Aaron Rodgers’ performance summed up the day, and the Steelers’ start as well. Against Tampa Bay, he had a negative EPA per play and a very low 3.91-yard average depth of target, according to Sumer Sports. Somehow the Steelers got the win. And they’re two games over .500 with Rodgers being below average across the board in his age-42 season.” – Frank Schwab USA Today: No.18 (Last Week No.17) “He’s only had the benefit of two starts, but WR Germie Bernard already ranks second among all rookies with 24 receptions (17 in those two starts, including 11 in Sunday’s win at Tampa.)” – Nate Davis ESPN: No.17 (Last Week No. 20) “The Steelers’ offensive consistency issues center on third-down inefficiency. They’ve converted only 33% of their attempts, fifth worst in the league. The passing game has struggled against man coverage on third down, and coach Mike McCarthy has acknowledged it, saying he “definitely wants to get the ball ran more.” Even in Sunday’s overtime win over the Bucs, the Steelers went 5-of-15 on third down, including a failed third-and-goal pass to DK Metcalf from the 1 late in the fourth quarter that helped give Tampa Bay enough time to force overtime.” – Cameron Wolfe While I was a bit shocked to see the Steelers fall in a few outlets’ rankings, I suppose it makes sense given the way the Steelers won. Pittsburgh looked lifeless on offense for three quarters before they picked things up with the help of turnovers. The Steelers have obvious problems on both sides of the ball, but keep finding ways to win games. Pittsburgh is the early favorite in Week 7, as they travel to Paris to take on the New Orleans Saints. Let us know what you think in the comments .
