title: Steelers Week 6 grades in win over Buccaneers
summary: The Pittsburgh Steelers are 4-2 after a come from behind 26-19 win over the Tampa Bay Buccaneers. It marks the Steelers’ first win streak of the year, and there were plenty of notable performances to grade, so let’s get into it. QB Aaron Rodgers Jarrett Bailey: For about 50 minutes, Rodgers was rough. Three points […]
full_text: (Photo by Cliff Welch/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The Pittsburgh Steelers are 4-2 after a come from behind 26-19 win over the Tampa Bay Buccaneers. It marks the Steelers’ first win streak of the year, and there were plenty of notable performances to grade, so let’s get into it. QB Aaron Rodgers Jarrett Bailey: For about 50 minutes, Rodgers was rough. Three points through the first three and a half quarters obviously isn’t a good performance, but what he did in the second half of the fourth quarter and overtime looked a lot like vintage Rodgers. He led two touchdown drives, and all five drives in the fourth quarter and overtime ended with points. He finished with 253 yards and two scores, but also had an interception early in the game, granted it was one that was more on Darnell Washington than Rodgers. Grade: B Joey Bray: This game made it pretty difficult to evaluate Aaron Rodgers. For much of the first three quarters, the Steelers offense was lifeless and fairly dysfunctional. However, Rodgers stepped up again in the clutch and kept putting the Steelers in positions to win. Rodgers took five sacks that can largely be attributed to his lack of mobility, which certainly showed up in this one. It was a mixed bag, but Rodgers continues to find ways to lead Pittsburgh to wins. Grade: B- Run game Jarrett Bailey: There was a time in the game where the Steelers went a dozen straight plays without a run. Granted, they were trying to come back from being down 13 points in the fourth quarter. However, they still finished with an average of four yards per carry, which is baseline play for a mid-level run game. Rico Dowdle had 40 yards on seven carries, so it was a nice return to the lineup for him. Jaylen Warren added 50 rushing yards. Overall, it was a largely fine performance. Grade: C+ Joey Bray: The Steelers backfield was back to more of a split this weekend with the return of Rico Dowdle. That being said, it was still Jaylen Warren leading the way with an over 70% snap share. Warren came into the game red hot coming off of three straight games in which he recorded over 100 scrimmage yards. However, Warren averaged under four yards per carry in a passing game script that in turn, meant less opportunities for him. It was Dowdle who averaged nearly six yards per attempt. The running game was not the focal point of the offense in this one, but it’s not like they played bad either. Grade: C WR Germie Bernard Jarrett Bailey: Bernard is going to be this team’s top wide receiver in 2027, and maybe even before the end of 2026. He made an early mistake running back behind the line to gain on fourth down, but more than made up for it throughout the remainder of the contest. He finished with a Steelers rookie receiver record 11 receptions for 87 yards and the game-winning touchdown. He and DK Metcalf were the only receivers to catch a pass in the game, and both made big catch after big catch. This duo has the potential to be a very good one. Grade: A Joey Bray: You simply cannot be too high on Germie Bernard. The rookie turned his 12 targets into 11 catches for 87 yards and scored his first career touchdown on Sunday, which ended up being the game-winning touchdown in overtime. Bernard has established himself as someone who Rodgers can trust with a high number of targets every week. His playstyle is something that will continue to benefit him well, as his ability after the catch is something the Steelers lacked through their first few games. Bernard should continue to see plenty of work in what is a high volume passing offense. Grade: A+ WR DK Metcalf Jarrett Bailey: Metcalf catches a lot of flack from Steelers fans, and a good bit of it is warranted. However, he showed up big time in Week 6. He caught 11 passes for 93 yards, including a potential game-saving catch on 3rd-and-13 in overtime that moved the chains. He also threw a key block on the Bernard touchdown, and he was as excited as anyone in the building when the rookie put the ball over the goal line. For all of the shortcomings when he has a game where he only catches three passes for 12 yards, he’s a selfless player and has shown up multiple times when the Steelers have really needed him. Grade: A Joey Bray: This was Metcalf’s best game of the season in my opinion. The veteran receiver was targeted 15 times on Sunday, as he collected 11 receptions for 93 yards. His 16-yard catch in overtime on 3rd and 13 kept the Steelers alive, eventually allowing them to score. Metcalf was the first to run over and celebrate with Bernard after scoring his first career touchdown. When the Steelers needed him most, Metcalf stepped up and delivered. Grade: A+ Pass rush Jarrett Bailey: Nick Herbig got his first two sacks of the year in what was by far his best showing of the season. Outside of his performance, though, the Steelers’ pass rushers were somewhat quiet. Neither T.J. Watt nor Alex Highsmith registered a sack, and Jalon Daniels finished in the middle of the pack in terms of the pressure percentage for quarterbacks in Week 6. Grade: B Joey Bray: You can’t ask for much more than five sacks in a game. It was Nick Herbig who stepped up in a big way and recorded two sacks in the game. It was refreshing to see Herbig sacking the quarterback after not recording a single sack through the team’s first five games. Yahya Black put together a nice game as he also got in on the action recording a sack. Overall, the Steelers pass rush did just enough to make life uncomfortable for the undrafted rookie quarterback Jalon Daniels. Grade: B+ CB Jamel Dean Jarrett Bailey: Dean set a Steelers record with six passes broken up against his former team, and his interception was one of the final pieces of the comeback. When the Steeler signed Dean, they expected him to be the CB2 opposite Joey Porter Jr. With Porter gone, he has stepped up and been a reliable No. 1. If he can stay healthy, he can be one of the pieces the defense revolves around: Grade: A+ Joey Bray: The Tampa Bay Buccaneers took a chance by choosing not to re-sign Jamel Dean this past offseason. It certainly seemed like Dean made it his mission to let them know they made a mistake this past Sunday. If that was his intention, mission accomplished. Dean came into the game nursing an ankle injury that caused him to miss Week 5, and even left the game injured at one point before returning. When he was on the field, the Steelers’ secondary looked significantly better. Dean made the play of the day when he intercepted Daniels late in the game, allowing the Steelers to take their first lead of the game. Dean is the Steelers’ best corner, and Week 6 showed that. Grade: A+ DB Jalen Ramsey Jarrett Bailey: Ramsey racking up 10 tackles, four tackles for loss, and two sacks with a broken frickin’ wrist (shoutout to Pittsburgh native Kurt Angle) is the type of stuff leaders do. They don’t complain, they don’t make excuses – they just show up and make plays. He’s become one of the Steelers’ irreplaceable pieces on that side of the ball. Grade: A+ Joey Bray: Jalen Ramsey set a career high last season with three sacks. The veteran corner recorded two sacks in this game alone. All of this is being done with a broken wrist, mind you, which has not slowed Ramsey down in the slightest. The defensive back is one of the Steelers’ most impactful defenders, and sealed another win for the team with his second sack of the contest on Sunday. Grade: A+ Defense Jarrett Bailey: There are still things we see on a weekly basis that worry me. The yards over the middle of the field are a concern, but when you only allow two touchdowns in two games, that’s something you can hang your hat on. Still, it’s not an A-worthy game when an undrafted rookie takes you to the brink. Grade: B Joey Bray: It didn’t look pretty early, but the Steelers defense came through in the clutch. Five sacks and two timely turnovers are an effort that is hard to be upset with. The Steelers…

title: Week 7 odds: Steelers open as slight favorites vs. Saints
summary: The Pittsburgh Steelers are coming off a tough road win against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers on Sunday. The AFC North race is heating up, and as crazy as it sounds, the Cleveland Browns lead the division, something nobody could have predicted before the season. The entire division is over .500, and three teams are 4-2. […]
full_text: (Photo by Mike Carlson/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Pittsburgh Steelers are coming off a tough road win against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers on Sunday. The AFC North race is heating up, and as crazy as it sounds, the Cleveland Browns lead the division, something nobody could have predicted before the season. The entire division is over .500, and three teams are 4-2. Every game is critical, and the Steelers look to continue their winning streak with a win over the New Orleans Saints in Paris, France. According to FanDuel Sportsbook , the Steelers open as three-point favorites despite the neutral site. The Saints are coming off a victory of their own after a furious comeback attempt by the New York Giants, and J.J. McCarthy fell just short. The over/under is 44.5, and Steelers moneyline odds sit at -174. The line will move with injury news from both teams, but this feels right. On the one hand, the Saints offense is a handful, but the defense, aside from Chase Young and a few other players, is vulnerable. The key will be getting off to a faster start on offense and defense. At the beginning of the Tampa Bay game and for much of the game, the Steelers felt stuck in neutral. The offense and defense kicked it into gear down the stretch and snatched victory from the jaws of defeat. Rookie wide receiver Germie Bernard was fantastic and has quickly earned the trust of Aaron Rodgers. Trust me, that isn’t easy to earn. Rodgers and Bernard looked like Rodgers and Cobb from the Packers days. D.K. Metcalf turned in a big game and made critical plays down the stretch. While the receiver room gets healthy, the two receivers will need to continue making plays. Jaylen Warren slowed down off his torrid pace, but Rico Dowdle was effective on Sunday. Still, at the end of the game, Warren was the one making big plays in overtime. It’s the NFL and every game is difficult, but the Steelers need this one and Vegas believes they will get it done. title: Seahawks host former SEC Defensive Player of the Year for a tryout
summary: Defense may not be a huge concern in Seattle at the moment, but the team is always looking to improve and bring in talent. The Seattle Seahawks brought in a pass rusher for a tryout this week. A fourth-round pick of the Los Angeles Chargers in the 2025 NFL draft, Kyle Kennard was hurt in […]
full_text: Defense may not be a huge concern in Seattle at the moment, but the team is always looking to improve and bring in talent. The Seattle Seahawks brought in a pass rusher for a tryout this week. A fourth-round pick of the Los Angeles Chargers in the 2025 NFL draft, Kyle Kennard was hurt in a joint practice with the San Francisco 49ers and subsequently waived from injured reserve by the Bolts on Sept. 4. Kennard was the SEC Defensive Player of the Year with the South Carolina Gamecocks in his final season in college, as well as bringing home the Bronko Nagurski Trophy as the top defensive player in the NCAA. The long-limbed EDGE rusher admitted some frustration in not playing as much as he was used to and said that there was “a learning curve” in his rookie season. When he got to Los Angeles, Kennard played in five games in his rookie season, recording 2 tackles. The Chargers ended up taking a pass rusher in the first round this past spring, in Ahkeem Mesidor. The Seahawks are tied for the fifth-highest total of sacks as a team so far this year (16), and have a strong rotation, but Connor O’Toole (2 tackles) has been mostly a special teams player, while Jared Ivey was claimed by the Atlanta Falcons . Could Kennard be a developmental piece in the pass rush? A tryout is just a tryout, but nice to see the team focused on bottom of the roster development.

title: Seahawks Reacts Survey: Will Kenneth Walker snap Seattle’s ‘No 100-yard rusher’ streak?
summary: Welcome to SB Nation Reacts, a survey of fans across the NFL. Throughout the year we ask questions of the most plugged-in Seahawks fans and fans across the country. One of these days, the Seattle Seahawks defense will allow a 100-yard rusher again. James Cook of the Buffalo Bills is the last one to crack […]
full_text: Welcome to SB Nation Reacts, a survey of fans across the NFL. Throughout the year we ask questions of the most plugged-in Seahawks fans and fans across the country. One of these days, the Seattle Seahawks defense will allow a 100-yard rusher again. James Cook of the Buffalo Bills is the last one to crack the century mark, rampaging for 111 yards and a couple of scores in a 31-10 thrashing at Lumen Field. It’s been 35 consecutive games of mostly exemplary run defense by the Seahawks since October 2024, but this week presents their toughest challenge yet… and yet their most familiar one. Kenneth Walker III is showing he can be an undisputed RB1 with the Kansas City Chiefs. The Super Bowl MVP leads the NFL in rushing with 665 yards, which is more than the entire Seahawks rushing attack put together. He’s averaging over six yards per carry and has only failed to crack the 100-yard mark once in five games. He’s now going up against the stingy Seahawks run defense, albeit one that that has been caught out a little more than last year in terms of giving up explosive runs. So… is it going to happen? Is K9 going to be the one to crack Seattle’s vaunted run defense? Or will the Seahawks defense find a way to shut down their former teammate? Keep in mind that if the Seahawks, say, jump out to a 31-3 lead in the first half and the Chiefs generally have no choice but to keep throwing the ball, Walker could be rendered a non-factor through sheer game script circumstances. Alternatively, if the Seahawks’ sick addiction to turnovers doesn’t stop and the game gets out of hand the other way, K9 could feast even more as the Chiefs keep running the ball relentlessly. Your other question is the weekly confidence poll, which I imagine is just going to keep tanking until the Seahawks win again. Vote in the surveys below! Will Kenneth Walker III go off? title: Seattle’s best things to do, see, and eat before heading to a Seahawks game
summary: Seattle. The Emerald City. Home of Starbucks, Pike Place Market, the Seattle Storm, and the reigning Super Bowl Champions Seattle Seahawks. People come to Seattle from all over to check out the sights of the rainy city; whether it is because of Grey’s Anatomy, Twilight, Dungeon Crawler Carl, or for sports, it is a travel […]
full_text: Photo by Steph Chambers/Getty Images | Getty Images Seattle. The Emerald City. Home of Starbucks, Pike Place Market, the Seattle Storm, and the reigning Super Bowl Champions Seattle Seahawks. People come to Seattle from all over to check out the sights of the rainy city; whether it is because of Grey’s Anatomy, Twilight, Dungeon Crawler Carl, or for sports, it is a travel destination. I have gone to Seattle plenty of times, and still find out new things to do. Seattle is a great sports city. It has basketball, baseball, hockey, soccer, rugby, and most importantly for this article, football. If you are looking to plan a trip to the Emerald City to watch the reigning Super Bowl Champions play a home game in one the toughest and loudest stadiums in the NFL, I am going to do my best to help you out in that endeavor. Looking at places to stay, things to do, places to grab something to eat, transportation, tailgating, and what it is like to be at the game! I will give three options per section to cover various budgets and experiences people are looking for. Let’s dive into it! Places to stay in Seattle Seattle is a major city, and there are plenty of places to stay. For those with families, I would recommend Lower Queen Anne/Seattle Center. It is a fairly quiet and safe area, with plenty of family-centric activities to experience, such as the Pacific Science Center , the Space Needle , and the Museum of Pop Culture (formerly the Entertainment Music Project aka EMP). The Mediterranean Inn and Hampton Inn & Suites are quite affordable for families, with prices ranging from $104 per night to $200 per night. You are also about 15 minutes from Lumen Field in this spot. For those who are visiting Seattle for the first time and price is not as much of a concern, Downtown & the Waterfront are the places to stay. You are near the Link light rail so it is easy to go straight from SeaTac Airport to where you will be staying and then back to SeaTac. You will have a lovely view of the waterfront and be near Pike Place Market. Lumen Field is about 10 minutes from where you will be staying so it is convenient. The Mayflower Park Hotel and the Inn at the Market are both highly recommended places to stay, with prices ranging from $160 to $350 per night. Now for those who like the night life and local vibes, Belltown and Capitol Hill are your choices. Belltown has plenty of coffee shops, bars, and restaurants for you to try out, while Capitol Hill has indie boutiques, historic parks, and a night life of its own. The Belltown Inn has prices starting at $93 per night and is about 20 minutes from Lumen Field. Meanwhile, the Seattle Gaslight Inn is a nice B&B with prices starting at $138 per night and is about 18 minutes from Lumen Field. Things to do in Seattle Like mentioned previously, there are plenty of things to do in Seattle, and it is hard to narrow it down to three things, but I will do my best. Starting off, the Museum of Pop Culture is near the top of my list. Whether you love music, fantasy, science fiction, horror, gaming, it has a bit of something for everyone. It regularly has traveling exhibits go through there. In past years it has had a Van Gogh exhibit, a Disney exhibit, and it currently has a History of Hip-Hop exhibit. General Admission will run you around $40 per person, and is located at the Seattle Center. The Seattle Waterfront is another great place to visit, and it has something for everyone, especially families. Miners Landing at Pier 57 has the Great Wheel, an arcade, the historic Ferris Wheel, and the underrated Wings Over Washington. Families will for sure find something interesting to do there. At Pier 59 there is the Seattle Aquarium , which has lots of Pacific sea life to learn about and see, and now has a behind-the-scenes tour to experience. Prices for the aquarium start around $55. Most people will recommend the Space Needle or Pike Place Market , or Chihuly Garden , which are great and I highly recommend. One thing to do in Seattle that is not talked about a lot and I definitely have recommended to people is the Underground Tours . Seattle is a city built upon a city, and you can take tours of underground old Seattle that the current city was built upon after the Great Fire of 1889. It is a fascinating experience. It’s about a 75-minute tour and tickets are about $10 for children and $30 for adults. CityPass offers some combined tickets at a discount if you’d like to check out multiple spots! Best places to eat in Seattle Seattle is a great food city. To start, if you love Asian cuisine, The Wild Ginger is one I personally recommend. With food inspired by eastern Pacific Rim, China, Indonesia, Malaysia and Vietnam, you will find something you like. I personally recommend their Sri Lankan Lamb Curry. It can be a bit more expensive, with prices for meals ranging from $17 to $52 per person, but it is well worth the price in my opinion. Beecher’s Handmade Cheese is a staple in Downtown Seattle right on Pike Place Market. When they say they have the best mac n’ cheese, they are not lying. I still dream about their mac n’ cheese some nights. They make their grilled cheese with their Flagship Cheddar Cheese, and it melts perfectly in your mouth. For those with young kids who love those staple comfort foods, and for those adults who live by the motto “what’s the point in being an adult if you cannot be a child at times” (it’s me, I am one of those adults), Beecher’s is a must. Prices range from between $3.12 and $27 depending on the item. A personal favorite of mine, and one that I take family and friends to when they visit Seattle, is the Athenian Seafood Restaurant . Seattle is known for its seafood, and the Athenian is a staple in that area. With a beautiful view of the water, nestled in Pike’s Place Market, it feels as though you are in the heart and soul of Seattle. Established in 1909 by the three Pappadakis brothers, it has been serving up local seafood for over one-hundred years. Their grilled salmon and halibut are some of the best that I have had, and their Dungeness crab fettuccine will haunt your dreams (in a good way) after you have had it. Prices typically range from $20 to $30 per person. Lumen Field parking, rideshare, and transit options Parking at Lumen Field will cost you. It is not very cheap. I parked a few blocks away on opening night against the New England Patriots this season and it cost me $80. Now, you can park at Lumen Field and get tickets for it through Ticketmaster . Prices vary, ranging from $50 to over $150, with an average price of around $75. My recommendation would be to use the Link light rail . Parking at the stations is free, and round trip tickets are $6. I used it with a friend of mine when we went to the Los Angeles Chargers game. It is clean, easy, and the light rail is about five minutes between stations, and they have four running so you can be sure to get to the station well in time. The downside is that you will need to walk to the stadium from the station, but it is not too far. You can also, of course, use Uber and Lyft or other ride share options to get to the stadium. You can also use MetroFlex or the King County Bus system to get to the stadium. The bus fare and MetroFlex fares are $3, which is very reasonable. It may take longer than Uber or Lyft, but it is more reasonably priced. Tailgating at Lumen Field There is no tailgating in the parking lot or garages at Lumen Field. There is an official tailgate at the WAMU Theater which is fun. Blue Thunder plays, it is connected to the stadium, and you can buy gear. Very convenient. Fun Seahawks museum, great food, and you can get some free gifts, like a Devon Witherspoon poster that I received at the Chargers game. Hawk Alley is also a popular tailgating area. Hawk Alley is a historic Seattle Seahawks pregame tailgating spot located along Utah Avenue South. Lots of fans, great atmosphere. It is a bit of a walk to the stadium, but it is definitely…

title: Mike Macdonald: Zach Charbonnet could make Seahawks return ‘in some capacity’ vs. Chiefs
summary: The Seattle Seahawks need any sort of running back help they can get, as they fittingly face the Kansas City Chiefs and former Seahawks star, Super Bowl 60 MVP, and current NFL rushing leader Kenneth Walker III on Sunday night. While Jadarian Price is not an option until Week 8 against the Chicago Bears, Zach […]
full_text: The Seattle Seahawks need any sort of running back help they can get, as they fittingly face the Kansas City Chiefs and former Seahawks star, Super Bowl 60 MVP, and current NFL rushing leader Kenneth Walker III on Sunday night. While Jadarian Price is not an option until Week 8 against the Chicago Bears, Zach Charbonnet seems on course to make his season debut this weekend. Seahawks head coach Mike Macdonald told reporters on Monday that Charbonnet could play, pending how this week’s practice goes. “Zach is going to have a full week’s worth of reps, so that’s exciting,” Macdonald said. “There is a possibility that you can see him on Sunday in some capacity.” Charbonnet has to be activated off injured reserve and onto the 53-man roster this week, otherwise he reverts to IR for the rest of the season. Even when he’s activated, that doesn’t necessarily mean he’ll play Week 7, but Macdonald’s quotes sound encouraging. In the meantime, he’s practiced in a limited capacity throughout his 21-day window, but it sounds like “full week’s worth of reps” could mean a full participant designation in the Wednesday, Thursday, and Friday practices. The fourth-year man out of UCLA was Seattle’s leader in total touchdowns last season with 12, to go along with his career-best 730 yards on the ground. With Emanuel Wilson and George Holani having ball security and efficiency struggles, Charbonnet’s impending return from a January ACL tear is about as welcome and desperately need outcome as the Super Bowl champions can get. “I know he’s had a certain date in mind, which is a really ambitious date,” Macdonald said. “For those who have tried to come back from significant knee surgery understand the undertaking that takes. Zach’s a beast. He looks great. It’s not easy to say, ‘Alright, let’s go.’ For him to have that courage to say that and work through the things that he’s worked through, you can’t do anything but tip your cap to him.” Charbonnet’s practice status on Wednesday should give us a solid indicator as far as whether or not he’ll be able to help out an otherwise struggling Seahawks offense on Sunday.

title: Why the Seattle Seahawks don’t need to bench Sam Darnold
summary: We’ve all sat with this one for a bit. Is Sam Darnold not the answer? Did he get rushed back from injury? Would the Seahawks be better off with Andrew Lock as the trigger man? One thing is clear: Seven interceptions in four games is… not good. Pulling the struggling quarterback can feel like the […]
full_text: We’ve all sat with this one for a bit. Is Sam Darnold not the answer? Did he get rushed back from injury? Would the Seahawks be better off with Andrew Lock as the trigger man? One thing is clear: Seven interceptions in four games is… not good. Pulling the struggling quarterback can feel like the quickest and easiest lever to pull. The Seattle Seahawks, of course, will have a long wait until they can wash the sour taste of recent putrid performances on offense out of their collective mouths. The run of losses to the San Francisco 49ers and the Denver Broncos in the last two games featured plenty of frustrating mistakes to pave the road to an unspectacular 3-3 record. How do the 2026 Seahawks continue to run it forward? Brock Purdy hadn’t been sacked before facing the ‘Hawks, then got taken down three times by the “Dark Side.” That stop unit held SF to 4/12 on 3rd downs and tainted his pristine trajectory to hand him his 2nd INT of the season (first since the opening week). Bo Nix was held under 110 passing yards. It’s the offense that failed in their mission to be complimentary. Does Seattle need to bench their championship quarterback? Let’s start by not turning the ball over. The Seahawks offense has lost more EPA on turnovers than any other team in the NFL. 12 turnovers through six weeks is the most for any Seahawks offense in the last 25 years. — Sheil Kapadia (@SheilKapadia) October 16, 2026 I want to preface all of this and say that backup halfback, George Holani was questionable to play in Santa Clara. With that in mind, he deserves some appropriate credit, as a warrior for this team. He also deserves credit for being a strong pass protector… at times. Having said that, the man put the ball on the ground twice against the Niners, contributing to a sloppy performance by the Hawks. If you did not know, NFL coaches are serious about fumbles . That hyperlink is the Buffalo Bills head coach Joe Brady talking about reducing the load of player who led the league in rushing TD’s in 2024 and rushing yards in 2025. The thing is, Holani averages over seven touches per game. Before TNF, Shaheed was averaging a little over two touches per. I know you don’t want to have tells when a specific back is in the game… but perhaps time for less? That’s what I thought before the Broncos game. Rashid Shaheed got $34M guaranteed on his contract extension this past offseason. I wanted to see the Hawks use short passes as an extension of the run game, if need be, just to get his involvement in line with his contract priority. Then that man fumbled twice. Who’s next to get added to the mix? Here are Tory Horton’s last 8 catches: first down, touchdown, 6 yards, touchdown, first down, first down, first down, touchdown. He was not targeted in Week 6 against the Niners. Tory, come on down!! View this post on Instagram Interceptions are a little more convoluted of a blame game than fumbles. Cooper Kupp addressed the throw to Horton : “certainly within the grounds of what that play was. Got to make a play.” The same Cooper who is no longer a dynamic threat on the field. Is it possible that the 2026 Seattle Seahawks are simply in need of another high-level playmaker to join JSN in the priority list for defenses to worry about? Kenneth Walker III was that last season, but I’m not sure he’s the only. Is the pantry now raided? Does Seattle need to draft a wideout in the first round in the upcoming offseason? Let’s hit pause on that for now. Is it the offensive line? I mean, Abe Lucas’ performance was groan-worthy at times. When discussing the five sacks that Darnold took and how it reflects on the offensive line, Mike Macdonald explained, saying , “I mean, you can say it’s on the offensive line–it’s on our offense. You know, it’s both. It’s how efficient we can run the ball; how efficient we can move the ball other ways. The quarterback is getting hit way too much, so everybody sees that.” There are multiple angles here. Role players may be touching the ball a little more than originally planned, but also there is the question of scheme. As Field Gulls’ own Mookie Alexander mentions , “At the moment, the Seahawks do not have the type of offense that can control a game through the run. They are a much better passing team on early downs yet adopt a run-first mentality.” Mike Macdoanld on why the ball is being put in jeopardy so often : “In short, it’s really a function of ‘who’s applying pressure to who?’ So, if we’re playing the way we want to play, we should be applying pressure to defenses. Then, all of a sudden –it’s funny how that works–ball isn’t as in jeopardy as much.” It’s unfortunate that the running back that the ‘Hawks took in Round 1 of the NFL draft joins another early round back on the injury ledger, in Zach Charbonnet. Those two, along with up-and-comers like Jacardia Wright and (the no longer on the roster) Kenny McIntosh all being unavailable is sad. Does that mean that we should hit the panic button? Darnold does need to get into flow state. And yes: Sam should be expected to be able to get it done… even in the absence of a run game. Even if conditions are not perfect, we should expect him to be able to figure it out. He’s a Super Bowl-winning signal caller, but if he keeps throwing two INT’s per game, Seattle brass may have to pull him at some point . That point is not now. Coach Mike addressed the controversy around Sam Darnold, saying that, “I know we’re harping on the turnovers… but he’s been able to escape some really nasty pressure situations and find ways to move the ball down the field, that not a lot of people can do. That’s definitely in his skillset and we encourage him to continue to do that, within your progressions and things like that.” Seattle prides itself on cultivating environments for passers to succeed in. That environment seems crippled at the moment. View this post on Instagram Macdonald plainly stated that, “we got to be able to execute our run game and hold on to the football… straight up.” All of the coaches on staff will be tasked with exploring ways to improve this slumping offense. Those of you who think Brian Fleury and, to some extent, Sam Darnold are under some level of pressure are kidding yourselves. There is a standard. It will be interesting to see what Fleury chooses to change, if anything, headed into a possible humiliation ritual against Ken Walker. Now, acknowledging that things need to change, we can also understand that making a QB change is a very big deal. It’s one that has ripple effects on the direction of the franchise for years to come. "To bench a quarterback is a huge sea change kind of shift that will affect not just this season, but the entire future of the organization." 👀 @TheMikeSalk on the #Seahawks sticking with QB Sam Darnold amid turnover struggles. pic.twitter.com/sVJYoW6oZ8 — Seattle Sports (@SeattleSports) October 17, 2026 We can blame the run game, we can blame injuries, we can blame Shaheed, we can blame Tory Horton, we can blame the offensive line, and yes… we can blame Sam Darnold. Hell, you can blame Hard Knocks if you want to. This is not the end of the season as we know it. The Seahawks have totaled 10 turnovers in their 3 losses… and still only lost those by a collective sum of 8 points overall. Maybe the sky isn’t truly falling quite yet. Let’s just wait and see what things look like when Jadarian Price, Zach Charbonnet and Anthony Bradford make their returns to the lineup. Yes, THAT Anthony Bradford. View Link

Mike Evans’ injury isn’t considered long-term, but the Niners would be wise to give Evans two weeks to recover from the Achilles soreness he’s dealing with. Without Evans, the 49ers don’t have a true X receiver. Kirk brings veteran presence and can win at multiple levels Here’s how the 49ers’ snap counts were against the Commanders at wide receiver: Jordan Watkins – 47 Brandin Cooks – 31 Mike Evans – 24 Jacob Cowing -15 Malik Turner – 3 Watkins will have to own that “X” role for at least a week. The decision to part ways with Jones is a reflection of getting James Thompson back from injury. San Francisco rolled with the foursome of Osa Odighizuwa, Sebastian Valdez, Gracen Halton, and Thompson. Keion White also gets a good number of snaps at defensive tackle.

title: Malik Mustapha channels early-season frustration into game-saving performance
summary: It was not an easy start to the season for Malik Mustapha, who, after missing most of training camp with a hamstring strain, spent much of the first four weeks of the new campaign watching from the sideline. Mustapha played only sporadic defensive snaps after falling behind Ji’Ayir Brown and Marques Sigle in the pecking […]
full_text: SANTA CLARA, CALIFORNIA - OCTOBER 19: Malik Mustapha #6 of the San Francisco 49ers reacts during the fourth quarter against the Washington Commanders at Levi's Stadium on October 19, 2026 in Santa Clara, California. (Photo by Brooke Sutton/Getty Images) | Getty Images It was not an easy start to the season for Malik Mustapha, who, after missing most of training camp with a hamstring strain, spent much of the first four weeks of the new campaign watching from the sideline. Mustapha played only sporadic defensive snaps after falling behind Ji’Ayir Brown and Marques Sigle in the pecking order at safety. But an injury to the latter opened the door for 2024 fourth-round pick Mustapha, whose performances in helping the 49ers improve to 6-0 have served as a reminder of why he was viewed as a potential cornerstone defensive piece following his rookie year. Mustapha played a crucial role in the 49ers’ Week 5 win over the Seattle Seahawks, consistently flying to the football and making a spectacular pass deflection before his hit on Cooper Kupp on the game’s decisive fourth down sealed victory for the Niners. And in the Niners’ tense primetime victory over the Washington Commanders, Mustapha was once again the player who rescued the game for San Francisco. With the Commanders on the 49er 17-yard line with 2:19 remaining in the game and hoping to complete a highly improbable comeback from 23-3 down, Mustapha made two successive outstanding plays that underlined his importance to a defense that is surging under coordinator Raheem Morris. What a HIT to stop the run 😳 WASvsSF on ESPN Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/bokW7WEjxE — NFL (@NFL) October 20, 2026 Mustapha displayed the downhill closing speed that is a predominant feature of his game as he fired into the backfield to stuff Jeremy McNichols on third-and-3, before then producing an outstanding play on the ball to prevent Treylon Burks from catching a touchdown on fourth down that would have left Washington with an extra point to take the lead. The Commanders got the ball back for one last chance at a remarkable turnaround, but their failure to get anywhere close to the endzone on the final series left Mustapha to take in the plaudits for his game-saving heroics. Said tight end George Kittle: “I know that Malik was like gnawing on a bone like a rabid dog when he wasn’t playing and so the fact that he’s getting in there and now he’s just taking advantage of that opportunity, I think I’ve said that 100,000 times up on this podium, talking about guys taking advantage of their opportunity. And that juice that he brings, I know that that helps Fred [Warner], that helps the defense, keeps his guys alive. And that play in the fourth quarter where he just came down and stuffed the running back, that was fantastic.” While Mustapha’s frustration at not being involved significantly in the opening weeks may have been obvious to Kittle, the critical thing for the former Wake Forest star is that he saw the situation of often being in the role of spectator as an opportunity to develop his game. And, over the last two games, it is clear that extra time to study and learn has been beneficial for Mustapha. “I didn’t have the start that I wanted this year, but it gave me a chance to really scale back, take a step back, observe, and see what ways I can improve my game, even if I’m not getting the physical reps, and then just being ready for my moment,” Mustapha said. MALIK MUSTAPHAAAAAA 🗣️ 📺: ESPN pic.twitter.com/a7Fa6wP1z8 — San Francisco 49ers (@49ers) October 20, 2026 “Everyone has a role on this team, and you never want to be too high or too low on yourself. You’re just trying to find ways to improve day in and day out. “Once my number is called, being in the best shape or best mindset to help my team win is key for us because they depend on me as I depend on them. I just thank God I was able to go out there these past couple of weeks and just put it out on full display.” Displays like the one Mustapha delivered on Monday are why he has been labeled as a ‘missile’ for the 49er defense. But left tackle Trent Williams believes such monikers undersell the skill set of a player whose coverage instincts are just as impressive as his ultra-physical style of play. “He’s an enforcer. We need guys like that,” Williams explained. “Not only that, I mean, you see what he does for us in the pass game. I mean, literally won the game for us in the corner. I mean, at the pylon, breaking up that pass. He had a major breakup last game, he got him [Kupp] out of bounds. He’s doing it all. “I think the missile really describes him well, but it doesn’t really encapsulate everything he does for this team.” After making the most of his time on the sideline and channeling the frustration of being on the bench early on into a memorable primetime performance, it is difficult to see Mustapha surrendering a grip on his starting berth. The missile should have plenty more chances this season to prove he is much more than that.
author: Nicholas McGee

title: 49ers give Christian McCaffrey a predictably high-usage game against the Commanders
summary: It got weird, but the San Francisco 49ers held on by the hair on their chinny chin chin moving to 6-0 on Monday night.  The 49ers had a 23-3 lead late in the third quarter, but Jayden Daniels and the Washington Commanders wouldn’t go away, cutting the 49ers’ lead to six. But that’s as close […]
full_text: (Photo by Brooke Sutton/Getty Images) | Getty Images It got weird, but the San Francisco 49ers held on by the hair on their chinny chin chin moving to 6-0 on Monday night. The 49ers had a 23-3 lead late in the third quarter, but Jayden Daniels and the Washington Commanders wouldn’t go away, cutting the 49ers’ lead to six. But that’s as close as things would get as San Francisco held on to a 23-17 win. It was a tale of two 49ers teams: one with an offense that couldn’t be stopped and a defense that complemented perfectly, but another with an offense that couldn’t move the ball and a defense that just couldn’t get off the field. Nonetheless, a win is a win. These are the three players most responsible for the 49ers’ sixth win of 2026: 3rd star: S Malik Mustapha The 49ers defense doesn’t survive Monday night without Mustapha’s late-game heroics. The safety wasted no time introducing his presence to the Washington offense. On a third-down play, Daniels found Stefon Diggs for what would have been a first down, but Diggs dropped the pass. The drop did not ensure Diggs’ safety. Mustapha came through with a hit big enough; had Diggs had possession of the ball, it would be easy to see the ball coming out. And while that was one of his first plays, Mustapha would wait until two of his final plays to make his biggest impact. With the 49ers clinging to a six-point lead late in the fourth quarter, Washington faced a third-and-3. Washington’s offensive coordinator David Blough decided to be cheeky with a run right before the two-minute warning to catch the 49ers defense off-guard. Mustapha read it perfectly, meeting Rachaad White in the hole for no gain, forcing a fourth down. Washington wasn’t content with just a first down on the potential game-deciding fourth down, and Blough went at Mustapha. Daniels targeted Treylon Burks on what would have been a 17-yard touchdown to tie the game pending PAT, but a Mustapha hit forced Burks to hard the ground hard on his back, knocking the ball free to give the ball back to the 49ers. The San Francisco defense had to do some cleanup after the offense went three-and-out, but Mustapha’s two-play span to end Washington’s last real chance to score earned the 49ers a victory. 2nd star: RB Christian McCaffrey For better or worse, it’s the type of game we’ve come to expect from McCaffrey. The worse: it was a 2025-usage game, something you’d hope Kyle Shanahan would steer away from. The most touches McCaffrey had in a game this season entering Week 6 was 19, which he achieved in Week 3 against Arizona. By halftime (and before Evans injury), McCaffrey had 16 touches, and he touched the ball nine more times on 20 plays in the second half. But for the better: McCaffrey paid off that heavy usage with a high-production game. Monday night marked McCaffrey’s second game with more than 100 scrimmage yards (first was also the Arizona game) this season, carrying the ball 16 times for 64 yards and a pair of rushing touchdowns while leading all pass-catchers with nine receptions for 53 yards. The two scores accounted for more than 50 percent of the 49ers’ scoring, earning McCaffrey the No. 2 star. But the usage will be something to monitor, more so with the potential of Mike Evans missing time adding to McCaffrey’s workload. 1st star: WR Mike Evans I mean, he has to be, right? Evans’ night ended at the 1:08 mark of the second quarter with a 16-yard reception to put the 49ers in the red zone. The 49ers would score five plays later to go up 17 points before halftime. In the five drives where Evans played, the 49ers offense totaled: 41 plays 303 net yards 17 first downs 214 passing yards 20 points After Evans exited, San Francisco’s offense could only muster: 19 plays 72 net yards 3 first downs 34 passing yards 3 points Evans 94 first-half yards were almost three times as much as what the passing game could put together in the second half. He might not have scored a touchdown on Monday, but his impact was felt on all three of the 49ers’ first-half scoring drives. On San Francisco’s opening drive, Purdy connected with Evans for a gain of 24, moving the ball from the 49ers’ 42 to Washington’s 34. Six plays later, the 49ers would jump out to a 7-0 lead. Evans wouldn’t waste time to move the ball on the 49ers’ second drive. With the defense holding Washington to a field goal, the offense looked for a quick response, and Evans would provide one. Purdy would put the ball in the perfect spot for Evans to catch the ball and turn upfield to run, resulting in a 54-yard gain, instantly giving the 49ers a red zone opportunity. The 49ers would cash in eight plays later, going up 10 early on. The day would end with Evans 16-yard catch to set up the 49ers final touchdown of the evening, but the 49ers offense wasn’t the same without him in the second half. Ideally, the injury isn’t long-term so we don’t have to find out if the second-half 49ers offense actually is that without Evans. Throughout the season, we will track the three stars of the season by tallying points for each star award using a complex scoring system: three points for being the first star, two for the second, and one for the third. Through Week 6, the standings are: WR Mike Evans – 8 points QB Brock Purdy – 7 points LB Fred Warner – 3 points
author: Andrew Pasquini

title: San Francisco’s best things to do, see, and eat before heading to a 49ers game
summary: One of my favorite pastimes is watching 49ers games and seeing San Francisco landmarks get shown. It’s very funny to me, because the actual game is happening over an hour away in a suburban office park. That shouldn’t deter you from staying in San Francisco if you ever make it out for a 49ers game, […]
full_text: Photo by Brooke Sutton/Getty Images | Getty Images One of my favorite pastimes is watching 49ers games and seeing San Francisco landmarks get shown. It’s very funny to me, because the actual game is happening over an hour away in a suburban office park. That shouldn’t deter you from staying in San Francisco if you ever make it out for a 49ers game, because with both transit and shuttle services, getting to the game from the city is straightforward. Just make sure to plan it out by giving yourself enough time to actually enjoy San Francisco. Otherwise, if you are staying closer to the stadium, then I highly recommend renting a car. Santa Clara is located in what’s called the South Bay, and it’s one massive suburban sprawl with not-great transit coverage. There’s some very pretty nature in the surrounding hills but otherwise it won’t feel much different than any other strip-mall-suburbia. Places to stay in San Francisco Avoid the downtown/Union Square area for hotels. Try to stay closer to Fisherman’s Wharf… the Wharf itself is super touristy and not worth hanging out, but it’s much safer than the downtown hotels. You’re much closer that way to North Beach, Russian Hill, the Marina, and the Embarcadero… and downtown/the financial district are still easily accessible. In the South Bay, it’s a sprawl so if time is limited and you don’t have a car, just stay in Santa Clara as close to the stadium as possible. Things to do in San Francisco SF is best enjoyed like a signature 13-play 8-minute Kyle Shanahan drive, where he takes his time and calls run plays over and over again. It’s a Big Walking city. If you have the good health and fortune to be able to walk around (or scooter/bike around), and if it’s not raining, then structure your day around big walks across scenic parts of the city. My favorite part of the city is the stretch from Aquatic Park through Fort Mason all the way down to Chrissy Field. If you’re crunched for time, you can easily just start from the Marina Green area and keep walking down Chrissy Field beach to get a spectacular angle of the bridge. Alternatively, the stretch from Crane Cove Park through Chase Center and Oracle Park is also really nice and bike-able, with some great bakeries such as SOHN , Breadbelly , and Arsicault in the general vicinity. If it’s colder/foggier, then do Golden Gate Park. Start on the Panhandle side and work your way westward until you get to Ocean Beach. If you’re after a foodie experience, then Bernal Heights has a lot of little gems. El Buen Comer for mole, Pinhole Coffee , Black Jet Bakery , Avedano’s sandwiches , and Holy Water for craft cocktails/beers are all some of my favorite spots within a half mile radius. If you’re staying in the South Bay closer to the stadium, then I recommend renting a car and taking a day trip as far down south the coast as you can go. Santa Cruz, Monterey, and Big Sur are all spectacular. Santa Cruz: Beaches and redwood hiking galore. Some of the most elite beer in the world is found in the block with Humble Sea and Private Press Brewing . Monterey: The aquarium is awesome but pricy/sells out, whale watching tours however are freaking awesome, and the kayaking in Elk Horn Slough gets you extremely close to some adorable sea otters. Alta Bakery can hang with any of the bakeries I listed in my bakery article , Alvarado St Brewery has a great kitchen for lunch/dinner (the location in Carmel is even better). Best places to eat in San Francisco If you’restaying near Levi’s: North Sunnyvale area: Surmai for Indian seafood, Slice of Homage for pizza/wings, Tres Potrillos and Chavez Supermarket are two S-tier taqueria right next to each other. A bit further south in Santa Clara, past Levi’s, is Santa Clara’s Koreatown with more Korean options than you can possibly eat. 10 Butchers and Chungdam are incredible KBBQ experiences, not as cheap. In Milpitas, you have Koi Palace for dim sum, Wah Jeeh Wah for Indian BBQ, and IBU Taproom for some elite craft beers. If you don’t mind waiting in line for a while: Four Kings for an upscale mind-blowing Chinese dinner, Khao Tiew for Thai food, Hamburguesa for their burgers, and Tony’s Pizza (although the Yelp waitlist app makes it easier) and be sure to try the squash blossoms + El Jefe pizza. On a casual Day Trip: If you’re doing the Marina walk, I highly recommend (from east-to-west): Equator Coffee ’s breakfast frittata sandwich, Lucca Deli ’s chicken mango chutney salad with added horseradish, and then Angela’s Ice Cream for dessert. If you’re in the Golden Gate Park area, I recommend (from east-to-west): Sandy’s Muffuletta for a sandwich, Flywheel Coffee at the beginning of the park, and then finishing off with Hook Fish at the very end (ideally paired with an Ocean Beach sunset, although you should order it ahead). Other elite sandwiches if that’s what you’re after: Dolores Deluxe in the Mission, Deli Board closer to downtown, and Molinari’s / Little Vine in North Beach. My hottest burrito take is that El Farolito / La Taqueria / all the hyped up Mission spots are a little over rated. I’m personally a fan of La Vaca Birria. Levi’s Stadium parking, rideshare, and transit options If you’re coming from SF, you can take Caltrain and connect at the VTA Light Rail in the Mountain View station, which goes directly to the stadium. If you’re coming from the East Bay/Sacramento, Amtrak also takes you right there. Otherwise, I had positive experiences on the M Ride party bus, it’s around 50ish bucks and goes directly from SF to the Stadium. Varies based on the game but it was fun. Whatever you do, do NOT drive and park there. It’s not worth it. Take a rideshare. If you use Waymo, my favorite hack is to connect my YouTube Premium and play from my “Liked Videos”… my own personal little concert. Tailgating at Levi’s Stadium Get there early, it’s a massive parking lot. The Green and Blue lots usually have a lot of tailgates happening. Show up with a case of beers and make friends. There’s some unofficial organized tailgates happening that you can find on social media, they usually take a donation and offer an all-you-can-eat/all-you-can-drink type buffet. I see 3rdRail9ers get mentioned a lot on Reddit. The 49ers game-day experience The online chatter about how hot and sunny it is in the visitor’s side understates it, if anything. It can really get miserable so don’t forget the sunscreen and to drink a lot of water. The Museum is worth checking out, it’s pretty cool seeing the five Lombardi trophies IRL.
author: Yinon Raviv

title: 10 Winners and 7 losers from the 49ers’ victory over the Commanders
summary: A win is a win. Ugly October victories don’t affect playoff seeding. We saw the Rams and Seahawks lose this very game in Week 6. That’s not to say the San Francisco 49ers can get away with going three-and-out three times in a row to end a game, or giving their opponents multiple first downs […]
full_text: (Photo by Lachlan Cunningham/Getty Images) | Getty Images A win is a win. Ugly October victories don’t affect playoff seeding. We saw the Rams and Seahawks lose this very game in Week 6. That’s not to say the San Francisco 49ers can get away with going three-and-out three times in a row to end a game, or giving their opponents multiple first downs via penalty. Overcoming self-inflicted wounds and escaping with a win is the tell of a contender. Here are the winners and losers from Week 6 Mike Evans Before he left with an injury, Evans was Brock Purdy’s favorite target on late downs once again. He saw 40% of his targets on third down. Evans caught three of his five targets for 94 yards, including a 54-yarder on your typical, run-of-the-mill 25-yard in-breaker . It’s fascinating how different the offense is with Evans on the field. Evans had four more yards than Washington did at the half. The offense finished the game with three consecutive three-and-outs. That’s not something we’re accustomed to seeing. That’s because Evans has been their lifeline. Malik Mustapha Mustapha had some bone-chilling hits in this one. He had a run stop on third down, the game-sealing play on fourth down, and also had a quarterback hit. He set the tone early with a big lick on Stefon Diggs. He’s one of the only trustworthy members in the secondary. Week 6 felt like there were several 2022-level hits. Where ball-carriers or intended wideouts were flatlined on contact. Mustapha is a big reason why. He’s making receivers second-guess catching the ball over the middle, and stopping running backs in their track. Romello Height Height finished the game with a Next Gen Stats pressure rate of 21.7% (league average is a little less than 13%) and saved his most impactful plays for when the 49ers needed them most. White’s 0.72 get-off time was the fastest among 49ers defenders this season. He led the 49ers with four quarterback hits and finished with a split sack. Height drew penalties and was active for much of the second half, living in Washington’s backfield. If the 49ers are going to play with the lead, they’ll need their pass rush to bail out their secondary. Height did on Monday night. Brock Purdy Eleven of Purdy’s 29 attempts went for 10+ yards, yet he still completed 72.4% of his passes. He had the sixth-highest EPA in Week 6 and the fourth-best success rate. Purdy was sacked twice, but one was on a free rusher, and the other came from two of his receivers running into each other downfield. Purdy’s aggressiveness was on point with Mike Evans on the field. He threw three 20+ yard completions and two 14+ yard completions. Purdy layered throws but also threw a couple of seeds. No quarterback generated more EPA with their legs than Purdy this week, nearly double that of the second-placed quarterback. He picked up a few first downs in short-yardage situations and scrambled for another 24 yards, including a key 11-yard conversion. Purdy was Purdy. Keion White White has been a revelation this season. He had five pressures and a half sack to end the game. He’s chaotic, but in a complementary way you need your defenders to be. As the Niners get more bodies back along the defensive line, White can focus on playing more pass-rushing snaps. White consistently flashes in the backfield and moves the quarterback off his spot. He’s the ideal interior rusher. Losers Penalties Sloppy. You can appreciate the defense’s intent. They were hitting. But it led to head hunting and some helmet-to-helmet/unnecessary roughness penalties — and some were called back. The 49ers gave Washington four first downs from penalties. Overall, they had 11-for-88 yards. That’s how you lose the game. The one-win team didn’t capitalize. Just about any other team will. Ashtyn Davis It’s never easy coming in cold late in the game. But that doesn’t mean it’s acceptable to be a sieve in coverage. One of Raheem Morris’s few missteps this season was putting in Davis over Jack Jones, a move they made on the final drive. Davis allowed all four of his targets to be completed, including a 30-yarder. He had a ticky-tack penalty, but it still benefited the Commanders. He was a free rusher on a well-schemed blitz, but missed the tackle in the backfield. Davis actually missed two tackles in limited action. I think it’s safe to say we won’t see Davis in the slot again. Renardo Green Green came back down to earth a week after two interceptions. He was fortunate that Daniels airmailed a deep crossing route, as the younger McCaffrey had a step on Green 25+ yards downfield. For the game, Green allowed three of his four targets to be completed for 68 yards and had a penalty. He also missed a tackle. Washington was going to throw the ball, but that’s no excuse for giving up chunk plays and first downs. He’s better than that. Dominick Puni If you were asked which offensive lineman allowed more than one pressure, the easy answer would be Connor Colby. You’d be wrong. Dominick Puni had his worst game of the year and allowed a double-digit pressure rate. Washington made it a point to blitz and send pressures Puni’s way. He was beaten four times. Jacob Cowing The writing is on the wall for Cowing, whose snap count has dwindled to 15. Cowing had every opportunity over the past month to carve out a role for himself, but he hasn’t gotten open. Brandin Cooks doubled Cowing’s snaps. If Christian Kirk returns, Cowing could be inactive, with Jordan Watkins returning punts. That’s because Cowing’s return game has been an adventure. He muffed a punt after catching it at the six-yard line. He left his feet and dove to catch another punt. He’s asking to be benched for his decision-making. Deommodore Lenoir Lenoir’s confidence from the first month no longer exists. Per Next Gen Stats, both cornerbacks allowed more than four yards of separation on their targets. Lenoir was targeted six times, allowing five completions for a nearly perfect passer rating of 149.3. None of his targets were tight windows. For the second week in a row, Lenoir gave up ground and backpedaled nearly into the end zone when the ball was thrown his way. Cooper Kupp picked up a first down last week. Rachaad White scored this week. The targets aren’t competitive, which is concerning. It feels like yesteryear, when the defensive line is masking a shaky secondary. Eddy Pineiro The honeymoon phase is officially over with Pineiro, who missed his third extra point of the year. He’s 31st in field-goal percentage and 28th in extra-point percentage. Pineiro can right these wrongs by finishing the year strong, but field goals decide playoff games. It makes you wonder whether Kyle Shanahan will lean on his offense down the stretch instead of putting the game on the line with a kicker who can’t seem to split the uprights. Winners Mykel Williams Williams had a sack and a tackle for loss in 25 snaps. He managed a 15% pressure rate, which is the most encouraging sign. There weren’t many plays to be made against the run, which is Mykel’s calling card. So seeing him flash multiple times as a pass rusher should give the player returning from injury even more self-assurance. The defensive tackles Gracen Halton dealt with a quad injury leading up to this game. He was outsnapped by Sebastian Valdez. James Thompson returned, but Osa Odighizuwa thrived against the Commanders’ pass-heavy attack. Osa led the way with four pressures and had a team-high five impact plays, per Sumer Sports. Odighizuwa also led the team with a 19.4% pass rush win rate. Odighizuwa and Valdez both had run stops. Valdez continues to impress. It makes you wonder what this would look like if Alfred Collins and CJ West had never gotten hurt. Valdez is clearly producing more than both would and could. Valdez had the highest pressure rate at 18.8%. Halton and Odighizuwa had sacks. The trio had one tackle for loss apiece. This position group has been the season’s biggest pleasant surprise, and they continue to show out each week. They…
