title: 3 things we learned about the 49ers in Week 6: Romello Height has arrived
summary: Boy, the San Francisco 49ers know how to make things interesting. A game that felt pretty much over at halftime turned into a thriller as the 49ers held off Jayden Daniels and the Commanders’ comeback attempt. In a game where Terry McLaurin was seriously injured, the Commanders’ passing attack came alive in the second half. […]
full_text: Photo by Brooke Sutton/Getty Images) | Getty Images Boy, the San Francisco 49ers know how to make things interesting. A game that felt pretty much over at halftime turned into a thriller as the 49ers held off Jayden Daniels and the Commanders’ comeback attempt. In a game where Terry McLaurin was seriously injured, the Commanders’ passing attack came alive in the second half. The 49ers lost Mike Evans before the half, but according to Kyle Shanahan, his Achilles is intact, and the injury is the same one he dealt with during the week. The 49ers are 6-0 with a chance to go 7-0 next week before their bye, which will be the turning point for the health of the roster as the team expects to have Nick Bosa, Demarcus Robinson, Christian Kirk, and other important players coming out of the bye. The team could get reinforcements back for Atlanta, but coming off the bye, it will be as close to healthy as possible. Here’s what we learned from Monday night’s win over the Commanders. The 49ers crowded safety room Before his injury, Marques Sigle was a revelation. Malik Mustapha was returning from injury, but during his time replacing Sigle, he has been fantastic and made the two biggest plays of the night in succession. A complete run stuff on third down from the safety position for no gain, followed by a hard-fought PBU on a target to the taller Treylon Burks, ended the Commanders’ drive. Washington would get the ball back one more time before the defensive line shut the door on the comeback attempt, but the question is: when Sigle returns, can you justify sending Mustapha to the bench? The thing is, Ji’Ayir Brown hasn’t played poorly in 2026. Mustapha has been a tone-setter with his physicality and is flashing every week. It’s a good problem to have, and perhaps it allows some more flexibility for Raheem Morris with all three safeties, but Mustapha has played like a man possessed. Mike Evans is the engine of the 49ers offense Brock Purdy has played his best football ever in 2026. It’s no coincidence that it comes in a season when Mike Evans was added to the fold. The first half was a laser show, with Evans nearly topping 100 yards before the half. The problem is that when Evans departed, the 49ers leaned on Christian McCaffrey, but the Commanders knew the 49ers were out of separators and blitzed constantly in the second half, knowing they wouldn’t be beat downfield. Herein lies the problem. The 49ers need to target another receiver by the trade deadline, one who can separate independently from Kyle Shanahan and his scheme. If that means knocking down Robinson in the pecking order when he returns, then so be it. The 49ers shouldn’t shy away from adding impact players because they have players returning. If adding a separator pushes Jordan Watkins or Jacob Cowing off the roster, you have to do it. The second half was a glimpse of the 49ers being down to their seventh and eighth receivers. Add more firepower. Do not get complacent and bank on returning players. Hello, Romello Height What a game for Height. Six total pressures, two sacks (one wiped away by a penalty), two QB hits, and two hurries. The rookie was a star on Monday night. The entire defensive line deserves credit, but Height’s breakout game in tandem with a returning Nick Bosa and Mykel Williams’ continued progress is such a plus for this 49ers defense. The 49ers are closer than ever to a championship defense. A deeper look into Height’s game on Monday night is even more impressive. In true pass sets (no play action or screens), Height generated five pressures, recorded a sack with two QB hits and two hurries. On 19 true pass sets, Height finished with a 26.7% win rate. Impressive game. The 49ers’ defensive line is getting better each game.
author: Jason Aponte

title: NFC West Recap: 49ers continue to distance themselves; Rams and Seahawks lose
summary: The San Francisco 49ers had another good week of football. Sure, their 23-17 win over the Washington Commanders unnecessarily came down to the wire, but they still won. The best part is, everyone else lost! AGAIN! The 49ers have beaten the Commanders—a team the Seattle Seahawks lost to. They have also beaten the Denver Broncos, […]
full_text: SANTA CLARA, CALIFORNIA - OCTOBER 19: Head Coach Kyle Shanahan of the San Francisco 49ers walks the field after winning the game against the Washington Commanders at Levi's Stadium on October 19, 2026 in Santa Clara, California. (Photo by Brooke Sutton/Getty Images) | Getty Images The San Francisco 49ers had another good week of football. Sure, their 23-17 win over the Washington Commanders unnecessarily came down to the wire, but they still won. The best part is, everyone else lost! AGAIN! The 49ers have beaten the Commanders—a team the Seattle Seahawks lost to. They have also beaten the Denver Broncos, a team both the Rams and Seahawks lost to. Should tiebreakers come into play, those two victories could be a deciding factor. So that puts the 49ers at 6-0 and 3-0 in the division. With the losses, they now have a three-game lead (and change if you could tiebreakers) over the second-place Seahawks. Yes, the Commanders win wasn’t pretty, but the 49ers are 6-0, and if we have to endure a game like that Commanders game to be 6-0, I don’t think there’s a fan in the world who wouldn’t take that. It’s not without some wrinkles. Wide receiver Mike Evans may miss some time . While Christian Kirk has resumed practice, it might take some time to get in sync with Brock Purdy. At least the 49ers get Dre Greenlaw back next week and maybe Nick Bosa. Seattle Seahawks (3-3) The biggest thing about the Seahawks’ loss to the Denver Broncos isn’t that they lost a game they probably should have won; it’s that Bo Nix may be getting more criticism for his play than Sam Darnold. Ryan Fitzpatrick absolutely destroyed Bo Nix on live TV 💀 pic.twitter.com/HGu3T5fi4A — PredictArena (@PredictArena) October 16, 2026 And he should. Nix has had a tendency to come back in the second half in 2026, but he didn’t do any of that here. You can also add in some very bad decision-making. Nix went 17 for 27 and 107 yards passing. Yes, 107 yards passing and the Broncos won. It’s fair to note the Broncos also had 74 yards rushing. So how did the Broncos win? Defense, all defense. How did the Seahawks lose? Well, not being able to run the ball might be the biggest reason. 113 yards total. Rashid Shaheed losing one of his two fumbles doesn’t help. Then there’s the other quarterback. Sam Darnold had two interceptions, zero touchdowns, and five sacks. 17-14, Broncos. The Broncos are 4-2 after that stat line from Bo Nix. He didn’t throw a touchdown or an interception and got sacked twice compared to Darnold’s five. Do the Broncos look like a 4-2 team? That’s up to you. The Seahawks are now games (yes, plural) behind the 49ers, and it’s not going to get any easier. Arizona Cardinals (2-4)/Los Angeles Rams (2-4) Oh, you know what time it is. Let’s Ram It! Let’s Ram it all the way to last place in the NFC West. The Arizona Cardinals not only beat the Los Angeles Rams, but did so by field-goal-ing the Rams to death. Six field goals were all the Cardinals needed to get the 18-16 victory. This was a Los Angeles Rams team that some thought would go undefeated before the season began. Now they are last place in their own division. My, what a tangled web we weave. And the Rams had a chance to win this thing. They marched down the field, got the touchdown, and the Cardinals only had 45 seconds left with no timeouts. Turns out 45 seconds is too much time for Jacoby Brissett, because next thing you know he’s pushing the ball down the field and getting into field goal range in 10 of those 45 seconds. Many are saying the Rams get an easier schedule so they can right the ship, but again: They lost to a team via six field goals. The only other team the Cardinals have beaten is from Los Angeles, and that team, the Chargers, is 0-6 right now. And yes, the Rams lost their kicker early in the game and didn’t have a kicker to make field goals. Then again, should the Rams need a kicker for the Cardinals? That’s a huge win for the Cardinals and an equally miserable loss for the Rams. Are they out? No. But they are now in last place with several divisional losses on them as well. They are almost at “run the table to get in the playoffs” territory. Almost. And it gets worse. First, wide receiver Davante Adams is out 6-10 weeks due to a hamstring injury. That’s devastating for the wide receiver group (something 49ers fans know all too well). Second, their shiny new kicker, Blake Grupe, was injured on Sunday, which was enough to add him to injured reserve. So the Rams need to overcome a four-game deficit without a kicker or their veteran wide receiver. Onto Week 7 The 49ers will travel to face the Atlanta Falcons, a game with the dreaded 10:00 AM start time. Not exactly ideal when the Falcons have been humming for a couple of games until Sunday—when the Chicago Bears crushed them. That score says 31-23, but 16 of the Falcons’ 23 points came in the fourth quarter. Meanwhile, Chicago was scoring touchdowns until the fourth quarter. Regardless of Atlanta’s performance, they have the best running back in the game in Bijan Robinson. With Robinson, the Falcons can run the ball, and if you’ve watched them lately, he’s not exactly the easiest thing to stop. It’s a great test for the 49ers, who have limited explosive runs. The Seahawks host the Kansas City Chiefs as the Sunday Night Football game. It feels strange to want the Seahawks to win just to hand the Chiefs a loss, but the Chiefs could do the 49ers a favor by putting the Seahawks to 3-4. As much as some of us may dislike both teams, that will be a fun game to watch. Chiefs running back Kenneth Walker III will probably be the star of the show; the Seahawks running game hasn’t been the same since he left in free agency, and the Chiefs have had a running game since acquiring him. The Cardinals host the Denver Broncos. The same Denver Broncos who managed to beat the Seahawks. Given what we’ve seen of this Cardinals team, a win isn’t out of the ordinary. The Rams will have their second straight week of not playing on primetime. They might play a bit more on Sunday afternoon if the league flexes them out of anything in the future. They host the Las Vegas Raiders. The Raiders lost to the Buffalo Bills, but were in it until the end. The Rams could be their get-right game. 1st: San Francisco 49ers Next at Atlanta Falcons 2nd: Seattle Seahawks; Next: vs. Kansas City Chiefs (Sunday Night Football ) 3rd: Arizona Cardinals; Next: vs. Denver Broncos 4th: Los Angeles Rams; Next: at Las Vegas Raiders
author: Patrick Holloway

title: 3 quick takeaways from the 49ers win over the Commanders: The fast start paid off
summary: It wasn’t the prettiest game and, at times, was quite a scary one, but the San Francisco 49ers found a way to edge past the Washington Commanders on Monday night to improve to 6-0 on the season. Heading into the game with injury questions once again, the 49ers lost Mike Evans just before halftime. But […]
full_text: SANTA CLARA, CA - OCTOBER 19: Brock Purdy #13 of the San Francisco 49ers scrambles against the Washington Commanders during the first half of an NFL football game at Levi's Stadium on October 19, 2026 in Santa Clara, California. (Photo by Cooper Neill/Getty Images) | Getty Images It wasn’t the prettiest game and, at times, was quite a scary one, but the San Francisco 49ers found a way to edge past the Washington Commanders on Monday night to improve to 6-0 on the season. Heading into the game with injury questions once again, the 49ers lost Mike Evans just before halftime. But their 17-point lead was too much to overcome, despite a furious comeback by Jayden Daniels and Co., allowing the 49ers to improve to 6-0 with the Atlanta Falcons up next before the bye week. Here are three quick takeaways from the 49ers win over the Commanders on Monday night. Fast start pays off One of my keys to the game for the 49ers was getting off to a fast start. Obviously, that’s important in any game, but it felt extra vital in this one. We’ve seen the 49ers operate well in the clutch over the past two weeks against the Denver Broncos and Seattle Seahawks, thanks to quality play from Brock Purdy, but I pointed to Evans’s injury status as a big reason why an early lead would be key. Getting off to a fast start could ease some of the pressure off a clearly-banged up Evans, while also allowing the 49ers to remain balanced and the Commanders to get even more one-dimensional. That all turned out to be true, as the 49ers offense couldn’t get going without Evans in the second half. One gripe from Kyle Shanahan in this game was also the 49ers’ lack of balance in the second half from a play-calling perspective over the final quarter. The 49ers went pass-pass-pass on two consecutive drives to start the fourth quarter, with both resulting in three-and-outs. The 1st started with a Brock Purdy sack, derailing the drive, while Purdy was sacked on second down on the second drive. Washington also excelled in the pass game, with Jayden Daniels going for 300 passing yards, despite their run game producing just 53 yards on 3.1 yards per carry. That’s all to say: it was extremely important the 49ers got off to a lead, as the hole proved too far for the Commanders to dig out of in the second half. Third and fourth down execution The 49ers didn’t win the time of possession battle, mainly because the Commanders had the ball for nearly 80 percent of the fourth quarter. But they did win the late-down battle, which was also a key of mine heading into the game. Coming in, the 49ers were the second-most efficient offense in the NFL, which meant they weren’t getting to third downs often, ranking 32nd in the NFL in third downs per game. But when they did get there, they still converted at a high rate, ranking first in the NFL coming into the game. Meanwhile, while the Commanders were a solid defense on early downs, they’ve really struggled on third downs, ranking 28th in the NFL in EPA allowed per play on third downs and 24th in the NFL in conversion rate. Through three quarters on Monday, the 49ers were 7 of 11 on third downs and 2 of 2 on fourth downs. So, in essence, they converted 9 of their 11 late-down opportunities, and that resulted in four scoring drives on six opportunities through three quarters, with the other two being Christian McCaffrey’s fumble and a punt. With the pass game options looking as they did, and the Commanders’ defense coming in as a solid run defense, it felt like this one could be a game with longer drives, and that proved to be the case for the 49ers. They had drives of 9, 8, 7, 14, and 11 plays through the first three quarters, but executed well on later downs to keep them going. Now, of course, the 49ers ended the game with three three-and-outs. But they also did a really good job defensively on later downs. The Commanders were just 3 of 12 on third downs and 1 of 3 on fourth downs, and it made a huge difference. To start the game, the 49ers forced a field goal on a successful Washington drive, got a sack on third down for a three-and-out, and forced a turnover on downs as the Commanders got to 4th & 2 on the 49ers 13-yard line. That’s three key late-down stops resulting in only three points. San Francisco also got a sack near midfield on third down on Washington’s opening drive of the second half. Then, after allowing two touchdown drives, the 49ers had multiple late-down stops. On Washington’s second-to-last drive, the 49ers forced an incompletion on third down and got a fourth-down sack, which was wiped out by an illegal contact. On the next set of downs, though, they got another third-down stop before Malik Mustapha’s big pass breakup forced a turnover on downs. Of course, on the final drive, the 49ers got a sack on Daniels on third down to end the game on the final play. Overall, the 49ers offense executed quite well on third and fourth downs through three quarters, setting themselves up in a good position, while the defense consistently came together with clutch plays on late downs to stop a very quality Commanders passing offense. Some step up, while others struggle to As in any close game, the 49ers don’t win this one without consistent play from some and clutch play from others. We have to continue to praise Brock Purdy for his performances. The 49ers quarterback kept the ball out of harm’s way and completed 21 of 29 passes for 264 yards and a touchdown. He continued to hit explosives to his pass-catcher group, despite the injuries, and had a couple of savvy third-down scrambles to extend drives. He’s seeing the field at a high level and isn’t making mistakes, while conducting a very efficient offense. Purdy averaged 9.1 yards per play, and it could’ve been more if some other plays were made in the second half. Mustapha deserves praise, not only for his huge fourth-quarter play, but for his overall start to the season. As I’ve said the last few weeks, he’s been vital for Raheem Morris’s defense as a glue piece in the secondary. On the defensive line, Romello Height continues to stack some really good games. He’s been a shoutout the last two weeks, and he played very well on Monday night, recording six pressures with his 0.5 sacks. Keion White, Mykel Williams, Gracen Halton, and Osa Odighizuwa all made key plays as well, as the 49ers pass rush got 21 pressures as a whole. I have to also point out the quality play of Jaden Dugger, who has really broken out the last two weeks in Dre Greenlaw’s absence. Dugger had a team-high 11 tackles, and his versatility, which was a big talking point in the offseason, is showing out. He had multiple pressures again on Monday. Then, even completely battered with injuries, Mike Evans had some big early plays that set up the 49ers scoring drives. That was key because the 49ers receivers were not targeted at all in the second half, with that group struggling to make plays. George Kittle had a strong first half as well, with five catches for 69 yards and a touchdown, but couldn’t come down with a key play on a third down in the second half that led to a quick punt. The 49ers offensive line also had another very solid game, creating some key holes in the run game against a defense that ranked top 10 against the run coming into the week. Brock Purdy was also pressured on just 7 of his 34 dropbacks, despite being blitzed nearly 45 percent of the time. One note to make: the 49ers benched Upton Stout again for a portion of the game, this time late in the fourth quarter. Raheem Morris initially had Ashtyn Davis in as a big nickel, then subbed him out as well after giving up a big play and committing a penalty. The 49ers then went with Deommodore Lenoir in the slot and Jack Jones outside to end the game. Stout played just 28 of the 67 defensive snaps. He was credited with giving up three catches on four targets for 22 yards and a touchdown, per PFF. I also do want to touch on Kyle Shanahan’s playcalling to end the game here as well.…

Shanahan said he didn’t think Evans would need further testing or imaging.” 49ers’ Mike Evans exits Commanders game with Achilles issue, but avoids major injury (paywall) “Head coach Kyle Shanahan indicated Evans avoided a serious injury. Shanahan said Evans couldn’t continue due to what Shanahan had previously termed “Achilles soreness,” an issue that prevented Evans from practicing during the week and made him to questionable to play in Monday’s game.“ Kyle Shanahan on Mike Evans’ injury: ‘We don’t think it’s a long-term thing’ “Christian Kirk is a “possibility” for Week 7 against the Falcons. “He had two good practices in. It’s just his first two practices of the year. We were down on wideouts, so it’s still something we discussed. But we decided to give it another week.” Per Shanahan, Demarcus Robinson will not be ready this week.“ How 49ers QB Brock Purdy mastered the art of layering passes over defenders “Renardo Green wants to go fishing. As one who enjoys his time alone, one who appreciates peace, he’s looking forward to picking it up as a pastime. But he’s not thinking of sitting on a boat with his feet up, letting idleness bring him tranquility. That’s not quite the adventure the 49ers cornerback has in mind. He wants to get into the water. Deep water. “In the shallows, I’ll do it (with my hands),” said Green, the San Francisco 49ers’ third-year cornerback. “But I want to go deep-sea fishing and go hop in that water and get to it. I want a spear.” How 49ers QB Brock Purdy mastered the art of layering passes over defenders “Equipped with an iPad and 3D glasses, he watches two squares move in, out and around. His job is to identify how and when those squares converge and diverge with his eyes moving in and out rapidly. Purdy also does daily work with saccades, a rapid eye movement exercise in which he must follow arrows that pop up all over a screen and touch the correct one when prompted. According to Purdy, the goal of the two-to-four-minute sessions is to force him to process movement and information as fast as possible while improving his depth perception. “All those things help me just work on my eyesight, my eyes moving, being quick with my eyes, making quick decisions,” Purdy said. “And then it records my decision-making, how fast, the percentage of getting right and wrong. I do think it helps.”

title: Washington Commanders Whiteboard: Notes and observations from Week 6
summary: Before the advent of media devices, football coaches at all levels used simple whiteboards to outline plays, map out player positions and explain schemes in real time. Nowadays digital playbooks and tablets have taken over, but coaches still use whiteboards on occasion to impart information quickly and effectively. The following are some quick notes and […]
full_text: Before the advent of media devices, football coaches at all levels used simple whiteboards to outline plays, map out player positions and explain schemes in real time. Nowadays digital playbooks and tablets have taken over, but coaches still use whiteboards on occasion to impart information quickly and effectively. The following are some quick notes and observations from the Washington Commanders ‘ tough 17-23 loss on Monday Night Football. Jayden Daniels failed to connect with his receiving options early in the game Stefon Diggs dropped pass for a first down to end Washington’s opening drive. The team would opt for a Drew Stevens’ field goal instead. Diggs also had two drops early in the Philadelphia game back in Week 1, and all have contributed to stalling out a Commanders offense that has struggled to get going early in games. On the season, Diggs has 4 drops total, with 24 receptions on 38 targets for a 63% catch rate. While he has been a valuable addition to the wide receiver corps, these types of mental lapses have hurt the offense. Over the entirety of last year, Stefon had three drops and a catch rate of 83.3% during the regular season as a New England Patriot. Terry McLaurin is second on the team with three drops despite only playing 61% of the total offensive snaps this season. 🚨 #Commanders Stefon Diggs with a drop then takes a hard hit pic.twitter.com/YnQS7m6EkW — NFL Rumors (@nflrums) October 20, 2026 Prior to the dropped pass, Daniels’ missed tight end Chig Okonkwo running open in the middle of the field on second down. It was trend that would continue for most of the first half, as Jayden missed an easy completion to Rachaad White on a swing pass and Antonio Williams running free on several plays including one that could have been an easy touchdown. Watching Jayden Daniels tape back. I'm only seven throws in. So far he's been clinically good. Made the right read and was accurate on almost every throw. But on this short toss to Bates he misses a wide open Antonio Williams for a 21-yard TD. pic.twitter.com/PRWQMQbSSo — Grant Paulsen (@GrantPaulsen) October 20, 2026 Two things with this play that ended up with a sack on Jayden Daniels 1). Rachaad White didn’t pick up the block 2). Stefon Diggs was wide open pic.twitter.com/pkjf7mx5U6 — brandon (@JayDanielsMVP) October 20, 2026 Daniels would eventually catch fire in the second half. He stood in the face of pressure and delivering to receiving options down the field, but it turned out to be too little too late, which would be a common theme for this game. For the most part, No. 5 had done everything in his power, including playing through injuries, to keep this team competitive. Fans are starting to see the signs that the missed playing time over the last two years has hurt his development at the position, including processing and situational awareness. Jayden needs more game reps to improve his consistency but also needs more help from both the players and coaches. By the way — this is the first time Jayden Daniels has completed two games back to back since early October of 2025. And has looked really good in both. — Damien Bartonek (@tvBartonek) October 20, 2026 The coaching staff continues to struggle Dan Quinn’s own situational awareness and clock management in this one have been well discussed, so we won’t touch on it more here, but he wasn’t the only coach to not leave last week’s issues behind them. Part of the offense’s struggles come from a scheme that seems to be awkward and unfamiliar to the players running it. David Blough’s plays take a long time to develop before the snap, with significant time in the huddle and players running lackadaisical motion concepts that seem to provide Jayden Daniels with no insight into the coverage and little time to make changes if he does. The net result is a sense of urgency right before the snap. Several times the play clock almost elapsed before the Commanders were able to get the snap off, resulting in several illegal shifts, false starts and miscommunications. The Commanders had seven penalties — six by the offense, with five charged to the offensive line. The inconsistent nature of their offensive-line play can’t continue to be accounted for by an ever-shifting lineup, and new offensive line coach Darnell Stapleton deserves some criticism. Six weeks into the season, the time for grace due to a learning curve is over. When the Commanders do get the snap off properly and the protection holds, the calls don’t always seem to provide Daniels many options. Often times wide receivers are right next to each other or not getting to the necessary levels on their routes. One particularly bad example happened on the intentional grounding play in the final seconds of the game. David Blough what is this route tree on 3rd and 8? 3 receivers bunched together. #Commanders keep killing themselves these with penalties and the 49ers are having their way. #RaiseHail pic.twitter.com/Q9pSMynbLt — Carolina Commander (@SC_Commanderr) October 20, 2026 The rushing attack continues to target the interior of the offensive line instead of working to the outside. Washington Commanders running backs contributed a mere 43 yards on the ground and Washington’s running backs rank 27th in rushing success rate Some might point to Daronte Jones’ defense holding the Niners offense to 23 points as a sign of improvement, but Kyle Shanahan and Brock Purdy did pretty much whatever they wanted in the first half. The Commanders run defense was exposed, as Christian McCaffrey accounted for 64 yards and two touchdowns while rookie Kaelon Black looked solid in relief as well. Jones’ squad did turn things around in the second half, as the departure of Mike Evans limited the Niners’ passing attack. But, once again, it was too little too late. Any defensive coordinator that takes Sonny Styles off the field in favor of Kain Medrano deserves to take some heat. #Commanders snap counts vs 49ers • Amik Robertson only defensive player to play all snaps • Trey Amos played in 58.1% of snaps in his return • Chig Okonkwo led the receivers in snaps pic.twitter.com/u6sRGndrvU — brandon (@JayDanielsMVP) October 20, 2026 Both Contain/edge (or lack thereof) & 2nd level defenders being 5 yards off the ball on the 1-yard line feels like a choice. https://t.co/L4NETFn5cc — Last of the Fullbacks (@TheLastFullback) October 20, 2026 Fans can look on the bright side with Sonny Styles Washington’s No. 7 overall draft pick looked the part again under the bright lights of Monday Night Football , as Sonny Styles continues to make a case for defensive rookie of the year. Styles had 13 total tackles on the night (seven solo) and provided several key stops in the game, including breaking up a pass to Evans. There were plenty of questions about Sonny’s disposition and physicality before the season, but the young linebacker may already be the best player on the defense and has shown the kind of mentality that could make him the captain of this team’s defense for years to come. . @Commanders @49ers @sonnystyles_ The captain & Commander of this defense gave them a chance to WIN…again… #BaldysBreakdowns pic.twitter.com/lwMu5qXp4b — Brian Baldinger (@BaldyNFL) October 20, 2026 Have fans seen the last of Terry Mclaurin in a Washington uniform? After gutting it out and contributing last week despite a hamstring injury, Terry McLaurin contributed early on Monday night with a 27-yard reception before being carted off the field with a knee injury shortly thereafter. After the game, Dan Quinn said there was concern the injury was significant and McLaurin was confirmed to have suffered a season-ending injury this afternoon. Terry has been a consummate professional and the heart and soul of Washington’s team, sticking with the franchise through all the highs and the lows of the last eight years. After negotiating an extension last offseason, McLaurin carries a $34 million cap hit in 2027, and it is fair to wonder if the team will…

(Photo by Thearon W. Henderson/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Washington Commanders season takes a pause as they enter their Week 7 bye. The team just lost to the San Francisco 49ers on Monday Night Football, dropping their record to 1-4-1 for the season. Dan Quinn got behind the mic for his weekly “Tell the Truth Monday Tuesday” and spoke to reporters who were still traveling back home from California. Terry McLaurin’s season is over after suffering a torn patellar tendon in the first quarter on a non-contact play. It’s a brutal injury that has a long recovery time, and casts a bigger question on McLaurin’s future in Washington after the new deal he signed last year. Quinn said the team would rely on the receivers on the roster, but they’ve already lost Jaylin Lane for the season to a broken ankle. The Commanders can’t play consistently throughout a game and that was evident again with Monday night’s tale of two halves. Jayden Daniels and the Commanders offense couldn’t get much done in the first half, but the script was flipped after halftime, almost ending in a comeback win for Washington. The defense also got a boost when Mike Evans left the game due to a lingering Achilles injury, and the 49ers offense wasn’t the same for the remainder of the game. Quinn also said the offensive line hasn’t been playing up to the standards the team sets for themselves. He was asked if continued poor play and penalties could lead to change, and he said absolutely. Quinn also wants to see more explosive plays from an offense that has done well protecting the ball. Several big plays have also been wiped off the board due to penalties this season. Terry McLaurin’s injury: Dan Quinn said Terry McLaurin has a torn patellar tendon and will undergo surgery. title: Commanders injury update: WR Terry McLaurin (knee) out for 2026 season
summary: Commanders receiver Terry McLaurin has suffered a torn patellar tendon in his knee and it out for the season.   Head coach Dan Quinn announced that difficult news during his Tuesday afternoon press conference.   McLaurin will have surgery to repair the injury in the coming days. According to the National Library of Medicine, it […]
full_text: Commanders receiver Terry McLaurin has suffered a torn patellar tendon in his knee and it out for the season. Head coach Dan Quinn announced that difficult news during his Tuesday afternoon press conference . McLaurin will have surgery to repair the injury in the coming days. According to the National Library of Medicine , it can take between 6-9 months of rehabilitation following such a procedure to return to contact sports. The team acknowledged the significant loss as well. HC Dan Quinn confirmed that WR Terry McLaurin suffered a season-ending injury in last night’s game Wishing our captain a healthy recovery 🤍 pic.twitter.com/grZgpn8CbJ — Washington Commanders (@Commanders) October 20, 2026 “I’m gutted for him,” Quinn said. “He’a captain and one of our real leaders. We’re all here to support him. That was certainly tough news.” The 31-year-old got hurt in the first quarter of Monday night’s 23-17 loss to the San Francisco 49ers . He went down running a route, tried to get up and get to the sideline but never got there. Terry goes down and immediately grabs his left knee pic.twitter.com/7EtIvcTsmM — Tiller56 (Hogs Haven) (@Tiller56) October 20, 2026 Trainers placed an air cast on McLaurin’s leg and carted him off the field . It didn’t look good at the time, with an presumption that he would be out a long time. Having him miss the season is particularly brutal. “He brings a lot on and off the field,” Quinn said. “I felt him in so many unique ways this season from training camp to in-season. We do have a deep crew at that position and we’ll lean in on several to fill the unique role that Terry does.” The Commanders will need Stefon Diggs to be a true No. 1 receiver and to have a relatively deep position group to step up and take on McLaurin’s workload. While others will fill in, McLaurin’s ability and leadership can’t be replaced. “It’s a big hit,” Quinn said, “and we’ll lean on a number of guys.” It must also be mentioned here that McLaurin has two seasons left on a three-year, $97 million contract extension . There’s no guaranteed money remaining, and his cap hit balloons to $34 million in 2027. Will the Commanders have to make a tough decision on McLaurin? It’s a question for the future, but it’s a factor in what Washington decides to do at the position moving forward.

full_text: SANTA CLARA, CALIFORNIA - OCTOBER 19: Jayden Daniels #5 of the Washington Commanders throws a pass against Mykel Williams #98 of the San Francisco 49ers during the third quarter of the game at Levi's Stadium on October 19, 2026 in Santa Clara, California. (Photo by Thearon W. Henderson/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Washington Commanders are 1-4-1 and we’re still talking about clock management which is a really bad sign for head coach Dan Quinn. Jayden Daniels is also catching some heat for throwing it away on fourth down, and leaving a lot of plays on the field in a game against the 49ers that Washington almost came back to win. The Commanders now enter their bye week with a lot of things to fix. Losing Terry McLaurin to a significant knee injury is the latest blow to a season that just hasn’t found a way to get right. The good news is that the rest of the NFC East is an absolute mess. Jalen Hurts is out for the season due to blood clots in his lungs, and the reset year for the Eagles is fully on. The Giants already lost Jaxson Dart for the season, and now they’re debating going to J.J. McCarthy while Cam Skattebo was benched for a fumble vs Washington. The Cowboys don’t have any of those QB excuses, they just have an overpaid Dak Prescott. The Commanders are still at the bottom of the division, but nobody wants to win this thing, and the schedule gets a lot easier after the bye. The Power Rankers are lower on the Washington Commanders after another loss, but they actually rose in a few after getting dangerously close to pulling off a road upset in primetime over the #1 team in a lot of the rankings. That doesn’t mean much in the long run, but the Commanders haven’t given up on the season, or on Dan Quinn yet, and that means they’re still alive in the most Washington way possible. Can a 7-8-1 team win the NFC East this year? 8-7-1? High: 20 Low: 30 Average: 27.4 #20 Walter Football Another week, another coaching gaffe by Dan Quinn, who yelled for this team to go for a field goal after Jayden Daniels foolishly threw the ball away on fourth down. Daniels, meanwhile, looked like he pissed his pants at the prospect of scrambling into a Fred Warner-led linebacker group. The giant wuss ran for only 10 yards in a loss. Pathetic! Last week: 20 #23 NFL.com (Shook) Washington’s latest loss will undoubtedly disappoint its ardent fan base, but the mettle it showed in the second half in the unfriendly confines of Levi’s Stadium told me this team is more than its 1-4-1 record. Jayden Daniels’ return has opened more avenues for the Commanders to choose in their pursuit of victory, and even after Terry McLaurin was carted off with a knee injury, the quarterback managed to find success by turning to the lesser-known members of his team and using his legs when necessary. Yes, it has only one win, but this team has fight in it. Now, it needs to rely on the likes of Daniels, Treylon Burks , Antonio Williams and Stefon Diggs to try to dig out of this hole. Last week: 28 #25 Yahoo Sports (Schwab) Jayden Daniels throwing the ball away even though it was fourth down and Dan Quinn seemingly not knowing it was fourth down at all says everything that needs to be said about the 2026 Commanders. If that wasn’t enough on Monday night, after last week’s game-management debacle at the end of overtime against the Giants, the Commanders had to use a timeout with the clock stopped with 3:01 left in the game before a fourth down play. That ended up costing Washington a valuable 40 seconds, as it ran out of time on a comeback attempt in a 23-17 loss to the 49ers. Washington has a bye coming up next, and whatever answers Quinn gives to why he seemingly didn’t know it was fourth down will be a big discussion point, not just among fans and media, but also within the organization. It seems like a team in desperate need of a reset. Last week: 25 #26 Sports Illustrated (Orr) Dan Quinn had one directive for the remainder of this season: Do not follow up one of the most egregious instances of clock mismanagement ever with another high-profile standalone game gaffe that shows an inability to handle game management. Last week: 28 NBC Sports (Wirth) Jayden Daniels looked absolutely lost in the first half before turning it on down the stretch, and now it appears he might have lost his top receiver for a while. Last week: 25 #27 The Athletic (Graff/Kendall) Fantasy focus: Jayden Daniels The Commanders quarterback hasn’t had much help this year, and things got worse Monday night after Terry McLaurin suffered what looked like a bad knee injury. Still, it has been a disappointing season for Daniels that has included another elbow injury, an inexplicable breakdown a week ago and a rally that came up short Monday night. He is 18th among quarterbacks in total fantasy points (85.7). Last week: 27 USA Today (Davis) After their Week 5 debacle and a nearly as uninspiring first half Monday night, Jayden Daniels and Co. finally came to life, almost derailing the Niners’ still-perfect season … and maybe laying the groundwork for their own surge in the eminently winnable NFC East. Last week: 28 Fox Sports (Vacchiano) Jayden Daniels looks closer to his old, magical self, but it all came too late to pull off the upset in San Francisco Monday night, and it might be too late to save the season in Washington. It might be too late for Dan Quinn too, since, for the second week in a row, his game management skills were exposed as … well, something. This time he was caught on camera seemingly surprised that the Commanders’ last play was a fourth-down play, as he tried to send the field goal unit on. Add that to last week’s clock disaster and Washington’s 1-4-1 record, and Quinn might not still be the Commanders coach anymore when they return from their bye. Last week: 25 The Score Dan Quinn: It’s going to be really hard for Quinn to erase the stench of that overtime debacle against the Giants when the Commanders accidentally let the clock expire and had to settle for a tie. And it doesn’t help that he’s a defensive coach with a porous defense and a record of 6-16-1 over the last two seasons. Last week: 25 FTN Fantasy (Kelley) The first-half Commanders Monday were a disaster. But the second-half team could easily win a terrible NFC East. It’s just a matter of what team we get. Last week: 27 Team Rankings Last week: 25 #28 CBS Sports (Prisco) They did a nice job battling back against the 49ers, but another loss keeps them in last in their division. The heat is on Dan Quinn. Last week: 28 Sporting News (Iyer) The Commanders are struggling most defensively under Dan Quinn in the red zone. Going into Week 6, they were allowing opponents inside the 20 to score touchdowns at a league-high 83.3 percent clip. That was rough against the 49ers, who led the NFL with an 87.5 percent TD success rate in the red zone. Last week: 25 Pro Football Network (Infante) Even in an NFC East that might be the worst division in the NFL, the Washington Commanders’ 1-4-1 start might be too much to overcome. They fought hard in the second half to make up for the large deficit they gave up to the 49ers in the first half, but their mismanagement in the clutch resulted in yet another loss. The Commanders could be without Terry McLaurin for the foreseeable future after his unfortunate injury on Monday , and if there’s one thing an NFL team with a struggling offense doesn’t need, it’s a serious injury to its top wide receiver. It will be very tough to Washington to crawl out of the hole it has dug for itself. Last week: 27 Clutch Sports (Johrendt) The hits just keep on coming for the Commanders, as their Monday Night Football loss to the 49ers is overshadowed by a serious injury suffered by WR Terry McLaurin. Likely losing McLaurin for the rest of the season, Washington is still sitting on only one win and staring up at yet another lost season, one that could finally spell the end for head coach Dan Quinn and other members of the coaching staff. Commanders links Articles The Athletic Jayden Daniels, Commanders under scrutiny after another game management mistake On fourth-and-2 from the 49ers’ 13-yard line early in the second quarter of what became a 49ers’ 23-17 win, Washington coach Dan Quinn decided to go for it. Running back Rachaad White was flagged for an illegal shift, which would have negated a successful play. But before that, Daniels scrambled right to bide more time — and then threw the ball out of bounds, looking as if he wanted to avoid a sack. “I just gotta execute better in that situation regardless of a flag or not,” Daniels said after the game. “Fourth down … don’t die with the ball, so I have to be better in that spot. Said ESPN analyst Troy Aikman on the broadcast: “You don’t throw (the) ball away on fourth down. You gotta at least give your receiver an opportunity.” Video circulated after the play of a frustrated Quinn. Earlier on the broadcast, ESPN’s Laura Rutledge reported that Quinn had said he would stand closer to first-year offensive coordinator David Blough in critical situations to make sure the Commanders avoided such embarrassments as allowing the clock to run out in overtime — the error that cost them the opportunity to kick a game-winning field goal last week against the New York Giants. Instead, the NFC East rivals finished in a 27-27 tie, and Quinn, his coaches and his quarterback were skewered for much of the past week. “Our time today as a team was spent on the how and why to make sure that it never does (happen) again,” Quinn told reporters last Monday afternoon. “So, yesterday’s ending was the biggest example, but we’ve got a lot of s— to clean up from yesterday’s game. And trust me, everyone in this building, starting with me, feels that urgency.” To read more of this article, CLICK HERE Riggo’s Rag Commanders fans should brace for the worst after Terry McLaurin’s injury Terry McLaurin has been the beating heart of Washington Commanders football almost since he was drafted as a third-round steal in 2019. But now, fans should prepare for the worst after a potentially devastating injury setback. After catching an impressive 27-yard gain on Washington’s first offensive play during their Monday Night Football loss to the San Francisco 49ers , things took a dark turn for McLaurin. The wide receiver went down with a non-contact injury , and concerns were immediate after he grabbed his knee. McLaurin was carted off the field and ruled out for the rest of the game. It seemed bad, and the reaction of the players from both sides told fans all they needed to know. To read more of this article, CLICK HERE Riggo’s Rag Dan Quinn’s fourth-down defense reignites calls for Commanders to fire him “I definitely knew it was fourth down. We were going for it, and I think with the illegal shift, there is not a penalty to go for a field goal. Like, it’s the turn(over) on downs, I think somebody had asked me.” "I definitely knew it was 4th down." Commanders HC Dan Quinn on the 4th down play that Jayden Daniels threw the ball away in the second quarter. pic.twitter.com/SiBP2SIClg — ESPN (@espn) October 20, 2026 To read more of this article, CLICK HERE NFL.com Commanders-49ers on ‘Monday Night Football’: What We Learned from San Francisco’s 23-17 win Daniels almost makes amends for previous loss. There could not have been a more trepidatious week for Jayden Daniels to play under the prime-time spotlight. His brain fart in Week 5 against the Giants, taking a sack and allowing time to run out in overtime when the Commanders were in position for a game-winning field goal, likely hung heavy over Daniels and the team during their Monday night preparations. That certainly looked to be the case early on, as Washington got little going and the defense appeared overpowered by a mighty 49ers crew. Daniels flipped a switch on the other side of half, though, completely rewriting the narrative of a game that initially looked to be too much for the Commanders. After penalties derailed Washington’s first third-quarter possession, Daniels led back-to-back scoring drives of 56 and 66 yards, carving up San Francisco’s defense despite Terry McLaurin being carted off in the opening frame with a knee injury. Daniels, who went 22 of 30 for 212 passing yards, two touchdowns and a 114.9 passer rating in the second half, then saw two different chances to lead a game-winning drive and quiet the noise from the past eight days. He not only came up just short, he unfortunately also made a massive mistake on each possession. On the first, he was forced to burn a timeout after letting the play clock run down on a fourth-and-8, which meant the Commanders would have one less chance to stop the clock if they didn’t convert. They did, but turned it over on downs a few plays later, leaving Washington only two timeouts already under the two-minute warning. After Washington’s defense, which had turned it on to make life hell for Brock Purdy and Co. throughout the second half, got Daniels the ball back, he again committed a huge no-no by intentionally grounding the ball to avoid a sack just after he’d led the offense to San Francisco’s 28-yard line. That left him with only a hail Mary chance left, which he was sacked on. Daniels and Washington showed so much fight, but there’s always been a Jekyll-and-Hyde nature to the quarterback’s play. And after this incident with the blood clots, it’s getting harder to see a future with him under center in 2027. It’s not because Hurts is a bad quarterback, because he clearly isn’t. But even when things looked their most optimistic, there were questions about whether the Eagles would hitch their wagons to Hurts long term after this season. Hurts’ contract extension only guarantees him $22 million following the 2026 season, and serves as an off-ramp for the team to change directions at that position if they want to. The 2026 season was supposed to determine whether Hurts would be able to play well enough to continue on in Sean Mannion’s offense. Unfortunately, we only saw five weeks of uneven play, with Hurts at times struggling to string together drives with an injury-plagued roster and a new offensive coordinator that is still getting his feet wet. And, Hurts also played one of those games on four hours’ sleep in another country after spending the previous night in the hospital because of concerns about blood clots. The Commanders did come out in the second half and make it somewhat of a game, but it felt as though Kyle Shanahan was simply toying with Dan Quinn all game. Washington is now 1-4-1 heading into a bye week and will look to make some much needed adjustments on both sides of the ball (and maybe at head coach) when they return to action Nov. 1 against a reeling Eagles team on Sunday Night Football. title: 2027 NFL mock draft: Yates' early predictions for top 10 picks, QB landing spots
summary: We're two months into the college football season, and Field Yates is projecting which prospects could go in the top 10 picks of the 2027 NFL draft -- including three QBs.
full_text:
The 2027 NFL draft is six months away, but it's never too early to project what's going to happen! Plus, we have six weeks of NFL play and two months of college football games  to fuel our educated guesses for prospect landing spots.

 But ... since there's plenty of football still ahead, I'm only going through the top 10 picks, with the order based on the inverse of the standings through Week 6  of the NFL season. But there's plenty of intrigue in these limited selections, including two picks for the Jets that they acquired via trades. And there will be plenty of quarterbacks coming off the board early.

 As we say before every mock draft, it's important to remember that some prospects could decide to head back to school and others could surprisingly declare early. And every NFL team's needs will change amid injuries, breakouts, trades, free agency moves and coaching changes before the draft starts April 29.

 Here are my early projections for the top 10 picks in 2027, starting with the reeling Chargers.

 

 

 1. Los Angeles Chargers (0-6) 
 Jeremiah Smith , WR, Ohio State 

 A pathetic season so far for the Chargers can be traced to several factors, one of which is that the team has no difference-makers among its pass catchers. The Chargers don't have a single receiver in the top 50 for receiving yards per game, and they're 29th in yards after the catch.

 Smith is the most decorated wideout in Ohio State's rich history, and he could be the Big Ten's all-time leader in receiving yards and receiving TDs as soon as Halloween against USC . He has 984 yards and 12 touchdowns this season alone. His combination of size (6-foot-4, 222 pounds), speed and force should immediately translate to the NFL. It has been 30 years since a wide receiver was taken No. 1 (Keyshawn Johnson in 1996). That is very much in play in 2027.

 
 

 

 2. Miami Dolphins (0-5) 
 Drew Mestemaker , QB, Oklahoma State 

 Miami has needs everywhere, but its modest investment in Malik Willis (whose three-year, $67.5 million contract has no guaranteed money beyond 2027) puts quarterback in play. The 20-year-old Mestemaker oozes upside, as the 6-3 215-pounder is a legitimate dual-threat player with exceptional creativity inside and outside of the pocket. I'm giving him the early lead as the top QB in the class, which aligns with Mel Kiper Jr.'s Big Board and Jordan Reid's QB rankings .

 Despite not starting at quarterback in high school, Mestemaker has shown enough in just two college seasons -- one at North Texas -- to contend for the No. 1 pick. He is a fearless playmaker who can impact nearly every blade of grass on the field with his mobility and off-platform throwing skills.

 
 

 3. Tennessee Titans (1-5) 
 Leonard Moore , CB, Notre Dame 

 In this scenario, the Titans have to consider a question on defensive philosophy: Do you build from the front to the back, or just take a surefire cornerback?

 Ultimately, I landed on Moore over someone like Texas'  Colin Simmons  at this early point of the process, as he is off to another exceptional start with just six receptions allowed on 153 coverage snaps. Moore has size (6-2, 197 pounds), a fierce mentality to covet tough matchups, excellent ball skills and solid overall anticipation. He is a true shutdown cornerback, which warrants a selection this high. But the Titans also need young edge rushers, so Simmons was nearly my pick here.

 
 

 4. Tampa Bay Buccaneers (1-5) 
 Colin Simmons , Edge, Texas 

 Tampa Bay is looking for more impact pass rushers -- a way too familiar spot for the team. The Bucs selected Rueben Bain Jr . in April and are getting strong play from 2025 draftee David Walker , but 11 total sacks through six games just won't cut it.

 Simmons is a hyper-charged playmaker who is a massive mismatch for offensive tackles because of his acceleration and overall twitchiness. Though he is listed at just 246 pounds, somewhat light for an NFL edge rusher, his production is off the charts. He's up to 31.5 sacks and eight forced fumbles since the start of the 2024 season.

 
 

 5. Washington Commanders (1-5) 
 Dylan Stewart , Edge, South Carolina 

 The Commanders spent big in free agency to land edge rusher Odafe Oweh , but they are still struggling to impact opposing quarterbacks. So far in 2026, they're 25th in sacks per dropback (4.5%) and 20th in pass rush win rate (48.2%).

 The best version of Stewart has a case for the top pass rusher in the class, as he's incredibly explosive, powerful, long and hell on wheels to try to block. But teams will have some questions about a recent one-game suspension for punching an Alabama player in the helmet and arguing with coaches on the sideline.

 Stewart is immensely talented, but he must harness that skill and find a way for those physical traits to translate into straight production. He has one sack this season and 12 over the past three years.

 

 
 

 6. Philadelphia Eagles (2-4) 
 Charlie Becker , WR, Indiana 

 This Eagles season has not completely gone by the wayside because of the overall NFC East struggles, but it's clear this team has a lot of roster work to do in the offseason. After filling out their slot position with rookie first-round pick Makai Lemon , adding another dynamic perimeter playmaker opposite  DeVonta Smith would be a big boost for the offense.

 Becker has flourished into a megastar in his first season as a full-time starter, ranking 11th nationally in receiving yards per game (99.1). He's 6-4 and 208 pounds with exceptional speed, terrific hands and a unique ability to beat man coverage on the outside.

 
 

 7. New York Jets ( via 2-4 DAL ) 
 CJ Carr , QB, Notre Dame 

 The early returns suggest the Jets went 3-for-3 with their trio of first-rounders in 2026 (edge rusher  David Bailey , tight end  Kenyon Sadiq and receiver  Omar Cooper Jr .), allowing those players to take a massive step forward in 2027. Carr would be their attempt to solve the biggest long-term problem, which is finding a solution under center -- 36-year-old  Geno Smith is currently on a one-year deal .

 In two seasons at Notre Dame, Carr has shown a strong ability to handle pre-snap duties and process quickly, while also being a mechanically sound and talented thrower. He's at his best operating from the pocket, but he's dangerous enough with his legs to keep a defense honest (six rushing touchdowns since the start of last season).

 
 

 8. Houston Texans (2-4) 
 Trevor Goosby , OT, Texas 

 It's important to say that I am bullish on the Texans picking much later than this, as they're coming off back-to-back wins against AFC South opponents. But you are what your record says you are, and this is how it presently shakes out.

 Houston's offensive line has been a multiyear project to get right, which included selecting LT Aireontae Ersery and LG Keylan Rutledge early in the past two drafts. Goosby and LSU's  Jordan Seaton  are among the top offensive tackles in this class. But I'm giving Goosby a narrow edge in this scenario for his standout run blocking and overall power.

 
 

 9. Arizona Cardinals (2-4) 
 Trinidad Chambliss , QB, Ole Miss 

 The Cardinals made enough of an investment in Carson Beck this April (65th overall) to suggest he could be the long-term starter, but I'm not sold on that being the case. Enter the dynamic Chambliss, who makes up for below-average size (6-foot, 205 pounds) with playmaking, clutch production, experience and craftiness.

 No quarterback in this class has played better in big games than Chambliss, who averaged 307 passing yards and accounted for six touchdowns in three College Football Playoff games last season. He has led Ole Miss to three wins over AP Top 25 teams in 2026.

 

 
 

 10. New York Jets ( via 2-4 IND ) 
 Ashton Hampton , CB, Clemson 

 This is the second of the two first-round selections the Jets got in the  Sauce Gardner trade  (the first of which was in 2026), which they could use to bolster their cornerbacks room.…

title: NFL Power Rankings: How all 32 teams stack up for Week 7, plus offensive issues
summary: How does every NFL team stack up heading into Week 7? We made our 1-32 list and picked the biggest offensive problem for every team.
full_text:
Week 6 of the 2026 NFL season featured some troubling performances from offenses around the league. The Cardinals went 0-for-5 in the red zone, yet still defeated the Rams, who lost a fumble and turned the ball over on downs twice. Chargers quarterback Justin Herbert had an interception for the sixth straight game, helping lead to a sixth straight loss. And Falcons quarterback Michael Penix Jr . was sacked five times against the Bears.

 Why did these offenses struggle so much? In addition to our updated 1-32 rankings, we asked our NFL Nation reporters to pick out the biggest offensive issue for each team. From ineffective run games to a lack of red zone efficiency, what is causing each team to falter this season?

 To form the list, our power panel of more than a dozen NFL analysts evaluates how all 32 teams stack up against one another. Here are a few highlights from this week's rankings:

 
 The Texans are slowly climbing up our list after a shocking 0-4 start to the season. After defeating the Titans in Week 5, Houston got another win over a divisional opponent in the Jaguars. The London matchup was also the Texans debut of wide receiver  Marvin Harrison Jr ., who had three receptions for 34 yards after being traded from the Cardinals last week. 
 The Rams are out of the top 10 in our rankings for the first time this season after their second straight loss Sunday . They are the fifth team in the past 50 seasons to enter a season as the outright Super Bowl favorite and lose at least four of their first six games, per ESPN Research. None of the previous four teams made the conference title game (2015 Seahawks, 2002 Rams, 1999 Vikings and 1987 Giants). 
 The NFC East is off to a rocky start, becoming the first division in NFL history to be winless in consecutive weeks in which every team in the division played a game, per ESPN Research. That struggle has been illustrated in our list. Compared with last week's rankings, the Cowboys are down six spots, the Eagles are down five, the Giants fell four and the Commanders were lowered one spot. Dallas is the only one of those teams to not play a backup QB this season. 
 
 Let's get into the full list, starting with the same No. 1 team from last week .

 

 
 Jump to a team: 
 ARI | ATL | BAL | BUF | CAR | CHI | CIN 
 CLE | DAL | DEN | DET | GB | HOU | IND 
 JAX | KC | LAC | LAR | LV | MIA | MIN 
 NE | NO | NYG | NYJ | PHI | PIT | SF 
 SEA | TB | TEN | WSH 

 
 

 

 1. San Francisco 49ers (6-0) 
 Week 6 result: Beat the Commanders 23-17 
 Week 6 ranking: 1 

 Biggest issue on offense: Wide receiver injuries

 

 The Niners haven't had many problems in terms of production, but they have had a significant amount of attrition at wideout. Ricky Pearsall ( knee ), De'Zhaun Stribling ( ankle ), Christian Kirk (calf) and Demarcus Robinson ( ankle ) were supposed to be four of the team's top five receivers and all landed on IR before Week 3. That doesn't account for Deebo Samuel Sr .'s multiweek hamstring injury  or the various bumps and bruises  Mike Evans  played through before departing Monday night's game with Achilles tendinitis . The good news? Most of them are expected back this season, but the 49ers have had to scramble in the meantime. -- Nick Wagoner 

 
 

 

 2. Kansas City Chiefs (5-0) 
 Week 6 result: Beat the Chargers 22-6 
 Week 6 ranking: 2 

 Biggest issue on offense: Offensive tackle health

 

 The Chiefs have done an admirable job protecting quarterback Patrick Mahomes , especially since left tackle Josh Simmons , their 2025 first-round pick, has been out because of a bulging disk in his lower back . Coach Andy Reid suggested Simmons won't be ready for Sunday's showdown against the Seahawks . Plus, right tackle Jaylon Moore sustained a concussion against the Chargers. Reid might have to continue altering the Chiefs' playbook if undrafted rookies Kahlil Benson (left tackle) and Joshua Ezeudu (right tackle) are the starters. -- Nate Taylor 

 
 

 3. Buffalo Bills (5-1) 
 Week 6 result: Beat the Raiders 33-30 
 Week 6 ranking: 3 

 Biggest issue on offense: Putting the ball on the ground

 

 Any criticism of an offense that leads the league in scoring and ranks top three in total offense and yards per play might seem like a nitpick. But running back James Cook III and quarterback Josh Allen have coughed up a few too many fumbles to start the season. Just imagine what this offense would look like if it weren't for five lost fumbles, including three in opposing territory. The Bills did show improvement against the Raiders on Sunday, though, committing zero turnovers. -- Nick Suss 

 
 

 4. Minnesota Vikings (5-0) 
 Week 6 result: Bye 
 Week 6 ranking: 6 

 Biggest issue on offense: Injuries across the board

 

 The Vikings spent the five games before their bye searching for smooth air offensively. There were plenty of reasons for that, but the biggest was simply health-related personnel turnover. Players who have missed at least one game include quarterback Kyler Murray ( concussion ), receivers Justin Jefferson ( ankle ) and Jordan Addison ( hamstring ), running back Jordan Mason ( finger ), left tackle Christian Darrisaw ( concussion ), left guard Donovan Jackson (knee), and tight ends T.J. Hockenson ( concussion ) and Josh Oliver (biceps). All but Jackson and Oliver are expected to return next week. -- Kevin Seifert 

 
 

 5. Jacksonville Jaguars (4-2) 
 Week 6 result: Lost to the Texans 34-31 
 Week 6 ranking: 5 

 Biggest issue on offense: Penalties

 

 Penalties have cost the Jaguars three touchdowns, including a pair of 3-yard touchdown runs by running back  Bhayshul Tuten . It happened again in Sunday's loss, with a questionable holding call on tight end  Brenton Strange . The Jaguars didn't get points on that possession because QB Trevor Lawrence threw an end zone interception two plays later. Jacksonville did score touchdowns after the other two penalties, against New England and Cincinnati, but it finally caught up to them in a three-point loss to the Texans. -- Michael DiRocco 

 
 

 6. Seattle Seahawks (3-3) 
 Week 6 result: Lost to the Broncos 17-14 
 Week 6 ranking: 4 

 Biggest issue on offense: Turnovers

 

 The Seahawks' run game has been underwhelming and their pass protection has been problematic, but no issue is holding first-year coordinator Brian Fleury's unit back like turnovers. It has committed 12 of them, third most of any offense so far. While  Sam Darnold 's struggles go beyond his interceptions, he has thrown seven picks in four games since returning from a glute injury . Seattle has also lost five fumbles. How costly have those giveaways been? Ten of the Seahawks' turnovers have come in their three losses, which were by a combined eight points. The opponents in those losses scored 44 points off those takeaways. -- Brady Henderson 

 

 
 

 7. New England Patriots (4-2) 
 Week 6 result: Beat the Jets 26-19 
 Week 6 ranking: 9 

 Biggest issue on offense: Offensive line health

 

 The Patriots had three starters -- right tackle Morgan Moses (ankle), left guard Alijah Vera-Tucker (hamstring) and right guard  Ben Brown  (knee) --  get knocked out of Sunday's game . And the only reason Brown was in the lineup was because opening-day starter Mike Onwenu ( ankle ) and his replacement Greg Van Roten ( hip ) were put on IR earlier in the season. The Patriots have started three different OL combinations in their first six games, and there will likely be a fourth Thursday in Chicago. -- Mike Reiss 

 
 

 8. Baltimore Ravens (4-2) 
 Week 6 result: Lost to the Browns 13-10 
 Week 6 ranking: 7 

 Biggest issue on offense: Penalties

 

 Baltimore's offense has been flagged an NFL-worst 31 times, with a bulk of the penalties coming from false starts (13) and holding (13). On Sunday, the Ravens were called for delay of game three times with backup quarterback Tyler Huntley , which led to a season-low 10 points. title: 'It's Groundhog Day': Why Ravens lead the NFL in blown double-digit leads
summary: Here is a look at the trends in the Ravens failing to hold double-digit leads.
full_text:
CLEVELAND -- All of the Baltimore Ravens ' confidence built up from their clutch play the past three weeks disappeared by the end of Sunday's 13-10 loss to the Cleveland Browns . 
 
 As Andre Szmyt's  37-yard game-winning field goal sailed through the uprights as time expired, the Ravens lamented another loss they felt they should have won. Even Ravens safety Kyle Hamilton , who is one of the most insightful players in this locker room, hit his breaking point when he didn't have an answer for how to solve another late-game collapse. 
 
 "I'm not going to sound like a broken record," Hamilton said. "It's 'Groundhog Day' with this question. I don't know. I'm not going to give you an answer. I really don't know. So, sorry, that's the best I can give you, but we've had this conversation so many times. I don't even feel like addressing it again." 
 
 Hamilton is referring to Baltimore's 16th blown double-digit lead since 2020, which is the most in the NFL in that span. It's three more than any other team (the Los Angeles Chargers are second with 13). 
 
 On Sunday, fill-in starting quarterback Tyler Huntley led the Ravens to a 10-0 lead after two drives. The Baltimore defense, meanwhile, didn't look like it was going to allow the Browns to score, recording as many sacks (three) as completions by halftime. 
 
 Then, all-too-familiar mistakes -- Derrick Henry 's fumble, Tyler Loop 's missed field goal and the secondary's lapses in coverage -- helped Cleveland score the final 13 points of the game. 
 
 "That's a type of game where I think [in] all three phases, you have chances to create more separation," coach Jesse Minter said. 
 
 
 The Ravens acknowledged their frustration because they had believed they had moved past these types of meltdowns. Baltimore's last three wins came in the final moments from Loop's game-winning field goal against the Dallas Cowboys in Brazil, Malaki Starks ' leaping catch of an onside kick against the Tennessee Titans and Hamilton's interception in overtime at Atlanta. 
 
 There is hope that quarterback Lamar Jackson will come back this week after missing the last two games with an ankle injury. It would be a timely return for the Ravens (4-2) considering the next three games are against the Cincinnati Bengals (3-2), who are considered Baltimore's biggest threat to the AFC North title, and two division leaders in the Buffalo Bills (5-1) and Jacksonville Jaguars (4-2). 
 
 "We just didn't make the plays that we wanted to make this game," defensive tackle Nnamdi Madubuike said. "One thing I know about this team [is that] we are going to learn from this, we are going to grow from this, and we are going to get better. We are going to have our eyes moving forward to the next opponent."' 
 
 Here is a look at the trends in the Ravens failing to hold double-digit leads: 
 
 

 

 
 
 
 Turnovers on offense 
 
 
 The momentum shifted Sunday when Henry fumbled in the fourth quarter, giving the ball to the Browns at the Ravens' 35-yard line with 12:36 left. Seven plays later, Cleveland running back Audric Estime rushed for a 2-yard touchdown to tie the game at 10. 
 
 After the loss, Henry told his teammates in the locker room: "Put this one on me." 
 
 "I got to take care of the ball," Henry said. "There's no excuses for that. I got to be better. I put the team's in harm's way. I sound like a broken record with this, but I got to go back to work on it. Can't put the team in that situation." 
 
 
 
 This was Henry's NFL-worst third lost fumble in the fourth quarter since the start of the 2025 season, but there's plenty of blame to go around. In those 16 blown double-digit leads, Baltimore has totaled 15 turnovers in the fourth quarter with seven interceptions and eight fumbles. 
 
 
 
 
 
 Missed field goals 
 
 
 Early in the fourth quarter Sunday, Baltimore could have made it a two-score game. But Loop's 49-yard field goal veered wide left to keep the Ravens' lead at 10-3. 
 
 "I just did not strike it the way I needed to," Loop said. "[I] didn't hit the ball clean. It ended up having some bad rotation, and [it] just slid out to the left." 
 
 
 
 
 Loop has made some huge kicks recently from the winning 56-yarder as time expired in Brazil to the 64-yarder against the Titans to the pair of 51-yarders at the Falcons. But three of his seven career misses came in the second half of collapses against the New England Patriots (Week 16 of last season), Pittsburgh Steelers (Week 18 of last season) and Sunday at the Browns. 
 
 "There is a confidence level for how Tyler prepares and how he practices and how he operates and how he strikes the ball, but at the same time, that position itself is completely results-driven," Minter said. "So, we'll continue to work with him and continue to try to put him in position, but we need to make second-half kicks. You could argue that second-half missed field goals are no different than turning the ball over in those situations. So, [that's] definitely something we want to keep striving to be better at." 
 
 
 
 
 
 Struggles in the secondary 
 
 
 Like so many times in these devastating defeats, the Ravens unraveled late against the Browns. 
 
 In the first three quarters, Baltimore held quarterback Deshaun Watson  to 8-of-14 passing for 70 yards. In the fourth quarter, the Ravens allowed Watson to complete eight of 12 passes for 94 yards. 
 
 "Being a member of the secondary, it seems like whenever we are losing these games, the ball is in the air," cornerback Marlon Humphrey said. "Obviously, we played a decent game before that, but when it counts, how can you win the game? I feel like that's usually won in the back end, and we just weren't able to do that today." 
 
 In the 16 blown double-digit leads, the secondary has struggled in the fourth quarter where quarterbacks have averaged 111.6 yards passing, throwing 17 touchdowns and no interceptions. 
 
 "It's pretty frustrating," Humphrey said. "I think we feel that we are better, we feel that we're equipped, [and] we feel that we're ready for these moments. We just [have] got to consistently do it. We [have] got to consistently believe that you trust the guy next to you. I think it all starts with communication. Someone has to end the game for us. I think that's the biggest thing. Are all 11 guys thinking, 'I'm going to be the one to end the game.' That's where it starts, and that's where it ends."

title: Bobby Okereke continues to play key role in Panthers' revival
summary: Bobby Okereke had a mixed stint with the New York Giants, but the linebacker's game has progressed in leaps and bounds in the opening five games of his stint at the Carolina Panthers.
full_text:
Bobby Okereke had a mixed stint with the New York Giants, but the linebacker's game has progressed in leaps and bounds in the opening five games of his stint at the Carolina Panthers.

 Okereke - who has deep family ties to Nigeria - takes the Africa Player of the Week for Week 6 for his performance against the Philadelphia Eagles, but he was not the only Nigerian-American NFL star who made a key impact in a win this week.

 Chimere Dike, Oluwafemi Oladejo (both Tennessee Titans) and Osa Odighizuwa (San Francisco 49ers) also put in memorable shifts.

 African Player of the Week: Bobby Okereke (Carolina Panthers) 

 

 Okereke - whose parents are Nigerian and has played a major role in the NFL's development work in Africa and particularly his home country - starred in week 8 with eight tackles, two passes defended and a sack in a 25-14 win over the Philadelphia Eagles.

 Seven of Okereke's tackles were solo as he was among the leaders of a stellar defensive performance which saw the Panthers go to 3-2 for the season.

 His sack on Tanner McKee on the first play of the game for an 11-yard loss was one of the most memorable moments of the week.

 With a sack, a forced fumble, an interception, and a total of four passes defended across his first five Panthers games, Okereke is at or near many of his tallies in key areas for the whole of his final season with the Giants.

 The Panthers, too, continue their upward trajectory - having improved year on year since a disastrous 2023 campaign which saw them win only two games. Last season's record of 8-9 was significantly better, and this time, they top the NFC South as it stands.

 

 African Moment of the Week: Chimere Dike (Tennessee Titans) 

 Dike's 58-yard punt return at the beginning of the fourth quarter was an instrumental play for the Tennessee Titans in their 26-20 win over the Indianapolis Colts.

 The return came right at the beginning of the quarter, with the Colts leading 13-6. Dike came close to going all the way for the touchdown himself, slicing through at least seven potential tacklers before he was eventually brought down.

 That run nevertheless set up a drive on which the Titans scored and levelled the game, and they never looked back from there - snatching control of the game and clinching their first win of the season.

 Dike - who has Nigerian ties through his father - played a key role. In addition to the 58-yard punt returns, he also tallied 118 yards across five kick returns.

 Honorable mentions 
 Dike's teammate and Nigerian-American compatriot, Oluwafemi Oladejo, scored a surprise touchdown in the Titans' win off a blocked punt.

 Osa Odighizuwa - also of Nigerian descent - picked up a sack in the Monday night game as the San Francisco 49ers beat the Washington Commanders 23-17.

 Another player of Nigerian descent, Emeka Egbuka, scored a touchdown for the Tampa Bay Buccaneers in a 26-19 overtime loss to the Pittsburgh Steelers. The Seattle Seahawks' Nick Emmanwori was another player with Nigerian roots to have big plays in a defeat, as he picked up seven tackles and a sack in the 17-14 loss to the Denver Broncos.

 Jaxon Smith-Njigba - who proudly represents Sierra Leone and comes from a family with deep West African ties despite being born in Nacogdoches, Texas himself - tallied 134 yards across 12 receptions in the Week 6 loss.

 Mo Alie-Cox - another NFL player with Sierra Leonean ties - scored a touchdown for the Colts in defeat to the Titans.

 Alvin Kamara (roots in Liberia) crossed over for a crucial touchdown in the New Orleans Saints' 34-27 win over the New York Giants.

 Africa-born Player Watch 

 It was not the best day at the office for Zimbabwe's Nate Landman as his LA Rams went down 18-16 to the Arizona Cardinals, but the linebacker still managed 10 tackles.

 Guinea-born Liberian defensive end Kwity Paye picked up a sack for the Las Vegas Raiders, but also ultimately in defeat as they went down 33-30 to the Buffalo Bills.
